# Changelog

## 0.1.0 (unreleased)

First release.

**Gateway**
- OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses, Anthropic Messages, and embeddings; pass-through or
  translation between the formats, streaming included.
- Backends: Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI,
  OpenRouter, direct open-model vendors (DeepSeek, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, Mistral), and any
  OpenAI-compatible server. Keyless on Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure with workload identity.
- Works unchanged with pi, Claude Code, and the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs (`meritorder setup`).

**Routing**
- Rule-based classifier sets a quality floor; a marginal-cost router picks the backend, counting the
  cost of rebuilding a session's prompt cache before moving it.
- GPUs priced by how busy they are (near free with headroom), so spare GPU capacity is used first.
- Routes that cost about the same go to the faster one, measured from real replies (time to first
  token and tokens per second). The `balanced` and `speed` priorities pay up to 20% or 100% more for
  a faster route, set per organization, team, or request (`X-MeritOrder-Priority`).
- Failover catches errors that arrive after a `200` (Anthropic's in-stream overload, OpenRouter error
  chunks) and streams that never start. Over capacity skips just that model on that backend, for the
  provider's `Retry-After`. Outage and recovery alerts go to the webhook, and responses say what they
  failed over from.
- Evals that separate the strongest models: a `frontier` suite of hard tasks (code checked by hidden
  tests in a Docker sandbox, multi-step tool use against scripted environments, long documents,
  exact-answer reasoning, and open-ended work graded by two judges from different model families).
  Scores come with a finer 0–5 ability figure and a flag where evidence is thin. Run them from the
  console's new Models → Evals page (estimate, progress, cancel, per-task results, apply scores as a
  config version) or with `meritorder eval`; both land in the same history.
- Outage alerts name the model's other live backends ("Requests go to anthropic, openrouter meanwhile"), even when the
  failing request was pinned to one backend. A model missing on a backend (404) is retried after 5 minutes, then
  less and less often up to hourly. Bedrock and Foundry can be switched off in `.env` until their models exist.
- Evals compare like with like: no output limit (each model may write as much as it can), every
  model at the same reasoning effort for a level, each on its own provider's API, and every answer,
  agent tool call and judge's reason kept for review. A reply cut off by the model's maximum fails
  and says so; one cut off by the per-request cost limit isn't graded. Runs also report what the
  work took: each model's median and 90th-percentile time to complete a task, turns and tool calls,
  output tokens, and cost per task solved.
- No arbitrary output limits: a request without `max_tokens` may write as much as its model can
  (`max_output_tokens`, from the price catalog), less what won't fit in the context window or under
  the per-request cost limit, which now trims such a reply instead of using a 16,000-token guess.
  Non-streaming requests that may run long are streamed from the provider and assembled, so they
  don't time out. `auto` sends high reasoning effort for level 4–5 work (Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5
  default to medium).
- Refusal fallback and automatic reasoning effort for `auto`; opt-in substitution for named
  models that have nowhere to run (never to a weaker model).
- A saturated GPU spills to other routes, and queues (bounded) only when it's the last resort.

**GPUs**
- Capacity controller starts and stops SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM deployments when demand pays for
  them, with SkyPilot catalog prices, hysteresis, and fleet-wide caps.
- Console controls: stop (drain or now), pin replicas, stop all; activity log; where each replica
  runs, uptime, burn rate, and cost.

**Models (as of November 10, 2026)**
- Claude Fable 5.2 ($8/$40), Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5; GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra and
  GPT-6 Luna (the `gpt-terra` and `gpt-luna` names now point at the current models, and `gpt-5.6-*` names
  still resolve to them). Sonnet 5.5's cache reads are priced at $0.10 per million tokens (they were $0.20).
- Gemini 4 Carbon and 4 Argon ($2/$10 until November 30, 2026, then $4/$20), Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.5
  Flash-Lite, through OpenRouter. They have no quality scores until an eval measures them, so `auto`
  doesn't pick them yet; requests that name them work. Gemini's reasoning details (which its tool calls
  need sent back) survive replies the gateway assembles from a stream.

**Spend and savings**
- Budgets per organization, GPU fleet, team, person, and session; rate limits; per-request cost cap.
  Each person can have their own monthly limit (People page, admin API, or their static key) that
  replaces their team's per-person default.
  The shipped config reads the organization-wide caps from `.env` (`MERITORDER_ORG_BUDGET_USD` and
  friends), and `.env` comments at the end of a line are read the way Docker Compose reads them.
- Savings ledger by cause (routing, caching, self-hosting, compression, response cache) against a
  per-team baseline.
- GPT-5.6 tool calls through OpenAI work: its Chat Completions endpoint rejects function tools with
  reasoning, so the OpenAI backend sends requests to the Responses API (`api: responses`) and converts
  the replies back. Agents like Claude Code and pi can use GPT models with reasoning on.
- Claude through OpenRouter is prompt-cached (it wasn't: every turn paid full price), and the router
  prices cache writes on every route, so it no longer prefers a route only because it skipped the write.
- OpenRouter requests record what OpenRouter billed, not a catalog estimate: it picks among providers
  whose prices differ (catalog prices were up to 56% low in testing). `billed_cost` sets this per backend.
- Every setting on the console's Config page explains itself: a "?" beside each field (hover, keyboard
  focus, or tap) says what it does and its default. The forms also cover the OpenAI endpoint, the
  first-token timeout, cost-or-speed priority, static-key monthly limits, and GPU launch rules.

# 02 — Request flow One turn of a pi session using `model="auto"`. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant H as Harness (pi) participant G as Gateway participant R as Redis participant P as Postgres participant B as Chosen backend H->>G: POST /v1/messages
key, X-Session-Id, model=auto, full history G->>G: Validate key (in-process cache for 60 s, Postgres on miss) G->>R: Check budgets (org, team, person), rate limits, session spend cap G->>R: Load session: model, backend, cache warm-until, prefix hash alt New session, new human prompt, or the harness compacted history G->>G: Classify task → quality floor G->>G: Candidate models: quality ≥ floor else Mid-task (tool results coming back) G->>G: Keep the session's model end G->>G: Score backends: rebuild + turns × per-turn cost, stickiness G->>G: Shape prompt: cache breakpoints, stable prefix G->>G: Compress huge tool outputs (deterministic, nothing stored) G->>B: Forward (translated to backend's API format) Note over G,B: On 5xx / 429 / timeout / bad key: next backend.
On a refusal (auto): next model. B-->>G: Stream tokens + usage (cached vs uncached tokens) G-->>H: Stream tokens (in the harness's API format) G->>R: Update session: model, backend, warm-until, prefix hash G-)P: Ledger row: actual cost, baseline cost, savings by cause G-)R: Spend counters, live feed event ``` ## Hot-path budget The gateway should add **single-digit milliseconds** before the first byte goes upstream. Everything on the hot path is in-memory or one Redis round trip: | Step | Where it reads from | |---|---| | Key validation | In-process LRU, Postgres on miss | | Rate limit / budget | Redis counters (Postgres is the source of truth, reconciled async) | | Session lookup | Redis | | GPU state and headroom | Published to Redis by the controller; each gateway reloads it every 5 s | | Classifier | Rules; only on new sessions and task boundaries | | Compression | Deterministic and in-memory; the same output always compresses the same way | Writes to Postgres (usage, ledger) are **async** and never block the response. ## What the harness sees Nothing unusual. Same API it already speaks, streamed tokens, usage numbers. Response headers tell curious users what happened: ``` x-meritorder-model: qwen3-coder-next # the model that answered x-meritorder-backend: gpu-qwen-coder # where it ran x-meritorder-floor: coding:3 # what the classifier decided (auto) x-meritorder-session: 3f9c… # the session it was counted under x-meritorder-request-id: 6b1e… # find it in the ledger x-meritorder-cost-usd: 0.000400 # non-streaming responses: cost, x-meritorder-baseline-usd: 0.031000 # what it would have cost without Merit Order, x-meritorder-savings-usd: 0.030600 # and the difference x-meritorder-refused-by: claude-opus # only when a model refused and another answered x-meritorder-substituted-for: qwen3-coder # only when a named model couldn't run (opt-in) ``` The whole decision, rule by rule, is in [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md).

import yaml

from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, Config, ModelConfig, Route, ServeConfig

    desired_replicas, parse_vllm_metrics,
)

SERVE = ServeConfig(model="ow", scale_up_after_minutes=10, hold_minutes=30, drain_minutes=15, max_replicas=4)


def test_desired_replicas_must_pay_for_themselves():
    # $50/h of API spend can pay for 2 replicas at $20/h (with 20% margin), throughput needs 3.
    d = desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=50, tokens_per_second=2000))
    assert d == 2
    assert desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=10, tokens_per_second=2000)) == 0
    warm = ServeConfig(model="ow", min_replicas=1)
    assert desired_replicas(warm, 20.0, 1000, Demand(0, 0)) == 1


def test_state_machine_full_cycle():
    t = 1_000_000.0
    rec, act = decide({}, SERVE, desired=2, status=Status(), now=t)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act is None  # must be justified for 10 minutes first
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + 601)
    assert rec["state"] == PROVISIONING and act.kind == "up" and act.replicas == 2
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM and rec["endpoint"] == "http://gpu/v1"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 3, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1600)
    assert act.kind == "scale" and act.replicas == 3
    # demand disappears, but GPUs are held for 30 minutes after warming
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1700)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801)
    assert rec["state"] == DRAINING
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801 + 901)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"


def test_provisioning_timeout_cools_down():
    t = 0.0
    rec = {"state": PROVISIONING, "since": t}
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 1)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 700)
    assert act is None  # still cooling down

class FakeProvisioner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
        self.ready = False

    async def status(self):
        return Status(ready=self.ready, endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1" if self.ready else None)

    async def up(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("up", n))

    async def scale(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("scale", n))

    async def down(self):
        self.calls.append(("down",))

def test_sky_python_found_next_to_sky_even_with_spaces_and_symlinks(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import os

    venv = tmp_path / "Example LLC" / "sky-venv" / "bin"
    venv.mkdir(parents=True)
    py = venv / "python"
    py.write_text("#!/bin/sh\n")
    py.chmod(0o755)
    sky = venv / "sky"
    sky.write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\n'''exec' \"{py}\" \"$0\" \"$@\"\n' '''\n")
    sky.chmod(0o755)
    links = tmp_path / "bin"
    links.mkdir()

    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(links))

    assert _shebang_python(sky.read_text().splitlines()) == str(py)
    assert _shebang_python(["#!/usr/local/bin/python3.12"]) == "/usr/local/bin/python3.12"

def candidate(most=128_000, window=1_000_000, fmt="anthropic", kind="api", price=Price(input=8, output=40)):
    bc = BackendConfig(name="b", format=fmt, kind=kind, base_url="https://b.example")
    m = ModelConfig(name="m", max_output_tokens=most, context_window=window, routes=[Route(backend="b", model="m-1", price=price)])
    return Candidate(model=m, route=m.routes[0], backend=Backend(bc), cost=0, warm=False, quality=5), bc, m


def gateway_for(bc, m, max_usd=None):
    return Gateway(Config(backends=[bc], models=[m], safeguards=Safeguards(max_request_usd=max_usd)), None, None, {}, None, None)


def test_allowance_is_the_models_limit_unless_something_smaller_applies():

"""Durable storage: users, API keys, the per-request ledger, and report queries.

Postgres in real deployments (ledger partitioned by month, hourly rollups);
an in-memory version for development and tests. The ledger holds metadata
only, never prompt or response content.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import secrets
import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

LEDGER_FIELDS = [
    "id", "ts", "user_id", "team", "key_id", "session_id", "tags", "client_format", "requested_model", "floor",
    "served_model", "upstream_model", "backend", "backend_kind", "status", "error", "stream", "upgraded", "proxy_cache",
    "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens", "latency_ms", "ttft_ms",
    "actual_cost", "served_api_cost", "baseline_cost", "list_cost",
    "savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache",
]
SUM_FIELDS = [
    "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens",
    "actual_cost", "served_api_cost", "baseline_cost", "list_cost",
    "savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache",
]
SAVINGS_FIELDS = ["savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache"]
GROUPS = {"user": "user_id", "team": "team", "model": "served_model", "backend": "backend", "day": "day", "hour": "hour", "month": "month", "none": None}
_TAG = re.compile(r"^tag:([A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64})$")


def hash_key(key: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()


def new_api_key() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Returns (key_id, secret). The secret is shown once and stored only as a hash."""
    return f"key_{secrets.token_hex(6)}", f"mo-{secrets.token_urlsafe(32)}"


def month_start(now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    return now.replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)


def validate_group(group_by: str) -> str:
    if group_by in GROUPS or _TAG.match(group_by):
        return group_by
    raise ValueError(f"group_by must be one of {', '.join(GROUPS)} or tag:<name>")


def complete_row(row: dict) -> dict:
    """Fill what a ledger row left out with the schema's defaults: a new id, now, no tags, zero counts."""
    out = {f: row.get(f) for f in LEDGER_FIELDS}
    out["id"] = out["id"] or uuid.uuid4()
    out["ts"] = out["ts"] or datetime.now(UTC)
    out["tags"] = out["tags"] or {}
    for f in SUM_FIELDS:
        out[f] = out[f] or 0
    for f in ("stream", "upgraded", "proxy_cache"):
        out[f] = bool(out[f])
    return {**row, **out}


def _finish_row(row: dict) -> dict:
    row["savings_total"] = sum(row.get(f) or 0 for f in SAVINGS_FIELDS)
    for k, v in list(row.items()):
        if isinstance(v, float):
            row[k] = round(v, 6)
        elif isinstance(v, datetime):
            row[k] = v.isoformat()
    return row


# ====================================================================== memory


class MemoryStore:
    kind = "memory"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.keys: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.ledger: list[dict] = []

    async def init(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def migrate(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def upsert_user(self, user_id: str, team: str, role: str, email: str | None = None, display_name: str | None = None,
                          source: str = "idp") -> None:
        """source="idp": a login refreshes team/role unless an admin pinned them; "ensure": only create if missing."""
        u = self.users.get(user_id)
        if u is None:
            self.users[user_id] = {"id": user_id, "team": team, "role": role, "email": email, "display_name": display_name,
                                   "managed": "idp", "disabled_at": None, "created_at": datetime.now(UTC)}
            return
        if source == "idp" and u.get("managed", "idp") == "idp":
            u.update(team=team, role=role)
        if email:
            u["email"] = email
        if display_name:
            u["display_name"] = display_name

    async def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> dict | None:
        u = self.users.get(user_id)
        return dict(u) if u else None

    async def update_user(self, user_id: str, team: str | None = None, role: str | None = None, disabled: bool | None = None,
                          managed: str | None = None) -> dict | None:
        u = self.users.get(user_id)
        if u is None:
            return None
        if team is not None or role is not None:
            u["managed"] = "local"
        if team is not None:
            u["team"] = team
        if role is not None:
            u["role"] = role
        if managed is not None:
            u["managed"] = managed
        if disabled is not None:
            u["disabled_at"] = datetime.now(UTC) if disabled else None
        return dict(u)

    async def find_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> dict | None:
        return next((dict(u) for u in self.users.values() if (u.get("email") or "").lower() == email.lower()), None)

    async def scim_groups(self) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(g) for g in self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {}).values()]

    async def scim_group(self, gid: str) -> dict | None:
        g = self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {}).get(gid)
        return dict(g) if g else None

    async def save_scim_group(self, group: dict) -> None:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {})[group["id"]] = dict(group)

    async def delete_scim_group(self, gid: str) -> bool:
        return self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {}).pop(gid, None) is not None

    async def list_users(self, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        out = []
        for u in self.users.values():
            if team and u["team"] != team:
                continue
            keys = [k for k in self.keys.values() if k["user_id"] == u["id"]]
            out.append({**u, "active_keys": sum(1 for k in keys if not k["revoked_at"]),
                        "last_seen": max((k.get("last_used_at") for k in keys if k.get("last_used_at")), default=None)})
        return out

    async def create_key(self, user_id: str, team: str, role: str, name: str | None = None, tags: dict | None = None,
                         expires_at: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key_id, secret = new_api_key()
        self.keys[hash_key(secret)] = {
            "id": key_id, "user_id": user_id, "team": team, "role": role, "name": name, "tags": tags or {},
            "created_at": datetime.now(UTC), "expires_at": expires_at, "revoked_at": None,
        }
        return key_id, secret

    async def find_key(self, key_hash: str) -> dict | None:
        return self.keys.get(key_hash)

    async def list_keys(self, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(k) for k in self.keys.values() if (user_id is None or k["user_id"] == user_id) and (team is None or k["team"] == team)]

    async def get_key(self, key_id: str) -> dict | None:
        return next((dict(k) for k in self.keys.values() if k["id"] == key_id), None)

    async def revoke_key(self, key_id: str) -> bool:
        for k in self.keys.values():
            if k["id"] == key_id and k["revoked_at"] is None:
                k["revoked_at"] = datetime.now(UTC)
                return True
        return False

    async def record(self, row: dict) -> None:
        self.ledger.append(complete_row(row))

    async def spend_since(self, field: str, value: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["actual_cost"] for r in self.ledger if r.get(field) == value and r["ts"] >= since)

    async def spend_all_since(self, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["actual_cost"] or 0 for r in self.ledger if r["ts"] >= since)

    # GPU time (cost of running replicas, accrued by the capacity controller) and the GPU activity log.

    async def add_gpu_usage(self, backend: str, ts: datetime, seconds: float, cost: float) -> None:
        hour = ts.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        u = self.__dict__.setdefault("_gpu_usage", {}).setdefault((hour, backend), [0.0, 0.0])
        u[0] += seconds
        u[1] += cost

    async def gpu_spend_since(self, since: datetime) -> dict[str, float]:
        out: dict[str, float] = {}
        for (hour, backend), (_, cost) in self.__dict__.get("_gpu_usage", {}).items():
            if hour >= since.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0):
                out[backend] = out.get(backend, 0.0) + cost
        return out

    async def gpu_daily(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        days: dict = {}
        for (hour, backend), (secs, cost) in self.__dict__.get("_gpu_usage", {}).items():
            if hour >= since:
                d = days.setdefault((hour.date().isoformat(), backend), [0.0, 0.0])
                d[0] += secs / 3600
                d[1] += cost
        return [{"day": k[0], "backend": k[1], "replica_hours": v[0], "cost": v[1]} for k, v in sorted(days.items())]

    async def gpu_event(self, kind: str, backend: str | None = None, actor: str | None = None, detail: dict | None = None) -> None:
        ev = self.__dict__.setdefault("_gpu_events", [])
        ev.append({"id": len(ev) + 1, "ts": datetime.now(UTC), "backend": backend, "kind": kind, "actor": actor, "detail": detail or {}})

    async def gpu_events(self, limit: int = 100, backend: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        ev = [e for e in self.__dict__.get("_gpu_events", []) if backend is None or e["backend"] == backend]
        return list(reversed(ev))[:limit]

    def _key(self, r: dict, group_by: str) -> Any:
        m = _TAG.match(group_by)
        if m:
            return (r.get("tags") or {}).get(m.group(1)) or "(untagged)"
        if group_by == "none":
            return "total"
        if group_by in ("day", "hour", "month"):
            ts: datetime = r["ts"]
            if group_by == "hour":
                return ts.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0).isoformat()
            if group_by == "day":
                return ts.date().isoformat()
            return ts.strftime("%Y-%m")
        return r.get(GROUPS[group_by])

    async def summary(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, group_by: str, user_id: str | None = None,
                      team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        validate_group(group_by)
        groups: dict[Any, dict] = defaultdict(lambda: {"requests": 0, "errors": 0, "upgraded": 0, **{f: 0 for f in SUM_FIELDS}})
        for r in self.ledger:
            if not (start <= r["ts"] < end):
                continue
            if user_id and r.get("user_id") != user_id:
                continue
            if team and r.get("team") != team:
                continue
            g = groups[self._key(r, group_by)]
            g["requests"] += 1
            g["errors"] += 1 if (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400 else 0
            g["upgraded"] += 1 if r.get("upgraded") else 0
            for f in SUM_FIELDS:
                g[f] += r.get(f) or 0
        rows = [_finish_row({"key": k, **v}) for k, v in groups.items()]
        return sorted(rows, key=lambda x: str(x["key"]))

    async def recent(self, limit: int, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        rows = [r for r in self.ledger if (not user_id or r.get("user_id") == user_id) and (not team or r.get("team") == team)]
        return [_finish_row({k: (str(v) if isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) else v) for k, v in r.items()}) for r in rows[-limit:][::-1]]

    async def needed_demand(self, model: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["served_api_cost"] for r in self.ledger if r.get("served_model") == model and not r.get("upgraded") and r["ts"] >= since)

    async def demand_by_hour(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        groups: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for r in self.ledger:
            if r["ts"] < since or r.get("upgraded") or (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400:
                continue
            hour = r["ts"].replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            k = (hour, r.get("floor"), r.get("served_model"), r.get("requested_model"))
            g = groups.setdefault(k, {"hour": hour, "floor": k[1], "served_model": k[2], "requested_model": k[3], "cost": 0.0, "tokens": 0})
            g["cost"] += r.get("served_api_cost") or 0
            g["tokens"] += sum(r.get(f) or 0 for f in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        return list(groups.values())

    async def export_rows(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, team: str | None = None):
        for r in sorted(self.ledger, key=lambda x: x["ts"]):
            if start <= r["ts"] < end and (team is None or r.get("team") == team):
                yield {k: r.get(k) for k in LEDGER_FIELDS}

    async def demand_rows(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        """Spend and tokens since ``since`` grouped by (floor, served_model, requested_model), excluding free upgrades."""
        groups: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for r in self.ledger:
            if r["ts"] < since or r.get("upgraded") or (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400:
                continue
            k = (r.get("floor"), r.get("served_model"), r.get("requested_model"))
            g = groups.setdefault(k, {"floor": k[0], "served_model": k[1], "requested_model": k[2], "cost": 0.0, "tokens": 0})
            g["cost"] += r.get("served_api_cost") or 0  # API-equivalent: stable whether or not GPUs serve it
            g["tokens"] += sum(r.get(f) or 0 for f in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        return list(groups.values())

    async def rollup(self, full: bool = False) -> int:
        return 0

    # --- config versions (the in-memory store keeps them for the life of the process)
    async def save_config(self, body: dict, author: str, comment: str | None) -> int:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("configs", [])
        vid = len(self.configs) + 1
        self.configs.append({"id": vid, "created_at": datetime.now(UTC), "author": author, "comment": comment, "body": body})
        return vid

    async def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        return (self.__dict__.get("configs") or [None])[-1]

    async def config_versions(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return [{k: v for k, v in c.items() if k != "body"} for c in reversed(self.__dict__.get("configs") or [])][:limit]

    async def get_config(self, vid: int) -> dict | None:
        return next((c for c in self.__dict__.get("configs") or [] if c["id"] == vid), None)

    async def get_setting(self, key: str):
        return self.__dict__.setdefault("settings", {}).get(key)

    async def set_setting(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("settings", {})[key] = value

    async def ensure_partitions(self) -> None:
        return None

class PostgresStore:
    kind = "postgres"

    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:
        self.dsn = dsn
        self.pool = None

    async def init(self) -> None:
        import asyncpg

        async def setup(conn):
            await conn.set_type_codec("jsonb", encoder=json.dumps, decoder=json.loads, schema="pg_catalog")

        # Reports group by day/hour/month in UTC regardless of the database server's timezone.
        # Per process. Behind many gateway processes, put PgBouncer in front so the total stays within max_connections.
        size = int(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DB_POOL_SIZE", "10"))
        self.pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(self.dsn, min_size=1, max_size=size, init=setup, server_settings={"timezone": "UTC"})

    async def close(self) -> None:
        if self.pool:
            await self.pool.close()

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("SELECT 1") == 1

    async def migrate(self) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version int PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())")
            applied = {r["version"] for r in await c.fetch("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations")}
            for version, sql in MIGRATIONS:
                if version in applied:
                    continue
                async with c.transaction():
                    await c.execute(sql)
                    await c.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ($1)", version)
        await self.ensure_partitions()

    async def ensure_partitions(self, months_ahead: int = 2) -> None:
        start = month_start()
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            for i in range(months_ahead + 1):
                lo = (start + timedelta(days=32 * i)).replace(day=1)
                hi = (lo + timedelta(days=32)).replace(day=1)
                name = f"requests_{lo:%Y_%m}"
                exists = await c.fetchval("SELECT to_regclass($1)", name)
                if exists:
                    continue
                # Rows that landed in the default partition for this range must move first.
                async with c.transaction():
                    await c.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {name} (LIKE requests INCLUDING DEFAULTS)")
                    await c.execute(
                        f"WITH moved AS (DELETE FROM requests_default WHERE ts >= $1 AND ts < $2 RETURNING *) "
                        f"INSERT INTO {name} SELECT * FROM moved", lo, hi)
                    await c.execute(f"ALTER TABLE requests ATTACH PARTITION {name} FOR VALUES FROM ('{lo.isoformat()}') TO ('{hi.isoformat()}')")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- users & keys

    async def upsert_user(self, user_id, team, role, email=None, display_name=None, source: str = "idp") -> None:
        """source="idp": a login refreshes team/role unless an admin pinned them; "ensure": only create if missing."""
        refresh = "team=EXCLUDED.team, role=EXCLUDED.role," if source == "idp" else ""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                """INSERT INTO users (id, team, role, email, display_name) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5)
                   ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
                   team=CASE WHEN users.managed='idp' AND $6 THEN EXCLUDED.team ELSE users.team END,
                   role=CASE WHEN users.managed='idp' AND $6 THEN EXCLUDED.role ELSE users.role END,
                   email=coalesce(EXCLUDED.email, users.email), display_name=coalesce(EXCLUDED.display_name, users.display_name),
                   updated_at=now()""",
                user_id, team, role, email, display_name, bool(refresh))

    async def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=$1", user_id)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def update_user(self, user_id, team=None, role=None, disabled=None, managed=None) -> dict | None:
        sets, args = [], [user_id]
        if team is not None:
            args.append(team)
            sets.append(f"team=${len(args)}")
        if role is not None:
            args.append(role)
            sets.append(f"role=${len(args)}")
        if (team is not None or role is not None) and managed is None:
            sets.append("managed='local'")  # an admin's edit sticks across IdP logins, unless told to follow the IdP
        if managed is not None:
            args.append(managed)
            sets.append(f"managed=${len(args)}")
        if disabled is not None:
            sets.append("disabled_at=now()" if disabled else "disabled_at=NULL")
        if not sets:
            return await self.get_user(user_id)
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow(f"UPDATE users SET {', '.join(sets)}, updated_at=now() WHERE id=$1 RETURNING *", *args)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def find_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM users WHERE lower(email)=lower($1) LIMIT 1", email)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def scim_groups(self) -> list[dict]:

                   ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET display_name=EXCLUDED.display_name, external_id=EXCLUDED.external_id,
                   members=EXCLUDED.members, updated_at=now()""",

    async def delete_scim_group(self, gid: str) -> bool:

    async def list_users(self, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT u.*, count(k.id) FILTER (WHERE k.revoked_at IS NULL) AS active_keys, max(k.last_used_at) AS last_seen
                 FROM users u LEFT JOIN api_keys k ON k.user_id = u.id""" + (" WHERE u.team = $1" if team else "") + """
                 GROUP BY u.id ORDER BY u.id"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *([team] if team else []))
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def create_key(self, user_id, team, role, name=None, tags=None, expires_at=None) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key_id, secret = new_api_key()
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO api_keys (id, key_hash, user_id, team, role, name, tags, expires_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8)",
                key_id, hash_key(secret), user_id, team, role, name, tags or {}, expires_at)
        return key_id, secret

    async def find_key(self, key_hash: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM api_keys WHERE key_hash=$1", key_hash)
            if row:
                await c.execute("UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND (last_used_at IS NULL OR last_used_at < now() - interval '5 minutes')", row["id"])
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def list_keys(self, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        where, args = [], []
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        sql = ("SELECT id, user_id, team, role, name, tags, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, last_used_at FROM api_keys "
               + ("WHERE " + " AND ".join(where) if where else "") + " ORDER BY created_at")
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def get_key(self, key_id: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT id, user_id, team, role, name, tags, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at FROM api_keys WHERE id=$1", key_id)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def revoke_key(self, key_id: str) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            res = await c.execute("UPDATE api_keys SET revoked_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND revoked_at IS NULL", key_id)
        return res.endswith("1")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- ledger

    async def record(self, row: dict) -> None:
        cols = ", ".join(LEDGER_FIELDS)
        params = ", ".join(f"${i + 1}" for i in range(len(LEDGER_FIELDS)))
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = complete_row(row)
            await c.execute(f"INSERT INTO requests ({cols}) VALUES ({params})", *[row[f] for f in LEDGER_FIELDS])

    async def spend_since(self, field: str, value: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        if field not in ("user_id", "team"):
            raise ValueError(field)
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval(f"SELECT coalesce(sum(actual_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE {field}=$1 AND ts >= $2", value, since))

    async def spend_all_since(self, since: datetime) -> float:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval("SELECT coalesce(sum(actual_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1", since))

    async def add_gpu_usage(self, backend: str, ts: datetime, seconds: float, cost: float) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO gpu_usage (hour, backend, replica_seconds, cost) VALUES (date_trunc('hour', $1::timestamptz), $2, $3, $4) "
                "ON CONFLICT (hour, backend) DO UPDATE SET replica_seconds = gpu_usage.replica_seconds + EXCLUDED.replica_seconds, "
                "cost = gpu_usage.cost + EXCLUDED.cost", ts, backend, seconds, cost)

    async def gpu_spend_since(self, since: datetime) -> dict[str, float]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT backend, sum(cost) AS cost FROM gpu_usage WHERE hour >= date_trunc('hour', $1::timestamptz) GROUP BY backend", since)
        return {r["backend"]: float(r["cost"]) for r in rows}

    async def gpu_daily(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT date_trunc('day', hour)::date AS day, backend, sum(replica_seconds)/3600 AS replica_hours, sum(cost) AS cost "
                                 "FROM gpu_usage WHERE hour >= $1 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2", since)
        return [{"day": r["day"].isoformat(), "backend": r["backend"], "replica_hours": float(r["replica_hours"]), "cost": float(r["cost"])} for r in rows]

    async def gpu_event(self, kind: str, backend: str | None = None, actor: str | None = None, detail: dict | None = None) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("INSERT INTO gpu_events (kind, backend, actor, detail) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)", kind, backend, actor, detail or {})

    async def gpu_events(self, limit: int = 100, backend: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT * FROM gpu_events WHERE ($2::text IS NULL OR backend = $2) ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT $1", limit, backend)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def summary(self, start, end, group_by, user_id=None, team=None) -> list[dict]:
        validate_group(group_by)
        tag = _TAG.match(group_by)
        use_rollup = not tag and (end - start) > timedelta(days=7)
        table, ts_col = ("usage_hourly", "hour") if use_rollup else ("requests", "ts")
        if tag:
            key_expr = f"coalesce(tags->>'{tag.group(1)}', '(untagged)')"
        elif group_by == "none":
            key_expr = "'total'"
        elif group_by in ("day", "hour", "month"):
            key_expr = f"date_trunc('{group_by}', {ts_col})"
        else:
            key_expr = GROUPS[group_by]
        if use_rollup:
            counts = "coalesce(sum(requests),0) AS requests, coalesce(sum(errors),0) AS errors, coalesce(sum(upgraded),0) AS upgraded"
        else:
            counts = "count(*) AS requests, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 400) AS errors, count(*) FILTER (WHERE upgraded) AS upgraded"
        where = [f"{ts_col} >= $1", f"{ts_col} < $2"]
        args: list[Any] = [start, end]
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        sql = f"SELECT {key_expr} AS key, {counts}, {_SUMS_SQL} FROM {table} WHERE {' AND '.join(where)} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1"
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [_finish_row({k: (float(v) if k in SUM_FIELDS else v) for k, v in dict(r).items()}) for r in rows]

    async def recent(self, limit: int, user_id=None, team=None) -> list[dict]:
        where, args = [], []
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        args.append(limit)
        sql = f"SELECT * FROM requests {'WHERE ' + ' AND '.join(where) if where else ''} ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ${len(args)}"
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [_finish_row({k: (str(v) if isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) else v) for k, v in dict(r).items()}) for r in rows]

    async def demand_rows(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT floor, served_model, requested_model, coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) AS cost,
                        coalesce(sum(input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens + output_tokens),0) AS tokens
                 FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND coalesce(status,0) < 400
                 GROUP BY 1,2,3"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, since)
        return [{**dict(r), "cost": float(r["cost"]), "tokens": int(r["tokens"])} for r in rows]

    async def demand_by_hour(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hour, floor, served_model, requested_model,
                        coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) AS cost,
                        coalesce(sum(input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens + output_tokens),0) AS tokens
                 FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND coalesce(status,0) < 400
                 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, since)
        return [{**dict(r), "cost": float(r["cost"]), "tokens": int(r["tokens"])} for r in rows]

    async def export_rows(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, team: str | None = None):
        """Stream ledger rows with a server-side cursor (constant memory for big ranges)."""
        cols = ", ".join(LEDGER_FIELDS)
        sql = f"SELECT {cols} FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND ts < $2" + (" AND team = $3" if team else "") + " ORDER BY ts"
        args = [start, end] + ([team] if team else [])
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            async with c.transaction():
                async for r in c.cursor(sql, *args, prefetch=2000):
                    yield dict(r)

    async def needed_demand(self, model: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval(
                "SELECT coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE served_model=$1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND ts >= $2",
                model, since))

    # --- config versions
    async def save_config(self, body: dict, author: str, comment: str | None) -> int:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("INSERT INTO config_versions (author, comment, body) VALUES ($1,$2,$3) RETURNING id",
                                    author, comment, body)

    async def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM config_versions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1")
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def config_versions(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT id, created_at, author, comment FROM config_versions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT $1", limit)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def get_config(self, vid: int) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM config_versions WHERE id=$1", vid)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def get_setting(self, key: str):
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key=$1", key)

    async def set_setting(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES ($1,$2) ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value=EXCLUDED.value, updated_at=now()",
                            key, value)

    async def rollup(self, full: bool = False) -> int:
        """Recompute hourly rollups from the raw ledger.

        Normally the last 3 hours (late rows land within that window). With ``full``,
        or when the rollup table is empty, everything is recomputed.
        """
        sums = ", ".join(f"coalesce(sum({f}),0)" for f in SUM_FIELDS)
        cols = ", ".join(SUM_FIELDS)
        updates = ", ".join(f"{f}=EXCLUDED.{f}" for f in ["requests", "errors", "upgraded", *SUM_FIELDS])
        sql = f"""
            INSERT INTO usage_hourly (hour, user_id, team, served_model, backend, requests, errors, upgraded, {cols})
            SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts), coalesce(user_id,''), coalesce(team,''), coalesce(served_model,''), coalesce(backend,''),
                   count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 400), count(*) FILTER (WHERE upgraded), {sums}
            FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1
            GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
            ON CONFLICT (hour, user_id, team, served_model, backend) DO UPDATE SET {updates}"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            if full or not await c.fetchval("SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM usage_hourly)"):
                since = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
            else:
                since = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=3)).replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            res = await c.execute(sql, since)
        return int(res.split()[-1]) if res else 0


def make_store(database_url: str | None):
    return PostgresStore(database_url) if database_url else MemoryStore()

# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports. Unknown, revoked, or expired keys get a 401. | Client | Auth | |---|---| | People with harnesses | `meritorder login` → virtual key (above) | | Services / apps | An Entra token directly as the bearer token, or a key from `meritorder keys create` | | Local dev / quickstart | `MERITORDER_DEV_KEY` (static admin key from the environment) | | Google (later) | Another OIDC issuer: same code path | Entra login switches on when `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` are set; map Entra group IDs to teams and roles in `auth.oidc` in the config. SCIM (later) revokes keys when people leave. ## People and teams | What | Where it's managed | |---|---| | Who exists, and their group membership | Your identity provider (Entra). People are created in Merit Order the first time they sign in with `meritorder login` (or when an admin issues them a key). | | Teams, with budgets, limits, and model policy | Merit Order: Config → Teams. An IdP has no notion of "$5,000 a month, these models only". | | Which team and role someone gets | Entra groups mapped to teams and roles in Config → Access, re-read at each sign-in. | | Exceptions | The People page: an admin can move someone, change their role (that pins it, so later sign-ins don't override it), let Entra decide again, or disable them. | The user record, not the key, decides a person's team and role. Moving or disabling someone takes effect within a minute on every gateway, including keys they already have. For the same reason, a team lead can issue keys only for themselves, for new people, or for people on their own team with the user role; keys for anyone else (another team, a lead, an admin) need an admin. | Role | Sees | Can change | |---|---|---| | user | Their own usage | Their own keys | | team lead | Their team: reports, requests, ledger export | Keys for their team's users | | finance | Every team, aggregated (no per-request rows or exports) | Nothing | | admin | Everything | Everything | **SCIM provisioning** (`/scim/v2`, enabled by `MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN`): Entra pushes people and group changes as they happen. Group membership recomputes team and role with the same mappings as sign-in, and anyone deactivated or removed in Entra is disabled immediately (spend history is kept). Setup: Entra → Enterprise applications → your app → Provisioning → Automatic; Tenant URL `https:///scim/v2`, Secret token = `MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN`. ## Budgets ```mermaid flowchart TD ORG["Org budget
$/month"] --> T1["Team: platform
$/month"] ORG --> T2["Team: data-science
$/month"] T1 --> U1["User budget"] T1 --> U2["User budget"] T2 --> U3["User budget"] U1 --> K1["Key"] U1 --> K2["Key"] ``` - A request must fit **every** level above it: organization, team, and person. - **Each person can have their own monthly limit.** Without one, the team's per-person default (`user_budget_usd_month`) applies. A person's own limit replaces that default, higher or lower; the team and organization budgets still apply on top. `$0` stops their requests. Set it in either place below; the People page wins when both are set, and changes apply within a minute on every gateway, keys already issued included: - The console's **People** page (admins), or `PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id}` with `{"budget_usd_month": 250}`. Send `null` to clear it and go back to the default. - `budget_usd_month` on a static key in the config file, for people who use one. - A person's limit counts everything they spent this month, on whichever team they were on. - Spend is checked before a request is sent and counted when it finishes (Redis counters seeded from the Postgres ledger, which stays the source of truth). - Alerts go out at 80% and 100%; at 100% requests are refused with a 429 that says which budget was reached. - Policy lives alongside budgets: allowed models, allowed providers, data residency (e.g. "DeepSeek weights only self-hosted or on Bedrock, never the vendor API"). ## Limits that stop runaway spend | Setting (per team) | What it does | |---|---| | `budget_usd_month`, `user_budget_usd_month` | Monthly caps for the team, and the default for each person on it; requests are refused at 100% (alerts at 80%). A person's own limit replaces the per-person default ([Budgets](#budgets)) | | `max_session_usd` | Stops one session (typically an agent stuck in a loop) once it has spent this much | | `rate_limits: {user_rpm, user_tpm, team_rpm, team_tpm}` | Requests and prompt tokens per minute; 429 with `Retry-After` | ## Organization-wide safeguards Hard limits for everyone, set under `safeguards:` or on the console's **Controls** page (which shows each one next to this month's spend and the pace it's on, and saves changes as a new config version). The shipped config reads them from the environment, so each install sets its own in `.env` without editing the file: `MERITORDER_ORG_BUDGET_USD`, `MERITORDER_GPU_BUDGET_USD`, `MERITORDER_MAX_GPU_USD_PER_HOUR`, `MERITORDER_MAX_GPU_REPLICAS`, and `MERITORDER_MAX_REQUEST_USD` (25 if unset). A blank or unset variable means no limit. These are the fastest stop there is: they act on the gateway's own ledger, request by request. Cloud budgets (AWS Budgets, Azure Cost Management) see spend hours later, and on their own only send email, so treat them as a backstop for anything that doesn't go through the gateway. | Setting | What it does | |---|---| | `org_budget_usd_month` | All spend in the ledger. At 100% every request is refused until the month ends or it's raised | | `gpu_budget_usd_month` | GPU time (replicas × hourly price). At 100% running GPUs drain and none start, pins included | | `max_gpu_usd_per_hour` | Burn-rate cap for the whole GPU fleet; deployments whose demand best covers their cost get capacity first | | `max_gpu_replicas` | Replica cap across all deployments | | `max_request_usd` | Worst case per request (context × input price + `max_tokens` × output price). Cheaper candidates are used instead; if none fit, the request is refused with what it would have cost | | `alert_at` | Fractions of the org and GPU budgets that send alerts (default 80% and 100%) | GPUs can also be stopped, pinned, or stopped all at once from the console; see [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md#controls-and-safeguards). ## What gets charged | Backend | Charged to the user's budget | |---|---| | API | Provider cost of the cached, uncached, and output tokens at catalog prices. OpenRouter picks among providers whose prices differ, so for OpenRouter the ledger records what it billed (`usage.cost`; with your own provider key, its fee plus the provider's charge). Set `billed_cost: reported` or `catalog` on a backend to choose | | Self-hosted | Chargeback: GPU-hour cost (SkyPilot's catalog price for the running replicas, else `gpu_cost_per_hour`) split by tokens served, so it's fair, not $0 | | Server-side tools | Anthropic web search at $10 per 1,000 searches (`price.web_search_per_1k`), on top of tokens. Web fetch adds only tokens; code-execution container time isn't modeled | Some `anthropic-beta` features change pricing (for example 1M-token context) in ways the cost model doesn't track. To keep them off, list the betas a backend may forward: `anthropic_betas: [...]` (prefix match; unset forwards everything the client sends). Budgets use chargeback; the router uses marginal cost. They answer different questions. ## The savings ledger One row per request, written async: | Field | Example | |---|---| | user, team, session | | | model requested / floor / served | `auto` / `coding:3` / `qwen3-coder-480b` | | backend | `self/qwen3-coder/replica-2` | | tokens: uncached in / cached in / out | 2,100 / 118,000 / 640 | | **actual marginal cost** | $0.0004 | | **chargeback cost** | $0.0090 | | **counterfactual cost** (floor model on API, no proxy caching) | $0.3700 | | upgraded for free? | yes | This is the dashboard that sells the project: *"$X spent, $Y avoided, Z% of requests upgraded at no cost."* How savings are calculated and reported is in [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md).

from meritorder.app import build_gateway

from meritorder.cache_shaping import shape_openai

from meritorder.store import MemoryStore

def test_claude_on_openrouter_gets_the_automatic_caching_marker():
    body = {"model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}
    assert shape_openai(body, OR, "sid") is True and body["cache_control"] == {"type": "ephemeral"}
    hour = {"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5", "messages": []}
    assert shape_openai(hour, OR.model_copy(update={"cache_ttl_seconds": 3600}), "sid") is True
    assert hour["cache_control"] == {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}

    for backend, model in ((OR, "moonshotai/kimi-k3.1"), (OR.model_copy(update={"base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1"}), "anthropic/x")):

    own = {"model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": [

def gateway(monkeypatch, upstream: Upstream):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MO_TEST_OR", "key-or")
    raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
    raw["backends"] = {"or": {"kind": "api", "format": "openai", "base_url": "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
                              "auth": {"type": "api_key", "value_env": "MO_TEST_OR"}}}
    raw["models"] = {"c": {"quality": {"coding": 4, "general": 4}, "routes": [
        {"backend": "or", "model": "anthropic/claude-x", "price": {"input": 1, "output": 5, "cache_read": 0.1, "cache_write": 1.25}}]}}
    raw["baseline_model"] = "c"
    gw = build_gateway(build_config(raw, quiet=True), store=MemoryStore(), state=MemoryState())
    gw.backends["or"].client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(upstream))

async def test_anthropic_client_on_openrouter_claude_is_cached_and_credited(monkeypatch):

# 05 — GPU autoscaling Only open-weight models (Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Llama, …) can be self-hosted. Every self-hostable model should also have **at least one API route serving the same weights** (OpenRouter, the vendor, Bedrock, …). APIs are the floor; GPUs are an optimization. The console warns about models without one before anyone stops their GPUs. The full decision logic, with every rule and default, is in [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md#when-gpus-start-scale-and-stop). ## Lifecycle of a self-hosted model ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> APIOnly APIOnly --> Provisioning: demand pays for a replica for 10 min,
or pinned by an admin Provisioning --> Warm: replicas answer /v1/models Provisioning --> APIOnly: failed / timed out (30 min cooldown),
or stopped Warm --> Warm: add or remove replicas Warm --> Draining: below break-even 10 min (and warm 30 min),
or stopped with drain Warm --> APIOnly: stopped now Warm --> Provisioning: lost readiness (e.g. spot preemption) Draining --> Warm: demand returns (unless stopped) Draining --> APIOnly: after 15 min, GPUs released note right of APIOnly All traffic on API routes. Controller watches demand. end note note right of Provisioning 10–20+ min for big MoE models. Traffic stays on API meanwhile. end note note right of Draining No new sessions. Warm sessions finish there. end note ``` ## Controller loop (every 60 s) ```mermaid flowchart TD L["Read the ledger
last 1 h and last 15 min"] --> A["Addressable demand for this model:
traffic whose quality floor it meets,
valued at API prices, free upgrades excluded"] A --> R["Desired replicas =
enough for throughput,
but each must pay for itself"] R --> CT["Admin controls and safeguards
stop all · stop · pin · GPU budget · fleet caps"] CT --> SM{"State machine
api_only · provisioning · warm · draining"} SM -- "up / scale / down" --> P["Provisioner
SkyPilot (sky serve) or static"] SM --> PUB["Publish state, endpoint,
vLLM utilization → Redis"] PUB --> GW["Gateways pick it up
within 5 s"] ``` A self-hosted model therefore needs a quality score: one the live quality source doesn't cover counts no `auto` demand (only requests that name it) until it gets a `quality_override`. Why *addressable* demand: if the controller only counted traffic already sent to a model, a model that isn't running would never look worth starting, because `auto` routes its traffic elsewhere. So it counts what you currently pay for all traffic this model *could* serve (its quality meets the request's floor), at API-equivalent prices. That value doesn't drop when the GPUs start serving, so the controller doesn't flap. ## The break-even test ``` demand_per_hour = addressable API-equivalent spend per hour (max of the 1 h and 4 × 15 min windows) throughput = addressable tokens per second (same windows) by_load = ceil(throughput / (capacity_tokens_per_second × target_utilization)) affordable = floor(demand_per_hour / (replica_price × (1 + margin))) replica_price = cheapest SkyPilot catalog offer in the allowed clouds/regions, else gpu_cost_per_hour desired_replicas = clamp(min(by_load ≥ 1, affordable), min_replicas, max_replicas) ``` Defaults, per deployment under `serve:`: `margin` 0.2 (demand must pay 1.2 × the replica price), `target_utilization` 0.7, `scale_up_after_minutes` 10, `hold_minutes` 30, `drain_minutes` 15, `provision_timeout_minutes` 45. State machine (`src/meritorder/gpu.py`, pure and unit-tested): | From | To | When | |---|---|---| | api_only | provisioning | `desired ≥ 1` continuously for `scale_up_after_minutes` (or `min_replicas > 0`) | | provisioning | warm | replicas answer `/v1/models` | | provisioning | api_only | failed or `provision_timeout_minutes` passed; 30-minute cooldown | | warm | warm | replica count follows `desired` | | warm | draining | `desired = 0` for `scale_up_after_minutes`, and warm for at least `hold_minutes` | | warm | provisioning | replicas stop answering (e.g. spot preemption); traffic goes to APIs until they're back | | draining | warm | demand returns | | draining | api_only | after `drain_minutes`; GPUs released | | any | api_only / draining | an admin stops it, Stop all GPUs, or the GPU budget runs out (see [Controls](#controls-and-safeguards)) | | api_only | provisioning | an admin pins replicas: at once, skipping the wait and any cooldown | Key details: - **Free upgrades don't count.** Traffic running above its floor because a GPU had headroom is excluded, so idle capacity can't keep itself alive by attracting traffic. - **Measured capacity, not benchmarks.** `capacity_tokens_per_second` should be what one replica sustains at your latency target on real agent traffic (prefill-heavy). - **Hysteresis everywhere.** Margins, minimum hold time, and the scale-up delay stop flapping. A 20-minute cold start is expensive to waste. - **Spot where it's safe.** SkyServe handles spot preemption; overflow to the API covers the gap. ## Will a GPU ever pay? (Models → GPU break-even) Before configuring a deployment, the console's **GPU break-even** tab (Models page; also `GET /v1/reports/gpu/breakeven`, team leads and up) shows how much traffic one replica needs to pay for itself by the rule above, next to your traffic: - **By quality level.** A replica takes traffic that `auto` would otherwise send to the cheapest API model good enough for its level, so that model's price is the one to beat. For each level: that model and its price, the tokens per minute (and about how many requests an hour) one replica needs, your average and busiest hour at that level, and which open-weight models qualify. A level where no open model qualifies can't use a GPU, whatever the numbers. - **By open-weight model.** What the traffic it could serve actually cost per million tokens over the window (the controller's own measure), its own API price, what it needs, and a verdict: pays now, pays from a given traffic, or never. - **Never** means one replica can't get there at any traffic: at full load (its target utilization) the GPU costs more per token than the API, so more replicas wouldn't help either. Cheaper GPUs, more tokens per second, or harder (pricier) work changes that, and the assumptions on the tab are there to try it. Prices are blended for the traffic's mix of input, cached input, cache writes and output (a level or model with at least 20 requests uses its own, otherwise everyone's; with no traffic, an assumed agent-like mix). Free tiers don't count as the price to beat: they're rate-limited and can't take sustained traffic. A model with its own deployment uses that deployment's price (SkyPilot's catalog price when the controller has one) and capacity; the others use the tab's assumptions (default: $16 an hour and 4,000 tokens a second, at 70%). ## Configuring a self-hosted model ```yaml backends: gpu-qwen-coder: kind: self_hosted format: openai gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0 # one replica (here 4× H100) capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000 serve: provisioner: skypilot # or `static` for a server you already run model: qwen3-coder-next # its hf_id is what vLLM serves accelerators: "H100:4" use_spot: true clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda] image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144" max_replicas: 4 ``` The model also needs a route to the deployment with a `price:` at the API-equivalent rate: `auto` skips unpriced routes, and the router scales that price down while the GPUs have room ([Overflow](#overflow)). Keep the API route for the same weights next to it: ```yaml models: qwen3-coder-next: hf_id: Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next routes: - {backend: gpu-qwen-coder, model: Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next, price: {input: 0.12, output: 0.80, cache_read: 0.07}} - {backend: openrouter, model: qwen/qwen3-coder-next} ``` The SkyPilot provisioner writes a SkyServe service (vLLM with `--enable-prefix-caching` and `--scheduling-policy priority`, fixed replica count, readiness probe on `/v1/models`) and drives `sky serve up / update / down`. It needs the `sky` CLI and cloud credentials (`sky check`). Set `HF_TOKEN` for gated models. ## Controls and safeguards The console's **GPUs** page shows, for every deployment: where each replica runs (cloud, region, zone, instance, spot or on-demand, from SkyPilot), how long it has been up, its burn rate, what this run and this month have cost, what demand would pay for it at API prices, and why the controller is doing what it's doing. An activity log records every state change, scale, and admin action with who did it. Admins can override the controller: | Control | Effect | |---|---| | **Stop** (drain first) | No new sessions; warm ones finish for up to `drain_minutes`, then the replicas go down. Skips the usual hold time | | **Stop now** | Replicas go down at once; their sessions continue on APIs (caches rebuild there) | | **Pin N replicas** | Runs N (up to `max_replicas`) regardless of demand, skipping the scale-up wait and any failure cooldown | | **Back to automatic** | Demand decides again | | **Stop all GPUs** | Every deployment stops and none start until someone resumes the fleet | Stops and pins can expire after a set number of hours and can carry a reason, which the activity log and the alert show. Gateways stop routing to a stopped deployment within seconds, before the controller acts; the controller wakes up as soon as a control changes. For a static server, Merit Order can only stop sending it traffic. Organization safeguards apply on top, to pins as well ([06](06-auth-and-spend.md#organization-wide-safeguards)): a monthly GPU budget, a fleet burn-rate cap, and a replica cap. ### What GPUs cost Prices come from **SkyPilot's catalog**, the same list prices its optimizer uses to pick a cloud: - **Before launching**, the break-even test uses the cheapest catalog offer for the deployment's accelerators within its allowed clouds and regions (spot or on-demand, per `use_spot`). - **While running**, each replica is priced for its actual cloud, region, instance type, and spot/on-demand, so a replica that lands in a pricier region costs what it really costs. - `gpu_cost_per_hour` is only a fallback, used for static servers (your own hardware) and when SkyPilot isn't installed where the controller runs. Cost is accrued every cycle from the moment provisioning starts until the replicas are down, and stored per hour (`gpu_usage`). Self-hosted tokens are charged back at the same live price. These are **list prices**, not your bill: they don't include negotiated discounts, reservations, or credits, and they leave out disks, egress, and the SkyServe controller VM. Spot prices in the catalog are refreshed periodically, not live. Reconciling against the cloud bill is on the roadmap. SkyPilot runs in its own Python environment (the `-gpu` image, built with `--build-arg SKYPILOT=`), so its dependencies never mix with the gateway's. Merit Order calls it through the `sky` CLI and, for prices, SkyPilot's Python (`MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON`, found from the `sky` command when unset). If the controller stops running while GPUs are up, the console flags it: nothing would scale them down. If a stop fails at the cloud, the deployment stays marked as running and the controller keeps retrying, so a GPU that may still be billing is never shown as off. ## Overflow ```mermaid flowchart LR REQ["New session for qwen3-coder"] --> H{"Self-hosted pool
has headroom?"} H -- "yes" --> SELF["Self-hosted deployment
(SkyServe picks the replica)"] H -- "no" --> API{"Another route?
e.g. Bedrock / Together"} API -- "yes" --> SPILL["Same model via API"] API -- "no" --> Q["Waits in vLLM's queue,
up to max_waiting per replica;
then 503"] SPILL -.-> SIG["Controller sees the demand:
adds replicas"] ``` Up to 60% load (`routing.shadow_knee`), a self-hosted token is priced at 2% of its route's price (`routing.shadow_floor`). Above that the shadow price rises toward the full price, so new sessions drift to APIs before the GPU is full. At 100%, nothing new goes there while any other route can take it; sessions already there move too. A saturated GPU that's a model's only route still takes requests, which wait in vLLM, until `max_waiting` (default 32) per replica are waiting. Set `max_concurrency` so gateways see saturation within seconds instead of at the controller's next sample. Details: [When a GPU is full](10-how-it-decides.md#when-a-gpu-is-full). ## Inside the GPU pool - **Continuous batching** is the engine's job (vLLM / SGLang). The gateway sends concurrently and never serializes requests per replica. - **Replica choice** is SkyServe's: its load balancer picks the replica for each request. Sending a session back to the replica that holds its KV cache is not built yet. - **Priority scheduling**: free-upgrade requests go to vLLM with `priority: 10` (lower runs first), so traffic at its own floor goes ahead of them. - **Engine knobs** go in `vllm_args` (e.g. `--max-num-seqs`, `--max-num-batched-tokens`, chunked prefill, speculative decoding). Prefix caching and priority scheduling are always on.

"""Who gets paged."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime

from .overrides import Override, on_call
from .rotation import Rotation


def escalation(rotation: Rotation, overrides: list[Override], ts: datetime) -> list[str]:
    """Who to page at ts, in order: whoever is on call (overrides included), then the backup.

    The backup is the member who has the next shift in the rotation; overrides don't change who that is. When the backup
    would be the person already paged first (a one-person rotation, or the next member covering this shift), the list
    has just one name.
    """
    primary = on_call(rotation, overrides, ts)
    backup = rotation.next_member(rotation.scheduled(ts))
    return [primary] if backup == primary else [primary, backup]
