# 09 — Decisions

What we decided, why, and what would make us revisit it. Newest decisions go at the bottom.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Python for the core | Accepted |
| 2 | Our own backend adapters; no LiteLLM dependency | Accepted |
| 3 | No Envoy | Accepted |
| 4 | Docker Compose and Kubernetes both supported | Accepted |
| 5 | The harness owns the conversation; no content stored | Accepted |
| 6 | Route by marginal cost, including cache rebuild cost | Accepted |
| 7 | SkyPilot for GPUs, provisioning as a plugin | Accepted |
| 8 | Generic OIDC, Entra first | Accepted |
| 9 | Postgres and Redis are the only state | Accepted |
| 10 | Continuous batching only; async batch APIs out of scope | Accepted |
| 11 | AGPL-3.0-only license | Accepted |
| 12 | Reporting UI in React/TypeScript | Accepted |
| 13 | Opt-in response cache may store responses | Accepted |
| 14 | Open-weight catalog with prices from OpenRouter | Accepted |
| 15 | GPU scaling on addressable demand at API prices | Accepted |
| 16 | Deterministic, rule-based compression first | Accepted |
| 17 | Configuration versions in Postgres, YAML as the starting point | Accepted |
| 18 | Control panel in Mantine, monitoring first | Accepted |
| 19 | The IdP owns identity; Merit Order owns teams; user records decide team and role | Accepted |
| 20 | Quality scores are measured with graded tasks, not a judge model | Accepted |
| 21 | Every cost is visible next to the switch that controls it | Accepted |
| 22 | GPU prices come from SkyPilot's catalog; SkyPilot runs in its own environment | Accepted |
| 23 | A named model is never silently swapped; substitution is opt-in and never to a weaker model | Accepted |
| 24 | Refusals are retried on another model only for `auto` | Accepted |
| 25 | Every process follows the stored configuration | Accepted |
| 26 | No request queue in the gateway; a full GPU queues only as a last resort | Accepted |
| 27 | Prices are live, never typed in | Accepted |

**Still open:** reconciling computed costs with provider and cloud bills; Kubernetes-native GPU
provisioning (llm-d / KServe); a learned router; model-based compression; Parquet export;
provider batch APIs (decision 10).

## 1. Python for the core

**Why:** The team prefers it, the ML and inference ecosystem (SkyPilot, vLLM, classifiers,
compression) is Python, and gateway overhead is a few milliseconds against model latency measured
in seconds. We scale by running more gateway copies.

**Revisit if:** a real deployment hits gateway CPU limits that more replicas can't fix.

## 2. Our own backend adapters; no LiteLLM dependency

**Why:**
- LiteLLM converts everything to the OpenAI format internally. That's lossy for `cache_control`,
  thinking signatures, and other provider fields, and prompt caching is our biggest savings lever.
- It has had supply-chain incidents, a large dependency tree, and SSO in a commercially licensed
  directory.
- The rest of what it offers (keys, budgets, spend tracking, routing, UI) we'd replace anyway,
  because our ledger, router, and reporting work differently.
- Almost every backend speaks the Anthropic or OpenAI format, so pass-through plus one pair of
  translators covers them in a few thousand lines we fully control.

**What we still take:** LiteLLM's MIT-licensed price list, fetched as data by the worker (never
imported as code) for direct provider APIs (see #27), and its code as a reference for provider quirks. Anyone needing a niche provider can run LiteLLM themselves
as an OpenAI-compatible backend.

**Revisit if:** keeping our adapters current with provider API changes becomes a significant
ongoing burden.

## 3. No Envoy

**Why:** Envoy AI Gateway is strong as a proxy layer, but all of our product logic (routing,
shaping, sessions, budgets, ledger) would still be Python, called by Envoy over gRPC on every
request. That adds a second system to operate and debug, assumes Kubernetes, narrows the
contributor pool, and solves a performance problem we don't have. Merit Order runs behind whatever
load balancer or ingress an organization already uses.

**Revisit if:** large deployments ask for it. The routing and shaping code could be packaged as an
Envoy external-processing service without being rewritten. Separately, an optional plugin could use
Kubernetes inference-routing tools (llm-d) inside a customer's own GPU cluster.

## 4. Docker Compose and Kubernetes both supported

**Why:** Compose gives the clone-and-run experience an open-source project needs; Kubernetes is
what enterprises at our target spend run in production. Same images, no Kubernetes-specific code in
the app. Details in [07 — Deployment](07-deployment.md).

## 5. The harness owns the conversation; no content stored

**Why:** Harnesses already resend history and compact it. Storing conversations would make the
proxy a retention, eDiscovery, and breach liability. The gateway stores routing metadata (hashes,
timestamps, backends) only. Compression stays cache-safe through a content-hash map, not stored
conversations.

**Revisit if:** we add the OpenAI Responses API's stored mode, which would be opt-in with explicit
retention.

## 6. Route by marginal cost, including cache rebuild cost

**Why:** A running GPU's spare capacity is already paid for, so it's nearly free, even for a better
model than the task needs. Moving a session re-pays for its whole context, so the router counts that
before moving. Details in [03 — Routing](03-routing.md).

## 7. SkyPilot for GPUs, provisioning as a plugin

**Why:** SkyPilot handles multi-cloud GPUs, spot instances, and replica scaling (SkyServe), and can
target Kubernetes clusters. Our controller decides *whether* to run a model; SkyPilot handles *how*.
A Kubernetes-native option (llm-d or KServe) can be another plugin later.

## 8. Generic OIDC, Entra first

**Why:** Entra is the first customer need; Google and others are configuration on the same code
path. Harnesses get short-lived virtual keys via a device-code login.

## 9. Postgres and Redis are the only state

**Why:** Both are available as managed services everywhere and are easy to run in Compose.
ClickHouse may become an optional reporting backend for very large deployments.

## 10. Continuous batching only; async batch APIs out of scope

**Why:** The product is for day-to-day interactive use. vLLM/SGLang batch concurrent requests on
their own. Provider batch APIs (about 50% off for work that can wait hours) may come later.

## 11. AGPL-3.0-only license

**Why:** Changes that others are offered over a network come back to the project.

## 12. Reporting UI in React/TypeScript

**Why:** Interactive filters and charts are much easier to build well, and the UI only talks to the
reports API, so it stays replaceable. The rest of the project remains Python.

**Alternative considered:** server-rendered pages with htmx (all-Python, clunkier interactivity).

## 13. Opt-in response cache may store responses

**Why:** Exact-match caching saves real money for chatbots, RAG, and evals. It can't work without
keeping the response, so it's the one exception to decision 5: off by default, enabled per team or
per request, scoped to a team or user, and expired by TTL (Redis).

## 14. Open-weight catalog with prices from OpenRouter

**Why:** There are dozens of useful open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, MiMo,
Mistral, Gemma, Nemotron, Muse, gpt-oss) and their prices change often. `config/models-open.yaml`
lists them with their Hugging Face IDs (needed for self-hosting); the worker keeps
their prices, context windows and output limits current from OpenRouter's public catalog (#27). A route with
no known price is never chosen by `auto`, so a missing price can't look free. OpenRouter is one
backend among many, not the system: it adds a fee, sends prompts through another company, and
doesn't count toward cloud commitments.

## 15. GPU scaling on addressable demand at API prices

**Why:** Counting only traffic already served by a model means a stopped model never looks worth
starting. The controller counts what all traffic the model *could* serve costs at API-equivalent
prices, excluding free upgrades. That number doesn't fall when GPUs take over the traffic, so it
doesn't flap. Two self-hosted models that address the same traffic are each credited with it; the
router then splits the traffic. Revisit if that over-provisions in practice.

## 16. Deterministic, rule-based compression first

**Why:** Compression must give identical output every turn or it breaks provider caching (and, on
recent Claude models, edited history can invalidate thinking). Rules (strip ANSI codes, collapse
repeated lines, keep head and tail of huge outputs) are deterministic, need no stored state, and add
no ML dependency. A model-based compressor (LLMLingua-2) can come later behind a content-hash cache.

## 17. Configuration versions in Postgres, YAML as the starting point

**Why:** Containers mount config read-only, and a fleet of gateways needs one source of truth. Saving
from the console validates the document, stores it as a new version (who, when, why), and every
gateway hot-reloads it within seconds; in-flight requests finish on the objects they started with.
Restore is one click. The YAML file is used until the first version is saved, and stays the format
for import, export, and GitOps. Secrets never enter the database: literal keys are refused and must
stay `${ENV}` references.

## 18. Control panel in Mantine, monitoring first

**Why:** Anyone running a company's LLM traffic through Merit Order will watch it far more than
they reconfigure it. The console opens on a live Dispatch view (the merit-order stack from real
traffic, a live request feed, backend health, the GPU fleet, and what needs attention), with
configuration one page among several. Mantine gives a complete admin component set with few
dependencies; charts stay hand-written SVG.

## 19. The IdP owns identity; Merit Order owns teams; user records decide team and role

**Why:** Enterprises expect Entra to be the source of truth for who exists and which groups they're
in, but budgets and model policy belong to Merit Order. People are created at first sign-in, their
team and role come from mapped groups, and admins can pin exceptions. Each request resolves team and
role from the user record (cached for a minute), not from the key, so moves and disables apply to
existing keys. SCIM provisioning (`/scim/v2`) applies Entra changes, including deprovisioning, as they happen.

## 20. Quality scores are measured with graded tasks; judges only where nothing else works

**Why:** Routing is only as good as its quality scores. Mechanical grading (exact answers, hidden
unit tests run in a sandbox, the end state of a scripted tool environment) is cheap, repeatable and
explainable, so it grades everything it can. Easy tasks can't tell the strongest models apart, so
the `frontier` suite adds hard work at levels 3–5. Open-ended work (summaries, critiques,
recommendations) can't be checked mechanically, so two judge models from different families grade
it against concrete rubric statements; both must agree, which offsets a judge's preference for its
own family. The eval suggests scores (with a finer 0–5 "ability" and a flag where evidence is thin);
an admin decides whether to apply them.

## 21. Every cost is visible next to the switch that controls it

**Why:** A gateway that starts cloud GPUs on its own has to be easy to overrule. The console shows
where each GPU runs, for how long, and what it has cost, with stop, pin, and stop-all controls that
take effect within seconds and are logged with who and why. Organization safeguards (org and GPU
budgets, fleet caps, a per-request ceiling) are hard limits that apply to admin pins too, so no
single action can exceed them. Limits are config (versioned, reviewable); stops and pins are
runtime controls (immediate, expiring), because an emergency shouldn't wait on a config review.

## 22. GPU prices come from SkyPilot's catalog; SkyPilot runs in its own environment

**Why:** A hand-typed `gpu_cost_per_hour` is wrong as soon as SkyPilot places a replica somewhere
else: 4×H100 spot ranges from about $4/h to over $20/h across clouds and regions. The controller
uses SkyPilot's catalog (the same prices its optimizer uses) for break-even decisions, and each
running replica's own cloud, region, instance, and spot price for burn rate, cost, and chargeback.
The configured price is the fallback, and the only price for your own hardware. These are list
prices; discounts, disks, and egress aren't included until bill reconciliation exists.

SkyPilot pulls in about 150 packages and, as a dependency, would have downgraded the gateway's
uvicorn. So it lives only in the controller's `-gpu` image, in a separate Python environment, and
Merit Order reaches it through the `sky` CLI and SkyPilot's own interpreter.

## 23. A named model is never silently swapped; substitution is opt-in and never to a weaker model

**Why:** Harnesses and apps that name a model depend on its behavior, especially with tools. When
a named model has nowhere to run (for example its GPUs were stopped), the default is a 503 that
explains why for each route and suggests `auto`. Teams that would rather keep working can turn on
`substitute_unavailable`: the request goes to a model at least as good for the task (never weaker),
and the response says which model was replaced. `auto` sessions always move to another model.

## 24. Refusals are retried on another model only for `auto`

**Why:** Safety classifiers sometimes refuse benign requests, and for `auto` the client has said any
suitable model is fine, so the next model gets a chance (the refused attempt is still billed and
logged). A client that named a model gets that model's answer, refusal included. Teams can turn the
retry off.

## 25. Every process follows the stored configuration

**Why:** Budgets and safeguards edited in the console must reach everything that enforces them.
Gateways, the worker (alerts), and the capacity controller (GPU budget, fleet caps) all load the
newest stored version and reload when it changes; the YAML file only applies until the first
version is saved. A version that fails to load is skipped and the last good one stays in effect.

## 26. No request queue in the gateway; a full GPU queues only as a last resort

**Why:** LLM calls are interactive and streaming, so a queue in Redis would add latency and a
second set of workers to pull from it, for no gain: vLLM already schedules and queues on the GPU.
A saturated GPU gets no new work while another route can take it, but when it's the only route,
sending the request there to wait beats a 503. The wait is bounded (`max_waiting` per replica) so
a backlog can't grow without limit. Gateways count in-flight requests and share the counts every
2 s, because the controller's one-minute metrics sample is too slow to catch a burst.

## 27. Prices are live, never typed in

**Why:** `auto` compares prices on every request, so a stale price sends traffic to the wrong place, and
prices change without notice: OpenRouter's provider prices move overnight, and Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon
double on 1 December 2026. Prices typed into the config were right only on the day they were typed.

**How:** The worker refreshes prices every `prices_refresh_minutes` (15): OpenRouter routes from
OpenRouter's catalog (what OpenRouter charges), and direct provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock,
Vertex, Azure, Foundry, Mistral) from the price list LiteLLM maintains, which also carries long-prompt
tiers (Claude Haiku 5.5 above 100K tokens, GPT-6.x above 272K) that costing and routing apply. Gateways
reload only when a price changes. Every change is reported; a maker's list price that disagrees with
OpenRouter's for the same model raises an alert, since one list is then wrong; a list that can't be
fetched keeps its routes' last prices and raises an alert. The Models page shows each route's source and
when prices were last checked. OpenRouter requests also record what OpenRouter actually billed.

**Not chosen:** Scraping the providers' pricing pages (fragile, and each one differs); trusting a single
list without a cross-check. A `price:` in the config remains for what no public list knows, such as a
negotiated discount, and is shown as an override.

"""Reports API (docs/08-reporting.md). Metadata only; never prompt content.

Who sees what:
* user       -> their own usage
* team_lead  -> their team
* finance    -> everything, aggregated (no per-request detail)
* admin      -> everything
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
import uuid
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response, StreamingResponse

from .auth import AuthError, Principal
from .store import SUM_FIELDS, month_start, validate_group

COUNT_FIELDS = ["requests", "errors", "upgraded"]


def _parse_day(value: str | None, default: datetime) -> datetime:
    if not value:
        return default
    try:
        return datetime.combine(date.fromisoformat(value), datetime.min.time(), tzinfo=UTC)
    except ValueError:
        raise HTTPException(400, f"dates must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {value!r}")


def _scope(p: Principal, user: str | None, team: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Clamp the requested filters to what this principal may see."""
    if p.at_least("finance"):
        return user, team
    if p.role == "team_lead":
        return user, p.team
    return p.user_id, None


def _totals(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t = {f: 0 for f in COUNT_FIELDS + SUM_FIELDS + ["savings_total"]}
    for r in rows:
        for f in t:
            t[f] += r.get(f) or 0
    return {k: round(v, 6) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in t.items()}


def build_router(gateway) -> APIRouter:
    router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1/reports", tags=["reports"])

    async def principal(request: Request) -> Principal:
        try:
            return await gateway.authn.authenticate({k.lower(): v for k, v in request.headers.items()})
        except AuthError as e:
            raise HTTPException(e.status, e.message)

    async def summary_rows(p, start, end, group_by, user, team):
        try:
            validate_group(group_by)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise HTTPException(400, str(e))
        user, team = _scope(p, user, team)
        rows = await gateway.store.summary(start, end, group_by, user_id=user, team=team)
        return rows, user, team

    @router.get("/summary")
    async def summary(
        request: Request,
        start: str | None = Query(None, description="YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (default: first of this month)"),
        end: str | None = Query(None, description="YYYY-MM-DD, exclusive (default: tomorrow)"),
        group_by: str = Query("model", description="user, team, model, backend, day, hour, month, none, or tag:<name>"),
        user: str | None = None,
        team: str | None = None,
    ):
        p = await principal(request)
        s = _parse_day(start, month_start())
        e = _parse_day(end, datetime.now(UTC).replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(days=1))
        rows, user, team = await summary_rows(p, s, e, group_by, user, team)
        return {"start": s.isoformat(), "end": e.isoformat(), "group_by": group_by, "user": user, "team": team,
                "rows": rows, "totals": _totals(rows)}

    @router.get("/summary.csv")
    async def summary_csv(request: Request, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None, group_by: str = "model",
                          user: str | None = None, team: str | None = None):
        p = await principal(request)
        s = _parse_day(start, month_start())
        e = _parse_day(end, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1))
        rows, _, _ = await summary_rows(p, s, e, group_by, user, team)
        buf = io.StringIO()
        fields = ["key"] + COUNT_FIELDS + SUM_FIELDS + ["savings_total"]
        w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=fields, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
        return Response(buf.getvalue(), media_type="text/csv",
                        headers={"content-disposition": f'attachment; filename="meritorder-{group_by.replace(":", "-")}.csv"'})

    @router.get("/me")
    async def me(request: Request):
        p = await principal(request)
        team_cfg = gateway.cfg.team(p.team)
        start = month_start()
        rows = await gateway.store.summary(start, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1), "model", user_id=p.user_id)
        totals = _totals(rows)
        return {
            "user": p.user_id,
            "team": p.team,
            "role": p.role,
            "month": start.strftime("%Y-%m"),
            "spend_usd": round(await gateway.spend("user", p.user_id), 6),
            "budget_usd": p.monthly_limit(team_cfg.user_budget_usd_month),
            "team_spend_usd": round(await gateway.spend("team", p.team), 6) if p.at_least("team_lead") else None,
            "team_budget_usd": team_cfg.budget_usd_month,
            "baseline_usd": totals["baseline_cost"],
            "savings_usd": totals["savings_total"],
            "requests": totals["requests"],
            "by_model": rows,
        }

    @router.get("/export.jsonl")
    async def export(request: Request, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None):
        """Per-request metadata as JSON lines (no prompt or response content)."""
        p = await principal(request)
        if p.role == "finance":
            raise HTTPException(403, "finance role sees aggregates only; use /v1/reports/summary.csv (by team, tag, model, or day)")
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "team leads and admins only")
        s = _parse_day(start, month_start())
        e = _parse_day(end, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1))
        team = None if p.role == "admin" else p.team

        async def lines():
            async for row in gateway.store.export_rows(s, e, team):
                yield json.dumps(row, default=str, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"

        name = f"meritorder-ledger-{s:%Y%m%d}-{e:%Y%m%d}.jsonl"
        return StreamingResponse(lines(), media_type="application/x-ndjson",
                                 headers={"content-disposition": f'attachment; filename="{name}"'})

    @router.get("/gpu")
    async def gpu(request: Request):
        """State of each self-hosted deployment, as published by the capacity controller."""
        from .controls import controller_status, describe_control, fleet

        p = await principal(request)
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "team leads, finance, and admins only")
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        controls = await gateway.store.get_setting("gpu_controls") or {}
        month_cost = await gateway.store.gpu_spend_since(month_start(now))
        out = []

        def stranded(backend: str) -> list[str]:
            """Chat models this deployment serves that have no API route: requests naming them fail while it's off."""
            names = []
            for m in gateway.cfg.models:
                if m.kind != "chat" or not any(r.backend == backend for r in m.routes):
                    continue
                if not any(r.backend in gateway.backends and gateway.backends[r.backend].kind != "self_hosted" for r in m.routes):
                    names.append(m.name)
            return names

        for b in gateway.cfg.backends:
            if b.kind != "self_hosted":
                continue
            rec = await gateway.state.get_json(f"deploy:{b.name}") or {}
            serve = b.serve
            out.append({"backend": b.name, "enabled": b.enabled, "managed": serve is not None,
                        "model": serve.model if serve else None, "provisioner": serve.provisioner if serve else None,
                        "state": rec.get("state", "api_only" if b.enabled else "disabled"), "gpu_usd_per_hour": b.gpu_cost_per_hour,
                        "month_cost": round(month_cost.get(b.name, 0.0), 4),
                        "only_route_for": stranded(b.name),
                        "control": describe_control(controls, b.name) if serve else None,
                        "spec": {"accelerators": serve.accelerators, "use_spot": serve.use_spot, "clouds": serve.clouds, "regions": serve.regions,
                                 "min_replicas": serve.min_replicas, "max_replicas": serve.max_replicas,
                                 "location": serve.location, "drain_minutes": serve.drain_minutes} if serve else None,
                        **{k: v for k, v in rec.items() if k != "state"}})
        g = gateway.cfg.safeguards
        return {"deployments": out, "paused": describe_control(controls, "") if controls.get("paused") else None,
                "controller": await controller_status(gateway.state), "fleet": await fleet(gateway),
                "gpu_month": {"spent": round(sum(month_cost.values()), 4), "budget": g.gpu_budget_usd_month},
                "limits": {"max_gpu_usd_per_hour": g.max_gpu_usd_per_hour, "max_gpu_replicas": g.max_gpu_replicas},
                "daily": await gateway.store.gpu_daily(now - timedelta(days=30))}

    @router.get("/gpu/candidates")
    async def gpu_candidates(request: Request):
        """Chat models with open weights (an hf_id): the ones that could be self-hosted."""
        p = await principal(request)
        team = gateway.cfg.team(p.team)
        return {"models": [{"id": m.name, "hf_id": m.hf_id, "quality": m.quality} for m in gateway.cfg.models
                           if m.kind == "chat" and m.hf_id and team.allows_model(m.name)]}

    @router.get("/gpu/whatif")
    async def gpu_whatif(request: Request, model: str, gpu_usd_per_hour: float = Query(..., gt=0),
                         capacity_tokens_per_second: float = Query(2000, gt=0), days: int = Query(30, ge=1, le=90)):
        """Replay recent traffic: what would self-hosting `model` have saved?"""
        from .gpu import simulate

        p = await principal(request)
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "team leads, finance, and admins only")
        m = gateway.cfg.model(model)
        if m is None or m.kind != "chat":
            raise HTTPException(404, f"chat model '{model}' is not configured")
        rows = await gateway.store.demand_by_hour(datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=days))
        result = simulate(m, gateway.cfg, rows, gpu_usd_per_hour, capacity_tokens_per_second)
        return {**result, "days": days, "gpu_usd_per_hour": gpu_usd_per_hour, "capacity_tokens_per_second": capacity_tokens_per_second,
                "self_hostable": bool(m.hf_id),
                "note": "Upper bound: ignores cold starts and hysteresis. Demand is traffic this model's quality could serve, at API prices."}

    @router.get("/gpu/breakeven")
    async def gpu_breakeven(request: Request, days: int = Query(7, ge=1, le=90), utilization: float = Query(0.7, gt=0, le=1),
                            efficiency: float = Query(0.1, gt=0, le=1), spot: bool = True,
                            weights: Literal["published", "fp8", "4bit"] = "published", clouds: str | None = None):
        """How much traffic a GPU replica needs to pay for itself, by quality level and by open-weight model, beside the
        traffic of the last `days`. Each model's replica is sized to it and priced from SkyPilot's catalog (fetched
        again first when the stored prices are over 6 hours old); `clouds` (comma-separated) narrows where. `weights`:
        served as published, or quantized (`fp8`: a 16-bit checkpoint in FP8; `4bit`: everything above 4 bits in 4)."""
        from . import gpu_sizing
        from .config import ServeConfig
        from .gpu import breakeven

        p = await principal(request)
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "team leads, finance, and admins only")
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        catalog, sizes = await gpu_sizing.current(gateway.cfg, gateway.store)
        offered = sorted({o["cloud"] for o in catalog.get("offers") or []})
        chosen = {c.strip().lower() for c in clouds.split(",") if c.strip()} if clouds else set(offered)
        prices = {}
        for b in gateway.cfg.backends:
            if b.kind == "self_hosted":
                rec = await gateway.state.get_json(f"deploy:{b.name}") or {}
                if (rec.get("price") or {}).get("usd_per_hour"):
                    prices[b.name] = float(rec["price"]["usd_per_hour"])
        plans = gpu_sizing.replica_plans(gateway.cfg, catalog, sizes, chosen, spot, weights, replica_prices=prices)
        rows = await gateway.store.demand_by_hour(now - timedelta(days=days))
        # Averages over the time there's been traffic in the window, so a gateway that started yesterday isn't diluted.
        first = min((r["hour"] for r in rows), default=now)
        hours = max(1.0, min(days * 24.0, (now - first).total_seconds() / 3600))
        live = {name for name, b in gateway.backends.items() if b.available}
        margin = ServeConfig.model_fields["margin"].default  # what the controller asks of demand by default
        result = breakeven(gateway.cfg, live, rows, hours, plans, utilization, margin, efficiency)
        result["assumptions"].update({"spot": spot, "weights": weights, "clouds": sorted(chosen), "fit": gpu_sizing.FIT})
        return {**result, "days": days,
                "prices": {"fetched_at": catalog.get("fetched_at"), "catalog_updated": catalog.get("catalog_updated"),
                           "skypilot": catalog.get("skypilot"), "clouds": offered, "problem": catalog.get("problem"),
                           "offers": len(catalog.get("offers") or [])},
                "sizes": {"fetched_at": sizes.get("fetched_at")}}

    @router.post("/gpu/breakeven/refresh")
    async def gpu_breakeven_refresh(request: Request):
        """Get the latest GPU prices now: SkyPilot downloads its catalogs again, and model sizes are fetched again.
        Without SkyPilot here, the GPU controller is asked to (202), and the report shows them once it has."""
        from . import gpu_sizing
        from .controller import PRICES_REQUESTED
        from .gpu import sky_available

        p = await principal(request)
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "team leads, finance, and admins only")
        if not sky_available():
            await gateway.state.set_json(PRICES_REQUESTED, {"by": p.user_id, "at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")})
            await gateway.state.set_json("controller:kick", uuid.uuid4().hex)  # wake it now rather than at its next cycle
            heartbeat = await gateway.state.get_json("controller:heartbeat")
            return JSONResponse({"requested": True, "controller": bool(heartbeat)}, status_code=202)
        try:
            return await gpu_sizing.refresh(gateway.cfg, gateway.store, download=True)
        except gpu_sizing.SkyPilotMissing as e:
            raise HTTPException(503, str(e))
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (the console shows why)
            raise HTTPException(502, f"couldn't get prices: {e}"[:300])

    @router.get("/requests")
    async def requests(request: Request, limit: int = Query(50, ge=1, le=1000), user: str | None = None, team: str | None = None):
        p = await principal(request)
        if p.role == "finance":
            raise HTTPException(403, "finance role sees aggregates only; use /v1/reports/summary")
        user, team = _scope(p, user, team)
        return JSONResponse({"rows": await gateway.store.recent(limit, user_id=user, team=team)})

    return router

from meritorder.config import OIDCConfig

SCIM = {"authorization": "Bearer scim-secret", "content-type": "application/scim+json"}


async def test_scim_disabled_without_token(client):
    r = await client.get("/scim/v2/Users", headers=SCIM)
    assert r.status_code == 404


async def test_scim_lifecycle(client, gateway, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN", "scim-secret")
    research = gateway.cfg.team("default").model_copy(update={"name": "research"})
    gateway.cfg.teams.append(research)
    gateway.cfg.auth.oidc = OIDCConfig(issuer="https://login.example.com", client_id="x",
                                       team_from_groups={"grp-research": "research"}, role_from_groups={"grp-leads": "team_lead"})
    assert (await client.get("/scim/v2/Users", headers={"authorization": "Bearer wrong"})).status_code == 401

    # Entra checks whether the user exists, then creates them
    r = await client.get('/scim/v2/Users?filter=userName eq "pat@example.com"', headers=SCIM)
    assert r.json()["totalResults"] == 0
    r = await client.post("/scim/v2/Users", headers=SCIM, json={
        "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"], "externalId": "oid-pat", "userName": "pat@example.com",
        "displayName": "Pat Lee", "active": True, "emails": [{"value": "pat@example.com", "type": "work", "primary": True}]})
    assert r.status_code == 201 and r.json()["id"] == "oid-pat"
    assert (await client.post("/scim/v2/Users", headers=SCIM, json={"externalId": "oid-pat", "userName": "pat@example.com"})).status_code == 409
    assert (await gateway.store.get_user("oid-pat"))["team"] == "default"

    # groups: membership drives team and role
    g = (await client.post("/scim/v2/Groups", headers=SCIM, json={"displayName": "Research", "externalId": "grp-research", "members": []})).json()
    await client.patch(f"/scim/v2/Groups/{g['id']}", headers=SCIM, json={"Operations": [{"op": "Add", "path": "members", "value": [{"value": "oid-pat"}]}]})
    assert (await gateway.store.get_user("oid-pat"))["team"] == "research"
    leads = (await client.post("/scim/v2/Groups", headers=SCIM, json={"displayName": "Leads", "externalId": "grp-leads",
                                                                         "members": [{"value": "oid-pat"}]})).json()
    assert (await gateway.store.get_user("oid-pat"))["role"] == "team_lead"
    r = await client.get('/scim/v2/Groups?filter=displayName eq "Leads"&excludedAttributes=members', headers=SCIM)
    assert r.json()["Resources"][0]["id"] == leads["id"] and "members" not in r.json()["Resources"][0]
    await client.patch(f"/scim/v2/Groups/{g['id']}", headers=SCIM, json={"Operations": [{"op": "Remove", "path": 'members[value eq "oid-pat"]'}]})
    assert (await gateway.store.get_user("oid-pat"))["team"] == "default"
    await client.delete(f"/scim/v2/Groups/{leads['id']}", headers=SCIM)
    assert (await gateway.store.get_user("oid-pat"))["role"] == "user"

    # their key works until Entra deactivates them, then stops at once
    key = (await gateway.store.create_key("oid-pat", "default", "user"))[1]
    assert (await client.get("/v1/reports/me", headers=auth(key))).status_code == 200
    r = await client.patch("/scim/v2/Users/oid-pat", headers=SCIM, json={"Operations": [{"op": "Replace", "path": "active", "value": "False"}]})
    assert r.json()["active"] is False
    assert (await client.get("/v1/reports/me", headers=auth(key))).status_code == 401
    await client.patch("/scim/v2/Users/oid-pat", headers=SCIM, json={"Operations": [{"op": "replace", "value": {"active": True}}]})
    assert (await client.get("/v1/reports/me", headers=auth(key))).status_code == 200
    assert (await client.delete("/scim/v2/Users/oid-pat", headers=SCIM)).status_code == 204
    assert (await client.get("/v1/reports/me", headers=auth(key))).status_code == 401
    assert (await client.get("/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig", headers=SCIM)).json()["patch"]["supported"] is True

# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports. People are created in Merit Order the first time they sign in with `meritorder login` (or when an admin issues them a key). | | Teams, with budgets, limits, and model policy | Merit Order: Config → Teams. $/month"] --> T1["Team: platform
$/month"] ORG --> T2["Team: data-science
$/month"] T1 --> U1["User budget"] T1 --> U2["User budget"] T2 --> U3["User budget"] U1 --> K1["Key"] U1 --> K2["Key"] ``` - A request must fit **every** level above it: organization, team, and person. - Spend is checked before a request is sent and counted when it finishes (Redis counters seeded from the Postgres ledger, which stays the source of truth). - Alerts go out at 80% and 100%; at 100% requests are refused with a 429 that says which budget was reached. - Policy lives alongside budgets: allowed models, allowed providers, data residency (e.g. "DeepSeek weights only self-hosted or on Bedrock, never the vendor API"). ## Limits that stop runaway spend | Setting (per team) | What it does | |---|---| | `budget_usd_month`, `user_budget_usd_month` | Monthly caps; requests are refused at 100% (alerts at 80%) | | `max_session_usd` | Stops one session (typically an agent stuck in a loop) once it has spent this much | | `rate_limits: {user_rpm, user_tpm, team_rpm, team_tpm}` | Requests and prompt tokens per minute; 429 with `Retry-After` | ## Organization-wide safeguards Hard limits for everyone, set under `safeguards:` or on the console's **Controls** page (which shows each one next to this month's spend and the pace it's on, and saves changes as a new config version): | Setting | What it does | |---|---| | `org_budget_usd_month` | All spend in the ledger. def install_idp(monkeypatch, poll, oidc=True, expires_in=60, exchange_status=200):
    """A fake gateway + identity provider for the OIDC device-code flow."""
    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        url = str(request.url)
        if url == "http://gw.test/auth/config":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"oidc": {"issuer": "https://idp.test/", "client_id": "cli", "scopes": ["openid", "email"]} if oidc else None})
        if url == "https://idp.test/.well-known/openid-configuration":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"device_authorization_endpoint": "https://idp.test/device", "token_endpoint": "https://idp.test/token"})
        if url == "https://idp.test/device":
            assert b"client_id=cli" in request.content and b"scope=openid+email" in request.content
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"device_code": "dc", "user_code": "ABCD", "verification_uri": "https://idp.test/activate",
                                             "interval": 1, "expires_in": expires_in})
        if url == "https://idp.test/token":
            assert b"device_code=dc" in request.content
            return httpx.Response(200, json=poll())
        if url == "http://gw.test/auth/exchange":
            assert json.loads(request.content) == {"id_token": "idt"}
            if exchange_status != 200:
                return httpx.Response(exchange_status, text="not in a team")
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"api_key": "mo-new", "user": "alice", "team": "eng", "expires_at": "2026-12-09T00:00:00Z"})
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected request {url}")

    real = httpx.Client
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli.httpx, "Client", lambda **kw: real(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler), **kw))

class LiveGateway:
    """A real gateway (in-memory storage, mock backends) served by uvicorn on a free port, in a thread."""

    def __init__(self, cfg):
        self.gw = build_gateway(cfg, store=MemoryStore(), state=MemoryState())
        self.gw.file_raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
        self.server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(gateway=self.gw), host="127.0.0.1", port=0, log_level="warning", lifespan="off"))
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.run, daemon=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        self.thread.start()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
        while not self.server.started:
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "gateway did not start"
            time.sleep(0.02)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.servers[0].sockets[0].getsockname()[1]}"
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.should_exit = True
        self.thread.join(10)

    def chat(self, n: int = 1, key: str = TEST_KEY, model: str = "small") -> None:
        before = len(self.gw.store.ledger)
        for _ in range(n):
            r = httpx.post(f"{self.url}/v1/chat/completions", headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
                           json={"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}, timeout=30)
            assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
        while len(self.gw.store.ledger) < before + n:  # ledger rows are written just after the response
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline
            time.sleep(0.01)

REQUIRED = {"id", "task", "level", "kind", "prompt", "env", "env_args", "max_turns", "summary"}


def spec(task_id: str) -> dict:
    return yaml.safe_load((ROOT / task_id / "task.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def build(task_id: str, sandbox=None) -> Env:
    s = spec(task_id)
    return load_env(s["env"])(sandbox=sandbox, **(s.get("env_args") or {}))


def J(text: str) -> dict:
    return json.loads(text)


def edit(env: Env, path: str, *replacements: tuple[str, str]) -> None:
    """Read a file through the tools, apply exact replacements, write it back."""
    text = env.handle("read_file", {"path": path})
    for old, new in replacements:
        assert old in text, (path, old)
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    assert env.handle("write_file", {"path": path, "content": text}).startswith("wrote")

ORACLE_SQL = """
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT provider_ref AS ref, order_id, datetime(event_at) AS at, amount_cents / 100.0 AS amount,
         COALESCE(currency, 'EUR') AS cur, lower(status) AS status FROM payments
  UNION ALL
  SELECT provider_ref, order_id, datetime(event_at), amount, currency, lower(status) FROM payments_v2
),
pay AS (
  SELECT ref, MIN(order_id) AS order_id, MIN(at) AS at, MIN(amount) AS amount, MIN(cur) AS cur, MIN(status) AS status
  FROM raw GROUP BY ref
),
real AS (
  SELECT pay.* FROM pay JOIN orders o ON o.id = pay.order_id LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
  WHERE c.is_test IS NOT 1
),
revenue AS (
  SELECT SUM(amount * CASE WHEN cur = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 ELSE (SELECT eur_per_unit FROM fx_rates f
         WHERE f.currency = real.cur AND f.day <= date(real.at) ORDER BY f.day DESC LIMIT 1) END) AS v
  FROM real WHERE status = 'captured'
    AND strftime('%Y-%m', CASE WHEN at >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' THEN datetime(at, '+1 hour') ELSE at END) = '2026-03'
),
refunded AS (
  SELECT SUM(COALESCE(r.amount, real.amount) * CASE WHEN real.cur = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 ELSE (SELECT eur_per_unit FROM fx_rates f
         WHERE f.currency = real.cur AND f.day <= date(r.refunded_at) ORDER BY f.day DESC LIMIT 1) END) AS v
  FROM refunds r JOIN real ON real.ref = r.provider_ref
  WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', CASE WHEN r.refunded_at >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' THEN datetime(r.refunded_at, '+1 hour')
                          ELSE r.refunded_at END) = '2026-03'
)
SELECT ROUND((SELECT v FROM revenue) - (SELECT v FROM refunded), 2) AS net_eur
"""


def independent_answer() -> Decimal:
    """The expected figure computed in Python straight from the rows, following the prompt's definitions."""
    db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    db.executescript((sqldb.DATASETS / "billing.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    is_test = dict(db.execute("SELECT id, is_test FROM customers"))
    customer = dict(db.execute("SELECT id, customer_id FROM orders"))
    pays = {}
    for ref, oid, at, cents, cur, status in db.execute("SELECT provider_ref, order_id, event_at, amount_cents, currency, status FROM payments"):
        pays[ref] = (oid, dt.datetime.strptime(at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), Decimal(cents) / 100, cur or "EUR", status.lower())
    for ref, oid, at, amount, cur, status in db.execute("SELECT provider_ref, order_id, event_at, amount, currency, status FROM payments_v2"):
        pays[ref] = (oid, dt.datetime.strptime(at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), Decimal(str(amount)), cur, status)
    fx = {(dt.date.fromisoformat(d), c): Decimal(str(r)) for d, c, r in db.execute("SELECT day, currency, eur_per_unit FROM fx_rates")}

    def rate(day: dt.date, cur: str) -> Decimal:
        while cur != "EUR" and (day, cur) not in fx:
            day -= dt.timedelta(days=1)
        return Decimal(1) if cur == "EUR" else fx[(day, cur)]

    def march(t: dt.datetime) -> bool:
        local = t + dt.timedelta(hours=1 if t >= dt.datetime(2026, 3, 29, 1) else 0)
        return (local.year, local.month) == (2026, 3)

    def real(oid: int) -> bool:
        return customer[oid] is None or is_test[customer[oid]] != 1

    total = sum((amt * rate(at.date(), cur) for oid, at, amt, cur, status in pays.values()
                 if status == "captured" and march(at) and real(oid)), Decimal(0))
    for ref, at, amount in db.execute("SELECT provider_ref, refunded_at, amount FROM refunds"):
        oid, _, full, cur, _ = pays[ref]
        when = dt.datetime.strptime(at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        if march(when) and real(oid):
            total -= (full if amount is None else Decimal(str(amount))) * rate(when.date(), cur)
    return total


def test_a5_sql_oracle():
    env = build("a5-march-revenue")
    assert float(independent_answer()) == pytest.approx(env.answer, abs=0.001)
    tables = {t["name"] for t in J(env.handle("list_tables", {}))["tables"]}
    assert tables == {"customers", "orders", "payments", "payments_v2", "refunds", "fx_rates"}

CARELESS_SQL = {
    # Only the legacy table, UTC month, no dedup, no FX, no test-account filter.
    "legacy only": "SELECT SUM(amount_cents) / 100.0 FROM payments WHERE status = 'CAPTURED' AND event_at LIKE '2026-03%'",
    # Both tables but no dedup, text comparison of mixed timestamp formats, is_test = 0, FX ignored.
    "naive union": """
        SELECT SUM(a) FROM (
          SELECT p.amount_cents / 100.0 AS a, p.order_id FROM payments p WHERE p.status = 'CAPTURED'
            AND p.event_at >= '2026-03-01 00:00:00' AND p.event_at < '2026-03-31 23:00:00'
          UNION ALL
          SELECT v.amount, v.order_id FROM payments_v2 v WHERE v.status = 'captured'
            AND v.event_at >= '2026-03-01 00:00:00' AND v.event_at < '2026-03-31 23:00:00'
        ) x JOIN orders o ON o.id = x.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = 0""",
    # Everything right except the month boundary: UTC instead of Lisbon.
    "utc month": ORACLE_SQL.replace("'2026-03-29 01:00:00'", "'2099-01-01 00:00:00'"),
    # Everything right except NULL is_test (legacy accounts) treated as test accounts.
    "is_test = 0": ORACLE_SQL.replace("WHERE c.is_test IS NOT 1", "WHERE c.is_test = 0 OR o.customer_id IS NULL"),
    # Everything right except the FX rate must exist on the exact day.
    "exact-day fx": ORACLE_SQL.replace("f.day <= date(real.at) ORDER BY f.day DESC", "f.day = date(real.at)"),
    # Everything right except the refunds join duplicates webhook retries (no dedup before joining refunds).
    "refund join dup": ORACLE_SQL.replace(
        "FROM refunds r JOIN real ON",
        "FROM refunds r JOIN (SELECT raw.* FROM raw JOIN orders o ON o.id = raw.order_id LEFT JOIN customers c"
        " ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.is_test IS NOT 1) real ON"),
}

def oracle_incident(env: IncidentEnv) -> str:
    alerts = J(env.handle("get_alerts", {}))["alerts"]
    assert any(a["service"] == "checkout-api" for a in alerts)
    graph = {s["name"]: s for s in J(env.handle("list_services", {}))["services"]}
    assert "search-svc" not in graph["checkout-api"]["depends_on"]
    overview = J(env.handle("get_metrics", {"service": "checkout-api", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "start": "08:00",
                                            "end": "16:00", "step_minutes": 10}))["points"]
    assert [t for t, v in overview if v > 1] == ["13:40", "13:50", "14:00", "14:10"]
    points = J(env.handle("get_metrics", {"service": "checkout-api", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "start": "13:00", "end": "15:00"}))["points"]
    i = next(i for i, (_, v) in enumerate(points) if v > 1)
    start = points[i][0]
    end = next(t for t, v in points[i:] if v <= 1)
    errors = J(env.handle("search_logs", {"service": "checkout-api", "level": "ERROR", "start": start, "end": end}))
    upstream = {re.search(r"upstream=(\S+)", ln).group(1) for ln in errors["lines"]}
    assert upstream == {"pricing-svc"} and errors["total_matches"] > len(errors["lines"])
    pool = J(env.handle("search_logs", {"service": "pricing-svc", "query": "pool", "start": "08:00", "end": start}))
    assert any("DB_POOL_MAX not set" in ln for ln in pool["lines"])
    pool_max = J(env.handle("get_metrics", {"service": "pricing-svc", "metric": "db_pool_max", "start": "10:00", "end": "13:42"}))["points"]
    changed = next(t for (t, v), (_, prev) in zip(pool_max[1:], pool_max) if v != prev)
    deploys = J(env.handle("get_deploys", {"service": "pricing-svc", "end": changed}))["deploys"]
    culprit = J(env.handle("get_deploy", {"deploy_id": deploys[-1]["id"]}))
    key = next(k for k, (old, new) in culprit["changes"]["config"].items() if old == "40")
    for other in J(env.handle("get_deploys", {"start": "13:30", "end": start}))["deploys"]:  # rule out the nearby changes
        assert "DB_POOL" not in json.dumps(J(env.handle("get_deploy", {"deploy_id": other["id"]}))["changes"])
    inventory = J(env.handle("get_metrics", {"service": "inventory-svc", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "start": "13:30", "end": "14:30",
                                             "step_minutes": 5}))["points"]
    assert max(v for _, v in inventory) < 1
    return ("Root cause: the pricing-svc deploy removed DB_POOL_MAX, falling back to 8 connections per replica.\n"
            + json.dumps({"deploy_id": culprit["id"], "service": culprit["service"], "config_key": key,
                          "impact_start": start, "impact_end": end}))


def test_a5_incident_oracle():
    env = build("a5-checkout-incident")
    answer = oracle_incident(env)
    assert 10 <= len(env.calls) <= 30
    ok, why = env.grade(answer)
    assert ok, why
    assert json.loads(answer.splitlines()[-1])["impact_end"] == "14:17"
    alt = {"deploy_id": "DEP-8B2F", "service": "pricing-svc", "config_key": "db_pool_max (40 -> unset, default 8)",
           "impact_start": "2026-11-03T13:41Z", "impact_end": "2026-11-03 14:16:00 UTC"}
    assert env.grade("```json\n" + json.dumps(alt) + "\n```")[0]

# 10 — How it decides Every decision Merit Order makes, in the order it makes them, with the exact rules and defaults. Each rule names the setting that controls it. The code is the source of truth: `proxy.py` (request pipeline), `router.py` (model and backend choice), `gpu.py` and `controller.py` (GPU scaling). - [A request, start to finish](#a-request-start-to-finish) - [Which model](#which-model) - [Which backend: GPU or API](#which-backend-gpu-or-api) - [When a backend fails or a model refuses](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses) - [When GPUs start, scale, and stop](#when-gpus-start-scale-and-stop) - [What happens when…](#what-happens-when) - [Every threshold in one table](#every-threshold-in-one-table) ## A request, start to finish Checks run in this order. The first one that fails ends the request with the error shown. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> K{"Valid key?
person not disabled?"} K -- "no" --> E401["401"] K -- "yes" --> B{"Org, personal, and team
monthly budgets left?"} B -- "no" --> E429a["429: which budget, how much spent"] B -- "yes" --> RL{"Within requests/tokens
per minute?"} RL -- "no" --> E429b["429 + Retry-After"] RL -- "yes" --> SC{"Session under its
spend cap?"} SC -- "no" --> E429c["429: start a new session"] SC -- "yes" --> M["Pick the model
(next section)"] M --> BK["List and rank backends
(GPU or API)"] BK -- "nothing can serve it" --> E503["503 with the reason for each route"] BK --> MR{"Worst case under
max_request_usd?"} MR -- "no candidate fits" --> E400["400: what it could cost"] MR -- "yes" --> RC{"Response cache on
and a hit?"} RC -- "hit" --> HIT["Return the cached answer ($0)"] RC -- "miss / off" --> CP["Compress huge tool outputs
(deterministic, if on)"] CP --> TRY["Try candidates in order
(failures and refusals below)"] TRY --> OK["Stream the answer back
in the client's format"] OK --> LED["Record cost, baseline, savings;
update session and spend counters"] ``` ## Which model ```mermaid flowchart TD R{"What did the
client ask for?"} R -- "a model name" --> NAMED["That model, never swapped"] R -- "auto" --> SESS{"Existing session,
same task?"} SESS -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep the session's model"] SESS -- "no: new session, new human prompt,
or the harness compacted history" --> CL["Classify the task → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] CL --> CANDS["Every chat model the team may use
with quality ≥ floor"] CANDS -- "none meets the floor" --> BEST["The best models available"] KEEP -- "it has nowhere to run
(e.g. its GPUs were stopped)" --> CL NAMED -- "it has nowhere to run" --> SUB{"Team turned on
substitute_unavailable?"} SUB -- "no" --> E503["503: why, per route;
suggests auto"] SUB -- "yes" --> EQ["Models at least as good
for this task (never weaker);
response says which was replaced"] ``` **The classifier** (rules, no model call): | Request | Floor | |---|---| | Has tools or code-like text | `coding:3` | | …with 5+ tools (an agent) | `coding:4` | | …and "hard" wording (architecture, race condition, security, performance, migration, …) or > 60k tokens of context | +1 | | Anything else | `general:2` | | …short (< 400 tokens, no tools) | `general:1` | | …analysis wording (analyze, compare, trade-offs, plan, …) or > 20k tokens of context | `general:3` | | `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | −1 / +1 | | `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | exactly that, skipping the rules | Quality scores (1–5 per task type) come from config and can be measured with `meritorder eval`. **What the client can force** | Client sends | Effect | |---|---| | A model name | That model; only the backend varies | | `reasoning_effort` / `output_config.effort` | Passed through as-is. Merit Order only picks an effort for `auto` requests that don't set one | | `X-Route-Floor`, `X-Route-Hint` | Changes the floor for `auto` | | `X-MeritOrder-Backend` | Pins the backend (admins only) | | `X-MeritOrder-Cache: off` | Skips the response cache | Team policy (allowed models and backends) applies before any of this, so nothing above can escape it. ## Which backend: GPU or API Each candidate model lists its routes (backends that serve it). A route is dropped when: | Dropped when | Why | |---|---| | The backend isn't enabled (no key, no URL) or the team may not use it | Policy and credentials | | The backend is being skipped after failures (see [When a backend fails](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses)) | Bad credentials or a network-level outage: the whole backend. Retried when the wait is up | | This model is being skipped on this backend: over capacity (429/503/529), or its deployment doesn't exist there (404) | Only that model there; the backend's other models are unaffected. A busy route is kept as a **last resort** if nothing else can take the request | | It's a GPU deployment that isn't warm (not started, starting, or stopped now) | Nothing to send to | | It's draining and this session has no warm cache there | Draining only finishes sessions already there | | It's a GPU at 100% (see [When a GPU is full](#when-a-gpu-is-full)) | Saturated: new work spills to other routes. Kept as a **last resort** if nothing else can take the request | | It's a saturated GPU whose queue is also full | No room to wait either | | `auto` and the route has no known price | An unknown price must never look free | | The model's context window is too small (prompt > 95% of it) and other models fit | Avoid a guaranteed error | | `auto` and it's a mock backend while real ones exist | Mocks are for trying things out | The rest are ranked by **what this session will cost from here**: ``` cost = rebuild + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn rebuild = 0 if the backend holds this session's cache, else context × (cache-write − cache-read price) per_turn = cached context × cache-read + new tokens × cache-write (input price for OpenAI-format backends) + ~600 output tokens × output price turns = turns so far, clamped to 3…30 (a long session is expected to keep going) ``` A **GPU's price is a shadow price**: what one token "costs" given how busy the GPU is. ```mermaid flowchart LR U{"GPU utilization"} -- "≤ 60%" --> F["2% of the same model's API price
(nearly free: it's already paid for)"] U -- "60–100%" --> RISE["Rises toward 100% of API price
(quadratically)"] U -- "100% / queueing" --> OUT["Last resort only:
used when no other route can take it"] ``` So GPUs win whenever they have room, even for a **better** model than the task needs (a "free upgrade", sent at low vLLM priority so traffic that needs that model goes first). As they fill up, APIs win again. **Then the tie-breakers:** 1. **Close on price, then quality and speed.** The same model often costs the same everywhere (Claude on Anthropic, Bedrock, Foundry and OpenRouter), so price alone can't choose. Routes that cost at most the priority's premium more than the cheapest compete on speed instead: | Priority | A faster route may cost up to | Within that range | |---|---|---| | `cost` (default) | 2% more (a tie) | the higher-quality model (`auto`), then the faster route | | `balanced` | 20% more | the faster route, then the higher-quality model | | `speed` | 100% more | the faster route, then the higher-quality model | The organization default is `routing.priority`; a team can set its own (`priority`), and a request can send `X-MeritOrder-Priority: cost|balanced|speed`. Speed is the expected time for a typical reply (`routing.est_output_tokens`, 600 tokens): time to the first token plus the writing time, both moving averages of real replies on that route (backend + upstream model). Timing starts when the route is called, so a route that took over after a failure isn't charged for it. A route is trusted after 2 replies; until then it ranks after measured ones, keeping cost order. 2. **Measuring the alternatives.** Otherwise the first route measured would win forever. Every 10th new session (`routing.speed_check_every`; 0 turns it off) can go to a route in that price range that hasn't been measured, or not in the last 10 minutes. Never mid-session, so no cache is lost. 3. **Stickiness:** a session stays on its current backend unless the cheapest one saves more than 10% + $0.01 over the rest of the session, which is usually only true once its cache has expired (5 minutes by default, `cache_ttl_seconds` per backend). That's what stops a session bouncing between Bedrock and Anthropic and paying to rebuild its cache each time. Speed never moves a session either: a warm cache is cheaper, and usually faster, than any other route. Each gateway process learns speeds from its own traffic. The console's **Backends** page shows them per model (first token, tokens per second). ## When a backend fails or a model refuses ```mermaid flowchart TD S["Send to the top candidate"] --> R{"Result"} R -- "over capacity (429/503/529),
unknown model (404), 408/409/425/500" --> NEXTM["Count a failure against this model here;
skip it on this backend for this request;
try the next"] R -- "timeout, network error, 502/504,
bad key or no access (401/403)" --> NEXT["Count a failure against the backend;
skip every candidate on it;
try the next"] R -- "200, then an error before any content
(Anthropic's in-stream overload,
an OpenRouter error chunk or body)" --> NEXTM R -- "stream sends nothing within
first_byte_timeout_seconds" --> NEXT R -- "other 4xx (bad request)" --> STOP["Return the error:
another backend would reject it too"] R -- "200, but the model refused
(before any content)" --> REF{"auto and team allows
refusal_fallback?"} REF -- "yes" --> NM["Try the next model
(refused attempt is billed and logged)"] REF -- "no" --> PASS["Return the refusal"] R -- "200" --> DONE["Respond"] NEXT --> LIM{"Candidates left?"} NEXTM --> LIM NM --> LIM LIM -- "yes" --> S LIM -- "no" --> ERR["Return the last error
(with the provider's Retry-After)"] ``` The gateway reads the start of every stream, up to its first content, before passing it on. So an error that arrives after a `200` still goes to the next source, and nothing reaches the client twice. Once content has started, an error is passed through: switching then would repeat output. How long a failing backend or model is skipped: | Failure | Skipped | For | |---|---|---| | Over capacity (429, 503, 529) | That model on that backend | The provider's `Retry-After` if it sends one, else 10 s doubling to 5 min. Still tried as a last resort | | Model or deployment not found (404) | That model on that backend | 5 min, doubling to 1 hour while it stays missing (a model not deployed there yet is checked less and less often). Turn a backend off in `.env` (`MERITORDER_BEDROCK=false`, `MERITORDER_FOUNDRY_CLAUDE=false`) until its models exist | | Credentials rejected (401, 403) | The backend | 1 min doubling to 10 min | | Anything else (5xx, timeouts, network) | The model (500) or the backend (502, 504, network) | After 3 in a row: 5 s doubling to 60 s | When something starts being skipped, an alert goes to the console's "needs attention" list, the log, and `MERITORDER_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`. It says why and where its traffic goes meanwhile. That's at most once per backend and model every 30 minutes, with a second alert when it works again. The Backends page shows what's skipped and for how long. `meritorder_failovers_total{backend,status}` counts every failed attempt, and responses served after one carry `X-MeritOrder-Failed-Over: backend/model status`. At most `max_attempts` (3) models are tried for refusals. Once a stream has started sending content to the client, a failure can't be retried: the client gets an error event, and the partial usage is still recorded. ## When GPUs start, scale, and stop The capacity controller runs every 60 s (one active at a time) and wakes immediately when an admin changes a GPU control. ```mermaid flowchart TD C0["Add up what running replicas cost
since the last cycle"] --> C1["Addressable demand for each deployment:
traffic its model is good enough for,
valued at API prices (free upgrades excluded),
max of last hour and 4 × last 15 min"] C1 --> C2["Price of one replica:
cheapest SkyPilot catalog offer in allowed
clouds/regions, else gpu_cost_per_hour"] C2 --> C3["Wanted replicas = enough for the throughput
(at 70% load), but no more than demand pays for
with a 20% margin; within min/max_replicas"] C3 --> P1{"Stop all GPUs
is on?"} P1 -- "yes" --> OFF["Stop every deployment"] P1 -- "no" --> P2{"Admin control
on this deployment?"} P2 -- "stop" --> OFF1["Stop it (drain or now)"] P2 -- "pin N" --> ON["Run exactly N"] P2 -- "none / expired" --> AUTO["Follow demand"] OFF1 --> G1 ON --> G1 AUTO --> G1{"GPU budget for the
month used up?"} G1 -- "yes" --> DR["Drain and stop everything,
pins included"] G1 -- "no" --> G2{"Fleet over max $/hour
or max replicas?"} G2 -- "yes" --> CAP["Pins first, then the deployments whose
demand best covers their cost;
the rest are held back or stopped"] G2 -- "no" --> SM["State machine (below)"] CAP --> SM DR --> SM OFF --> SM SM --> PUB["Publish state, endpoint, where replicas run,
prices → Redis; gateways follow within 5 s"] ``` **The state machine** (per deployment): ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> api_only api_only --> provisioning: start provisioning --> warm: ready provisioning --> api_only: failed, timed out, or stopped warm --> warm: scale warm --> draining: demand gone, or stop (drain) warm --> api_only: stop now warm --> provisioning: lost readiness draining --> warm: demand returns draining --> api_only: drained, or stop now ``` | Transition | Exactly when | |---|---| | **start** | Wanted ≥ 1 continuously for 10 min and not in a cooldown. At once, ignoring any cooldown, when an admin pins replicas or `min_replicas > 0` | | **ready** | The replicas answer `/v1/models` | | **failed, timed out** | SkyPilot reports failure, or 45 min pass; the replicas are shut down and the deployment cools down for 30 min | | **stopped** (while starting) | An admin stop, Stop all GPUs, the GPU budget, or a fleet cap: provisioning is cancelled at once | | **scale** | Wanted changes while warm: `sky serve update` to the new count | | **demand gone** | Wanted = 0 for 10 min, and the deployment has been warm at least 30 min | | **stop (drain)** | An admin stop with "drain first", the GPU budget, or a fleet cap. Skips the 30-minute hold | | **stop now** | An admin stop with "stop now", or Stop all GPUs (unless set to drain) | | **lost readiness** | Replicas stop answering (e.g. a spot preemption SkyServe is replacing); traffic goes to APIs until they're back | | **demand returns** | Wanted ≥ 1 again while draining, unless it was stopped | | **drained** | 15 min after draining started | | State | Gets traffic? | Billing? | |---|---|---| | `api_only` | No; its models' traffic goes to APIs (or other models for `auto`) | No | | `provisioning` | No | Yes, from the moment `sky serve up` runs | | `warm` | Yes, first choice while it has headroom | Yes | | `draining` | Only sessions whose cache is already there | Yes | ## When a GPU is full **How "full" is measured.** Two signals; a backend is saturated when either reaches 100%: | Signal | Source | How fresh | |---|---|---| | vLLM's own load: KV-cache use, pushed to 100% by ~10 waiting requests | The controller reads `/metrics` once per cycle | Up to one cycle (60 s) old | | Requests in flight ÷ (`max_concurrency` × replicas) | Every gateway counts its own requests to the backend and publishes the count to Redis every 2 s | Live for this gateway, ≤ 2 s for others | The second signal only exists when the backend sets `max_concurrency` (vLLM's `--max-num-seqs`, or what its KV cache fits). Without it, a burst can pile up in vLLM for up to a minute before the gateways notice. Set it. **Where requests wait.** Merit Order has no queue of its own, in Redis or anywhere else: LLM calls are interactive and streaming, so the gateway forwards each request at once and holds the connection open. The only queue is **vLLM's scheduler**, on the GPU. ```mermaid flowchart TD S{"GPU saturated?"} -- "no" --> USE["Candidate at its shadow price"] S -- "yes" --> OTHER{"Another route can take it?
(same model on an API, or
another model for auto)"} OTHER -- "yes" --> SPILL["Goes there.
Warm sessions too: rebuilding the cache
beats waiting behind a full GPU"] OTHER -- "no" --> Q{"Waiting requests <
max_waiting × replicas?"} Q -- "yes" --> QUEUE["Sent to the GPU anyway: waits in vLLM.
Response header x-meritorder-queued: 1"] Q -- "no" --> REJ["503 overloaded_error:
saturated and its queue is full"] ``` Waiting requests are in-flight requests beyond `max_concurrency × replicas`; without `max_concurrency`, the controller's last count of vLLM's waiting requests is used. With neither, a saturated GPU that's the only route takes everything and each request waits up to the backend's `timeout_seconds`. Meanwhile the controller sees the demand and adds replicas (after `scale_up_after_minutes`, up to `max_replicas`). ## What happens when… | When | What happens | |---|---| | **A GPU is saturated** | New requests go to an API route for the same model, or (for `auto`) another model; sessions on it move too and rebuild their cache. If nothing else can take a request, it waits in vLLM's queue (`x-meritorder-queued: 1`) | | **A GPU is saturated, it's the only route, and its queue is full** | 503 `overloaded_error` saying so; the client retries. The controller adds replicas if the demand lasts | | **A burst hits a GPU** | With `max_concurrency` set, gateways see it within 2 s and spill the excess; without it, up to a minute of requests queue in vLLM first | | **Demand drops** | After 10 min below break-even (and 30 min warm), the deployment drains for 15 min, then stops | | **Demand rises** | After 10 min above break-even, GPUs start; traffic stays on APIs until they're ready (10–20+ min for big models) | | **An admin stops a GPU (drain)** | No new sessions there at once; warm sessions finish for up to 15 min; then it's shut down | | **An admin stops a GPU (now)** | Gateways stop sending to it within seconds; the next request in each session goes elsewhere and rebuilds its cache there; shutdown starts within seconds (the cloud takes a few minutes) | | **An admin pins N replicas** | Started at once (no 10-min wait, no cooldown), kept regardless of demand, until unpinned or the pin expires; safeguards still apply | | **Stop all GPUs** | Every deployment stops, none start, until someone resumes | | **An `auto` session's model has nowhere to run** | It's routed again from scratch to another model meeting the floor | | **A named model has nowhere to run** | 503 explaining each route ("stopped by dana: cost review", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set") unless the team turned on `substitute_unavailable`; then a model at least as good, with `x-meritorder-substituted-for` | | **The GPU budget runs out** | All GPUs drain and none start until next month or the budget is raised; traffic goes to APIs | | **The fleet hits max $/hour or max replicas** | Lower-value deployments are held to fewer replicas or stopped | | **The org budget runs out** | Every request gets a 429 until next month or it's raised | | **A team or person hits their budget** | Their requests get a 429; everyone else is unaffected | | **An agent loops** | The session stops at `max_session_usd`; a spend-spike alert fires when someone's hour is 5× their norm | | **A request could cost more than `max_request_usd`** | Cheaper candidates are used; if none fit, a 400 says what it could have cost | | **Provisioning fails or takes > 45 min** | Shut down, 30-min cooldown, alert; traffic stays on APIs | | **A spot replica is preempted** | SkyServe replaces it; if no replica is ready, the deployment shows "starting" and traffic goes to APIs meanwhile | | **A stop fails at the cloud** | The deployment stays marked running and the controller keeps retrying; the console shows it in red | | **The controller isn't running** | GPUs stay as they are (nothing scales or stops them); gateways keep using the last published state; the console flags it if GPUs are up | | **A provider is over capacity** (429/529, or overloaded inside a stream) | Next backend for the same model (e.g. Anthropic → Bedrock), then the next model for `auto`. That model is skipped there for `Retry-After` (or 10 s doubling); its other models keep working; alert | | **A provider is down** (timeouts, connection errors, 5xx) | Same: next backend; skipped after 3 failures in a row; alert, and another when it recovers | | **A provider accepts a stream but never answers** | Abandoned after `first_byte_timeout_seconds` (120 s; off for self-hosted GPUs) and sent to the next backend | | **A provider rejects the key (401/403)** | Next backend; the backend is skipped for a minute (doubling). Fix the key; `meritorder check` shows what's usable | | **A model refuses** (`stop_reason: refusal`, `content_filter`) | `auto`: retried on the next model, refusal billed and logged. Named model: the refusal is returned | | **The harness compacts history** | Every cache for that session is dead, so it's a free moment to re-route | | **A session's cache expires** (idle > 5 min) | Moving is now free, so it may move to a cheaper backend | | **A stream breaks midway** | The client gets an error event; partial usage is recorded | | **Redis is down** | Requests fail (sessions, budgets, and rate limits live there). Use a managed Redis with failover | | **A burst exceeds the Redis connection pool** | Requests wait for a free connection (up to 10 s) rather than failing | | **Postgres is down** | Static and cached keys keep working for up to a minute; new sign-ins and key lookups fail; ledger rows that can't be written are logged and lost | | **Someone saves a bad config** | It's rejected on save; gateways, the worker, and the controller keep the last good version | ## Every threshold in one table | What | Default | Setting | |---|---|---| | Stickiness margin to move a session | 10% + $0.01 | `routing.switch_margin_pct`, `switch_margin_usd` | | Expected turns for cost estimates | 3–30 | `routing.min_expected_turns`, `max_expected_turns` | | How much more a faster route may cost | cost 2%, balanced 20%, speed 100% | `routing.priority`, `priority_premium_pct`; team `priority`; `X-MeritOrder-Priority` | | Checking an unmeasured or stale route's speed | every 10th new session; stale after 10 min | `routing.speed_check_every` | | GPU shadow price below the knee | 2% of API price | `routing.shadow_floor` | | GPU utilization where the shadow price starts rising | 60% | `routing.shadow_knee` | | Models tried on refusals | 3 | `routing.max_attempts` | | Reasoning effort for `auto` by floor | 1–2: low, 3: medium | `routing.effort_by_floor` | | How long a backend keeps a session's cache warm | 300 s | `backends.*.cache_ttl_seconds` | | Skipping a failing backend or model | See [When a backend fails](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses) | fixed; `Retry-After` from the provider | | Waiting for a stream to start | 120 s for APIs, none for self-hosted | `backends.*.first_byte_timeout_seconds` | | Demand before starting GPUs, and below break-even before draining | 10 min | `serve.scale_up_after_minutes` | | Minimum time warm before draining | 30 min | `serve.hold_minutes` | | Draining time | 15 min | `serve.drain_minutes` | | Provisioning timeout | 45 min (then 30 min cooldown) | `serve.provision_timeout_minutes` | | Break-even margin | 20% | `serve.margin` | | Target load per replica | 70% | `serve.target_utilization` | | Replicas | 0–4 | `serve.min_replicas`, `max_replicas` | | Requests one replica runs at once (live saturation) | not set | `backends.*.max_concurrency` | | Requests allowed to wait per replica when a saturated GPU is the only route | 32 | `backends.*.max_waiting` | | Gateways share in-flight counts | every 2 s | fixed | | Controller cycle | 60 s (wakes early on admin changes) | `meritorder controller --interval` | | Gateways pick up GPU state and config | ≤ 5 s | fixed | | Budget alerts | 80%, 100% | `safeguards.alert_at` (org, GPU); fixed for teams | | Spend spike alert | an hour at 5× the person's norm | fixed |

# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports.
