"""Responses API conversion edge cases (Codex CLI and other stateless clients)."""

import json

import pytest
from conftest import auth

from meritorder.formats.responses import ChatToResponsesStream, ResponsesError, chat_to_responses, responses_to_chat
from meritorder.formats.sse import SSEEvent, event


def test_input_items_tools_and_options():
    body = {
        "model": "m", "instructions": "be terse", "max_output_tokens": 64, "temperature": 0.1, "top_p": 0.5,
        "parallel_tool_calls": False, "user": "u1", "prompt_cache_key": "k", "reasoning": {"effort": "high"},
        "stream": True,
        "input": [
            {"type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "dev rules"}]},
            {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "see "},
                                         {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "https://img.test/a.png"},
                                         {"type": "input_image", "file_id": "file_1"},
                                         {"type": "input_image"}]},
            {"type": "reasoning", "summary": []},  # no Chat equivalent: dropped
            {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "c1", "name": "ls", "arguments": '{"p":"."}'},
            {"type": "function_call", "id": "c2", "name": "pwd"},
            {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "c1", "output": {"files": ["a"]}},
            {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "c2", "output": "/home"},
            {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "done"}]},
        ],
        "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "ls", "description": "list", "parameters": {"type": "object"}, "strict": True},
                  {"type": "web_search"}],
        "tool_choice": {"type": "function", "name": "ls"},
        "text": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "out", "schema": {"type": "object"}, "strict": True}},
    }
    out = responses_to_chat(body)
    m = out["messages"]
    assert m[0] == {"role": "system", "content": "be terse"} and m[1] == {"role": "system", "content": "dev rules"}
    assert [p["type"] for p in m[2]["content"]] == ["text", "image_url", "image_url"]
    assert m[2]["content"][2]["image_url"]["url"] == "file:file_1"
    assert m[3] == {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [
        {"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "ls", "arguments": '{"p":"."}'}},
        {"id": "c2", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "pwd", "arguments": "{}"}}]}
    assert m[4] == {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c1", "content": json.dumps({"files": ["a"]})}
    assert m[5]["content"] == "/home" and m[6] == {"role": "assistant", "content": "done"}
    assert out["max_tokens"] == 64 and out["reasoning_effort"] == "high" and out["prompt_cache_key"] == "k"
    assert out["parallel_tool_calls"] is False and out["user"] == "u1" and out["temperature"] == 0.1
    assert out["tools"] == [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "ls", "description": "list", "parameters": {"type": "object"},
                                                              "strict": True}}]
    assert out["tool_choice"] == {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "ls"}}
    assert out["response_format"]["json_schema"] == {"name": "out", "schema": {"type": "object"}, "strict": True}
    assert out["stream_options"] == {"include_usage": True}


def test_string_input_trailing_calls_and_simple_tool_choice():
    out = responses_to_chat({"input": "hi", "reasoning": {"effort": "turbo"}})
    assert out["messages"] == [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}] and "reasoning_effort" not in out
    out = responses_to_chat({"input": [{"type": "function_call", "call_id": "c", "name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}],
                             "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "f"}], "tool_choice": "required"})
    assert out["messages"][-1]["tool_calls"][0]["id"] == "c" and out["tool_choice"] == "required"
    with pytest.raises(ResponsesError, match="previous_response_id"):
        responses_to_chat({"previous_response_id": "resp_1", "input": "x"})


def test_chat_to_responses_tools_and_truncation():
    r = chat_to_responses({"choices": [{"finish_reason": "length", "message": {"content": "partial", "tool_calls": [
        {"function": {"name": "f"}}]}}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 3,
                                                   "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 4}}}, "m")
    assert r["status"] == "incomplete" and r["incomplete_details"] == {"reason": "max_output_tokens"}
    assert [o["type"] for o in r["output"]] == ["message", "function_call"]
    assert r["output"][1]["arguments"] == "{}" and r["output"][1]["call_id"].startswith("call_")
    assert r["usage"]["input_tokens"] == 10 and r["usage"]["input_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 4
    empty = chat_to_responses({}, "m")
    assert empty["output"] == [] and empty["status"] == "completed"


def kinds(events):
    return [e.json()["type"] for e in events if e.json()]


def test_stream_text_tool_text_and_sequence_numbers():
    s = ChatToResponsesStream("m")
    out = []
    for d in [{"choices": [{"delta": {"content": "Look"}}]},
              {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "id": "c1", "function": {"name": "ls", "arguments": '{"a"'}}]}}]},
              {"choices": [{"delta": {"tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": ":1}"}}]}}]},
              {"choices": [{"delta": {"content": "Then"}}]},
              {"choices": [{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "tool_calls"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 5, "completion_tokens": 2}}]:
        out += s.feed(event(d))
    out += s.feed(SSEEvent(data="[DONE]"))
    out += s.feed(SSEEvent(data="[DONE]"))
    k = kinds(out)
    assert k[:2] == ["response.created", "response.in_progress"] and k[-1] == "response.completed"
    assert k.count("response.output_item.added") == 3  # message, function call, second message
    seqs = [e.json()["sequence_number"] for e in out]
    assert seqs == list(range(1, len(seqs) + 1))
    final = out[-1].json()["response"]
    assert [o["type"] for o in final["output"]] == ["message", "function_call", "message"]
    assert final["output"][1]["arguments"] == '{"a":1}' and all(o["status"] == "completed" for o in final["output"])
    assert final["usage"]["total_tokens"] == 7


def test_stream_errors_truncation_and_empty_upstream():
    s = ChatToResponsesStream("m")
    out = s.feed(event({"error": {"type": "rate_limit_error", "message": "slow down"}}))
    assert kinds(out) == ["response.created", "response.in_progress", "error"] and out[-1].json()["code"] == "rate_limit_error"
    assert s.feed(event({"error": "plain"}))[-1].json()["message"] == "plain"
    assert s.feed(SSEEvent(data="")) == []

    t = ChatToResponsesStream("m")
    t.feed(event({"choices": [{"delta": {"content": "x"}, "finish_reason": "length"}]}))
    fin = t.finish_events()
    assert kinds(fin)[-1] == "response.incomplete" and fin[-1].json()["response"]["incomplete_details"]["reason"] == "max_output_tokens"

    quiet = ChatToResponsesStream("m")
    assert kinds(quiet.finish_events()) == ["response.created", "response.in_progress", "response.completed"]
    assert quiet.finish_events() == []


async def test_responses_endpoint_tool_call_round_trip_through_anthropic_backend(client):
    body = {"model": "big", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "use the tool [tool:ls]"}],
            "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "ls", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}]}
    r = await client.post("/v1/responses", json=body, headers=auth())
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["object"] == "response"
    r = await client.post("/v1/responses", json={"model": "big", "input": "x", "previous_response_id": "resp_1"}, headers=auth())
    assert r.status_code == 400 and "previous_response_id" in r.text

  - "Concludes that the recommendation, including the claim of 223 engineers of extra capacity, is not supported by the evidence presented."
reference_answer: |
  1. Self-selected pilot group (section 1). The seven pilot teams volunteered and included all three of last year's
  Delivery Excellence award winners, so they were likely more productive and more engaged before the pilot began. The
  18% gap against the 12 non-volunteer teams could be entirely pre-existing. Fix: compare each group's change from its
  own pre-pilot baseline (difference-in-differences), or randomly assign teams to the pilot.

  2. The productivity metric was gamed by design (section 2). Pilot teams were coached to split work into smaller
  tickets, and their average ticket fell from 5.0 to 3.4 story points while the comparison group stayed at 5.0.
  Counting tickets therefore inflates the pilot's output. In story points the pilot delivered 9.2 x 3.4 = 31.3 points
  per engineer per week against 7.8 x 5.0 = 39.0 for the comparison group, about 20% less, not 18% more. Fix: measure
  output in a unit unaffected by ticket granularity (story points, or completed features or customer outcomes).

  3. Attrition periods don't match (section 3). 2 of 61 over 13 weeks is a quarterly rate of 3.3%, compared with an
  annual company rate of 9%. Annualised, the pilot's rate is roughly 1 - (1 - 0.033)^4, about 12.5% (about 13% if you
  simply multiply by four), which is higher than 9%. And two departures is far too few events to support any
  conclusion. Fix: compare attrition over the same 13-week window for the comparison group (or annualise both), ideally
  over a longer period.

  The measurement process, the shared calendar period, the CSAT comparison and the engagement survey are not flaws as
  presented. Verdict: the recommendation, and with it the claim of 223 engineers of free capacity, is not supported:
  the memo's own numbers are consistent with the four-day week reducing output while attrition is no better.

"""Live data for the control panel (the Dispatch page and friends).

Admins and finance see the whole organization; team leads see their own team.
Users don't get these endpoints (they have /v1/reports/me).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, Request

from .auth import AuthError, Principal
from .config import effort_format
from .store import month_start


def build_router(gateway) -> APIRouter:
    router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1/console", tags=["console"])

    async def principal(request: Request) -> Principal:
        try:
            p = await gateway.authn.authenticate({k.lower(): v for k, v in request.headers.items()})
        except AuthError as e:
            raise HTTPException(e.status, e.message)
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "the control panel is for team leads, finance, and admins")
        return p

    def team_scope(p: Principal) -> str | None:
        return None if p.at_least("finance") else p.team

    @router.get("/overview")
    async def overview(request: Request):
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        today = now.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
        store = gateway.store

        async def totals(start):
            rows = await store.summary(start, tomorrow, "none", team=team)
            return rows[0] if rows else None

        t_today, t_month = await totals(today), await totals(month_start(now))
        teams = [t for t in gateway.cfg.teams if team is None or t.name == team]
        budget = sum(t.budget_usd_month or 0 for t in teams) or None
        elapsed_days = (now - month_start(now)).total_seconds() / 86400
        days_in_month = ((month_start(now) + timedelta(days=32)).replace(day=1) - month_start(now)).days
        month_spend = t_month["actual_cost"] if t_month else 0.0
        health = await gateway.state.backend_health(list(gateway.backends), minutes=5)
        rpm = sum(h["requests"] for h in health.values()) / 5

        def pack(t):
            if not t:
                return {"spend": 0, "baseline": 0, "saved": 0, "requests": 0, "cache_hit_rate": 0}
            prompt = t["input_tokens"] + t["cache_read_tokens"] + t["cache_write_tokens"]
            return {"spend": t["actual_cost"], "baseline": t["baseline_cost"], "saved": t["savings_total"],
                    "requests": t["requests"], "cache_hit_rate": t["cache_read_tokens"] / prompt if prompt else 0,
                    "savings_by_cause": {c: t.get(f"savings_{c}", 0) for c in
                                         ("routing", "caching", "self_hosting", "compression", "response_cache")}}

        return {
            "scope": team or "organization",
            "today": pack(t_today),
            "month": pack(t_month),
            "budget": budget,
            "forecast": month_spend / elapsed_days * days_in_month if elapsed_days > 0.25 else None,
            "requests_per_minute": round(rpm, 1),
            "gateways": await gateway.state.live_gateways(),
            "config_version": gateway.config_version,
        }

    @router.get("/merit")
    async def merit(request: Request, minutes: int = Query(15, ge=1, le=240)):
        """The dispatch stack: models in order of what a token actually cost, widths = tokens served."""
        p = await principal(request)
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        rows = await gateway.store.summary(now - timedelta(minutes=minutes), now + timedelta(seconds=1), "model", team=team_scope(p))
        gpu_models = {m.name for m in gateway.cfg.models for r in m.routes
                      if r.backend in gateway.backends and gateway.backends[r.backend].kind == "self_hosted"
                      and gateway.backends[r.backend].available}
        tiers = []
        for r in rows:
            tokens = r["input_tokens"] + r["cache_read_tokens"] + r["cache_write_tokens"] + r["output_tokens"]
            if tokens <= 0:
                continue
            tiers.append({"model": r["key"], "tokens": tokens, "tokens_per_second": tokens / (minutes * 60),
                          "cost": r["actual_cost"], "price_per_m": r["actual_cost"] / tokens * 1e6,
                          "requests": r["requests"], "gpu": r["key"] in gpu_models})
        tiers.sort(key=lambda t: t["price_per_m"])
        total = sum(t["tokens"] for t in tiers)
        meaningful = [t for t in tiers if total and t["tokens"] / total >= 0.01]
        return {"minutes": minutes, "demand_tokens_per_second": total / (minutes * 60), "tiers": tiers,
                "clearing_price_per_m": meaningful[-1]["price_per_m"] if meaningful else None,
                "blended_price_per_m": sum(t["cost"] for t in tiers) / total * 1e6 if total else None}

    @router.get("/feed")
    async def feed(request: Request, limit: int = Query(60, ge=1, le=500)):
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        events = await gateway.state.recent_events(500 if team else limit)
        if team:
            events = [e for e in events if e.get("team") == team][:limit]
        return {"events": events}

    @router.get("/backends")
    async def backends(request: Request, minutes: int = Query(5, ge=1, le=30)):
        await principal(request)
        names = [b.name for b in gateway.cfg.backends]
        health = await gateway.state.backend_health(names, minutes=minutes)
        now = time.time()
        out = []
        for b in gateway.cfg.backends:
            live = gateway.backends.get(b.name)
            h = health.get(b.name, {})
            n = h.get("requests", 0)
            out.append({
                "name": b.name, "kind": b.kind, "format": b.format, "host": urlparse(b.base_url).hostname if b.base_url else None,
                "enabled": b.enabled, "live": bool(live and live.available), "reason": b.disabled_reason,
                "circuit_open": bool(live and not live.healthy(now)), "draining": bool(live and live.draining),
                "effort_format": effort_format(b),
                "models": sorted({m.name for m in gateway.cfg.models for r in m.routes if r.backend == b.name}),
                "requests": int(n), "errors": int(h.get("errors", 0)),
                "error_rate": h.get("errors", 0) / n if n else 0.0,
                "avg_latency_ms": h.get("latency_ms", 0) / n if n else None,
                "avg_ttft_ms": h.get("ttft_ms", 0) / h["ttft_n"] if h.get("ttft_n") else None,
            })
        return {"minutes": minutes, "backends": out}

    @router.get("/teams")
    async def teams(request: Request):
        """Each team's limits from config next to its spend this month."""
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        start = month_start()
        rows = {r["key"]: r for r in await gateway.store.summary(start, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1), "team", team=team)}
        out = []
        names = [t.name for t in gateway.cfg.teams] + [k for k in rows if k not in {t.name for t in gateway.cfg.teams}]
        for name in names:
            if team is not None and name != team:
                continue
            t = gateway.cfg.team(name)
            r = rows.get(name) or {}
            out.append({"name": name, "configured": any(x.name == name for x in gateway.cfg.teams),
                        "budget_usd_month": t.budget_usd_month, "user_budget_usd_month": t.user_budget_usd_month,
                        "max_session_usd": t.max_session_usd, "rate_limits": t.rate_limits.model_dump(),
                        "baseline_model": t.baseline_model or gateway.cfg.baseline_model,
                        "allowed_models": t.allowed_models, "allowed_backends": t.allowed_backends,
                        "compression": t.compression.enabled, "response_cache": t.response_cache.enabled,
                        "spend": r.get("actual_cost", 0.0), "saved": r.get("savings_total", 0.0), "requests": r.get("requests", 0)})
        return {"teams": out}

    @router.get("/attention")
    async def attention(request: Request):
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        items = []
        health = await gateway.state.backend_health(list(gateway.backends), minutes=5)
        now = time.time()
        for name, b in gateway.backends.items():
            h = health.get(name, {})
            n, errs = h.get("requests", 0), h.get("errors", 0)
            if not b.healthy(now):
                items.append({"level": "critical", "title": f"{name} is failing", "detail": "Circuit open after repeated errors; traffic goes to other backends.", "page": "backends"})
            elif n >= 5 and errs / n >= 0.2:
                items.append({"level": "warning", "title": f"{name}: {errs / n:.0%} errors", "detail": f"{int(errs)} of {int(n)} requests failed in the last 5 minutes.", "page": "backends"})
        start = month_start()
        by_team = {r["key"]: r["actual_cost"] for r in await gateway.store.summary(start, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1), "team", team=team)}
        for t in gateway.cfg.teams:
            if t.budget_usd_month and (team is None or t.name == team):
                used = by_team.get(t.name, 0.0) / t.budget_usd_month
                if used >= 0.8:
                    items.append({"level": "critical" if used >= 1 else "warning", "title": f"Team {t.name} at {used:.0%} of budget",
                                  "detail": f"${by_team.get(t.name, 0):,.2f} of ${t.budget_usd_month:,.0f} this month.", "page": "teams"})
        for b in gateway.cfg.backends:
            if b.kind == "self_hosted" and b.serve is not None and b.enabled:
                rec = await gateway.state.get_json(f"deploy:{b.name}") or {}
                if "failed" in (rec.get("reason") or ""):
                    items.append({"level": "warning", "title": f"GPU deployment {b.name}", "detail": rec["reason"], "page": "gpus"})
        cutoff = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=24)
        for a in await gateway.state.recent_alerts(20):
            try:
                ts = datetime.fromisoformat(a["ts"])
            except (KeyError, ValueError):
                continue
            if ts >= cutoff and (team is None or a.get("team") in (None, team)):
                items.append({"level": a.get("level", "info"), "title": a.get("title", "Alert"), "detail": a.get("text", ""), "page": a.get("page"), "ts": a["ts"]})
        order = {"critical": 0, "warning": 1, "info": 2}
        items.sort(key=lambda i: order.get(i["level"], 3))
        return {"items": items}

    return router

245035cd41b6b194:
"""Sizing a GPU replica to a model, priced from SkyPilot's catalog.

- **What a model needs** comes from Hugging Face: its weights' size in bytes at the precision they're published
  in (safetensors metadata), and for mixture-of-experts models the parameters active per token (its config.json,
  or a name such as "A3B"), which is what sets throughput.
- **What GPUs cost** comes from SkyPilot's catalog, through SkyPilot itself (in its own environment, as the
  controller uses it): on-demand and spot prices for every instance with GPUs, by cloud and region. SkyPilot keeps
  its catalogs current on its own schedule; a refresh downloads them again first. Lookups never use cloud
  credentials (none are needed for prices).
- **A replica** is the setup (GPU type and count, 1-8 on one machine) where the weights fill at most ``FIT`` of the
  GPUs' memory, leaving the rest for the KV cache, at the lowest cost per token when full.
- **Its throughput** is an estimate: a share of the GPUs' peak dense compute, at two operations per active parameter
  per token. Input read from the prompt cache isn't computed again, so it doesn't count against it. A deployment's
  configured ``capacity_tokens_per_second`` (measured) replaces the estimate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger("meritorder.gpu_sizing")

DEFAULT_CLOUDS = ("aws", "gcp", "azure", "lambda", "runpod", "nebius")
HF_API = "https://huggingface.co/api/models/{id}?expand[]=safetensors"
HF_CONFIG = "https://huggingface.co/{id}/resolve/main/config.json"
FIT = 0.7  # the weights may fill this share of the GPUs' memory; the rest is the KV cache's
CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 6  # the report fetches prices again when they're older than this
SIZES_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 24 * 7


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Accelerator:
    memory_gb: float
    bf16_tflops: float  # dense, from the vendor's spec sheet
    fp8_tflops: float | None = None


# Datacenter GPUs vLLM serves on, by SkyPilot's names for them. Peak dense tensor throughput from the spec sheets.
ACCELERATORS = {
    "L4": Accelerator(24, 121, 242),
    "A10G": Accelerator(24, 70),
    "A10": Accelerator(24, 125),
    "L40S": Accelerator(48, 362, 733),
    "A100": Accelerator(40, 312),
    "A100-80GB": Accelerator(80, 312),
    "A100-80GB-SXM": Accelerator(80, 312),
    "H100": Accelerator(80, 989, 1979),
    "H100-SXM": Accelerator(80, 989, 1979),
    "H100-MEGA": Accelerator(80, 989, 1979),
    "H100-NVL": Accelerator(94, 835, 1671),
    "GH200": Accelerator(96, 989, 1979),
    "H200": Accelerator(141, 989, 1979),
    "H200-SXM": Accelerator(141, 989, 1979),
    "B200": Accelerator(180, 2250, 4500),
    "B300": Accelerator(288, 2250, 4500),
    "MI300X": Accelerator(192, 1307, 2615),
}

DTYPE_BYTES = {"F64": 8, "I64": 8, "F32": 4, "I32": 4, "U32": 4, "BF16": 2, "F16": 2, "I16": 2, "U16": 2,
               "F8_E4M3": 1, "F8_E5M2": 1, "I8": 1, "U8": 1, "BOOL": 1}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ what a model needs

def _name_params(hf_id: str) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    """(total, active) parameters from a name like "Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B" or "Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E"."""
    name = hf_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    active = (re.search(r"(?:^|[-_])A(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)B(?![a-z])", name, re.I)  # "...-A52B"
              or re.search(r"(?:^|[-_])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)B-\d+E(?![a-z])", name, re.I))  # "...-17B-128E": 17B active
    totals = [float(m.group(1)) * (1e12 if m.group(2).upper() == "T" else 1e9)
              for m in re.finditer(r"(?:^|[-_])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)([BT])(?![a-z])(?!-\d+E)", name, re.I)]
    return (totals[-1] if totals else None), (float(active.group(1)) * 1e9 if active else None)


def active_from_config(config: dict) -> float | None:
    """Parameters each token goes through in a mixture-of-experts model, from its layer sizes: attention, the experts
    it's routed to plus any shared expert, dense layers, and the output head. None when the config describes no
    experts (a dense model) or not enough to work it out. Counted from the shapes, not the stored weights, which
    for 4-bit experts hold two parameters per byte."""
    c = {**config, **(config.get("text_config") if isinstance(config.get("text_config"), dict) else {})}
    experts = c.get("n_routed_experts") or c.get("num_experts") or c.get("num_local_experts") or c.get("moe_num_experts")
    per_token = c.get("num_experts_per_tok") or c.get("moe_topk") or c.get("num_experts_per_token")
    h, layers = c.get("hidden_size"), c.get("num_hidden_layers")
    width = c.get("moe_intermediate_size") or c.get("intermediate_size")
    if not (experts and per_token and h and layers and width) or experts <= per_token:
        return None
    heads = c.get("num_attention_heads")
    head_dim = c.get("head_dim") or (h // heads if heads else None)
    if heads and head_dim:
        kv = c.get("num_key_value_heads") or heads
        attention = 2 * h * heads * head_dim + 2 * h * kv * head_dim  # q and o, k and v
    else:
        attention = 4 * h * h
    freq = c.get("moe_layer_freq")
    moe_layers = sum(1 for x in freq if x) if isinstance(freq, list) else layers - int(c.get("first_k_dense_replace") or 0)
    dense_width = c.get("dense_intermediate_size") or c.get("intermediate_size") or width
    shared = (c.get("shared_expert_intermediate_size") or c.get("shared_intermediate_size")
              or (int(c.get("n_shared_experts") or 0) * width))
    ffn = moe_layers * (per_token * width + shared) * 3 * h + (layers - moe_layers) * dense_width * 3 * h
    return float(layers * attention + ffn + (c.get("vocab_size") or 0) * h)


def _hf_headers() -> dict:
    token = os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN")
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"} if token else {}


async def _get(client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str) -> httpx.Response:
    """GET from Hugging Face, waiting out a rate limit or a hiccup twice before giving up."""
    for attempt in range(3):
        r = await client.get(url, headers=_hf_headers(), follow_redirects=True)
        if r.status_code not in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) or attempt == 2:
            return r
        await asyncio.sleep(1.0 * (attempt + 1))
    return r


async def fetch_model_size(hf_id: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> dict:
    """{weight_bytes, total_params, active_params, fp8_share, basis}; ``error`` instead when nothing is known."""
    total = weight = fp8 = None
    sixteen = 0
    basis = []
    try:
        r = await _get(client, HF_API.format(id=hf_id))
        st = (r.json().get("safetensors") or {}) if r.status_code == 200 else {}
        params = st.get("parameters") or {}
        if params:
            weight = sum(n * DTYPE_BYTES.get(k, 2) for k, n in params.items())
            fp8 = sum(n for k, n in params.items() if k.startswith("F8")) / max(1, sum(params.values()))
            sixteen = sum(n * 2 for k, n in params.items() if k in ("BF16", "F16"))
            total = float(st.get("total") or sum(params.values()))
            basis.append("weights from Hugging Face")
    except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as e:
        log.debug("%s: model info failed: %s", hf_id, e)
    name_total, name_active = _name_params(hf_id)
    if total is None and name_total:
        total, weight, fp8, sixteen = name_total, name_total * 2, 0.0, name_total * 2
        basis.append("size from its name, at 16 bits")
    if total is None:
        return {"error": "no size published (gated, or no weights on Hugging Face)"}
    active = name_active
    if active:
        basis.append("active parameters from its name")
    else:
        try:
            r = await _get(client, HF_CONFIG.format(id=hf_id))
            if r.status_code == 200:
                moe = active_from_config(r.json())
                active = min(moe, total) if moe else total
                basis.append("active parameters estimated from its config" if moe else "dense")
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as e:
            log.debug("%s: config failed: %s", hf_id, e)
    if not active:
        active = total
        basis.append("assumed dense (no config to read)")
    return {"weight_bytes": int(weight), "sixteen_bit_bytes": int(sixteen), "total_params": int(total), "active_params": int(active),
            "fp8_share": round(fp8 or 0.0, 3), "basis": "; ".join(basis)}


def as_fp8(size: dict) -> dict:
    """The model served with its 16-bit weights quantized to FP8 (vLLM --quantization fp8): half their memory."""
    if "error" in size or not size.get("sixteen_bit_bytes"):
        return size
    weight = size["weight_bytes"] - size["sixteen_bit_bytes"] / 2
    return {**size, "weight_bytes": int(weight), "fp8_share": 1.0, "basis": size["basis"] + "; 16-bit weights served in FP8"}


async def fetch_model_sizes(hf_ids: list[str], client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> dict:
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(8)

    async def one(i: str):
        async with sem:
            return i, await fetch_model_size(i, client)

    return dict(await asyncio.gather(*(one(i) for i in sorted(set(hf_ids)))))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ what GPUs cost

class SkyPilotMissing(RuntimeError):
    pass


async def fetch_catalog(clouds: list[str], refresh: bool = False) -> dict:
    """GPU offers in these clouds from SkyPilot's catalog (see ``gpu.catalog_offers``)."""
    from .gpu import catalog_offers, sky_available

    if not sky_available():
        raise SkyPilotMissing("SkyPilot isn't installed where the gateway runs: build its image with --build-arg SKYPILOT=0.14.2, "
                              "or point MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON at SkyPilot's Python")
    found = await asyncio.to_thread(catalog_offers, clouds, refresh)
    if not found:
        raise RuntimeError("SkyPilot's catalog lookup failed (see the gateway log)")
    return found


def catalog_clouds(cfg) -> list[str]:
    """The clouds to price: SkyPilot deployments' own clouds first, then the common GPU clouds."""
    own = [c.lower() for b in cfg.backends if b.serve and b.serve.provisioner == "skypilot" for c in b.serve.clouds]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(own + list(DEFAULT_CLOUDS)))


async def refresh(cfg, store, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None, sizes: bool = True, download: bool = False,
                  catalog: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Fetch GPU prices from SkyPilot (``download``: its catalogs too, rather than on its own schedule) and, with
    ``sizes``, every open-weight model's size, and keep them in the store."""
    own = client is None
    client = client or httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60, headers={"User-Agent": "merit-order"})
    try:
        now = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        clouds = catalog_clouds(cfg)
        failed: Exception | None = None
        out: dict = {}
        try:
            if catalog:
                found = {**await fetch_catalog(clouds, download), "fetched_at": now, "clouds": clouds}
                await store.set_setting("gpu_catalog", found)
                out = {"catalog": {k: found.get(k) for k in ("fetched_at", "clouds", "catalog_updated", "skypilot")}, "offers": len(found["offers"])}
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (sizes are still worth fetching; the caller hears about it below)
            failed = e
        if sizes:
            ids = [m.hf_id for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat" and m.hf_id]
            found = await fetch_model_sizes(ids, client)
            await store.set_setting("model_sizes", {"fetched_at": now, "models": found})
            out["models"] = len(found)
            out["unsized"] = sorted(i for i, s in found.items() if "error" in s)
        if failed:
            raise failed
        return out
    finally:
        if own:
            await client.aclose()


def _age_hours(stamp: str | None) -> float:
    if not stamp:
        return float("inf")
    return (datetime.now(UTC) - datetime.fromisoformat(stamp)).total_seconds() / 3600


async def current(cfg, store, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """The stored catalog and model sizes, fetched again first when stale or missing (at the time of the report).
    Prices come through SkyPilot where the gateway has it; otherwise the GPU controller publishes them
    (controller.publish_gpu_prices), and a stale catalog is reported as a problem."""
    from .gpu import sky_available

    catalog = await store.get_setting("gpu_catalog") or {}
    sizes = await store.get_setting("model_sizes") or {}
    ids = {m.hf_id for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat" and m.hf_id}
    stale_sizes = _age_hours(sizes.get("fetched_at")) > SIZES_MAX_AGE_HOURS or not ids <= set(sizes.get("models") or {})
    stale_catalog = _age_hours(catalog.get("fetched_at")) > CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS
    here = sky_available()
    problem = None
    if (stale_catalog and here) or stale_sizes:
        try:
            await refresh(cfg, store, client, sizes=stale_sizes, catalog=stale_catalog and here)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (a source that's down: the last prices stand, and the report says how old they are)
            log.warning("GPU prices or model sizes couldn't be fetched: %s", e)
            problem = str(e)
        catalog = await store.get_setting("gpu_catalog") or catalog
        sizes = await store.get_setting("model_sizes") or sizes
    if stale_catalog and not here and not problem:
        problem = ("SkyPilot isn't installed where the gateway runs, so GPU prices come from the GPU controller, which "
                   + ("hasn't published any in the last 6 hours" if catalog.get("fetched_at") else "hasn't published any yet")
                   + ": run it (compose --profile gpu, or controller.enabled in the Helm chart), or install SkyPilot in the gateway's image")
    return {**catalog, "problem": problem} if problem else catalog, sizes


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ a replica for a model

def peak_tflops(acc: Accelerator, fp8_share: float) -> float:
    """Compute per GPU for these weights: FP8 rate when the weights are mostly FP8 and the GPU has it."""
    return acc.fp8_tflops if fp8_share >= 0.5 and acc.fp8_tflops else acc.bf16_tflops


def size_replica(size: dict, offers: list[dict], clouds: set[str], spot: bool, fit: float = FIT,
                 accelerators: str | None = None, regions: list[str] | None = None) -> dict:
    """The replica for a model: the cheapest per hour among the offers in ``clouds`` whose memory holds its weights at
    ``fit``, on 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs (how vLLM splits a model), the faster one on a tie. ``accelerators`` ("H100:4")
    fixes the GPU, as a deployment does. Spot prices where asked for and offered, else on-demand."""
    if "error" in size and not accelerators:
        return {"error": size["error"]}
    need_gb = size.get("weight_bytes", 0) / 1e9 / fit
    want = None
    if accelerators:
        name, _, n = accelerators.partition(":")
        want = (name.upper() if name.upper() in ACCELERATORS else name, int(n or 1))
    best = None
    for o in offers:
        acc = ACCELERATORS.get(o["accelerator"])
        if acc is None or o["cloud"] not in clouds or o["count"] not in (1, 2, 4, 8) \
                or (want and (o["accelerator"].upper(), o["count"]) != (want[0].upper(), want[1])):
            continue
        if not want and acc.memory_gb * o["count"] < need_gb:
            continue
        price, used_spot = (o["spot"], True) if spot and o["spot"] else (o["on_demand"], False)
        if price is None or (regions and price.get("region") not in regions):
            continue
        tflops = peak_tflops(acc, size.get("fp8_share", 0.0)) * o["count"]
        key = (price["usd_per_hour"], -tflops)
        if best is None or key < best[0]:
            best = (key, {"accelerator": o["accelerator"], "count": o["count"], "memory_gb": acc.memory_gb * o["count"], "tflops": tflops,
                          "cloud": o["cloud"], "region": price.get("region"), "instance_type": price.get("instance_type"),
                          "spot": used_spot, "usd_per_hour": price["usd_per_hour"],
                          "on_demand_usd_per_hour": (o["on_demand"] or {}).get("usd_per_hour"),
                          "spot_usd_per_hour": (o["spot"] or {}).get("usd_per_hour")})
    if best is None:
        largest = max((ACCELERATORS[o["accelerator"]].memory_gb * o["count"] for o in offers
                       if o["cloud"] in clouds and o["accelerator"] in ACCELERATORS and o["count"] in (1, 2, 4, 8)), default=0)
        if want:
            return {"error": f"no {accelerators} offer in {', '.join(sorted(clouds))}"}
        return {"error": f"needs {need_gb:,.0f} GB of GPU memory; the largest machine on offer has {largest:,.0f} GB"
                if largest and need_gb > largest else "no offer in the chosen clouds"}
    return best[1]


def capacity_tps(replica: dict, size: dict, efficiency: float, cache_read_share: float) -> float:
    """Estimated tokens per second one replica serves: ``efficiency`` of its peak compute at 2 operations per active
    parameter per token, for the tokens it has to compute (cache reads are served from the prefix cache)."""
    computed = efficiency * replica["tflops"] * 1e12 / (2 * size["active_params"])
    return computed / max(1.0 - cache_read_share, 0.1)


def replica_plans(cfg, catalog: dict, sizes: dict, clouds: set[str], spot: bool, fp8: bool = False,
                  replica_prices: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Per open-weight chat model, the replica its break-even is worked out for: its own deployment's (its GPUs,
    clouds and spot setting, priced from the catalog or at the controller's current price, and its configured
    capacity), else one sized to it. Each is {deployment, replica, size, capacity_tps} or {error}."""
    from .gpu import deployment_for

    offers = catalog.get("offers") or []
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for m in cfg.models:
        if m.kind != "chat" or not m.hf_id:
            continue
        size = (sizes.get("models") or {}).get(m.hf_id) or {"error": "its size hasn't been fetched yet"}
        size = as_fp8(size) if fp8 else size
        dep = deployment_for(cfg, m)
        sized = "error" not in size
        if dep and dep.serve and dep.serve.provisioner == "skypilot":
            s = dep.serve
            replica = size_replica(size, offers, {c.lower() for c in s.clouds} or clouds, s.use_spot, accelerators=s.accelerators,
                                   regions=s.regions or None)
            if "error" in replica:  # not in the catalog: the configured price
                replica = {"accelerator": s.accelerators.partition(":")[0], "count": int(s.accelerators.partition(":")[2] or 1),
                           "usd_per_hour": dep.gpu_cost_per_hour, "spot": s.use_spot, "source": "configured"}
            else:
                replica["source"] = "catalog"
        elif dep:  # a server you run: its configured price
            replica = {"usd_per_hour": dep.gpu_cost_per_hour, "source": "configured"}
        else:
            replica = size_replica(size, offers, clouds, spot)
            if "error" in replica:
                out[m.name] = {"error": replica["error"], "size": size if sized else None}
                continue
            replica["source"] = "catalog"
        if dep and (replica_prices or {}).get(dep.name):  # what the controller is paying, or would
            replica = {**replica, "usd_per_hour": replica_prices[dep.name], "source": "controller"}
        configured = dep.capacity_tokens_per_second if dep and dep.capacity_tokens_per_second else None
        if not replica.get("usd_per_hour") or not (configured or (sized and replica.get("tflops"))):
            out[m.name] = {"error": "no price or capacity for its deployment", "size": size if sized else None}
            continue
        out[m.name] = {"deployment": dep.name if dep else None, "replica": replica, "size": size if sized else None, "capacity_tps": configured}
    return out

# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports. Unknown, revoked, or expired keys get a 401. | Client | Auth | |---|---| | People with harnesses | `meritorder login` → virtual key (above) | | Services / apps | An Entra token directly as the bearer token, or a key from `meritorder keys create` | | Local dev / quickstart | `MERITORDER_DEV_KEY` (static admin key from the environment) | | Google (later) | Another OIDC issuer: same code path | Entra login switches on when `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` are set; map Entra group IDs to teams and roles in `auth.oidc` in the config. SCIM (later) revokes keys when people leave. ## Budgets ```mermaid flowchart TD ORG["Org budget
$/month"] --> T1["Team: platform
$/month"] ORG --> T2["Team: data-science
$/month"] T1 --> U1["User budget"] T1 --> U2["User budget"] T2 --> U3["User budget"] U1 --> K1["Key"] U1 --> K2["Key"] ``` - A request must fit **every** level above it. - Each request **reserves** an estimate up front (Redis counter) and **settles** to actual cost after the response. Postgres is the source of truth; Redis counters are reconciled async. - Soft limit → warn (response header, notification). Hard limit → reject or downgrade to a cheaper model, per team policy. - Policy lives alongside budgets: allowed models, allowed providers, data residency (e.g. "DeepSeek weights only self-hosted or on Bedrock, never the vendor API"). ## Limits that stop runaway spend | Setting (per team) | What it does | |---|---| | `budget_usd_month`, `user_budget_usd_month` | Monthly caps; requests are refused at 100% (alerts at 80%) | | `max_session_usd` | Stops one session (typically an agent stuck in a loop) once it has spent this much | | `rate_limits: {user_rpm, user_tpm, team_rpm, team_tpm}` | Requests and prompt tokens per minute; 429 with `Retry-After` | ## What gets charged | Backend | Charged to the user's budget | |---|---| | API | Actual provider cost (cached / uncached / output tokens) | | Self-hosted | Chargeback: GPU-hour cost split by tokens served (so it's fair, not $0) | Budgets use chargeback; the router uses marginal cost. They answer different questions. ## The savings ledger One row per request, written async: | Field | Example | |---|---| | user, team, session | | | model requested / floor / served | `auto` / `coding:3` / `qwen3-coder-480b` | | backend | `self/qwen3-coder/replica-2` | | tokens: uncached in / cached in / out | 2,100 / 118,000 / 640 | | **actual marginal cost** | $0.0004 | | **chargeback cost** | $0.0090 | | **counterfactual cost** (floor model on API, no proxy caching) | $0.3700 | | upgraded for free? | yes | This is the dashboard that sells the project: *"$X spent, $Y avoided, Z% of requests upgraded at no cost."* How savings are calculated and reported is in [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md).

# 09 — Decisions

What we decided, why, and what would make us revisit it. Newest decisions go at the bottom.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Python for the core | Accepted |
| 2 | Our own backend adapters; no LiteLLM dependency | Accepted |
| 3 | No Envoy | Accepted |
| 4 | Docker Compose and Kubernetes both supported | Accepted |
| 5 | The harness owns the conversation; no content stored | Accepted |
| 6 | Route by marginal cost, including cache rebuild cost | Accepted |
| 7 | SkyPilot for GPUs, provisioning as a plugin | Accepted |
| 8 | Generic OIDC, Entra first | Accepted |
| 9 | Postgres and Redis are the only state | Accepted |
| 10 | Continuous batching only; async batch APIs out of scope | Accepted |
| 11 | AGPL-3.0-only license | Accepted |
| 12 | Reporting UI in React/TypeScript | Accepted |
| 13 | Opt-in response cache may store responses | Accepted |
| 14 | Open-weight catalog with prices from OpenRouter | Accepted |
| 15 | GPU scaling on addressable demand at API prices | Accepted |
| 16 | Deterministic, rule-based compression first | Accepted |
| 17 | Configuration versions in Postgres, YAML as the starting point | Accepted |
| 18 | Control panel in Mantine, monitoring first | Accepted |

## 1. Python for the core

**Why:** The team prefers it, the ML and inference ecosystem (SkyPilot, vLLM, classifiers,
compression) is Python, and gateway overhead is a few milliseconds against model latency measured
in seconds. We scale by running more gateway copies.

**Revisit if:** a real deployment hits gateway CPU limits that more replicas can't fix.

## 2. Our own backend adapters; no LiteLLM dependency

**Why:**
- LiteLLM converts everything to the OpenAI format internally. That's lossy for `cache_control`,
  thinking signatures, and other provider fields, and prompt caching is our biggest savings lever.
- It has had supply-chain incidents, a large dependency tree, and SSO in a commercially licensed
  directory.
- The rest of what it offers (keys, budgets, spend tracking, routing, UI) we'd replace anyway,
  because our ledger, router, and reporting work differently.
- Almost every backend speaks the Anthropic or OpenAI format, so pass-through plus one pair of
  translators covers them in a few thousand lines we fully control.

**What we still take:** LiteLLM's MIT-licensed pricing data, copied in with attribution, and its
code as a reference for provider quirks. Anyone needing a niche provider can run LiteLLM themselves
as an OpenAI-compatible backend.

**Revisit if:** keeping our adapters current with provider API changes becomes a significant
ongoing burden.

## 3. No Envoy

**Why:** Envoy AI Gateway is strong as a proxy layer, but all of our product logic (routing,
shaping, sessions, budgets, ledger) would still be Python, called by Envoy over gRPC on every
request. That adds a second system to operate and debug, assumes Kubernetes, narrows the
contributor pool, and solves a performance problem we don't have. Merit Order runs behind whatever
load balancer or ingress an organization already uses.

**Revisit if:** large deployments ask for it. The routing and shaping code could be packaged as an
Envoy external-processing service without being rewritten. Separately, an optional plugin could use
Kubernetes inference-routing tools (llm-d) inside a customer's own GPU cluster.

## 4. Docker Compose and Kubernetes both supported

**Why:** Compose gives the clone-and-run experience an open-source project needs; Kubernetes is
what enterprises at our target spend run in production. Same images, no Kubernetes-specific code in
the app. Details in [07 — Deployment](07-deployment.md).

## 5. The harness owns the conversation; no content stored

**Why:** Harnesses already resend history and compact it. Storing conversations would make the
proxy a retention, eDiscovery, and breach liability. The gateway stores routing metadata (hashes,
timestamps, backends) only. Compression stays cache-safe through a content-hash map, not stored
conversations.

**Revisit if:** we add the OpenAI Responses API's stored mode, which would be opt-in with explicit
retention.

## 6. Route by marginal cost, including cache rebuild cost

**Why:** A running GPU's spare capacity is already paid for, so it's nearly free, even for a better
model than the task needs. Moving a session re-pays for its whole context, so the router counts that
before moving. Details in [03 — Routing](03-routing.md).

## 7. SkyPilot for GPUs, provisioning as a plugin

**Why:** SkyPilot handles multi-cloud GPUs, spot instances, and replica scaling (SkyServe), and can
target Kubernetes clusters. Our controller decides *whether* to run a model; SkyPilot handles *how*.
A Kubernetes-native option (llm-d or KServe) can be another plugin later.

## 8. Generic OIDC, Entra first

**Why:** Entra is the first customer need; Google and others are configuration on the same code
path. Harnesses get short-lived virtual keys via a device-code login.

## 9. Postgres and Redis are the only state

**Why:** Both are available as managed services everywhere and are easy to run in Compose.
ClickHouse may become an optional reporting backend for very large deployments.

## 10. Continuous batching only; async batch APIs out of scope

**Why:** The product is for day-to-day interactive use. vLLM/SGLang batch concurrent requests on
their own. Provider batch APIs (about 50% off for work that can wait hours) may come later.

## 11. AGPL-3.0-only license

**Why:** Changes that others are offered over a network come back to the project.

## 12. Reporting UI in React/TypeScript

**Why:** Interactive filters and charts are much easier to build well, and the UI only talks to the
reports API, so it stays replaceable. The rest of the project remains Python.

**Alternative considered:** server-rendered pages with htmx (all-Python, clunkier interactivity).

## 13. Opt-in response cache may store responses

**Why:** Exact-match caching saves real money for chatbots, RAG, and evals. It can't work without
keeping the response, so it's the one exception to decision 5: off by default, enabled per team or
per request, scoped to a team or user, and expired by TTL (Redis).

## 14. Open-weight catalog with prices from OpenRouter

**Why:** There are dozens of useful open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, MiMo,
Mistral, Gemma, Nemotron, Muse, gpt-oss) and their prices change often. `config/models-open.yaml`
lists them with their Hugging Face IDs (needed for self-hosting); `meritorder prices refresh` pulls
current prices and context windows from OpenRouter's public catalog into `prices.json`. A route with
no known price is never chosen by `auto`, so a missing price can't look free. OpenRouter is one
backend among many, not the system: it adds a fee, sends prompts through another company, and
doesn't count toward cloud commitments.

## 15. GPU scaling on addressable demand at API prices

**Why:** Counting only traffic already served by a model means a stopped model never looks worth
starting. The controller counts what all traffic the model *could* serve costs at API-equivalent
prices, excluding free upgrades. That number doesn't fall when GPUs take over the traffic, so it
doesn't flap. Two self-hosted models that address the same traffic are each credited with it; the
router then splits the traffic. Revisit if that over-provisions in practice.

## 16. Deterministic, rule-based compression first

**Why:** Compression must give identical output every turn or it breaks provider caching (and, on
recent Claude models, edited history can invalidate thinking). Rules (strip ANSI codes, collapse
repeated lines, keep head and tail of huge outputs) are deterministic, need no stored state, and add
no ML dependency. A model-based compressor (LLMLingua-2) can come later behind a content-hash cache.

## 17. Configuration versions in Postgres, YAML as the starting point

**Why:** Containers mount config read-only, and a fleet of gateways needs one source of truth. Saving
from the console validates the document, stores it as a new version (who, when, why), and every
gateway hot-reloads it within seconds; in-flight requests finish on the objects they started with.
Restore is one click. The YAML file is used until the first version is saved, and stays the format
for import, export, and GitOps. Secrets never enter the database: literal keys are refused and must
stay `${ENV}` references.

## 18. Control panel in Mantine, monitoring first

**Why:** Anyone running a company's LLM traffic through Merit Order will watch it far more than
they reconfigure it. The console opens on a live Dispatch view (the merit-order stack from real
traffic, a live request feed, backend health, the GPU fleet, and what needs attention), with
configuration one page among several. Mantine gives a complete admin component set with few
dependencies; charts stay hand-written SVG.

"""Entra/OIDC tokens: verified against the issuer's keys, mapped to team and role, exchanged for keys.

A local RSA key plays the identity provider; discovery and JWKS fetches are stubbed, so no network.
"""

import base64
import json
import time

import jwt
import pytest
from conftest import auth
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

from meritorder.auth import AuthError, Authenticator, OIDCVerifier
from meritorder.config import OIDCConfig

ISSUER = "https://login.example.com/tenant/v2.0"
CLIENT = "meritorder-client"


def _key():
    return rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)


IDP_KEY, OTHER_KEY = _key(), _key()


def jwk(private, kid):
    d = json.loads(jwt.algorithms.RSAAlgorithm.to_jwk(private.public_key()))
    return {**d, "kid": kid, "use": "sig", "alg": "RS256"}


def token(claims=None, key=IDP_KEY, kid="k1", alg="RS256", **over):
    now = int(time.time())
    body = {"iss": ISSUER, "aud": CLIENT, "iat": now, "nbf": now, "exp": now + 3600, "sub": "sub-1", "oid": "oid-alice",
            "preferred_username": "alice@example.com", "name": "Alice", "groups": ["g-eng"], **(claims or {})}
    for k, v in over.items():
        if v is None:
            body.pop(k, None)
        else:
            body[k] = v
    return jwt.encode(body, key, algorithm=alg, headers={"kid": kid})


@pytest.fixture
def oidc_cfg():
    return OIDCConfig(issuer=ISSUER, client_id=CLIENT, team_from_groups={"g-eng": "eng", "g-ops": "ops"},
                      role_from_groups={"g-leads": "team_lead", "g-admins": "admin"}, default_team="default", key_ttl_days=7)


@pytest.fixture
def idp(monkeypatch):
    """Serve discovery and JWKS (key k1 only) without network."""
    jwks = {"keys": [jwk(IDP_KEY, "k1")]}
    fetched = []

    async def discovery(self):
        return {"issuer": ISSUER, "jwks_uri": "https://login.example.com/keys"}

    def fetch_data(self):
        fetched.append(self.uri)
        return jwks

    monkeypatch.setattr(OIDCVerifier, "discovery", discovery)
    monkeypatch.setattr(jwt.PyJWKClient, "fetch_data", fetch_data)
    return fetched


async def test_valid_token_maps_groups_to_team_and_highest_role(idp, oidc_cfg):
    v = OIDCVerifier(oidc_cfg)
    claims = await v.verify(token({"groups": ["g-other", "g-eng", "g-leads", "g-admins"]}))
    p, email, name = v.principal(claims)
    assert (p.user_id, p.team, p.role, email, name) == ("oid-alice", "eng", "admin", "alice@example.com", "Alice")
    p, _, _ = v.principal({"sub": "s-2", "groups": []})  # no oid: falls back to sub; no groups: defaults
    assert (p.user_id, p.team, p.role) == ("s-2", "default", "user")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", ["expired", "wrong_audience", "wrong_issuer", "forged_signature", "unknown_kid",
                                  "not_yet_valid", "no_exp"])
async def test_bad_tokens_are_rejected(idp, oidc_cfg, case):
    v = OIDCVerifier(oidc_cfg)
    now = int(time.time())
    bad = {
        "expired": lambda: token(exp=now - 10),
        "wrong_audience": lambda: token(aud="someone-else"),
        "wrong_issuer": lambda: token(iss="https://evil.example.com"),
        "forged_signature": lambda: token(key=OTHER_KEY),  # claims kid k1 but signed by another key
        "unknown_kid": lambda: token(kid="k-missing"),
        "not_yet_valid": lambda: token(nbf=now + 600),
        "no_exp": lambda: token(exp=None),  # must not be valid forever
    }[case]()
    with pytest.raises(AuthError) as e:
        await v.verify(bad)
    assert e.value.status == 401 and "invalid identity token" in e.value.message


async def test_algorithm_confusion_is_rejected(idp, oidc_cfg):
    """'none' and HS256-signed-with-the-public-key tokens must never verify."""
    v = OIDCVerifier(oidc_cfg)
    unsigned = jwt.encode({"iss": ISSUER, "aud": CLIENT, "exp": int(time.time()) + 60, "sub": "x"}, None, algorithm="none",
                          headers={"kid": "k1"})
    with pytest.raises(AuthError):
        await v.verify(unsigned)
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization

    pem = IDP_KEY.public_key().public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM, serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo)
    header = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({"alg": "HS256", "kid": "k1", "typ": "JWT"}).encode()).rstrip(b"=")
    payload = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps({"iss": ISSUER, "aud": CLIENT, "exp": int(time.time()) + 60,
                                                   "sub": "x"}).encode()).rstrip(b"=")
    import hashlib
    import hmac

    sig = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hmac.new(pem, header + b"." + payload, hashlib.sha256).digest()).rstrip(b"=")
    with pytest.raises(AuthError):
        await v.verify((header + b"." + payload + b"." + sig).decode())


async def test_bearer_token_through_the_gateway_is_cached_and_follows_the_user_record(idp, oidc_cfg, gateway, client):
    gateway.cfg.auth.oidc = oidc_cfg
    gateway.authn = Authenticator(gateway.cfg, gateway.store)
    tok = token({"groups": ["g-ops"]})
    body = {"model": "small", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}
    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {tok}"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    p = await gateway.authn.authenticate({"authorization": f"Bearer {tok}"})
    assert (p.user_id, p.team) == ("oid-alice", "ops")
    assert len(idp) == 1  # JWKS fetched once, then cached

    # An admin moves Alice; after the per-gateway cache is dropped, her token maps to the new team.
    await gateway.store.upsert_user("oid-alice", "ops", "user")
    await gateway.store.update_user("oid-alice", team="eng")
    gateway.authn.forget_user("oid-alice")
    assert (await gateway.authn.authenticate({"authorization": f"Bearer {tok}"})).team == "eng"
    # Disabled: refused even with a valid token.
    await gateway.store.update_user("oid-alice", disabled=True)
    gateway.authn.forget_user("oid-alice")
    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {tok}"})
    assert r.status_code == 401 and "disabled" in r.text

    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {token(exp=int(time.time()) - 5)}"})
    assert r.status_code == 401


async def test_oidc_cache_never_outlives_the_token(idp, oidc_cfg, gateway):
    gateway.cfg.auth.oidc = oidc_cfg
    authn = Authenticator(gateway.cfg, gateway.store)
    tok = token(exp=int(time.time()) + 5)
    await authn.authenticate({"authorization": f"Bearer {tok}"})
    [(_, until)] = authn._cache.values()
    assert until <= time.time() + 5.5


async def test_exchange_trades_a_token_for_a_short_lived_key(idp, oidc_cfg, gateway, client):
    gateway.cfg.auth.oidc = oidc_cfg
    gateway.authn = Authenticator(gateway.cfg, gateway.store)
    r = await client.post("/auth/exchange", json={"id_token": token({"groups": ["g-eng", "g-leads"]})})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    out = r.json()
    assert out["user"] == "alice@example.com" and out["team"] == "eng"
    user = await gateway.store.get_user("oid-alice")
    assert (user["team"], user["role"], user["email"]) == ("eng", "team_lead", "alice@example.com")
    me = await client.get("/v1/reports/me", headers=auth(out["api_key"]))
    assert me.status_code == 200
    bad = await client.post("/auth/exchange", json={"id_token": token(key=OTHER_KEY)})
    assert bad.status_code == 401
    assert (await client.post("/auth/exchange", json={})).status_code == 401


async def test_exchange_without_oidc_configured(gateway, client):
    r = await client.post("/auth/exchange", json={"id_token": "a.b.c"})
    assert r.status_code == 400 and "not configured" in r.text


async def test_api_key_states(gateway):
    from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

    authn = gateway.authn
    with pytest.raises(AuthError, match="missing API key"):
        await authn.authenticate({})
    with pytest.raises(AuthError, match="invalid API key"):
        await authn.authenticate({"x-api-key": "mo-nope"})
    key_id, secret = await gateway.store.create_key("bob", "default", "user", expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1))
    with pytest.raises(AuthError, match="expired"):
        await authn.authenticate({"x-api-key": secret})
    key_id, secret = await gateway.store.create_key("bob", "default", "user")
    assert (await authn.authenticate({"authorization": f"Bearer {secret}"})).key_id == key_id
    await gateway.store.revoke_key(key_id)
    authn.forget(key_id)
    with pytest.raises(AuthError, match="revoked"):
        await authn.authenticate({"x-api-key": secret})


async def test_bootstrap_admin_key(monkeypatch, gateway):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MERITORDER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_KEY", "mo-bootstrap-123")
    p = await Authenticator(gateway.cfg, gateway.store).authenticate({"x-api-key": "mo-bootstrap-123"})
    assert p.role == "admin" and p.key_id == "static:bootstrap"

def _then(close, release):
    """A stream's close callback that also releases its in-flight slot, exactly once."""
    async def wrapped() -> None:
        try:
            if close is not None:
                await close()
        finally:

NEXT_BACKEND_ON = {401, 403, 404}  # the backend's fault, not the request's: try the next one
