# Merit Order configuration.
#
# Strings support ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Secrets come from the
# environment (see .env.example), never from this file.
#
# Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are switched off automatically,
# so this file works with whatever provider keys you have. Run `meritorder check`
# to see what is usable.
#
# PRICES are live: the worker refreshes them every prices_refresh_minutes (15) from OpenRouter's catalog
# (OpenRouter routes) and the price list LiteLLM maintains (direct provider APIs: Anthropic, OpenAI,
# Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Foundry), long-prompt tiers included, and alerts when one changes or the two
# lists disagree. prices.json is the last refresh. Set `price:` on a route only to override the list,
# e.g. for a negotiated discount; `price_key:` names the model when a route's id isn't its name (an
# Azure deployment). QUALITY scores (1-5) are starting points; measure them with evals (Models → Evals).

# "What you'd use without Merit Order": the counterfactual for savings reports.
baseline_model: claude-sonnet

# Open-weight models, direct vendor APIs, and OpenRouter's free tier.
include:
  - models-open.yaml
  - models-embeddings.yaml

default_max_tokens: 16000

routing:
  auto_model: auto              # clients send model="auto" to let the router choose
  switch_margin_pct: 10         # only move a session if it's this much cheaper (after cache rebuild)
  est_output_tokens: 600
  # Among routes that cost about the same, the faster one wins. cost: only ties (2%); balanced: a faster
  # route may cost 20% more; speed: up to 100% more. Teams (priority:) and X-MeritOrder-Priority override it.
  priority: cost

backends:
  # Keys come from the environment (value_env). In Kubernetes you can also add
  # value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/<NAME> so a rotated key works without a restart
  # (docs/07-deployment.md#secrets). Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure can run keyless on workload identity.
  # --- always available: in-process mocks for trying things out and for tests
  mock-anthropic:
    kind: mock
    format: anthropic
    mock_min_cache_tokens: 1024   # like Anthropic: shorter prompts aren't cached
  mock-openai:
    kind: mock
    format: openai

  # --- Anthropic Messages API family
  anthropic:
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://api.anthropic.com
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}

  bedrock:                      # Claude in Amazon Bedrock (Messages API, SigV4 or bearer token)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_BEDROCK:-true}   # false until the account can use the models (quotas, model access)
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic
    anthropic_version: "2026-10-21"
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}", profile: "${AWS_PROFILE:-}"}

  foundry-claude:               # Claude in Microsoft Foundry
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_FOUNDRY_CLAUDE:-true}   # false until the Claude deployments exist
    format: anthropic
    base_url: ${AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT}/anthropic
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY}

  vertex:                       # Claude on Vertex AI (needs: uv sync --extra gcp; the Docker image has it)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_VERTEX:-true}   # switched off automatically without Google credentials
    format: anthropic
    flavor: vertex
    project: ${GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT}
    region: global
    auth: {type: google}

  vertex-gemini:                # Gemini on Vertex AI, through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint: Google's own prices and quotas
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_VERTEX:-true}
    format: openai
    base_url: https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT}/locations/global/endpoints/openapi
    auth: {type: google}
    effort_format: openai
    price_prefix: "vertex_ai/"

  # --- OpenAI-compatible family
  azure-openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: ${AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT}/openai/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, header: api-key, value_env: AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENAI_API_KEY}
    supports_prompt_cache_key: true
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens
    api: responses                # GPT-5.6 and later take function tools with reasoning only on the Responses API

  openrouter:                   # one key for open-weight and Chinese models (and most others)
    format: openai
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY}

  local-vllm:                   # a vLLM/SGLang server you already run (always used while it's up)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_LOCAL_VLLM:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 8.0          # per replica; used for chargeback and break-even
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 2500
    max_concurrency: 64             # vLLM --max-num-seqs (or what the KV cache fits): saturation seen within seconds
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: static
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      static_url: ${LOCAL_VLLM_URL:-http://localhost:8000/v1}
      min_replicas: 1

  gpu-qwen-coder:               # SkyPilot starts this on cloud GPUs when demand pays for it
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_SKYPILOT:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0         # fallback only: with SkyPilot installed, prices come from its catalog per cloud/region/instance
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000
    max_concurrency: 64             # per replica; at full, requests spill to APIs or wait (max_waiting, default 32)
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: skypilot
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      accelerators: "H100:4"
      use_spot: true
      clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda]
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
      vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144"
      max_replicas: 4
      scale_up_after_minutes: 10
      hold_minutes: 30

models:
  # --- frontier
  claude-fable:                  # Anthropic's most capable tier; priced above Opus, so `auto` only picks it when it scores higher
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-fable-*", "anthropic/claude-fable*", "fable"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 5}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-fable-5-2}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-fable-5-2}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-fable-5-2}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-fable-5-2}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-fable-5.2}

  claude-opus:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-opus-*", "anthropic/claude-opus*", "opus"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 5}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5-5}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-opus-5-5}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-opus-5-5}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-opus-5.5}

  claude-sonnet:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-sonnet-*", "anthropic/claude-sonnet*", "sonnet"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 4}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-sonnet-5-5}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5}

  claude-haiku:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-haiku-*", "anthropic/claude-haiku*", "haiku"]
    quality: {coding: 3, general: 3}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-haiku-5-5}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-haiku-5-5}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-haiku-5-5}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5}

  # OpenAI's tiers, largest first: Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna. Prompts over 272K tokens cost more (a tier in the price list).
  # Older names (gpt-5.6-*) are kept as aliases so clients that ask for them get the current model of the tier.

    effort_levels: [low, medium, high]

    routes:
      - {backend: openai, model: gpt-6-astra}

    effort_levels: [low, medium, high]

import difflib
import random

from solution import PatchError, apply_patch


def _err(original, diff, reverse=False):
    """The hunk number of the PatchError apply_patch raises, or 'no error'."""
    try:
        apply_patch(original, diff, reverse=reverse)
    except PatchError as e:
        assert isinstance(e, Exception)
        return e.hunk
    return "no error"


def _split_lf(text):
    parts = text.split("
")
    return [p + "
" for p in parts[:-1]] + ([parts[-1]] if parts[-1] else [])


def _make_diff(a, b, n):
    """A unified diff of a -> b with n lines of context, with no-newline markers."""
    al, bl = _split_lf(a), _split_lf(b)
    out = ["--- a/file
", "+++ b/file
"]
    for group in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, al, bl, autojunk=False).get_grouped_opcodes(n):
        i1, i2, j1, j2 = group[0][1], group[-1][2], group[0][3], group[-1][4]

        def rng(s, e):
            return f"{s + 1 if e > s else s},{e - s}"

        out.append(f"@@ -{rng(i1, i2)} +{rng(j1, j2)} @@
")

        def emit(prefix, line):
            out.append(prefix + line.rstrip("
") + "
")
            if not line.endswith("
"):
                out.append("\ No newline at end of file
")

        for tag, x1, x2, y1, y2 in group:
            if tag == "equal":
                for ln in al[x1:x2]:
                    emit(" ", ln)
            else:
                for ln in al[x1:x2]:
                    emit("-", ln)
                for ln in bl[y1:y2]:
                    emit("+", ln)
    return "".join(out)

# Merit Order configuration.
#
# Strings support ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Secrets come from the
# environment (see .env.example), never from this file.
#
# Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are switched off automatically,
# so this file works with whatever provider keys you have. Run `meritorder check`
# to see what is usable.
#
# PRICES are dollars per million tokens. Anthropic prices are from published
# rates on 2026-11-09; routes without a price use prices.json, which
# `meritorder prices refresh` updates from OpenRouter's catalog; AWS, Azure, and GCP set their
# own prices and you may have negotiated discounts, so verify before trusting
# the savings numbers. QUALITY scores (1-5) are starting points; tune them with
# your own evals.

# "What you'd use without Merit Order": the counterfactual for savings reports.
baseline_model: claude-sonnet

# Open-weight models, direct vendor APIs, and OpenRouter's free tier.
include:
  - models-open.yaml
  - models-embeddings.yaml

default_max_tokens: 16000

routing:
  auto_model: auto              # clients send model="auto" to let the router choose
  switch_margin_pct: 10         # only move a session if it's this much cheaper (after cache rebuild)
  est_output_tokens: 600

backends:
  # Keys come from the environment (value_env). In Kubernetes you can also add
  # value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/<NAME> so a rotated key works without a restart
  # (docs/07-deployment.md#secrets). Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure can run keyless on workload identity.
  # --- always available: in-process mocks for trying things out and for tests
  mock-anthropic:
    kind: mock
    format: anthropic
  mock-openai:
    kind: mock
    format: openai

  # --- Anthropic Messages API family
  anthropic:
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://api.anthropic.com
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}

  bedrock:                      # Claude in Amazon Bedrock (Messages API, SigV4 or bearer token)
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic
    anthropic_version: "2026-10-21"
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}", profile: "${AWS_PROFILE:-}"}

  foundry-claude:               # Claude in Microsoft Foundry
    format: anthropic
    base_url: ${AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT}/anthropic
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY}

  vertex:                       # Claude on Vertex AI (needs: uv sync --extra gcp)
    enabled: false
    format: anthropic
    flavor: vertex
    project: ${GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT}
    region: global
    auth: {type: google}

  # --- OpenAI-compatible family
  azure-openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: ${AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT}/openai/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, header: api-key, value_env: AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENAI_API_KEY}
    supports_prompt_cache_key: true
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openrouter:                   # one key for open-weight and Chinese models (and most others)
    format: openai
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY}

  local-vllm:                   # a vLLM/SGLang server you already run (always used while it's up)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_LOCAL_VLLM:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 8.0          # per replica; used for chargeback and break-even
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 2500
    max_concurrency: 64             # vLLM --max-num-seqs (or what the KV cache fits): saturation seen within seconds
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: static
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      static_url: ${LOCAL_VLLM_URL:-http://localhost:8000/v1}
      min_replicas: 1

  gpu-qwen-coder:               # SkyPilot starts this on cloud GPUs when demand pays for it
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_SKYPILOT:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0         # fallback only: with SkyPilot installed, prices come from its catalog per cloud/region/instance
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000
    max_concurrency: 64             # per replica; at full, requests spill to APIs or wait (max_waiting, default 32)
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: skypilot
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      accelerators: "H100:4"
      use_spot: true
      clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda]
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
      vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144"
      max_replicas: 4
      scale_up_after_minutes: 10
      hold_minutes: 30

models:
  # --- frontier
  claude-opus:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-opus-*", "anthropic/claude-opus*", "opus"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 5}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}

  claude-sonnet:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-sonnet-*", "anthropic/claude-sonnet*", "sonnet"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 4}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}}

  claude-haiku:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-haiku-*", "anthropic/claude-haiku*", "haiku"]
    quality: {coding: 3, general: 3}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-haiku-5-5, price: {input: 0.10, output: 0.50, cache_read: 0.01, cache_write: 0.125}}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5, price: {input: 0.10, output: 0.50, cache_read: 0.01, cache_write: 0.125}}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-haiku-5-5, price: {input: 0.10, output: 0.50, cache_read: 0.01, cache_write: 0.125}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5, price: {input: 0.10, output: 0.50, cache_read: 0.01, cache_write: 0.125}}

  gpt-terra:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high]
    aliases: ["gpt-5.6-terra*", "openai/gpt-5.6-terra*"]
    quality: {coding: 4, general: 4}
    routes:
      - {backend: openai, model: gpt-5.6-terra, price: {input: 2, output: 12, cache_read: 0.20}}
      - {backend: azure-openai, model: "${AZURE_OPENAI_GPT_DEPLOYMENT:-gpt-5.6-terra}", price: {input: 2, output: 12, cache_read: 0.20}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: openai/gpt-5.6-terra, price: {input: 2, output: 12, cache_read: 0.20}}

  gpt-luna:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high]
    aliases: ["gpt-5.6-luna*", "openai/gpt-5.6-luna*"]
    quality: {coding: 3, general: 3}
    routes:
      - {backend: openai, model: gpt-5.6-luna, price: {input: 0.20, output: 1.20, cache_read: 0.02}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna, price: {input: 0.20, output: 1.20, cache_read: 0.02}}

  # --- mocks (used by `model=auto` only when no real backend is available)
  mock-large:
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 5}
    routes:
      - {backend: mock-anthropic, model: mock-large, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 2.5}}
  mock-small:
    quality: {coding: 3, general: 3}
    routes:
      - {backend: mock-openai, model: mock-small, price: {input: 0.10, output: 0.50, cache_read: 0.01}}

# Hard limits for everyone (also editable on the console's Controls page). Leave a value out for no limit.
safeguards:
  # org_budget_usd_month: 50000     # all LLM spend; requests are refused once reached
  # gpu_budget_usd_month: 20000     # GPU time; GPUs drain and none start once reached
  # max_gpu_usd_per_hour: 100       # whole-fleet burn rate
  # max_gpu_replicas: 8
  max_request_usd: 25               # refuse a single request whose worst case would cost more
  alert_at: [0.8, 1.0]

teams:
  default:
    budget_usd_month: 5000
    user_budget_usd_month: 500

auth:
  static_keys:
    # Development key from the environment. In production, create keys with
    # `meritorder keys create` or use OIDC login.
    - {key_env: MERITORDER_DEV_KEY, user: dev, team: default, role: admin}
  # Entra ID (or any OIDC provider). Switched off while MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER is empty.
  # Entra issuer: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0
  oidc:
    issuer: ${MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER}
    client_id: ${MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID}
    team_from_groups: {}      # {"<entra-group-object-id>": platform}

# 11 — Evals: measuring model quality

`auto` routing sends each request to the cheapest model good enough for it. "Good enough" comes from
each model's **quality scores**: 1–5 per task type (coding, general). The classifier gives every
request a floor (coding:3 for ordinary coding, coding:4 for agent work with many tools, +1 for hard
tasks or large contexts), and only models scoring at least that are considered. Scores that are too
high send hard work to models that can't do it; scores that are too low waste money. Evals measure
them.

## Running one

**From the console:** Models → **Evals** → *Run an eval…*. Pick models and suites, see the
estimated cost, and start it. The worker runs it in the background, against the gateway like any
client. Progress, cost, and every task's result show on the page. When it finishes, *Apply
scores…* writes the measured scores into the configuration as a new version, which you can roll
back from Config → History. *Run again…* repeats a run with the same settings.

**From the command line** (on a machine with Docker, so code tasks run too):

```bash
uv run meritorder eval --models claude-sonnet,claude-opus,claude-fable          # estimates cost, asks first
uv run meritorder eval --models ... --only 'c5-*,a5-*' --repeat 3               # just the hardest coding work, 3 times each
uv run meritorder eval --models ... --apply                                      # also write the scores into the config
```

CLI runs are recorded too, so they appear on the Evals page, and cancelling one there stops it.

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--suite` | `starter,frontier` | Built-in suites, task directories or YAML files, comma-separated |
| `--only` | all tasks | Task id patterns, e.g. `c5-*,g4-*` |
| `--repeat` | 1 | Runs per task. More runs mean less luck in the scores, at proportional cost |
| `--judges` | `claude-opus,gpt-terra` | Models that grade open-ended tasks (those with a live route) |
| `--sandbox` | `docker` | `none` skips tasks that run model-written code |
| `--threshold` | 0.75 | Pass rate a model needs at a level to earn it |

Eval traffic goes through the gateway with its usual budgets, rate limits and per-request cap, and is
tagged `eval=<suite>-<time>` in the ledger. Its spend counts like any other (for the person who ran it,
their team, the models, and the organization), and Reports → Breakdown → **Tag** → `eval` shows each
run's cost on its own line. It isn't counted as savings: a run on Haiku isn't money saved and one on
Fable isn't money lost, because you'd have run those models anyway, so its baseline is the model it
ran. Runs from the console use
a temporary key for the person who started them, revoked when the run ends.

## How each model is run

A comparison is only fair if nothing but the model differs, so a run fixes everything else and records it:

- **No output limit.** Requests set no `max_tokens`, so each model may write as much as it can
  (`max_output_tokens`: 128,000 for current Claude and GPT models), thinking included. A reply that
  fills the model's own maximum fails and is marked *cut off*. The per-request cost limit on Controls
  still applies: if it stops a reply first, the result is *not graded* (left out of the scores) and
  says how many tokens it allowed, so you can raise the limit and run it again. At $40 per million
  output tokens, Fable's full 128,000 costs $5.12.
- **The same effort.** Each task runs at the reasoning effort `auto` uses for its level
  (`routing.effort_by_floor`: low for 1–2, medium for 3, high for 4–5), not at each model's own
  default, which differs (Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium, Fable and Sonnet to high).
  A model that doesn't take that effort runs at its default. A task can set its own (`effort: max`).
- **One route per model.** Each model runs on its first live route, which in the shipped config is
  its own provider's API, rather than whichever reseller the router finds cheapest or fastest that
  minute. Judges too.
- **Each model in its own API.** Agent tasks talk to Claude over Anthropic's Messages API, the way
  Claude Code does, sending each reply back unchanged so Claude's thinking carries from one tool call
  to the next (Chat Completions has nowhere to put it, so it would be lost). Other models use Chat
  Completions; Gemini's reasoning details go back with each turn's tool results.
- **Answers are kept.** Each result keeps what the model wrote (the first 60,000 characters), an
  agent's tool calls in order, and each judge's verdict and reason on every rubric point. Click a
  result on the Evals page to read them, for instance to see which judge was right when they
  disagree.

Long replies take a while: 100,000 tokens is 15–20 minutes on the largest models. The gateway streams
from the provider meanwhile, so nothing times out.

## The suites

| Suite | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `starter` | 24 short tasks, levels 1–5: facts, arithmetic, one tool call, small code questions. Cheap; strong models max it out |
| `frontier` | 32 hard tasks at levels 3–5, built so strong models separate from the very top: 12 code tasks with 14–48 hidden tests each (an interpreter with tail calls, a regex engine matching Python's, unified diffs, recurrence rules, cron, a streaming JSON tokenizer…), 6 multi-step tool tasks (fixing bugs in small repositories, a purchase with traps, revenue from a messy database, an incident's root cause), and 14 general tasks (multi-hop questions over documents of 6k–45k words, logic grids, exact combinatorics, writing under constraints, and 3 judged pieces of open-ended work) |

Levels mean what the classifier means by them: 3 is ordinary coding, analysis or long context;
4 is agent work with many tools, or hard reasoning; 5 is the hardest of both.

## Four kinds of task

| Kind | The model gets | Graded by |
|---|---|---|
| `answer` | One prompt | Mechanical checks: an exact final answer (`Final answer: …`), a number, JSON fields, a tool call, or writing constraints (word count, bullets, required phrases) |
| `code` | A precise spec for a Python module | Hidden unit tests, run against its code in a sandbox. Every test must pass |
| `agent` | A goal and tools | A scripted environment answers the tools (a small repository, a booking API, a database, logs), then checks the end state: the right fix with stricter hidden tests, the right booking made once, the exact figure |
| `judged` | Open-ended work (a summary, a critique, a recommendation) | Two judge models from different families, against a rubric of concrete statements and a reference answer. Both must agree every point is met |

**Why two judges from different families.** A model tends to rate answers like its own higher. The
judges don't know which model wrote the answer, every criterion is a checkable statement ("states
the outage lasted 47 minutes"), and an answer passes only if a Claude judge and a GPT judge both say
every criterion is met. Their reasons are kept with the result. Everything else is graded
mechanically, which is cheaper and repeatable.

**The sandbox.** Model-written code runs in a throwaway Docker container (`python:3.12-slim`):
no network, a read-only filesystem apart from a small `/tmp`, an unprivileged user, no
capabilities, and limits on memory, CPU, processes and time. Each hidden test also has its own
CPU-time limit (10 s), so one runaway loop fails that test, not the whole task. A task can forbid
imports (the regex task forbids `re`); that's checked in the code's syntax tree, which keeps honest
solutions honest but wouldn't stop code written to get around it. Without Docker, those tasks are skipped
and the results say so. The worker in the Docker Compose stack has no Docker access by default, so
console runs skip code tasks there: run those with `meritorder eval` on a machine with Docker, and
their results land on the same page. (Giving a container the Docker socket gives it control of the
host, so it isn't on by default.)

## From results to scores

For each model and task type:

- **Score** (what routing uses): the highest level L where the model passes at least 75% of tasks at
  L **and every level below**. A model that aces level 5 but fails level 3 scores 2.
- **Ability** (0–5, shown next to it): the sum of its pass rates by level. Two models with the same
  score can differ a lot here; it's the finer view. A level the suite doesn't cover counts as the
  level below it did.
- **?**: at some level, there were too few task runs to be sure which side of 75% the model is on
  (its 90% confidence interval straddles 75%). Run again with `--repeat` to firm it up.

Beside the scores, each model shows what its tasks took, because two models that pass the same tasks
can still differ a lot in time and money:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Median time** (and 90th percentile) | The model's own time to complete a task: every request it answered, without grading, judges or the environment's tools |
| **Turns / tools** | Average requests and tool calls per task. An agent that needs 20 turns where another needs 6 is slower and costs more even at the same price per token |
| **Output** | Average output tokens per task, thinking included |
| **Per solve** | Cost divided by tasks passed: what a solved task costs on this model, which is what matters when choosing one |
| **Cut off** | Replies that hit an output limit |

Runs that say nothing about quality are skipped and don't count: no sandbox, no judges, a judge that
failed to give a verdict, a provider's rate limit or outage (HTTP 429 or 5xx), or a reply the
per-request cost limit stopped. Run again to fill them in. Other errors (a reply that fills the
model's maximum output or its context window, a request the model rejects) count as fails.

## Writing your own tasks

The best suite is made from your own work: a model that's good at public puzzles may still be wrong
for your codebase. A suite is a directory of task directories (or a YAML file of `answer` tasks).

```yaml
# my-suite/c4-invoice-rounding/task.yaml
id: c4-invoice-rounding
task: coding          # or general
level: 4
kind: code            # answer | code | agent | judged
prompt_file: prompt.md
code: {tests: tests.py, timeout: 30}   # hidden tests: top-level test_* functions; forbid: [re] bans imports
reference: reference.py                                    # a correct solution, never sent to models
```

- `answer`: `prompt` and `checks` (see `src/meritorder/evals/runner.py` → `grade`). Ask for
  `Final answer: …` on the last line and check it with `final`, `final_number` or `final_one_of`.
- `agent`: `env: module:Class`, `env_args`, `max_turns`. Environments subclass
  `meritorder.evals.envs.Env`: tools, `call`, and `grade`.
- `judged`: `rubric` (concrete statements) and `reference_answer`.
- Generated prompts (long documents built from a seed): `generate: module:function` with
  `generate_args`.
- Optional on any task: `effort` (instead of the level's) and `max_tokens` (only if you want the
  task to have a limit; built-in tasks don't).

Run it with `meritorder eval --suite ./my-suite`, or alongside the built-in ones:
`--suite starter,frontier,./my-suite`. Check every task offline before trusting it: the repository's
`tests/evals/` shows how (reference solutions pass the hidden tests, deliberately wrong ones fail).

**Public tasks leak.** Anything in a public repository can end up in a model's training data, which
makes it easier than it looks. Keep a private suite for the decisions that matter, and refresh it.

## Cost

The estimate before a run counts each task's prompt and a typical reply for every model, and
judging. Reasoning models often write several times more than that, and with no output limit a hard
task can run to tens of thousands of tokens, so treat it as a rough guide.
Long-document and agent tasks dominate: a level-5 document task sends about 60k tokens, and an agent
task resends its growing conversation every turn. Organization and personal budgets and the
per-request cap (Controls) apply to eval traffic like any other.

Strings in the YAML may reference environment variables as ``${NAME}`` or
``${NAME:-default}``. Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are
disabled automatically, so one config file works with whatever keys you have.

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import logging
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal

import yaml
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

from .compression import CompressionConfig
from .response_cache import ResponseCacheConfig

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

Role = Literal["user", "team_lead", "finance", "admin"]
Priority = Literal["cost", "balanced", "speed"]
PRIORITIES = ("cost", "balanced", "speed")


class PriceTier(BaseModel):
    """Prices for requests whose prompt is longer than ``above`` tokens (e.g. Claude Haiku 5.5 above 100K,
    OpenAI's GPT-6.x above 272K). Dollars per million tokens."""

    above: int
    input: float
    output: float
    cache_read: float | None = None
    cache_write: float | None = None


class Price(BaseModel):
    """Dollars per million tokens."""

    input: float = 0.0
    output: float = 0.0
    cache_read: float | None = None  # default: 0.1 x input
    cache_write: float | None = None  # default: input (no write premium)
    # Server-side tools billed per call, on top of tokens: Anthropic web search is $10 per 1,000.
    # (Web fetch adds only tokens. Code-execution container time isn't modeled.)
    web_search_per_1k: float = 10.0
    tiers: list[PriceTier] = []  # long-prompt prices, which replace the ones above when they apply
    # Where the price came from: "openrouter" or "litellm" (live lists, refreshed by the worker), or "config"
    # (written into the configuration: an override such as a negotiated discount, or a price no list has).
    source: str | None = None

    def read(self) -> float:
        return self.cache_read if self.cache_read is not None else self.input * 0.1

    def write(self) -> float:
        return self.cache_write if self.cache_write is not None else self.input

    def at(self, prompt_tokens: int) -> "Price":
        """The price for a request with this many prompt tokens (cached ones included), long-context tiers applied."""
        tier = max((t for t in self.tiers if prompt_tokens > t.above), key=lambda t: t.above, default=None)
        if tier is None:
            return self
        return self.model_copy(update={"input": tier.input, "output": tier.output, "tiers": [],
                                       "cache_read": tier.cache_read if tier.cache_read is not None else (
                                           None if self.cache_read is None else self.cache_read * tier.input / self.input if self.input else None),
                                       "cache_write": tier.cache_write if tier.cache_write is not None else (
                                           None if self.cache_write is None else self.cache_write * tier.input / self.input if self.input else None)})


class BackendAuth(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["none", "api_key", "aws_sigv4", "azure_ad", "google"] = "none"
    header: str = "authorization"  # api_key: header to put the key in
    prefix: str | None = None  # api_key: defaults to "Bearer " for the authorization header
    value_env: str | None = None  # api_key: env var holding the key
    # api_key: file holding the key (e.g. a mounted Kubernetes Secret). Re-read when it changes, so a
    # rotated key takes effect without a restart. Falls back to value_env if the file is missing or empty.
    value_file: str | None = None
    value: str | None = None  # api_key: literal key (prefer value_env)
    service: str | None = None  # aws_sigv4
    region: str | None = None  # aws_sigv4
    profile: str | None = None  # aws_sigv4
    scope: str | None = None  # azure_ad

    def key(self) -> str | None:
        if self.value:
            return self.value
        if self.value_file:
            key = read_secret_file(self.value_file)
            if key:
                return key
        if self.value_env:
            return os.environ.get(self.value_env) or None
        return None

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """Where the key is expected, for "not set" messages."""
        where = [w for w in (self.value_file, self.value_env) if w]
        return " or ".join(where) or "api key"


_SECRET_FILES: dict[str, tuple[tuple[int, int], str | None]] = {}


def read_secret_file(path: str) -> str | None:
    """The file's contents, stripped; cached until its modification time or size changes.

    Kubernetes updates a mounted Secret by swapping a symlink, so ``stat`` (which follows it) sees the change.
    """
    try:
        st = os.stat(path)
    except OSError:
        _SECRET_FILES.pop(path, None)
        return None
    sig = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
    cached = _SECRET_FILES.get(path)
    if cached and cached[0] == sig:
        return cached[1]
    try:
        value = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() or None
    except OSError:
        value = None
    _SECRET_FILES[path] = (sig, value)
    return value

class BackendConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str = ""
    enabled: bool = True
    kind: Literal["api", "self_hosted", "mock"] = "api"
    format: Literal["anthropic", "openai"]
    base_url: str = ""
    auth: BackendAuth = BackendAuth()
    flavor: Literal["standard", "vertex"] = "standard"
    project: str | None = None  # vertex
    region: str | None = None  # vertex
    anthropic_version: str | None = None  # force this anthropic-version header
    forward_anthropic_beta: bool = True
    # With forwarding on: None forwards every beta the client sends; a list forwards only those (prefix
    # match). Some betas change pricing (e.g. 1M-token context) in ways Merit Order's cost model doesn't track.
    anthropic_betas: list[str] | None = None
    supports_prompt_cache_key: bool = False
    # How this backend takes reasoning effort: anthropic -> output_config.effort, openai -> reasoning_effort,
    # openrouter -> reasoning.effort, none -> never sent. "auto" picks from the format and URL.
    effort_format: Literal["auto", "anthropic", "openai", "openrouter", "none"] = "auto"
    max_tokens_field: str = "max_tokens"
    # Where this backend's live prices come from: "openrouter" (OpenRouter's catalog), "litellm" (the price list
    # LiteLLM maintains, for direct provider APIs), or "none" (self-hosted, priced by the GPU hour). "auto" picks
    # from the URL. price_prefix is the provider's prefix in LiteLLM's list (e.g. "vertex_ai/"); None picks it.
    price_source: Literal["auto", "openrouter", "litellm", "none"] = "auto"
    price_prefix: str | None = None
    # OpenAI format only: which endpoint to call. "responses" sends Chat Completions requests to /responses
    # (needed for function tools with reasoning on OpenAI's GPT-5.6 models) and converts the replies back.
    api: Literal["chat", "responses"] = "chat"
    # What a request cost: "reported" uses the amount the backend bills and returns with the response
    # (OpenRouter's usage.cost, which reflects whichever provider it picked); "catalog" prices the tokens
    # from the catalog. "auto" picks reported for OpenRouter and catalog otherwise.
    billed_cost: Literal["auto", "reported", "catalog"] = "auto"
    cache_ttl_seconds: int = 300
    timeout_seconds: float = 600.0
    # Streams only: give up on this backend (and try the next one) if it hasn't started answering by then: response
    # headers plus the first event (not the first token, so slow reasoning models are fine). None: wait timeout_seconds.
    # Default 120 s for APIs; off for self-hosted GPUs, where a request may wait in vLLM's queue on purpose.
    first_byte_timeout_seconds: float | None = Field(default=120.0, gt=0)

    def first_byte_timeout(self) -> float | None:
        if self.kind == "self_hosted" and "first_byte_timeout_seconds" not in self.model_fields_set:
            return None
        return self.first_byte_timeout_seconds
    extra_headers: dict[str, str] = {}
    # self-hosted economics
    gpu_cost_per_hour: float = 0.0  # per replica
    capacity_tokens_per_second: float = 2000.0  # per replica, measured at your latency target
    # Requests one replica runs at once (vLLM --max-num-seqs, or what its KV cache fits). When set, gateways
    # count their in-flight requests and treat the backend as saturated at this many per replica, within
    # seconds, instead of waiting for the controller's next metrics sample.
    max_concurrency: int | None = None
    # When this backend is saturated and no other route can take a request, the request still goes here and
    # waits in vLLM's queue, up to this many waiting per replica. Beyond that the gateway answers 503.
    max_waiting: int = 32
    serve: ServeConfig | None = None  # set: the controller provisions this backend on demand
    disabled_reason: str | None = None  # set at load time when credentials or URL are missing
    # mock
    mock_latency_ms: int = 15
    mock_min_cache_tokens: int = 0  # prompts shorter than this aren't cached (Anthropic: 1024 on most models)

    price_key: str | None = None

    @property
    def priced(self) -> bool:
        return self.price is not None

class ModelConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str = ""
    kind: Literal["chat", "embedding"] = "chat"
    aliases: list[str] = []
    # 1-5 per task type (decimals allowed). Used with `quality.source: config`, or until a live source has been
    # fetched; once it has, a task type it doesn't cover scores 0 and `auto` won't pick the model for it.
    # quality_override always wins.
    quality: dict[str, float] = {}
    quality_override: dict[str, float] = {}
    benchmark_name: str | None = None  # the model's name in benchmark data, when its route ids don't match it
    quality_sources: dict[str, str] = {}  # set when loaded: where each score came from (epoch, artificial_analysis, config, override)
    hf_id: str | None = None  # Hugging Face repo, used when self-hosting the weights
    context_window: int | None = None  # tokens; filled from prices.json when not set
    # The most output (thinking plus reply) the model can write in one response; filled from prices.json when not set.
    # Requests that don't set max_tokens get this, so nothing is cut short by a limit the model doesn't have.
    max_output_tokens: int | None = None
    effort_levels: list[str] = []  # reasoning effort levels the model accepts; empty = don't set effort
    license: str | None = None
    routes: list[Route]

    def matches(self, requested: str) -> bool:
        if requested == self.name:
            return True
        return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(requested, pattern) for pattern in self.aliases)

    def q(self, task: str) -> float:
        return self.quality.get(task, self.quality.get("general", 0))


class QualityConfig(BaseModel):
    """Where `auto` gets each model's quality scores (see quality_data.py)."""

    # epoch: Epoch AI's benchmark data; artificial_analysis: the AA Intelligence Index (ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY);
    # config: the scores written in each model's `quality` (or applied from eval runs).
    source: Literal["epoch", "artificial_analysis", "config"] = "epoch"
    # best: 5 x a model's results / the best configured model's (the best is 5; adding a weak model changes nothing).
    # range: the weakest configured model with data is 1, the best 5.
    scale: Literal["best", "range"] = "best"
    refresh_hours: float = Field(default=24.0, gt=0)
    # Epoch: per task type, the benchmark whose difficulty scores are measured against (a model's chance of solving a
    # task that hard), and the benchmarks whose results show a model's strength at that kind of work.
    # FrontierSWE for both: hard enough that Fable 5.2 solves 70% and Haiku 5.5 44%, so the scale spreads
    # models out, while ordinary work (level 3) still goes to models like Sonnet. A harder reference spreads them more.
    reference: dict[str, str] = {"coding": "FrontierSWE", "general": "FrontierSWE"}
    evidence: dict[str, list[str]] = {"coding": ["FrontierSWE", "FrontierCode"], "general": []}
    # Older benchmarks of the kind, used only for a model with no evidence and no ECI (some open models): they predict
    # FrontierSWE/FrontierCode results no better than the ECI, so they never replace it.
    fallback: dict[str, list[str]] = {"coding": ["Terminal Bench", "GSO-Bench", "MirrorCode"], "general": []}

    name: str = ""

    budget_usd_month: float | None = None
    user_budget_usd_month: float | None = None  # default monthly limit for each person; a person's own limit replaces it
    max_session_usd: float | None = None  # stop a single session (e.g. an agent in a loop) at this spend
    refusal_fallback: bool = True  # `auto` requests a model refuses are retried on the next eligible model
    # A request naming a model that has nowhere to run (e.g. its GPUs are stopped) goes to a model at least as
    # good for the task instead of failing. Off by default: a different model can behave differently with tools.
    substitute_unavailable: bool = False
    priority: Priority | None = None  # cost, balanced or speed; unset uses routing.priority
    baseline_model: str | None = None
    allowed_models: list[str] = ["*"]
    allowed_backends: list[str] = ["*"]

    def allows_model(self, model: str) -> bool:
        return _allowed(model, self.allowed_models)

    def allows_backend(self, backend: str) -> bool:
        return _allowed(backend, self.allowed_backends)


def _allowed(name: str, patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Glob allow-list with ``!pattern`` exclusions, e.g. ["*", "!openrouter-free", "!deepseek"]."""
    if any(p.startswith("!") and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, p[1:]) for p in patterns):
        return False
    return any(not p.startswith("!") and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, p) for p in patterns)

class RoutingConfig(BaseModel):
    auto_model: str = "auto"
    switch_margin_pct: float = 10.0
    switch_margin_usd: float = 0.01
    est_output_tokens: int = 600
    est_new_tokens_per_turn: int = 2000
    min_expected_turns: int = 3
    max_expected_turns: int = 30
    shadow_knee: float = 0.6  # self-hosted utilization where the shadow price starts rising
    shadow_floor: float = 0.02  # shadow price below the knee, as a fraction of API price
    max_attempts: int = 3
    # Reasoning effort for `auto` requests by quality-floor level (levels not listed keep the model default).
    # Set for every level so a model runs the same way whichever it is (Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium,
    # most others to high), and evals measure each level at the effort it's served with.
    effort_by_floor: dict[int, str] = {1: "low", 2: "low", 3: "medium", 4: "high", 5: "high"}
    # The highest level `auto` gives a Claude Code request of each class (the x-claude-code-request-class header).
    # Side requests (session titles, summaries, permission checks) are small jobs; a compaction summary needs a
    # capable model, not the conversation's top level. Classes not listed (main, subagent, workflow) aren't capped.
    request_class_levels: dict[str, int] = {"auxiliary": 1, "compaction": 3}
    # What decides among routes that cost about the same. Each priority is how much more (%) a route may cost
    # than the cheapest and still win by being faster: `cost` only breaks ties, `speed` pays up to double.
    # Teams (`priority`) and requests (X-MeritOrder-Priority) can choose another one.
    priority: Priority = "cost"
    priority_premium_pct: dict[str, float] = {"cost": 2.0, "balanced": 20.0, "speed": 100.0}
    # Every Nth new session can go to a route within that range whose speed is unknown or out of date, so
    # the router keeps measuring the alternatives. 0 never does.
    speed_check_every: int = Field(default=10, ge=0)

    @field_validator("request_class_levels")
    @classmethod
    def _class_levels(cls, v: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
        bad = {k: n for k, n in v.items() if not 1 <= int(n) <= 5}
        if bad:
            raise ValueError(f"request class levels must be 1-5: {bad}")
        return {k.lower(): int(n) for k, n in v.items()}

    @field_validator("priority_premium_pct", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _all_priorities(cls, v):
        """A partial map (just `balanced: 30`) keeps the other defaults."""
        merged = {"cost": 2.0, "balanced": 20.0, "speed": 100.0, **(v or {})}
        unknown = set(merged) - set(PRIORITIES)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown priorities {sorted(unknown)}; use {', '.join(PRIORITIES)}")
        if any(float(x) < 0 for x in merged.values()):
            raise ValueError("a priority's premium can't be negative")
        return merged


class Safeguards(BaseModel):
    """Organization-wide hard limits. They apply to everyone, including admin pins on GPUs."""

    org_budget_usd_month: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)  # all ledger spend; requests are refused once reached
    gpu_budget_usd_month: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)  # GPU time; GPUs drain and none start once reached
    max_gpu_usd_per_hour: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)  # whole fleet burn rate
    max_gpu_replicas: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)  # across all deployments
    max_request_usd: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)  # refuse a request whose worst case would cost more
    alert_at: list[float] = [0.8, 1.0]  # alert when org or GPU spend crosses these fractions of its budget

    @field_validator("org_budget_usd_month", "gpu_budget_usd_month", "max_gpu_usd_per_hour", "max_gpu_replicas", "max_request_usd",
                     mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _unset_when_blank(cls, v):
        """``${MERITORDER_ORG_BUDGET_USD:-}`` with the variable unset or empty means no limit, not an error."""
        return None if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip() else v


class Config(BaseModel):
    backends: list[BackendConfig]
    models: list[ModelConfig]
    teams: list[TeamConfig] = Field(default_factory=lambda: [TeamConfig(name="default")])
    baseline_model: str | None = None
    auth: AuthConfig = AuthConfig()
    routing: RoutingConfig = RoutingConfig()
    safeguards: Safeguards = Safeguards()
    quality: QualityConfig = QualityConfig()
    # Only for models whose output limit isn't known (max_output_tokens unset and not in prices.json): what to
    # send to Anthropic-format backends, which require a limit, when the client doesn't set one.
    default_max_tokens: int = 16000
    prices_file: str = "prices.json"
    # How often the worker refreshes prices from the live lists. Routing compares prices on every request, so
    # they must be current; a refresh that changes nothing changes nothing.
    prices_refresh_minutes: float = Field(default=15.0, gt=0)
    config_dir: str = "."

    def team(self, name: str) -> TeamConfig:
        for t in self.teams:
            if t.name == name:
                return t
        for t in self.teams:
            if t.name == "default":
                return t
        return TeamConfig(name=name)

    def model(self, name: str | None) -> ModelConfig | None:
        if not name:
            return None
        for m in self.models:
            if m.name == name:
                return m
        for m in self.models:
            if m.matches(name):
                return m
        return None

    def backend(self, name: str) -> BackendConfig | None:
        for b in self.backends:
            if b.name == name:
                return b
        return None


_ENV_RE = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(?::-([^}]*))?\}")


def _interpolate(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return _ENV_RE.sub(lambda m: os.environ.get(m.group(1)) or (m.group(2) or ""), value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_interpolate(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: _interpolate(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    return value


def _named(section: Any) -> list[dict]:
    """Accept either a mapping of name -> settings or a list of settings with names."""
    if section is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(section, dict):
        return [{**(v or {}), "name": k} for k, v in section.items()]
    return list(section)


def default_config_path() -> Path:
    env = os.environ.get("MERITORDER_CONFIG")
    if env:
        return Path(env)
    for candidate in (Path("meritorder.yaml"), Path("config/meritorder.yaml")):
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    return Path("config/meritorder.yaml")


def _load_raw(path: Path, seen: set[Path]) -> dict:
    """Read one YAML file plus anything it lists under ``include:`` (merged in order)."""
    path = path.resolve()
    if path in seen:
        return {}
    seen.add(path)
    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}
    merged: dict = {}
    for inc in raw.pop("include", None) or []:
        sub = _load_raw((path.parent / inc), seen)
        for section in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
            if section in sub:
                merged.setdefault(section, {}).update(_as_mapping(sub[section]))
        for k, v in sub.items():
            if k not in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
                merged.setdefault(k, v)
    for section in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
        if section in raw:
            merged.setdefault(section, {}).update(_as_mapping(raw[section]))
    for k, v in raw.items():
        if k not in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
            merged[k] = v
    return merged


def _as_mapping(section: Any) -> dict:
    if isinstance(section, dict):
        return section
    return {item["name"]: item for item in section or []}


def parse_prices(data: dict) -> tuple[dict[str, Price], dict[str, int], set[str], dict[str, int]]:
    """prices.json: route prices, context windows, models that take a reasoning effort, and output limits."""
    prices = {k: Price.model_validate(v) for k, v in (data.get("prices") or {}).items()}
    return (prices, {k: int(v) for k, v in (data.get("context") or {}).items()}, set(data.get("reasoning") or []),
            {k: int(v) for k, v in (data.get("max_output") or {}).items()})


def load_catalog(path: Path) -> dict:
    """prices.json: the live catalog (prices, limits, and the `quality` section), as last refreshed."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}
    return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}


def load_prices(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Price], dict[str, int], set[str], dict[str, int]]:
    return parse_prices(load_catalog(path))


def apply_quality(cfg: "Config", catalog: dict) -> None:
    """Each model's quality: the live source's scores where it has them (if it's the configured source and scale);
    quality_override always wins. A task type the live source doesn't cover gets 0 ("unmeasured"): `auto` won't pick
    the model for it on a score nobody measured, though requests that name it still work. Without live data at all
    (never fetched), the configured scores stand. Records where each came from in ``quality_sources``."""
    section = catalog.get("quality") or {}
    same = section.get("source") == cfg.quality.source and section.get("scale") == cfg.quality.scale
    live = (section.get("scores") or {}) if cfg.quality.source != "config" and same else {}
    mock = {b.name for b in cfg.backends if b.kind == "mock"}
    for m in cfg.models:
        m.quality_sources = {t: "config" for t in m.quality}
        if live and m.kind == "chat" and not all(r.backend in mock for r in m.routes):
            for task in list(m.quality):
                if task not in (live.get(m.name) or {}):
                    m.quality[task] = 0.0
                    m.quality_sources[task] = "unmeasured"
        for task, v in (live.get(m.name) or {}).items():
            m.quality[task] = float(v)
            m.quality_sources[task] = cfg.quality.source
        for task, v in m.quality_override.items():
            m.quality[task] = float(v)
            m.quality_sources[task] = "override"


def effort_format(b: "BackendConfig") -> str:
    if b.effort_format != "auto":
        return b.effort_format
    if b.format == "anthropic":
        return "anthropic"
    host = b.base_url.lower()
    if "openrouter.ai" in host:
        return "openrouter"
    if "api.openai.com" in host or ".openai.azure.com" in host:
        return "openai"
    return "none"


def uses_reported_cost(b: "BackendConfig") -> bool:
    if b.billed_cost != "auto":
        return b.billed_cost == "reported"
    return b.kind == "api" and "openrouter.ai" in b.base_url.lower()


def load_raw_config(path: str | Path | None = None) -> dict:
    """The merged config document (includes resolved, ${ENV} references left as written)."""
    path = Path(path) if path else default_config_path()
    return _load_raw(path, set())


def build_config(raw: dict, config_dir: str | Path = ".", prices_data: dict | None = None, quiet: bool = False) -> Config:
    """Validate a merged config document and resolve environment references, prices, and capabilities.

    ``prices_data`` (the prices.json structure) overrides the file in ``config_dir``; the
    database-backed config passes the prices it stores.
    """
    import copy

    raw = _interpolate(copy.deepcopy(raw))
    oidc = (raw.get("auth") or {}).get("oidc")
    if isinstance(oidc, dict) and not (oidc.get("issuer") and oidc.get("client_id")):
        raw["auth"]["oidc"] = None
    raw["backends"] = _named(raw.get("backends"))
    raw["models"] = _named(raw.get("models"))
    if "teams" in raw:
        raw["teams"] = _named(raw.get("teams"))
    cfg = Config.model_validate(raw)
    _disable_unusable_backends(cfg, quiet)
    cfg.config_dir = str(Path(config_dir).resolve())
    catalog = prices_data if prices_data is not None else load_catalog(Path(config_dir) / cfg.prices_file)
    prices, contexts, reasoning, outputs = parse_prices(catalog)
    apply_quality(cfg, catalog)
    unpriced = []
    for m in cfg.models:
        if m.context_window is None:
            m.context_window = contexts.get(m.name)
        if m.max_output_tokens is None:
            m.max_output_tokens = outputs.get(m.name)
        if not m.effort_levels and m.name in reasoning and m.kind == "chat":
            m.effort_levels = ["low", "medium", "high"]
        for r in m.routes:
            if r.price is None:
                r.price = prices.get(f"{r.backend}:{r.model}")
                if r.price is None:
                    unpriced.append(f"{m.name}@{r.backend}")
            elif r.price.source is None:
                r.price.source = "config"
    unknown = sorted({r.backend for m in cfg.models for r in m.routes} - {b.name for b in cfg.backends})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"routes refer to backends that aren't defined: {', '.join(unknown)}")
    # Savings are measured against the baseline model: a typo there would silently zero them.
    chat = {m.name for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat"}
    for where, name in [("baseline_model", cfg.baseline_model)] + [(f"teams.{t.name}.baseline_model", t.baseline_model) for t in cfg.teams]:
        if name and name not in chat:
            raise ValueError(f"{where} is '{name}', which isn't a configured chat model")
    if unpriced and not quiet:
        log.info("routes without a known price (excluded from auto routing): %s", ", ".join(unpriced))
    return cfg


def load_config(path: str | Path | None = None) -> Config:
    path = Path(path) if path else default_config_path()
    return build_config(load_raw_config(path), path.parent)


_AZURE_PROJECT = re.compile(r"(\.services\.ai\.azure\.com)/api/projects/[^/]+", re.IGNORECASE)


def normalize_base_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Accept the endpoint forms people actually have in their environment.

    * Azure AI Foundry project URLs (``.../api/projects/<name>``): Claude and the
      OpenAI v1 API live at the resource root, so the project path is dropped.
    * An endpoint that already ends in the API path the config appends
      (``.../openai/v1/openai/v1``) is collapsed.
    """
    url = _AZURE_PROJECT.sub(r"\1", url.rstrip("/"))
    for suffix in ("/openai/v1", "/anthropic", "/v1"):
        while url.endswith(suffix + suffix):
            url = url[: -len(suffix)]
    return url


def _disable_unusable_backends(cfg: Config, quiet: bool = False) -> None:
    for b in cfg.backends:
        b.base_url = normalize_base_url(b.base_url)
        if not b.enabled:
            continue
        reason = None
        if b.kind == "self_hosted" and b.serve is not None:
            pass  # endpoint is published by the capacity controller at runtime
        elif b.kind != "mock":
            if b.flavor == "vertex":
                if not b.project:
                    reason = "no GCP project configured"
            elif not b.base_url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                reason = f"base_url {b.base_url!r} is not a URL"
            if b.auth.type == "api_key" and not b.auth.key():
                reason = f"{b.auth.describe()} is not set"
        if reason:
            b.enabled = False
            b.disabled_reason = reason
            if not quiet:
                log.info("backend %s disabled: %s", b.name, reason)

    out = []

# Merit Order — how it works

An open-source, self-hostable LLM gateway whose job is to **cut LLM spend for day-to-day use**
(coding agents like pi and Claude Code, internal apps, SDKs) without users changing how they work.

The name comes from power grids. Operators dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest
marginal cost first, with expensive "peaker" plants switched on only when demand requires them.
Merit Order does the same with tokens. When steady load justifies it, your own GPUs become the
cheap baseload. API endpoints are always available as the peakers that cover spikes and everything
else. The router dispatches every session to the cheapest capacity that meets its quality bar.

It does three things:

1. **Routes** each session to the cheapest model/backend that meets the task's quality bar.
2. **Runs open-weight models on its own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when sustained load makes that cheaper
   than paying per token — and turns them off when it doesn't. API endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex,
   Foundry, …) are always on, as the fallback and the overflow.
3. **Saves tokens** with provider prompt caching, cache-aware routing, and careful compression.

Around that: enterprise auth (Entra first, generic OIDC, SCIM), budgets and hard safeguards, a
**savings ledger** that shows what every request would have cost without the proxy, and a web
console to watch and control all of it: spend, savings, where every GPU runs and what it costs,
and the switches to stop it.

## Read in this order

| Doc | What you'll understand |
|---|---|
| [01 — Architecture](01-architecture.md) | The boxes and what each one owns |
| [02 — Request flow](02-request-flow.md) | What happens to one request, start to finish |
| [03 — Routing](03-routing.md) | How a model/backend is picked: marginal cost + switching cost |
| [04 — Caching & sessions](04-caching-and-sessions.md) | Who owns what state; why caches don't move between backends |
| [05 — GPU autoscaling](05-gpu-autoscaling.md) | When GPUs come up/down, and overflow to APIs |
| [06 — Auth & spend](06-auth-and-spend.md) | Entra login → virtual keys, budgets, the ledger |
| [07 — Deployment](07-deployment.md) | Compose or Kubernetes, `docker compose up`, supply-chain security |
| [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md) | Spend and savings reports by user, team, project, and time |
| [09 — Decisions](09-decisions.md) | What we decided, why, and what's still open |
| [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md) | **Every rule, as diagrams:** which model, GPU or API, retries, when GPUs start and stop, and what happens when things go wrong |

## Six ideas that drive every design decision

1. **Marginal cost, not list price.** A GPU that is already running is a sunk cost for that hour,
   so its spare capacity is ~free. Use it — even for a *better* model than the task needs.
2. **Moving a session costs money.** Prompt caches live on the backend. Switching backends means
   re-paying for the whole context, so the router counts that before moving anything.
3. **The harness owns the conversation.** The proxy stores routing *metadata* (hashes, timestamps,
   which backend), never conversation content.
4. **APIs are the floor, GPUs are an optimization.** Every model that runs on our GPUs should also
   have an API route, so GPUs never become a single point of failure. The console warns about any
   model that doesn't before anyone stops its GPUs.
5. **Clone and run.** One `docker compose up` with one API key gives you a working gateway. GPUs,
   Entra, and Kubernetes are opt-in layers.
6. **Every cost is visible next to the switch that controls it.** Anything that spends money (a
   team, a GPU, the whole organization) shows what it's costing and can be capped or stopped from
   the console.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Harness** | The client driving the model: pi, Claude Code, Cursor, an SDK app |
| **Session** | One conversation/agent run; the unit of stickiness and caching |
| **Backend** | A concrete place a model runs: `bedrock/us-east-1/claude-sonnet`, `self/qwen3-coder/replica-2` |
| **Quality floor** | Minimum capability the classifier says a task needs (e.g. `coding:3`) |
| **Headroom** | Spare capacity on a running GPU replica before it misses its latency target |
| **Shadow price** | Internal price for self-hosted tokens: ~0 when idle, rising toward API price as it fills |
| **Rebuild cost** | Cost to re-process a session's context on a backend whose cache is cold |
| **Counterfactual cost** | What a request would have cost on the default/floor model's API price |

## Status

| Area | Built | Not yet |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway | OpenAI Chat + Responses, Anthropic Messages, embeddings; pass-through and translation; Anthropic, Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, OpenRouter, direct open-model vendors, any OpenAI-compatible server | Gemini native API |
| Routing | Rule classifier, marginal-cost router with rebuild cost, stickiness, refusal fallback, opt-in substitution, automatic reasoning effort, measured quality scores (`meritorder eval`) | A learned router |
| GPUs | Break-even controller, SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM, static servers, SkyPilot catalog prices, stop / drain / pin / stop-all, fleet safeguards, activity log | Kubernetes-native provisioning (llm-d / KServe) |
| Token savings | Automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, deterministic compression, opt-in response cache | Model-based compression (LLMLingua) |
| Identity and spend | Keys, Entra/OIDC login, SCIM, roles, People page, team/user/org/GPU budgets, rate limits, per-session and per-request caps | Google sign-in (works as generic OIDC, untested) |
| Reporting | Ledger, savings by cause, reports API, console, CSV/JSONL export to S3, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, alerts and weekly digests to a webhook | Reconciliation with provider bills, Parquet, Grafana dashboard |

def install_idp(monkeypatch, poll, oidc=True, expires_in=60, exchange_status=200):
    """A fake gateway + identity provider for the OIDC device-code flow."""
    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        url = str(request.url)
        if url == "http://gw.test/auth/config":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"oidc": {"issuer": "https://idp.test/", "client_id": "cli", "scopes": ["openid", "email"]} if oidc else None})
        if url == "https://idp.test/.well-known/openid-configuration":
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"device_authorization_endpoint": "https://idp.test/device", "token_endpoint": "https://idp.test/token"})
        if url == "https://idp.test/device":
            assert b"client_id=cli" in request.content and b"scope=openid+email" in request.content
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"device_code": "dc", "user_code": "ABCD", "verification_uri": "https://idp.test/activate",
                                             "interval": 1, "expires_in": expires_in})
        if url == "https://idp.test/token":
            assert b"device_code=dc" in request.content
            return httpx.Response(200, json=poll())
        if url == "http://gw.test/auth/exchange":
            assert json.loads(request.content) == {"id_token": "idt"}
            if exchange_status != 200:
                return httpx.Response(exchange_status, text="not in a team")
            return httpx.Response(200, json={"api_key": "mo-new", "user": "alice", "team": "eng", "expires_at": "2026-12-09T00:00:00Z"})
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected request {url}")

    real = httpx.Client
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli.httpx, "Client", lambda **kw: real(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler), **kw))

class LiveGateway:
    """A real gateway (in-memory storage, mock backends) served by uvicorn on a free port, in a thread."""

    def __init__(self, cfg):
        self.gw = build_gateway(cfg, store=MemoryStore(), state=MemoryState())
        self.gw.file_raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
        self.server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(gateway=self.gw), host="127.0.0.1", port=0, log_level="warning", lifespan="off"))
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.run, daemon=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        self.thread.start()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
        while not self.server.started:
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "gateway did not start"
            time.sleep(0.02)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.servers[0].sockets[0].getsockname()[1]}"
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.should_exit = True
        self.thread.join(10)

    def chat(self, n: int = 1, key: str = TEST_KEY, model: str = "small") -> None:
        before = len(self.gw.store.ledger)
        for _ in range(n):
            r = httpx.post(f"{self.url}/v1/chat/completions", headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
                           json={"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}, timeout=30)
            assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
        while len(self.gw.store.ledger) < before + n:  # ledger rows are written just after the response
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline
            time.sleep(0.01)

# 03 — Routing The router answers: **which model, on which backend, for this request?** It optimizes **marginal cost** — what this request adds to the bill *right now* — subject to a quality floor and team policy. ## Decision flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> B{"Harness pinned
a model?"} B -- "yes" --> FIX["Model is fixed
(only the backend can vary)"] B -- "no, model=auto" --> C{"Existing session,
mid-task, cache warm?"} C -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep session's model"] C -- "no" --> D["Classifier → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] D --> E["Candidates = models allowed for team
with quality ≥ floor"] FIX --> S KEEP --> S E --> S["Score every backend of every candidate
cost = rebuild + turns × per-turn"] S --> T{"Cheapest beats current
by more than hysteresis margin?"} T -- "yes" --> MOVE["Route to cheapest
(ties → higher quality)"] T -- "no" --> STAY["Stay on current backend"] MOVE --> PRI{"Running above floor
only because it's free?"} STAY --> PRI PRI -- "yes" --> LOW["Send with low priority
(paid traffic preempts it)"] PRI -- "no" --> NORM["Send with normal priority"] ``` ## The cost function For each candidate backend `b`, over the session's expected remaining turns: ``` cost(b) = rebuild(b) + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn(b) ``` **Per-turn cost by backend type** | Backend state | `per_turn(b)` | |---|---| | API | uncached tokens × input price + cached tokens × cache-read price + output × output price | | Self-hosted, plenty of headroom | ≈ 0 (shadow price near zero) | | Self-hosted, filling up | shadow price rises toward the same model's API price | | Self-hosted, at latency target | unavailable (or priced as the API version of the same model) | **Rebuild cost** | Situation | `rebuild(b)` | |---|---| | `b` already holds a warm cache for this session | 0 | | API, cold | prefix tokens × (cache-write price − cache-read price) | | Self-hosted, cold | prefix tokens × shadow price + latency penalty for the prefill | Illustrative (check real prices): a 120k-token Claude session costs ~$0.04/turn in cache reads to stay. Moving it to another Claude backend costs ~$0.45 to rewrite the cache. A move has to save more than ~$0.41 over the rest of the session to be worth it. ## Shadow price Self-hosted tokens aren't literally free — capacity is finite. The shadow price makes spare capacity attractive while protecting latency: ![Shadow price vs replica utilization](img/shadow-price.svg) ## Free upgrades (and why they're safe) If a strong open model is running with headroom and the task only needs a medium model, the user gets the strong model at ~zero cost. Three guardrails keep this from backfiring: 1. **Low priority.** Opportunistic requests use vLLM priority scheduling, so traffic that *needs* that model always goes first. 2. **Doesn't keep GPUs alive.** The controller values upgraded traffic at its *floor* model's API price, so free traffic can't make a GPU look worth keeping. (See [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md).) 3. **Only at boundaries.** Upgrades/downgrades happen at session start or task boundaries — never mid-task — so tool-calling behavior and caches stay stable. ## Free moments to re-route Moving costs nothing when the session's cache is already gone: - Session idle longer than the cache TTL. - The harness compacted history (prefix hash no longer matches). - The replica evicted the session's KV cache (from vLLM / llm-d KV events). - A natural task boundary. ## When a model refuses Some models decline requests through safety classifiers (Claude returns HTTP 200 with `stop_reason: "refusal"`; OpenAI-style APIs use `finish_reason: "content_filter"`). For `auto` requests, Merit Order retries on the next eligible model: - Streams are buffered only until the first content arrives, so a refusal before any content is retried invisibly; one that arrives after content has started streams through. - The refused attempt is recorded in the ledger (it cost tokens), and the response carries `x-meritorder-refused-by`. - A model the client named is never substituted. Teams can turn this off (`refusal_fallback: false`). ## Measuring quality scores The 1–5 quality scores in `config/` start as informed guesses. `meritorder eval` measures them: it sends a suite of mechanically graded tasks (no model-as-judge) through the gateway to each model, and suggests a score per task type: the highest level L such that the model passes at least 75% of tasks at every level up to L. ```bash uv run meritorder eval --models claude-haiku-5-5,qwen3-coder,glm-5.3-flash # estimates cost, asks first uv run meritorder eval --models ... --apply # also write scores as a new config version ``` The starter suite (`src/meritorder/evals/starter.yaml`) covers coding and general tasks at every level; use `--suite` for your own. Results show on the console's Models page next to the configured scores, flagged where they differ. Eval traffic is tagged `eval=` in the ledger, so its cost shows up in reports. ## Harness overrides | Harness sends | Behavior | |---|---| | `model: "claude-sonnet-4-5"` (explicit) | No model substitution. Router picks the cheapest *backend* for that model. | | `model: "auto"` | Classifier + router choose. | | `model: "auto"` + `X-Route-Floor: coding:3` | Harness sets the floor; router chooses above it. | | `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges the classifier's floor down / up. | | `reasoning_effort` / `output_config.effort` | Always passed through (translated between formats). Merit Order only picks an effort for `auto` requests that don't set one. | | `X-MeritOrder-Backend: ` (admins) | Pins the backend, e.g. to test one provider. | ## When a model's GPUs are stopped - `auto` traffic, including sessions in the middle of a task, moves to the next eligible model (the session's cache is rebuilt there). - A request that names a model whose only routes are stopped GPUs gets a 503 that says why for each route ("stopped by dana: cost review", "no API key") and suggests `auto`. A named model is never silently swapped. Give open models an API route (OpenRouter, the vendor, Bedrock) to keep them available; the GPUs page warns which models have none before anyone stops a deployment. Team policy (allowed models, allowed providers, data-residency rules) is applied **before** scoring, so an override can never escape policy.

class LiveGateway:
    """A real gateway (in-memory storage, mock backends) served by uvicorn on a free port, in a thread."""

    def __init__(self, cfg):
        self.gw = build_gateway(cfg, store=MemoryStore(), state=MemoryState())
        self.gw.file_raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
        self.server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(gateway=self.gw), host="127.0.0.1", port=0, log_level="warning", lifespan="off"))
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.run, daemon=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        self.thread.start()
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
        while not self.server.started:
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "gateway did not start"
            time.sleep(0.02)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.servers[0].sockets[0].getsockname()[1]}"
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.server.should_exit = True
        self.thread.join(10)

    def chat(self, n: int = 1, key: str = TEST_KEY, model: str = "small") -> None:
        before = len(self.gw.store.ledger)
        for _ in range(n):
            r = httpx.post(f"{self.url}/v1/chat/completions", headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
                           json={"model": model, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}, timeout=30)
            assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
        while len(self.gw.store.ledger) < before + n:  # ledger rows are written just after the response
            assert time.monotonic() < deadline
            time.sleep(0.01)
