# 07 — Deployment Goal: **clone, add one API key, `docker compose up`, point pi at it.** Everything else is an opt-in layer. ## Two supported ways to run it The same container images run under **Docker Compose** or **Kubernetes (Helm chart)**. Each organization picks one. | | Docker Compose | Kubernetes (Helm) | |---|---|---| | **For** | Trying it out, small teams, a single VM | Production at organizations with real spend | | **Setup** | `docker compose up`, minutes | Needs a cluster and Helm | | **High availability** | One machine | Multiple gateways, restarts, rolling upgrades | | **Scaling** | Manual | Gateway autoscales | | **Postgres / Redis** | Containers in the compose file | Usually managed cloud services | | **Secrets** | `.env` | A Secret synced from your cloud's store by External Secrets ([Secrets](#secrets)) | What keeps supporting both cheap: - **No Kubernetes-specific code in the app.** Config is env vars plus one YAML file, health checks are plain HTTP (`/healthz`, `/readyz`), logs go to stdout. - **One active controller, enforced by a Postgres advisory lock.** Works the same under both. - **Migrations are a command** (`meritorder migrate`): a one-off service in Compose, a pre-install / pre-upgrade hook in Helm. - **CI checks both** on every change: a Compose smoke test (build, start, send requests) and a Helm lint plus schema validation of the rendered manifests (kubeconform). - Nomad, ECS, Docker Swarm, etc. can be community recipes; they aren't officially supported. Where GPUs run is a separate choice. SkyPilot can start GPU VMs on clouds and neoclouds, or target an existing Kubernetes cluster with GPUs, from either deployment style. ## Containers One image runs every Merit Order process; the command picks which. Docker Compose builds it from the repo (`meritorder:dev`, and `meritorder:gpu` for the controller). The release workflow publishes it as `ghcr.io/therick/meritorder` when a `v*` tag is pushed; no release is tagged yet (2026-11-11). | Service | Image and command | Required? | |---|---|---| | gateway | `meritorder serve`: APIs, console at `/ui/`, reports, admin, SCIM | Yes | | worker | `meritorder worker`: rollups, partitions, alerts, digests, live prices (every 15 minutes), quality scores (daily), eval runs started on the console | Yes, for reports, alerts, and live prices | | migrate | `meritorder migrate`, once per upgrade | Yes | | controller | `meritorder controller` on the **`-gpu` image variant**, which adds SkyPilot in its own environment (`--build-arg SKYPILOT=`) | Only for the GPU tier | | postgres | People, keys, config versions, prices and quality scores, ledger, GPU cost, eval runs | Yes | | redis | Sessions, counters, GPU state, live feed | Yes | | caddy (profile: tls) | HTTPS for single-machine installs | No | The SkyPilot controller needs cloud credentials and keeps state in `~/.sky`: mount them into the controller (commented example in `compose.yaml`) or point it at a SkyPilot API server. For local testing without a cloud, `scripts/fake_vllm.py` stands in for a GPU server (`provisioner: static`). ## Topology: laptop / single VM ```mermaid flowchart LR pi["pi / Claude Code"] --> gw subgraph compose["docker compose"] gw["gateway"] pg[("postgres")] rd[("redis")] wk["worker"] ctl["controller
(profile: gpu, -gpu image)"] gw --> pg gw --> rd wk --> pg wk --> rd ctl --> pg ctl --> rd end gw --> own["Your own vLLM server
(provisioner: static)"] gw --> apis["API backends
Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry / OpenRouter"] ctl --> sky["SkyPilot → cloud GPUs"] gw --> sky ``` ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/therick/meritorder && cd meritorder cp .env.example .env # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY and at least one provider key docker compose up -d # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080, UI at /ui/ docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin ``` Turning on more: ```bash docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d # use your ~/.aws profile (incl. SSO) for Bedrock docker compose --profile gpu up -d # adds the GPU capacity controller docker compose --profile tls up -d # adds Caddy for HTTPS on one machine ``` Entra: set `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`. Vertex AI (Claude and Gemini): set `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (the absolute path to a service-account JSON) in `.env`. Compose mounts that file read-only at `/run/secrets/google-credentials.json` and points the variable there. `MERITORDER_VERTEX=false` switches Vertex off. ## Topology: production (Kubernetes) ```mermaid flowchart LR users["Harnesses / apps"] --> ing["Ingress / LB"] subgraph k8s["Kubernetes (Helm chart)"] ing --> gw1["gateway"] ing --> gw2["gateway"] ing --> gw3["gateway"] ctl["controller, -gpu image
(1 active: Postgres lock)"] end gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> rd[("Managed Redis")] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> pg[("Managed Postgres")] ctl --> pg ctl --> skyapi["SkyPilot API server"] skyapi --> gpus["GPU clusters
any cloud / neocloud"] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> gpus gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> apis["API backends"] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 -.-> otel["OpenTelemetry →
Grafana / Datadog / ..."] ``` - Gateways are stateless; scale with HPA on CPU. - One controller is active at a time, enforced by a Postgres advisory lock; a standby is fine. - Same images as Compose. ## Performance and scaling Measured against zero-latency mock backends with real Postgres and Redis (one laptop, Apple M4 Max), so the numbers are Merit Order's own work. The benchmark is in `scripts/bench_gateway.py`. **Added latency per call** (before the request goes upstream; the same for time to first token on streams): | Request | Merit Order's own time | |---|---| | Chat with a short or 2k-token prompt | ~0.6 ms | | Agent turn: 30k tokens of history + tools | ~2 ms | | Agent turn: 120k tokens of history + tools | ~6.5 ms (mostly parsing and hashing a ~500 KB body) | Add the network hop to the gateway, and **two Redis round trips** (one pipeline for budgets, rate limits, session, and GPU load and in-flight counts; one to save the session). With a managed Redis in the same zone, that's about 0.5–2 ms. Ledger writes, spend counters, and telemetry happen after the response, in one more pipeline. For comparison, models take 0.3–2 s to first token, and many seconds to prefill 120k tokens. **Throughput:** about **1,100 requests/s per process** (one CPU core); it scales nearly linearly with processes (7,100 requests/s with 8 on one machine that was also running Redis, Postgres, and the load generator). Gateways share nothing but Redis and Postgres, so add pods or `--workers` (`MERITORDER_WORKERS`) to scale. Long streams are cheap to hold open: what limits a process is CPU per request, not open connections. A rough sizing for 10,000 requests/s: 10–16 gateway cores, one Redis node (~20 commands per request in three pipelines), and Postgres taking 10,000 ledger inserts/s, the first part that would need work (batched inserts) at that scale. For perspective, an organization spending $300k a month on LLMs makes about 5–50 requests/s. Connection pools, all per process: | Pool | Default | Setting | |---|---|---| | Upstream, per backend (each stream holds one connection) | 500 | `MERITORDER_UPSTREAM_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `MERITORDER_UPSTREAM_KEEPALIVE` (100) | | Redis (waits for a free connection rather than failing) | 200 | `MERITORDER_REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | | Postgres | 10 | `MERITORDER_DB_POOL_SIZE`; with many processes, put PgBouncer in front | Request bodies are capped at 32 MB (`MERITORDER_MAX_BODY_MB`; Anthropic's own limit), 64 KB for sign-in, and 1 MB for SCIM; larger ones get a 413 before anything reads them. ## Ingress and TLS Merit Order is a plain HTTP service. It runs behind whatever the organization already uses: a cloud load balancer, an existing ingress controller, NGINX, Envoy. Nothing requires a proxy in front of it. Single-machine installs that want HTTPS can enable the Caddy profile (`MERITORDER_DOMAIN` is the hostname it gets a certificate for); the Helm chart can create an Ingress (`ingress.enabled`). What's exposed: Docker Compose publishes the gateway on `127.0.0.1` (set `MERITORDER_BIND=0.0.0.0` to open it to your network). Behind a public ingress, `/metrics` is reachable too; it shows spend and traffic totals, not prompts or users, but set `MERITORDER_METRICS_TOKEN` (and Helm `metrics.tokenKey`) to require a token. The console is served with a strict Content-Security-Policy and refuses to be framed. ## Configuration `config/meritorder.yaml` (plus `include:`d files and environment variables for secrets) describes everything. The image ships the default config. Compose mounts the repo's `config/` over it (read-only); in Helm, override files with `--set-file configFiles.=...`. API prices are not typed in. The worker refreshes them every 15 minutes from OpenRouter's catalog (OpenRouter routes) and LiteLLM's price list (direct provider APIs); `price:` on an API route only overrides the list, e.g. for a negotiated discount. Quality scores come from Epoch AI's benchmark data by default (`quality.source`; `artificial_analysis` needs `ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY`), refreshed daily; the `quality:` written on a model is the fallback for models the source doesn't cover. ```yaml baseline_model: claude-sonnet # counterfactual for savings reports include: [models-open.yaml, models-embeddings.yaml] # open-weight catalog, direct vendor APIs, embeddings quality: {source: epoch} # where `auto` gets 1-5 quality scores backends: bedrock: format: anthropic base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"} models: claude-sonnet: aliases: ["claude-sonnet-*"] quality: {coding: 5, general: 4} # fallback if the quality source doesn't cover it routes: - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5} # price from the live list - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5} teams: platform: budget_usd_month: 20000 user_budget_usd_month: 500 allowed_models: ["*"] allowed_backends: ["*", "!openrouter-free"] compression: {enabled: true} ``` Useful commands: | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `meritorder check` | Which backends and models are usable with the current credentials | | `meritorder prices refresh` | Write the live prices, context windows, output limits, and quality scores to `prices.json` (the worker keeps the stored ones current on its own) | | `meritorder models discover` | List the model IDs each enabled backend serves | | `meritorder keys create / list / revoke` | Manage API keys | | `meritorder login` or `use-key `, then `meritorder setup pi` / `claude-code` | Sign in with Entra (or save a key you were given) and point a harness at the gateway; # Merit Order

An open-source LLM gateway that cuts LLM spend for day-to-day use, without changing how
people work.

Power grids dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest marginal cost first, with expensive
peaker plants switched on only when demand requires them. Merit Order does the same with tokens:

- **Routes** every session to the cheapest model and backend that meets the task's quality bar,
  counting what it would cost to rebuild the prompt cache somewhere else.
- **Runs open-weight models on your own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when steady load makes that cheaper
  than paying per token, and turns them off when it doesn't. APIs (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex,
  Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, ...) are always there for overflow.
- **Saves tokens**: automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, cache-safe compression of huge tool
  outputs, and an optional response cache.
- **Shows the money**: every request is recorded with what it cost and what it would have cost
  without Merit Order, broken down by cause, per user, team, project, and day.

Point Claude Code, pi, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or anything that speaks either API at it.

## Quickstart (no keys needed)

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env            # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY (and any provider keys you have)
uv run meritorder serve         # http://localhost:8080, reports UI at /ui/
```

```bash
curl localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $MERITORDER_DEV_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}'
```

With no provider keys, requests go to built-in mock backends. `uv run meritorder check` shows
which backends and models are live with the keys you've set. Without `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`,
storage is in memory; use Docker Compose for the real thing.

## Run the full stack with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add at least one provider key
docker compose up -d            # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080
docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin
```

Bedrock with your AWS profile (including SSO): `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d`.
Kubernetes: `helm install mo charts/meritorder` (see [docs/07-deployment.md](docs/07-deployment.md)).

## Point your harness at it

```bash
meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com   # Entra sign-in; or: meritorder use-key <key>
meritorder setup pi                                    # adds a "meritorder" provider to pi
meritorder setup claude-code                           # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + apiKeyHelper
```

Or by hand: OpenAI-compatible clients use base URL `<gateway>/v1`; Claude Code uses
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>`. Use `model: "auto"` to let Merit Order choose, or name a model
(`claude-sonnet`, `kimi-k3.1`, `qwen3-coder`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, ...) to pin it.

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Session-Id` | Groups requests into a session (pi sends it; otherwise inferred) |
| `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | Minimum quality for `auto` routing |
| `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges `auto` routing down or up |
| `X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=foo` | Cost-allocation tags for reports |
| `X-MeritOrder-Cache: on` / `off` | Use or bypass the response cache |
| `X-MeritOrder-Backend: <name>` | Admins only: pin a backend (testing, debugging) |

Responses carry `x-meritorder-model`, `x-meritorder-backend`, and (non-streaming)
`x-meritorder-cost-usd` / `x-meritorder-savings-usd`.

## What's in the box

| Area | Built |
|---|---|
| APIs | OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages, streaming and not; pass-through when formats match, translation when they don't |

import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import pytest
from conftest import ADMIN_KEY, LEAD_KEY, TEST_KEY, auth, ledger_row

from meritorder.backends import build_backends
from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, Config, ServeConfig
from meritorder.controls import describe_control, fleet, month_fraction


@pytest.fixture
def gpus(gateway):
    """Two managed deployments the gateway can route to."""
    cfgs = [BackendConfig(name=n, kind="self_hosted", format="openai", gpu_cost_per_hour=3.0,
                          serve=ServeConfig(model="small", provisioner="static", static_url=f"http://{n}.test/v1"))
            for n in ("gpu-a", "gpu-b")]
    gateway.cfg.backends.extend(cfgs)
    gateway.backends.update(build_backends(Config(backends=cfgs, models=[])))
    return gateway


async def post(client, path, body=None, key=ADMIN_KEY):
    return await client.post(path, json=body if body is not None else {}, headers=auth(key))


async def test_only_admins_change_controls(client, gpus):
    _, fin =await gpus.store.create_key("fin", "ops", "finance")
    for key in (TEST_KEY, LEAD_KEY, fin):
        assert (await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-a/control", {"mode": "off"}, key)).status_code == 403
        assert (await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/resume", None, key)).status_code == 403
    assert (await client.post("/v1/admin/gpu/stop-all", json={})).status_code == 401
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/controls", headers=auth(fin))).status_code == 200  # finance can look
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/controls", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).status_code == 403


async def test_stop_now_with_expiry_takes_the_backend_out_of_routing(client, gpus):
    await gpus.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-a", {"state": "warm", "endpoint": "http://gpu-a.test/v1", "replicas": 1})
    await gpus.refresh_deployments()
    assert gpus.backends["gpu-a"].available
    r = await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-a/control", {"mode": "off", "drain": False, "hours": 2, "reason": "cost review"})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    dep = r.json()["controls"]["deployments"]["gpu-a"]
    assert dep["mode"] == "off" and dep["drain"] is False and dep["by"] == "root" and dep["replicas"] is None
    assert 2 * 3600 - 60 < dep["until"] - time.time() <= 2 * 3600
    assert "warning" in r.json()  # no controller heartbeat: routing changed, cloud GPUs didn't
    assert not gpus.backends["gpu-a"].available and "stopped by root: cost review" in gpus.backends["gpu-a"].unavailable_reason
    assert await gpus.state.get_json("controller:kick")  # the controller is woken early
    alert = (await gpus.state.recent_alerts(1))[0]
    assert alert["title"] == "GPU gpu-a stopped now" and "for 2h" in alert["text"] and "(cost review)" in alert["text"]
    ev = (await client.get("/v1/admin/gpu/events?backend=gpu-a", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).json()["events"]
    assert ev[0]["kind"] == "control" and ev[0]["detail"]["mode"] == "off" and isinstance(ev[0]["ts"], str)


async def test_drain_pin_and_back_to_auto(client, gpus):
    await gpus.state.set_json("controller:heartbeat", {"at": time.time(), "host": "ctl-1", "interval": 60})
    r = await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-b/control", {"mode": "off"})
    assert r.json()["controls"]["deployments"]["gpu-b"]["drain"] is True and "warning" not in r.json()
    assert r.json()["controller"]["alive"] and r.json()["controller"]["host"] == "ctl-1"
    assert (await gpus.state.recent_alerts(1))[0]["title"] == "GPU gpu-b stopping after warm sessions finish"

    assert (await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-b/control", {"mode": "on"})).status_code == 422  # how many?
    assert (await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-b/control", {"mode": "on", "replicas": 0})).status_code == 422
    r = await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-b/control", {"mode": "on", "replicas": 2})
    assert r.json()["controls"]["deployments"]["gpu-b"] == {**r.json()["controls"]["deployments"]["gpu-b"], "mode": "on", "replicas": 2}
    assert describe_control(r.json()["controls"], "gpu-b")["mode"] == "on"

    r = await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-b/control", {"mode": "auto", "reason": "done"})
    assert "gpu-b" not in r.json()["controls"]["deployments"]
    assert (await gpus.state.recent_alerts(1))[0]["text"] == "GPU gpu-b back to automatic: root (done)"
    assert (await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/nope/control", {"mode": "off"})).status_code == 404
    assert (await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-b/control", {"mode": "sideways"})).status_code == 422
    kinds = [e["kind"] for e in (await client.get("/v1/admin/gpu/events?limit=10", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()["events"]]
    assert kinds == ["control", "control", "control"]
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/gpu/events", headers=auth(TEST_KEY))).status_code == 403


async def test_stop_all_then_resume_keeps_per_deployment_controls(client, gpus):
    await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/gpu-a/control", {"mode": "on", "replicas": 1})
    r = await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/stop-all", {"reason": "incident", "drain": True})
    c = r.json()["controls"]
    assert c["paused"] and c["drain"] is True and c["paused_by"] == "root"
    d = describe_control(c, "gpu-a")
    assert d["fleet"] is True and d["mode"] == "off" and d["reason"] == "incident"  # the fleet-wide stop wins
    await gpus.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-a", {"state": "warm", "endpoint": "http://gpu-a.test/v1", "replicas": 1})
    await gpus.refresh_deployments()
    assert gpus.backends["gpu-a"].draining  # drain: warm sessions finish
    r = await post(client, "/v1/admin/gpu/resume")
    c = r.json()["controls"]
    assert not any(k in c for k in ("paused", "paused_by", "reason", "drain"))
    assert c["deployments"]["gpu-a"]["mode"] == "on"


async def test_fleet_summary(gpus):
    await gpus.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-a", {"state": "warm", "replicas": 2})  # no live price: configured $3/h each
    await gpus.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-b", {"state": "draining", "replicas": 1, "burn_usd_per_hour": 4.35})
    f = await fleet(gpus)
    assert f == {"replicas": 3, "usd_per_hour": 10.35, "deployments": ["gpu-a", "gpu-b"]}
    await gpus.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-a", {"state": "api_only", "replicas": 0})
    assert (await fleet(gpus))["replicas"] == 1


async def test_controls_page_spend_and_projection(client, gpus):
    gpus.cfg.safeguards.org_budget_usd_month = 500.0
    for team, cost in (("default", 20.0), ("retired", 5.0)):

    assert c["safeguards"]["org_budget_usd_month"] == 500.0 and c["controller"]["alive"] is False

"""The ``meritorder`` command."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from .harness import CREDENTIALS, KEY_FILE, save_key, saved


def load_dotenv(path: str | Path = ".env") -> None:
    """Load KEY=VALUE lines from .env without overriding variables already set."""
    try:
        lines = Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return
    for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key, value = key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        if key and value and key not in os.environ:
            os.environ[key] = value


def _setup_logging(level: str = "INFO") -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(level=level, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")


def _store():
    from .store import make_store

    store = make_store(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL"))
    if store.kind != "postgres":
        raise SystemExit("this command needs Postgres: set MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL")
    return store


def _saved() -> dict:
    return saved()


def _gateway(args) -> str:
    return (getattr(args, "gateway", None) or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_URL") or _saved().get("gateway") or "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")


def _key(args) -> str:
    key = getattr(args, "key", None) or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_API_KEY") or _saved().get("api_key")
    if not key:
        raise SystemExit("no API key: pass --key, set MERITORDER_API_KEY, or run 'meritorder login'")
    return key


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def cmd_serve(args) -> None:
    import uvicorn

    if args.config:
        os.environ["MERITORDER_CONFIG"] = args.config
    uvicorn.run("meritorder.app:create_app", factory=True, host=args.host, port=args.port, log_level=args.log_level.lower(),
                proxy_headers=True)


def cmd_migrate(args) -> None:
    async def run():
        store = _store()
        await store.init()
        await store.migrate()
        await store.close()
        print("database is up to date")

    asyncio.run(run())


def cmd_worker(args) -> None:
    from .worker import run_worker

    from .config import load_config

    asyncio.run(run_worker(once=args.once, interval=args.interval, cfg=load_config(args.config), backfill=args.backfill))


def cmd_controller(args) -> None:
    from .config import load_config
    from .controller import run_controller

    asyncio.run(run_controller(load_config(args.config), once=args.once, interval=args.interval))


def cmd_keys(args) -> None:
    async def run():
        store = _store()
        await store.init()
        try:
            if args.keys_cmd == "create":
                expires = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=args.expires_days) if args.expires_days else None
                tags = dict(t.split("=", 1) for t in args.tag or [])
                await store.upsert_user(args.user, args.team, args.role, source="ensure")
                key_id, secret = await store.create_key(args.user, args.team, args.role, args.name, tags, expires)
                print(f"key id:  {key_id}")
                print(f"api key: {secret}")
                print("Store it now; it is not shown again.")
            elif args.keys_cmd == "list":
                for k in await store.list_keys(args.user):
                    state = "revoked" if k["revoked_at"] else ("expired" if k["expires_at"] and k["expires_at"] < datetime.now(UTC) else "active")
                    print(f"{k['id']:18} {k['user_id']:24} {k['team']:16} {k['role']:10} {state:8} {k.get('name') or ''}")
            elif args.keys_cmd == "revoke":
                print("revoked" if await store.revoke_key(args.key_id) else "no active key with that id")
        finally:
            await store.close()

    asyncio.run(run())


def cmd_usage(args) -> None:
    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    resp = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/reports/me", headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=30)
    if resp.status_code != 200:
        raise SystemExit(f"{resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
    me = resp.json()
    budget = f" of ${me['budget_usd']:,.2f}" if me.get("budget_usd") is not None else ""
    print(f"{me['user']} ({me['team']}), {me['month']}")
    print(f"  spent     ${me['spend_usd']:,.4f}{budget}")
    print(f"  baseline  ${me['baseline_usd']:,.4f}   (what the same work would cost without Merit Order)")
    print(f"  saved     ${me['savings_usd']:,.4f}   across {me['requests']} requests")
    if me["by_model"]:
        print(f"\n  {'model':28} {'requests':>9} {'cost':>12} {'saved':>12}")
        for r in me["by_model"]:
            print(f"  {str(r['key']):28} {r['requests']:>9} {r['actual_cost']:>12.4f} {r['savings_total']:>12.4f}")


def cmd_login(args) -> None:
    gateway = (args.gateway or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_URL") or "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")
    with httpx.Client(timeout=30) as c:
        oidc = c.get(f"{gateway}/auth/config").json().get("oidc")
        if not oidc:
            raise SystemExit("this gateway has no OIDC login configured; ask an admin for an API key")
        disc = c.get(oidc["issuer"].rstrip("/") + "/.well-known/openid-configuration").json()
        dev = c.post(disc["device_authorization_endpoint"], data={"client_id": oidc["client_id"], "scope": " ".join(oidc["scopes"])}).json()
        print(dev.get("message") or f"Open {dev['verification_uri']} and enter code {dev['user_code']}")
        interval = int(dev.get("interval", 5))
        deadline = time.time() + int(dev.get("expires_in", 900))
        while time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(interval)
            tok = c.post(disc["token_endpoint"], data={
                "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
                "device_code": dev["device_code"],
                "client_id": oidc["client_id"],
            }).json()
            if "id_token" in tok:
                break
            err = tok.get("error")
            if err == "slow_down":
                interval += 5
            elif err != "authorization_pending":
                raise SystemExit(f"login failed: {tok.get('error_description') or err}")
        else:
            raise SystemExit("login timed out")
        resp = c.post(f"{gateway}/auth/exchange", json={"id_token": tok["id_token"]})
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"key exchange failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}")
        result = resp.json()
    save_key(gateway, result["api_key"], {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "api_key"})
    print(f"\nLogged in as {result['user']} (team {result['team']}); key expires {result['expires_at'][:10]}.")
    print(f"Key saved to {KEY_FILE}\n")
    print("Next: `meritorder setup pi` and/or `meritorder setup claude-code`.")


def cmd_use_key(args) -> None:
    """Save an API key an admin gave you (instead of OIDC login)."""
    save_key(_gateway(args), args.api_key)
    print(f"Key saved to {KEY_FILE}")


def cmd_token(args) -> None:
    print(_key(args))


def cmd_setup(args) -> None:
    from .harness import write_claude_code, write_pi

    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        save_key(gateway, key)
    if args.harness == "pi":
        resp = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/models", headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=30)
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"could not list models from {gateway}: {resp.status_code} {resp.text[:200]}")
        path = write_pi(gateway, resp.json()["data"])
        print(f"Wrote the 'meritorder' provider to {path} ({len(resp.json()['data'])} models).")
        print("In pi, open /model and pick 'auto (Merit Order)' or a specific model.")
    else:
        path = write_claude_code(gateway)
        print(f"Updated {path}: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL={gateway}, apiKeyHelper reads {KEY_FILE}.")
        print("Claude Code's model names (claude-sonnet-*, claude-opus-*, ...) route through Merit Order.")


def cmd_export(args) -> None:
    """Download the ledger for a date range to a file or S3 (s3://bucket/key)."""
    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    params = {k: v for k, v in (("start", args.start), ("end", args.end)) if v}
    tmp = Path(args.out if not args.out.startswith("s3://") else f".meritorder-export-{os.getpid()}.jsonl")
    rows = 0
    with httpx.stream("GET", f"{gateway}/v1/reports/export.jsonl", params=params, headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
                      timeout=None) as resp:
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"{resp.status_code}: {resp.read().decode()[:300]}")
        with open(tmp, "w") as f:
            for line in resp.iter_lines():
                if not line:
                    continue
                if args.format == "csv":
                    import csv as _csv

                    row = json.loads(line)
                    if rows == 0:
                        writer = _csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(row))
                        writer.writeheader()
                    row["tags"] = json.dumps(row.get("tags") or {})
                    writer.writerow(row)
                else:
                    f.write(line + "\n")
                rows += 1
    if args.out.startswith("s3://"):
        from botocore.session import Session

        bucket, _, obj = args.out[5:].partition("/")
        client = Session().create_client("s3", endpoint_url=os.environ.get("MERITORDER_S3_ENDPOINT") or None)
        with open(tmp, "rb") as f:
            client.put_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=obj, Body=f.read(),
                              ContentType="text/csv" if args.format == "csv" else "application/x-ndjson")
        tmp.unlink()
    print(f"exported {rows} requests to {args.out}")


def cmd_eval(args) -> None:
    """Measure model quality on a graded suite; suggest (or apply) quality scores."""
    from datetime import UTC, datetime

    from .evals.runner import load_suite, run_suite, score

    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    suite = load_suite(args.suite)
    h = {"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}
    admin_cfg = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/config", headers=h, timeout=30)
    if admin_cfg.status_code != 200:
        raise SystemExit(f"needs an admin key ({admin_cfg.status_code}: {admin_cfg.text[:120]})")
    cfg = admin_cfg.json()
    live = {m["name"]: m for m in cfg["models"] if m.get("routes") and any(r["live"] for r in m["routes"])}
    models = [m.strip() for m in args.models.split(",")] if args.models else [
        n for n, m in live.items() if not n.startswith("mock-") and not m.get("kind") == "embedding"]
    missing = [m for m in models if m not in live]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"no live route for: {', '.join(missing)} (see `meritorder check`)")
    n_tasks = len(suite["tasks"]) * args.repeat
    est = 0.0
    for m in models:
        prices = [r["price"] for r in live[m]["routes"] if r["live"] and r.get("price")]
        if prices:
            p = min(prices, key=lambda x: x["input"])
            est += n_tasks * (150 * p["input"] + 500 * p["output"]) / 1e6
    print(f"Suite '{suite['name']}': {len(suite['tasks'])} tasks x {args.repeat} on {len(models)} models: {', '.join(models)}")
    print(f"Estimated cost: about ${est:.2f} (reasoning models can use several times more output)")
    if not args.yes and input("Run it? [y/N] ").strip().lower() != "y":
        raise SystemExit("cancelled")

    done = [0]

    def progress(res):
        done[0] += 1
        mark = "pass" if res.passed else ("ERROR" if res.error else "fail")
        print(f"  [{done[0]}/{n_tasks * len(models)}] {res.model:22} {res.task_id:14} {mark}")

    results = asyncio.run(run_suite(gateway, key, models, suite, args.concurrency, args.repeat, progress))
    scores = score(results, args.threshold)
    print(f"\n{'model':22} {'pass':>6} {'coding':>7} {'general':>8} {'cost':>9} {'latency':>8}  configured")
    for m, s in scores.items():
        configured = live[m].get("quality") or {}
        sug = {t: v["suggested"] for t, v in s["tasks"].items()}
        print(f"{m:22} {s['pass_rate']:>6.0%} {sug.get('coding', '-'):>7} {sug.get('general', '-'):>8} {s['cost']:>9.4f} {s['avg_latency_ms'] / 1000:>7.1f}s  {configured}")
        for f in s["failed"][: args.show_failures]:
            print(f"    x {f['id']}: {f['why'][:110]}")
    payload = {"suite": suite["name"], "ran_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "models": scores}
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str))
        print(f"\nResults saved to {args.out}")
    httpx.put(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/evals", headers=h, json=json.loads(json.dumps(payload, default=str)), timeout=30)
    if args.apply:
        src = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/config/source", headers=h, timeout=30).json()
        doc = src["document"]
        for m, s in scores.items():
            for task, v in s["tasks"].items():
                if v["suggested"]:
                    doc.setdefault("models", {}).setdefault(m, {}).setdefault("quality", {})[task] = v["suggested"]
        r = httpx.put(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/config", headers=h, timeout=60,
                      json={"document": doc, "comment": f"quality scores from eval '{suite['name']}'"})

"""Hot-path state: session metadata, spend counters, rate limits, GPU utilization.

Redis in real deployments; an in-memory version for development and tests.
Postgres (store.py) stays the source of truth for spend; these counters are a
fast cache of it, re-seeded from Postgres when missing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from collections import deque
from typing import Any

HEALTH_FIELDS = ("requests", "errors", "latency_ms", "ttft_ms", "ttft_n")


class MemoryState:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._kv: dict[str, tuple[Any, float]] = {}
        self._spend: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._util: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._events: deque = deque(maxlen=500)
        self._alerts: deque = deque(maxlen=200)
        self._health: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
        self._gateways: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._config_version: str | None = None

    def _get(self, key: str) -> Any:
        item = self._kv.get(key)
        if item is None:
            return None
        value, expires = item
        if expires and expires < time.time():
            self._kv.pop(key, None)
            return None
        return value

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def get_session(self, sid: str) -> dict | None:
        return self._get(f"sess:{sid}")

    async def put_session(self, sid: str, data: dict, ttl: int) -> None:
        self._kv[f"sess:{sid}"] = (data, time.time() + ttl)

    async def get_spend(self, key: str) -> float | None:
        return self._spend.get(key)

    async def seed_spend(self, key: str, amount: float) -> None:
        self._spend.setdefault(key, amount)

    async def add_spend(self, keys: list[str], amount: float) -> None:
        for k in keys:
            self._spend[k] = self._spend.get(k, 0.0) + amount

    async def rate_hit(self, key: str, window_seconds: int, amount: int = 1) -> int:
        bucket = f"rate:{key}:{int(time.time() // window_seconds)}"
        count = (self._get(bucket) or 0) + amount
        self._kv[bucket] = (count, time.time() + window_seconds)
        return count

    async def utilization(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        return dict(self._util)

    async def set_utilization(self, backend: str, util: float) -> None:
        self._util[backend] = util

    async def set_json(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: int = 0) -> None:
        self._kv[key] = (value, time.time() + ttl if ttl else 0)

    async def get_json(self, key: str) -> Any:
        return self._get(key)

    # --- live telemetry for the console
    async def push_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
        self._events.appendleft(event)

    async def recent_events(self, limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
        return list(self._events)[:limit]

    async def push_alert(self, alert: dict) -> None:
        self._alerts.appendleft(alert)

    async def recent_alerts(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return list(self._alerts)[:limit]

    async def record_backend(self, backend: str, ok: bool, latency_ms: int | None, ttft_ms: int | None) -> None:
        minute = int(time.time() // 60)
        h = self._health.setdefault(f"{backend}:{minute}", dict.fromkeys(HEALTH_FIELDS, 0.0))
        h["requests"] += 1
        h["errors"] += 0 if ok else 1
        h["latency_ms"] += latency_ms or 0
        if ttft_ms:
            h["ttft_ms"] += ttft_ms
            h["ttft_n"] += 1

    async def backend_health(self, backends: list[str], minutes: int = 5) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
        now = int(time.time() // 60)
        out = {}
        for b in backends:
            agg = dict.fromkeys(HEALTH_FIELDS, 0.0)
            for m in range(now - minutes + 1, now + 1):
                for k, v in self._health.get(f"{b}:{m}", {}).items():
                    agg[k] += v
            out[b] = agg
        return out

    async def heartbeat(self, gateway_id: str) -> None:
        self._gateways[gateway_id] = time.time()

    async def live_gateways(self, within: int = 20) -> int:
        return sum(1 for t in self._gateways.values() if t > time.time() - within)

    async def get_config_token(self) -> str | None:
        return self._config_version

    async def set_config_token(self, token: str) -> None:
        self._config_version = token


class RedisState:
    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        import redis.asyncio as redis

        self.r = redis.from_url(url, decode_responses=True)

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return bool(await self.r.ping())

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self.r.aclose()

    async def get_session(self, sid: str) -> dict | None:
        raw = await self.r.get(f"mo:sess:{sid}")
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else None

    async def put_session(self, sid: str, data: dict, ttl: int) -> None:
        await self.r.set(f"mo:sess:{sid}", json.dumps(data), ex=ttl)

    async def get_spend(self, key: str) -> float | None:
        raw = await self.r.get(f"mo:spend:{key}")
        return float(raw) if raw is not None else None

    async def seed_spend(self, key: str, amount: float) -> None:
        await self.r.set(f"mo:spend:{key}", amount, nx=True, ex=40 * 86400)

    async def add_spend(self, keys: list[str], amount: float) -> None:
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        for k in keys:
            pipe.incrbyfloat(f"mo:spend:{k}", amount)
            pipe.expire(f"mo:spend:{k}", 40 * 86400)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def rate_hit(self, key: str, window_seconds: int, amount: int = 1) -> int:
        bucket = f"mo:rate:{key}:{int(time.time() // window_seconds)}"
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.incrby(bucket, amount)
        pipe.expire(bucket, window_seconds * 2)
        count, _ = await pipe.execute()
        return int(count)

    async def utilization(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        raw = await self.r.hgetall("mo:util")
        return {k: float(v) for k, v in raw.items()}

    async def set_utilization(self, backend: str, util: float) -> None:
        await self.r.hset("mo:util", backend, util)

    async def set_json(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: int = 0) -> None:
        await self.r.set(f"mo:{key}", json.dumps(value), ex=ttl or None)

    async def get_json(self, key: str) -> Any:
        raw = await self.r.get(f"mo:{key}")
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else None

    # --- live telemetry for the console (shared by every gateway)
    async def push_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.lpush("mo:events", json.dumps(event, default=str))
        pipe.ltrim("mo:events", 0, 499)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def recent_events(self, limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
        return [json.loads(x) for x in await self.r.lrange("mo:events", 0, limit - 1)]

    async def push_alert(self, alert: dict) -> None:
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.lpush("mo:alerts", json.dumps(alert, default=str))
        pipe.ltrim("mo:alerts", 0, 199)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def recent_alerts(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return [json.loads(x) for x in await self.r.lrange("mo:alerts", 0, limit - 1)]

    async def record_backend(self, backend: str, ok: bool, latency_ms: int | None, ttft_ms: int | None) -> None:
        key = f"mo:bh:{backend}:{int(time.time() // 60)}"
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hincrby(key, "requests", 1)
        if not ok:
            pipe.hincrby(key, "errors", 1)
        if latency_ms:
            pipe.hincrby(key, "latency_ms", int(latency_ms))
        if ttft_ms:
            pipe.hincrby(key, "ttft_ms", int(ttft_ms))
            pipe.hincrby(key, "ttft_n", 1)
        pipe.expire(key, 1800)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def backend_health(self, backends: list[str], minutes: int = 5) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
        now = int(time.time() // 60)
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        for b in backends:
            for m in range(now - minutes + 1, now + 1):
                pipe.hgetall(f"mo:bh:{b}:{m}")
        results = await pipe.execute()
        out, i = {}, 0
        for b in backends:
            agg = dict.fromkeys(HEALTH_FIELDS, 0.0)
            for _ in range(minutes):
                for k, v in (results[i] or {}).items():
                    agg[k] = agg.get(k, 0.0) + float(v)
                i += 1
            out[b] = agg
        return out

    async def heartbeat(self, gateway_id: str) -> None:
        await self.r.hset("mo:gateways", gateway_id, time.time())

    async def live_gateways(self, within: int = 20) -> int:
        raw = await self.r.hgetall("mo:gateways")
        return sum(1 for t in raw.values() if float(t) > time.time() - within)

    async def get_config_token(self) -> str | None:
        return await self.r.get("mo:config_token")

    async def set_config_token(self, token: str) -> None:
        await self.r.set("mo:config_token", token)


def make_state(redis_url: str | None):
    return RedisState(redis_url) if redis_url else MemoryState()

class InFlight:
    """Requests this gateway process has open per backend. Entries older than the backend timeout are
    dropped, so a leaked release (a stream the client never started reading) can't pin a count."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._open: dict[str, dict[int, float]] = {}
        self._seq = 0

    def acquire(self, backend: str, ttl: float):
        self._seq += 1
        token, deadline = self._seq, time.monotonic() + ttl
        self._open.setdefault(backend, {})[token] = deadline

        def release() -> None:
            self._open.get(backend, {}).pop(token, None)

        return release

    def count(self, backend: str) -> int:
        open_ = self._open.get(backend)
        if not open_:
            return 0
        now = time.monotonic()
        for token in [t for t, deadline in open_.items() if deadline < now]:
            del open_[token]
        return len(open_)

    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        return {b: self.count(b) for b in list(self._open)}


class Gateway:
