# 07 — Deployment Goal: **clone, add one API key, `docker compose up`, point pi at it.** Everything else is an opt-in layer. ## Two supported ways to run it The same container images run under **Docker Compose** or **Kubernetes (Helm chart)**. Each organization picks one. | | Docker Compose | Kubernetes (Helm) | |---|---|---| | **For** | Trying it out, small teams, a single VM | Production at organizations with real spend | | **Setup** | `docker compose up`, minutes | Needs a cluster and Helm | | **High availability** | One machine | Multiple gateways, restarts, rolling upgrades | | **Scaling** | Manual | Gateway autoscales | | **Postgres / Redis** | Containers in the compose file | Usually managed cloud services | | **Secrets** | `.env` | A Secret synced from your cloud's store by External Secrets ([Secrets](#secrets)) | What keeps supporting both cheap: - **No Kubernetes-specific code in the app.** Config is env vars plus one YAML file, health checks are plain HTTP (`/healthz`, `/readyz`), logs go to stdout. - **One active controller, enforced by a Postgres advisory lock.** Works the same under both. - **Migrations are a command** (`meritorder migrate`): a one-off service in Compose, a pre-install / pre-upgrade hook in Helm. - **CI checks both** on every change: a Compose smoke test (build, start, send requests) and a Helm lint plus schema validation of the rendered manifests (kubeconform). - Nomad, ECS, Docker Swarm, etc. can be community recipes; they aren't officially supported. Where GPUs run is a separate choice. SkyPilot can start GPU VMs on clouds and neoclouds, or target an existing Kubernetes cluster with GPUs, from either deployment style. ## Containers One image runs every Merit Order process; the command picks which. Docker Compose builds it from the repo (`meritorder:dev`, and `meritorder:gpu` for the controller). The release workflow publishes it as `ghcr.io/therick/meritorder` when a `v*` tag is pushed; no release is tagged yet (2026-11-11). | Service | Image and command | Required? | |---|---|---| | gateway | `meritorder serve`: APIs, console at `/ui/`, reports, admin, SCIM | Yes | | worker | `meritorder worker`: rollups, partitions, alerts, digests, live prices (every 15 minutes), quality scores (daily), eval runs started on the console | Yes, for reports, alerts, and live prices | | migrate | `meritorder migrate`, once per upgrade | Yes | | controller | `meritorder controller` on the **`-gpu` image variant**, which adds SkyPilot in its own environment (`--build-arg SKYPILOT=`) | Only for the GPU tier | | postgres | People, keys, config versions, prices and quality scores, ledger, GPU cost, eval runs | Yes | | redis | Sessions, counters, GPU state, live feed | Yes | | caddy (profile: tls) | HTTPS for single-machine installs | No | In the compose stack every service is built with SkyPilot in its own environment (`SKYPILOT_VERSION`, default 0.14.2; empty leaves it out), so the gateway prices GPUs for the console's break-even itself; price lookups use no credentials. In the Helm chart only the controller has SkyPilot, and it publishes those prices. The SkyPilot controller needs cloud credentials and keeps state in `~/.sky`: mount them into the controller (commented example in `compose.yaml`) or point it at a SkyPilot API server. For local testing without a cloud, `scripts/fake_vllm.py` stands in for a GPU server (`provisioner: static`). ## Topology: laptop / single VM ```mermaid flowchart LR pi["pi / Claude Code"] --> gw subgraph compose["docker compose"] gw["gateway"] pg[("postgres")] rd[("redis")] wk["worker"] ctl["controller
(profile: gpu, -gpu image)"] gw --> pg gw --> rd wk --> pg wk --> rd ctl --> pg ctl --> rd end gw --> own["Your own vLLM server
(provisioner: static)"] gw --> apis["API backends
Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry / OpenRouter"] ctl --> sky["SkyPilot → cloud GPUs"] gw --> sky ``` ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/therick/meritorder && cd meritorder cp .env.example .env # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY and at least one provider key docker compose up -d # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080, UI at /ui/ docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin ``` Turning on more: ```bash docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d # use your ~/.aws profile (incl. SSO) for Bedrock docker compose --profile gpu up -d # adds the GPU capacity controller docker compose --profile tls up -d # adds Caddy for HTTPS on one machine ``` Entra: set `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`. Vertex AI (Claude and Gemini): set `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (the absolute path to a service-account JSON) in `.env`. Compose mounts that file read-only at `/run/secrets/google-credentials.json` and points the variable there. `MERITORDER_VERTEX=false` switches Vertex off. ## Topology: production (Kubernetes) ```mermaid flowchart LR users["Harnesses / apps"] --> ing["Ingress / LB"] subgraph k8s["Kubernetes (Helm chart)"] ing --> gw1["gateway"] ing --> gw2["gateway"] ing --> gw3["gateway"] ctl["controller, -gpu image
(1 active: Postgres lock)"] end gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> rd[("Managed Redis")] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> pg[("Managed Postgres")] ctl --> pg ctl --> skyapi["SkyPilot API server"] skyapi --> gpus["GPU clusters
any cloud / neocloud"] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> gpus gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> apis["API backends"] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 -.-> otel["OpenTelemetry →
Grafana / Datadog / ..."] ``` - Gateways are stateless; scale with HPA on CPU. - One controller is active at a time, enforced by a Postgres advisory lock; a standby is fine. - Same images as Compose. ## Performance and scaling Measured against zero-latency mock backends with real Postgres and Redis (one laptop, Apple M4 Max), so the numbers are Merit Order's own work. The benchmark is in `scripts/bench_gateway.py`. **Added latency per call** (before the request goes upstream; the same for time to first token on streams): | Request | Merit Order's own time | |---|---| | Chat with a short or 2k-token prompt | ~0.6 ms | | Agent turn: 30k tokens of history + tools | ~2 ms | | Agent turn: 120k tokens of history + tools | ~6.5 ms (mostly parsing and hashing a ~500 KB body) | Add the network hop to the gateway, and **two Redis round trips** (one pipeline for budgets, rate limits, session, and GPU load and in-flight counts; one to save the session). With a managed Redis in the same zone, that's about 0.5–2 ms. Ledger writes, spend counters, and telemetry happen after the response, in one more pipeline. For comparison, models take 0.3–2 s to first token, and many seconds to prefill 120k tokens. **Throughput:** about **1,100 requests/s per process** (one CPU core); it scales nearly linearly with processes (7,100 requests/s with 8 on one machine that was also running Redis, Postgres, and the load generator). Gateways share nothing but Redis and Postgres, so add pods or `--workers` (`MERITORDER_WORKERS`) to scale. Long streams are cheap to hold open: what limits a process is CPU per request, not open connections. A rough sizing for 10,000 requests/s: 10–16 gateway cores, one Redis node (~20 commands per request in three pipelines), and Postgres taking 10,000 ledger inserts/s, the first part that would need work (batched inserts) at that scale. For perspective, an organization spending $300k a month on LLMs makes about 5–50 requests/s. Connection pools, all per process: | Pool | Default | Setting | |---|---|---| | Upstream, per backend (each stream holds one connection) | 500 | `MERITORDER_UPSTREAM_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `MERITORDER_UPSTREAM_KEEPALIVE` (100) | | Redis (waits for a free connection rather than failing) | 200 | `MERITORDER_REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | | Postgres | 10 | `MERITORDER_DB_POOL_SIZE`; with many processes, put PgBouncer in front | Request bodies are capped at 32 MB (`MERITORDER_MAX_BODY_MB`; Anthropic's own limit), 64 KB for sign-in, and 1 MB for SCIM; larger ones get a 413 before anything reads them. ## Ingress and TLS Merit Order is a plain HTTP service. It runs behind whatever the organization already uses: a cloud load balancer, an existing ingress controller, NGINX, Envoy. Nothing requires a proxy in front of it. Single-machine installs that want HTTPS can enable the Caddy profile (`MERITORDER_DOMAIN` is the hostname it gets a certificate for); the Helm chart can create an Ingress (`ingress.enabled`). What's exposed: Docker Compose publishes the gateway on `127.0.0.1` (set `MERITORDER_BIND=0.0.0.0` to open it to your network). Behind a public ingress, `/metrics` is reachable too; it shows spend and traffic totals, not prompts or users, but set `MERITORDER_METRICS_TOKEN` (and Helm `metrics.tokenKey`) to require a token. The console is served with a strict Content-Security-Policy and refuses to be framed. ## Configuration `config/meritorder.yaml` (plus `include:`d files and environment variables for secrets) describes everything. The image ships the default config. Compose mounts the repo's `config/` over it (read-only); in Helm, override files with `--set-file configFiles.=...`. API prices are not typed in. The worker refreshes them every 15 minutes from OpenRouter's catalog (OpenRouter routes) and LiteLLM's price list (direct provider APIs); `price:` on an API route only overrides the list, e.g. for a negotiated discount. Quality scores come from Epoch AI's benchmark data by default (`quality.source`; `artificial_analysis` needs `ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY`), refreshed daily; the `quality:` written on a model is the fallback for models the source doesn't cover. ```yaml baseline_model: claude-sonnet # counterfactual for savings reports include: [models-open.yaml, models-embeddings.yaml] # open-weight catalog, direct vendor APIs, embeddings quality: {source: epoch} # where `auto` gets 1-5 quality scores backends: bedrock: format: anthropic base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"} models: claude-sonnet: aliases: ["claude-sonnet-*"] quality: {coding: 5, general: 4} # fallback if the quality source doesn't cover it routes: - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5} # price from the live list - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5} teams: platform: budget_usd_month: 20000 user_budget_usd_month: 500 allowed_models: ["*"] allowed_backends: ["*", "!openrouter-free"] compression: {enabled: true} ``` Useful commands: | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `meritorder check` | Which backends and models are usable with the current credentials | | `meritorder prices refresh` | Write the live prices, context windows, output limits, and quality scores to `prices.json` (the worker keeps the stored ones current on its own) | | `meritorder models discover` | List the model IDs each enabled backend serves | | `meritorder keys create / list / revoke` | Manage API keys | | `meritorder login` or `use-key `, then `meritorder setup pi` / `claude-code` | Sign in with Entra (or save a key you were given) and point a harness at the gateway; `setup claude-code --config-dir ` writes a separate Claude Code profile | | `meritorder usage` | Your own spend | | `meritorder eval --models a,b [--apply]` | Measure quality scores with graded tasks (asks before spending) | | `meritorder export --out file.jsonl` or `s3://…` (`--format csv` for CSV) | Export the ledger | | `meritorder worker --backfill` | Rebuild hourly report rollups from the raw ledger | | `meritorder controller [--once] [--interval 60]` | Run the GPU capacity controller | Once the first configuration is saved from the console, the stored version (in Postgres) is what gateways, the worker, and the controller use; the YAML file is the starting point and the format for import and export. ## Secrets Merit Order never stores provider keys. It reads them from the environment (`value_env`) or from a file (`value_file`), and a configuration saved from the console is refused if it contains a literal key, so keys never reach Postgres or the config history. Where each secret lives: | Secret | Where | How | |---|---|---| | Provider keys | Environment or a mounted file | Supplied by the platform from your secret store | | `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`, `MERITORDER_REDIS_URL` | Environment | Same Secret as the provider keys | | Merit Order keys (`mo-…`) for people and harnesses | Postgres | Shown once; stored only as a SHA-256 hash (random 256-bit tokens, so a slow hash isn't needed) | | Entra / OIDC tokens | Not stored | Verified against the issuer's signing keys, then exchanged for a short-lived `mo-` key | **The best key is no key.** For each cloud's own models, use the workload's identity instead: | Models | Config | Identity | |---|---|---| | Claude in Bedrock | `auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: …}` | IRSA or EKS Pod Identity: a role allowed to invoke the Bedrock models you route to | | Claude and Gemini on Vertex | `auth: {type: google}` | GKE Workload Identity: a Google service account with `roles/aiplatform.user` | | Azure OpenAI, Foundry | `auth: {type: azure_ad}` | AKS Workload Identity: a managed identity with *Cognitive Services OpenAI User* (or the Foundry equivalent) on the resource | The image includes the Google and Azure identity libraries. In Helm, put the identity on the service account (`serviceAccount.annotations`; AKS also needs the pod label `podLabels: {azure.workload.identity/use: "true"}`). Third-party providers (Anthropic direct, OpenAI, OpenRouter, xAI, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, Mistral) always need a key. ### Kubernetes: three ways to provide the Secret Every component reads its environment from one Secret. Set exactly one of these (the chart refuses more than one): | Value | What it does | Use for | |---|---|---| | `externalSecret.enabled` | The chart creates an `ExternalSecret`; [External Secrets Operator](https://external-secrets.io) syncs it from AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Vault, … | Production (recommended) | | `existingSecret` | Use a Secret you create and manage some other way (Sealed Secrets, SOPS, CSI sync, by hand) | Production | | `secretEnv` | The chart creates the Secret from Helm values | Trying it out only: the values end up in Helm's release history (one Secret per revision) and in whatever values file you passed | The `ExternalSecret` is a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook, because the migration hook needs `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL` before anything else starts. Its synced Secret is kept across upgrades; delete it by hand after `helm uninstall`. ### Rotating keys | Approach | Values | What happens when a key changes | |---|---|---| | **Rolling restart** (default) | `secrets.reloadOnChange: true` and [Stakater Reloader](https://github.com/stakater/Reloader) installed in the cluster | Reloader rolls the gateways, worker, and controller; pods start with the new environment. Works for every secret, including the database and Redis URLs | | **No restart** | `secrets.mountAsFiles: true`, and `value_file:` on each backend's `auth` | The Secret is also mounted as files under `/run/secrets/meritorder/`; Kubernetes refreshes them about a minute after the Secret changes, and the next request uses the new key. Provider keys only | With External Secrets, a rotation in the cloud store reaches the Secret within `externalSecret.refreshInterval` (default 1 h; lower it, or annotate the ExternalSecret with `force-sync` to pull at once). For zero-restart rotation of provider keys: ```yaml # values.yaml secrets: {mountAsFiles: true, reloadOnChange: false} ``` ```yaml # meritorder.yaml: the file when it's there, the environment otherwise (so the same config works locally) backends: openrouter: auth: {type: api_key, value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/OPENROUTER_API_KEY, value_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY} ``` Keep the old key valid until the new one is everywhere (most providers allow two keys at once), then revoke it. ### AWS: Secrets Manager One JSON secret holding every variable: ```bash aws secretsmanager create-secret --name meritorder/prod --secret-string '{ "MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://…", "MERITORDER_REDIS_URL": "rediss://…", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "…", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY": "…"}' ``` ```yaml # Once per cluster. ESO's own service account has an IRSA role allowed to read meritorder/*. apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1 kind: ClusterSecretStore metadata: {name: aws-secrets-manager} spec: provider: aws: {service: SecretsManager, region: us-east-1} --- # values.yaml externalSecret: enabled: true secretStoreRef: {kind: ClusterSecretStore, name: aws-secrets-manager} dataFrom: - extract: {key: meritorder/prod} # every JSON key becomes an environment variable serviceAccount: annotations: {eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/meritorder} # keyless Bedrock ``` Without Kubernetes (ECS), put the same secret ARNs in the task definition's `secrets` (`valueFrom`) and give the task role the Bedrock permissions. ### GCP: Secret Manager Secret Manager holds one value per secret, so map each one: ```bash printf '%s' "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | gcloud secrets create meritorder-anthropic-api-key --data-file=- ``` ```yaml apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1 kind: ClusterSecretStore metadata: {name: gcp-secret-manager} spec: provider: gcpsm: {projectID: my-project} # ESO authenticates with its own Workload Identity --- # values.yaml externalSecret: enabled: true secretStoreRef: {kind: ClusterSecretStore, name: gcp-secret-manager} data: - {secretKey: MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-database-url}} - {secretKey: MERITORDER_REDIS_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-redis-url}} - {secretKey: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-anthropic-api-key}} serviceAccount: annotations: {iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: meritorder@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com} # keyless Vertex env: {GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT: my-project} ``` Without Kubernetes (Cloud Run), use `--set-secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=meritorder-anthropic-api-key:latest` and run the service as a service account with `roles/aiplatform.user`. ### Azure: Key Vault Key Vault secret names allow only letters, digits, and dashes, so map them to variable names: ```bash az keyvault secret set --vault-name my-vault --name anthropic-api-key --value "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ``` ```yaml apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1 kind: ClusterSecretStore metadata: {name: azure-key-vault} spec: provider: azurekv: vaultUrl: https://my-vault.vault.azure.net authType: WorkloadIdentity serviceAccountRef: {name: external-secrets, namespace: external-secrets} --- # values.yaml externalSecret: enabled: true secretStoreRef: {kind: ClusterSecretStore, name: azure-key-vault} data: - {secretKey: MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-database-url}} - {secretKey: MERITORDER_REDIS_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-redis-url}} - {secretKey: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, remoteRef: {key: anthropic-api-key}} serviceAccount: annotations: {azure.workload.identity/client-id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000} # keyless Azure OpenAI podLabels: {azure.workload.identity/use: "true"} ``` Without Kubernetes (Container Apps), add each secret as a Key Vault reference (`--secrets name=keyvaultref:,identityref:`) and map it to an environment variable. ### Locally `.env` (git-ignored) is plain text on your disk: fine for development, not for shared machines. Compose reads it into every Merit Order container (not Postgres, Redis, or Caddy). ## Helm values worth knowing | Value | Default | Notes | |---|---|---| | `image.repository`, `image.tag` | `ghcr.io/therick/meritorder`, the chart's appVersion (`0.1.0`) | No release is published yet: build and push the image yourself and point these at it | | `env` | `{}` | Non-secret environment for every component. `MERITORDER_GATEWAY_URL` (how the worker reaches the gateway to run evals started on the console) defaults to the chart's gateway Service; set it here to override | | `externalSecret` | off | Sync the env Secret from a cloud secret store via External Secrets Operator ([Secrets](#secrets)) | | `existingSecret` | `""` | A Secret you manage with provider keys, `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`, `MERITORDER_REDIS_URL` | | `secretEnv` | `{}` | Chart-made Secret from values: for trying it out only | | `secrets.reloadOnChange` | `true` | Reloader annotation: roll pods when the Secret changes | | `secrets.mountAsFiles` | `false` | Also mount the Secret as files, for `value_file:` keys that rotate without a restart | | `configFiles` | `{}` | Files mounted over `/app/config/` | | `gateway.autoscaling` | on, 2–10 | HPA on CPU | | `controller.enabled` | `false` | Turn on with self-hosted backends; extra replicas stand by | | `controller.imageSuffix` | `-gpu` | The controller runs the image variant with SkyPilot | | `migrations.enabled` | `true` | `meritorder migrate` as a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook | | `serviceAccount.annotations`, `podLabels` | `{}` | Workload identity (IRSA, GKE, AKS) for keyless Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure OpenAI | | `metrics.serviceMonitor` | `false` | Prometheus Operator scraping `/metrics` | ## Open-source hygiene - AGPL-3.0-only license. - Multi-arch images (amd64 / arm64) for GHCR, from the release workflow (none released yet; see [Containers](#containers)). - No telemetry phone-home. """Capacity controller (docs/05-gpu-autoscaling.md).

Every interval, for each self-hosted backend with a ``serve:`` section:

1. Measure addressable demand: what traffic this model could serve costs per hour
   at API prices, and its token throughput. Free upgrades are excluded, so idle
   capacity can't keep GPUs alive by attracting traffic.
2. Size replicas: enough for throughput, but each replica must pay for itself.
   Then apply admin controls (stop, pin, stop all) and safeguards (GPU budget, fleet caps).
3. Advance the state machine (gpu.decide) and act through the provisioner.
4. Publish state, endpoint, where replicas run, and vLLM utilization to Redis for the gateways.
5. Accrue GPU cost (replicas x hourly price) and log state changes to the GPU activity log.

Only one controller is active at a time (Postgres advisory lock).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
import socket
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

from .alerts import notify
from .config import Config
from .configstore import ConfigFollower
from .gpu import (API_ONLY, Deployment, Demand, Status, addressable, decide, desired_replicas, fetch_load, make_provisioner,
                  plan_fleet)
from .state import make_state
from .store import make_store, month_start

log = logging.getLogger("meritorder.controller")
LOCK_ID = 0x4D45524954  # "MERIT"


def deployments(cfg: Config) -> list[Deployment]:
    out = []
    for b in cfg.backends:
        if b.kind != "self_hosted" or b.serve is None or not b.enabled:
            continue
        model = cfg.model(b.serve.model)
        if model is None:
            log.warning("backend %s serves unknown model %r; skipping", b.name, b.serve.model)
            continue
        out.append(Deployment(backend=b, model=model, provisioner=make_provisioner(b, cfg)))
    return out


async def tick(cfg: Config, store, state, deps: list[Deployment], now: float | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    now = now or time.time()
    wall = datetime.fromtimestamp(now, UTC)
    rows_1h = await store.demand_rows(wall - timedelta(hours=1))
    rows_15m = await store.demand_rows(wall - timedelta(minutes=15))
    controls = await store.get_setting("gpu_controls") or {}
    await state.set_json("gpu:controls", controls)  # gateways read it to stop routing to stopped GPUs right away
    guards = cfg.safeguards

    # Accrue what running replicas cost since the last cycle (you pay while provisioning and draining too).
    recs: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for dep in deps:
        b = dep.backend
        rec = await state.get_json(f"deploy:{b.name}") or {}
        last = rec.get("accrued_at") or now
        elapsed = min(max(now - last, 0), 86400)
        if rec.get("state", API_ONLY) != API_ONLY and rec.get("replicas") and elapsed:
            burn = rec.get("burn_usd_per_hour")
            burn = burn if burn is not None else rec["replicas"] * b.gpu_cost_per_hour
            cost = burn * elapsed / 3600
            await store.add_gpu_usage(b.name, wall, rec["replicas"] * elapsed, cost)
            rec["run_cost"] = (rec.get("run_cost") or 0) + cost
        rec["accrued_at"] = now
        recs[b.name] = rec
    gpu_spent = sum((await store.gpu_spend_since(month_start(wall))).values())

    sized = []
    for dep in deps:
        b, serve = dep.backend, dep.backend.serve
        cost_1h, tok_1h = addressable(dep.model, rows_1h, cfg)
        cost_15, tok_15 = addressable(dep.model, rows_15m, cfg)
        demand = Demand(usd_per_hour=max(cost_1h, cost_15 * 4), tokens_per_second=max(tok_1h / 3600, tok_15 / 900))
        price = await replica_price(dep)
        desired = desired_replicas(serve, price["usd_per_hour"], b.capacity_tokens_per_second, demand)
        sized.append((dep, demand, desired, price))
    plans = plan_fleet([{"name": d.backend.name, "desired": want, "price": price["usd_per_hour"],
                         "max_replicas": d.backend.serve.max_replicas, "value": dem.usd_per_hour} for d, dem, want, price in sized],
                       controls, guards, gpu_spent, now)

    published = []
    for dep, demand, desired, price in sized:
        b, serve = dep.backend, dep.backend.serve
        plan = plans[b.name]
        key = f"deploy:{b.name}"
        rec = recs[b.name]
        before = rec.get("state", API_ONLY)
        if before == API_ONLY and serve.provisioner != "static":
            status = Status()  # don't poll the cloud for something that isn't running
        else:
            status = await dep.provisioner.status()
        new, action = decide(rec, serve, plan.desired, status, now, force=plan.force, drain=plan.drain, why=plan.note)
        if action is not None:
            try:
                if action.kind == "up":
                    await dep.provisioner.up(action.replicas)
                elif action.kind == "scale":
                    await dep.provisioner.scale(action.replicas)
                elif action.kind == "down":
                    await dep.provisioner.down()
            except Exception as e:
                log.error("%s: %s failed: %s", b.name, action.kind, e)
                await store.gpu_event("error", b.name, "controller", {"action": action.kind, "error": str(e)[:500]})
                if action.kind == "down":
                    # Keep trying to stop it: never report a GPU as off when it may still be billing.
                    new = {**rec, "reason": f"stop failed, will retry: {e}"[:300]}
                else:
                    new.update(state=API_ONLY, since=now, endpoint=None, replicas=0, cooldown_until=now + 1800, reason=f"{action.kind} failed: {e}"[:300])
            else:
                if action.kind == "scale":
                    await store.gpu_event("scale", b.name, "controller", {"replicas": action.replicas, "reason": plan.note or "demand"})
                if action.kind == "up":
                    # A server that is already running (static) or comes up fast goes warm this cycle.
                    status = await dep.provisioner.status()
                    if status.ready:
                        new, _ = decide(new, serve, plan.desired, status, now, force=plan.force, drain=plan.drain, why=plan.note)
        if new.get("state") != API_ONLY and status.replicas_info:
            new["replicas_info"] = status.replicas_info
        # What it's costing right now: each replica's own catalog price when known, else the expected price.
        running = (new.get("replicas") or 0) if new.get("state", API_ONLY) != API_ONLY else 0
        priced = [r.get("usd_per_hour") for r in new.get("replicas_info") or [] if r.get("usd_per_hour") is not None]
        if running and len(priced) >= running:
            new["burn_usd_per_hour"] = round(sum(sorted(priced)[:running]), 4)
        else:
            new["burn_usd_per_hour"] = round(running * price["usd_per_hour"], 4)
        new["price"] = price
        if new.get("endpoint"):
            load = await fetch_load(new["endpoint"])
            if load is not None:
                await state.set_utilization(b.name, load["utilization"])
                new["utilization"] = round(load["utilization"], 3)
                new["waiting"] = load["waiting"]  # gateways bound the last-resort queue with this
                new["sampled_at"] = now
        new.update(
            backend=b.name,
            model=dep.model.name,
            desired=desired,
            planned=plan.desired,
            note=plan.note,
            demand_usd_per_hour=round(demand.usd_per_hour, 4),
            demand_tokens_per_second=round(demand.tokens_per_second, 1),
            gpu_usd_per_hour=price["usd_per_hour"],
            updated=wall.isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        )
        if new.get("state") != before:
            await store.gpu_event("state", b.name, "controller", {"from": before, "to": new["state"], "reason": new.get("reason", "")})
            await notify(f"GPU tier: {b.name} ({dep.model.name}) {before} -> {new['state']}: {new.get('reason', '')}. "
                         f"Demand ${demand.usd_per_hour:,.2f}/h at API prices vs ${price['usd_per_hour']:,.2f}/h per replica.",
                         state=state, title=f"GPU {b.name}: {new['state'].replace('_', ' ')}", level="info", page="gpus")
        await state.set_json(key, new)
        published.append(new)
        log.info("%s (%s): %s, demand $%.2f/h at API prices, %.0f tok/s, desired %d replica(s) at $%.2f/h each%s",
                 b.name, dep.model.name, new["state"], demand.usd_per_hour, demand.tokens_per_second, desired, price["usd_per_hour"],
                 f" ({plan.note})" if plan.note else "")
    return published


async def replica_price(dep: Deployment) -> dict:
    """Price of one replica for sizing decisions: SkyPilot's catalog when available, else the configured price."""
    b = dep.backend
    offer = None
    getter = getattr(dep.provisioner, "expected_price", None)
    if getter is not None:
        try:
            offer = await getter()
        except Exception as e:
            log.debug("%s: price lookup failed: %s", b.name, e)
    if offer:
        return {**offer, "source": "skypilot_catalog", "configured_usd_per_hour": b.gpu_cost_per_hour}
    return {"usd_per_hour": b.gpu_cost_per_hour, "source": "configured"}


PRICES_REQUESTED = "gpu_prices:requested"  # set by the console's "Get latest prices" when the gateway has no SkyPilot


async def publish_gpu_prices(cfg: Config, store, state) -> None:
    """Keep SkyPilot's GPU prices in the store for the break-even report, whose gateway may not have SkyPilot: when
    they're older than gpu_sizing.CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS, and right away (catalogs downloaded again) when asked."""
    from . import gpu_sizing

    asked = await state.get_json(PRICES_REQUESTED)
    catalog = await store.get_setting("gpu_catalog") or {}
    if not asked and gpu_sizing._age_hours(catalog.get("fetched_at")) <= gpu_sizing.CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS:
        return
    try:
        out = await gpu_sizing.refresh(cfg, store, sizes=False, download=bool(asked))
        log.info("GPU prices published: %s offers", out.get("offers"))
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (prices are a report's; the controller's own work goes on)
        log.warning("GPU prices couldn't be fetched: %s", e)
    if asked:
        await state.set_json(PRICES_REQUESTED, None)


async def wait_or_kick(state, interval: int, seen: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Sleep until the next cycle, waking early when an admin changes a GPU control."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + interval
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        await asyncio.sleep(min(2, max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic())))
        kick = await state.get_json("controller:kick")
        if kick and kick != seen:
            return kick
    return seen


async def run_controller(cfg: Config | None = None, once: bool = False, interval: int = 60, path: str | None = None) -> None:
    store = make_store(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL"))
    state = make_state(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_REDIS_URL"))
    if store.kind != "postgres":
        raise SystemExit("the controller needs Postgres: set MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL")
    await store.init()
    follower = ConfigFollower(store, path=path, cfg=cfg)
    cfg = await follower.current()
    deps = deployments(cfg)
    if not deps:
        log.warning("no self-hosted backends with a `serve:` section are enabled; nothing to control")
    lock_conn = await store.pool.acquire()
    try:
        while not await lock_conn.fetchval("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)", LOCK_ID):
            log.info("another controller is active; standing by")
            if once:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)
        log.info("controller is active for: %s", ", ".join(d.backend.name for d in deps) or "(none)")
        kick = await state.get_json("controller:kick")
        while True:
            try:
                latest = await follower.current()
                if latest is not cfg:
                    cfg, deps = latest, deployments(latest)
                    log.info("configuration changed; controlling: %s", ", ".join(d.backend.name for d in deps) or "(none)")
                await tick(cfg, store, state, deps)
                await publish_gpu_prices(cfg, store, state)
            except Exception:
                log.exception("controller cycle failed")
            await state.set_json("controller:heartbeat", {"at": time.time(), "host": socket.gethostname(), "interval": interval,
                                                          "deployments": [d.backend.name for d in deps]})
            if once:
                return
            kick = await wait_or_kick(state, interval, kick)
    finally:
        await store.pool.release(lock_conn)
        await store.close()
        await state.close()

import json

from conftest import ADMIN_KEY

from meritorder.evals.runner import TaskResult, grade, load_suite, run_suite, score


def reply(text="", tool=None):
    msg = {"role": "assistant", "content": text}
    if tool:
        msg["tool_calls"] = [{"id": "c1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": tool[0], "arguments": json.dumps(tool[1])}}]
    return {"choices": [{"index": 0, "message": msg, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}


def test_checks():
    assert grade({"contains": "canberra"}, reply("Canberra."))[0]
    assert not grade({"not_contains": "Dan"}, reply("Dan"))[0]
    assert grade({"equals": "OK"}, reply("OK."))[0] and not grade({"equals": "OK"}, reply("OK, sure"))[0]
    assert grade({"number": 155}, reply("2 hours 35 minutes = 155 minutes"))[0]
    assert grade({"number": 1200}, reply("1,200"))[0]
    assert grade({"json": {"name": "Maria Lopez", "age": 34}}, reply('```json\n{"name": "Maria Lopez", "age": 34}\n```'))[0]
    assert not grade({"json": {"age": 34}}, reply('{"age": "34"}'))[0]
    assert grade({"tool_call": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Oslo"}}}, reply(tool=("get_weather", {"city": "oslo"})))[0]
    assert not grade({"tool_call": {"name": "get_weather"}}, reply("It's sunny"))[0]
    zip_check = {"regex_behaves": {"match": ["12345", "98765-4321"], "reject": ["1234", "12345-678"]}}
    assert grade(zip_check, reply(r"`^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$`".strip("`")))[0]
    assert not grade(zip_check, reply(r"\d{5}.*"))[0]


def test_starter_suite_and_scoring():
    suite = load_suite()
    assert len(suite["tasks"]) == 24 and {t["task"] for t in suite["tasks"]} == {"coding", "general"}

    def results(model, passed_levels):
        return [TaskResult(model=model, task_id=f"t{lvl}", task="coding", level=lvl, passed=lvl in passed_levels) for lvl in range(1, 6)]

    s = score(results("strong", {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}) + results("mid", {1, 2, 3, 5}) + results("weak", {2, 3}))
    assert s["strong"]["tasks"]["coding"]["suggested"] == 5
    assert s["mid"]["tasks"]["coding"]["suggested"] == 3  # must clear every level up to the score
    assert s["weak"]["tasks"]["coding"]["suggested"] == 1  # floor of 1 once anything passes


async def test_run_suite_through_gateway(client, gateway):
    suite = {"name": "mini", "tasks": [
        {"id": "a", "task": "general", "level": 1, "prompt": "hello there", "checks": [{"contains": "hello"}]},
        {"id": "b", "task": "general", "level": 2, "prompt": "say banana", "checks": [{"contains": "cherry"}]}]}
    res = await run_suite("http://test", ADMIN_KEY, ["small"], suite, client=client)
    assert {r.task_id: r.passed for r in res} == {"a": True, "b": False}  # the mock echoes the prompt

from typing import Any

LEDGER_FIELDS = [
    "id", "ts", "user_id", "team", "key_id", "session_id", "tags", "client_format", "requested_model", "floor",
    "served_model", "upstream_model", "backend", "backend_kind", "status", "error", "stream", "upgraded", "proxy_cache",
    "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens", "latency_ms", "ttft_ms",
    "actual_cost", "served_api_cost", "baseline_cost", "list_cost",
    "savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache",
]
SUM_FIELDS = [
    "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens",
    "actual_cost", "served_api_cost", "baseline_cost", "list_cost",
    "savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache",
]
SAVINGS_FIELDS = ["savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache"]
GROUPS = {"user": "user_id", "team": "team", "model": "served_model", "backend": "backend", "day": "day", "hour": "hour", "month": "month", "none": None}
_TAG = re.compile(r"^tag:([A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64})$")


def hash_key(key: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()


def new_api_key() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Returns (key_id, secret). The secret is shown once and stored only as a hash."""
    return f"key_{secrets.token_hex(6)}", f"mo-{secrets.token_urlsafe(32)}"


def month_start(now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    return now.replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)


def validate_group(group_by: str) -> str:
    if group_by in GROUPS or _TAG.match(group_by):
        return group_by
    raise ValueError(f"group_by must be one of {', '.join(GROUPS)} or tag:<name>")


def _finish_row(row: dict) -> dict:
    row["savings_total"] = sum(row.get(f) or 0 for f in SAVINGS_FIELDS)
    for k, v in list(row.items()):
        if isinstance(v, float):
            row[k] = round(v, 6)
        elif isinstance(v, datetime):
            row[k] = v.isoformat()
    return row


# ====================================================================== memory


class MemoryStore:
    kind = "memory"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.keys: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.ledger: list[dict] = []

    async def init(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def migrate(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def upsert_user(self, user_id: str, team: str, role: str, email: str | None = None, display_name: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.users[user_id] = {"id": user_id, "team": team, "role": role, "email": email, "display_name": display_name}

    async def create_key(self, user_id: str, team: str, role: str, name: str | None = None, tags: dict | None = None,
                         expires_at: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key_id, secret = new_api_key()
        self.keys[hash_key(secret)] = {
            "id": key_id, "user_id": user_id, "team": team, "role": role, "name": name, "tags": tags or {},
            "created_at": datetime.now(UTC), "expires_at": expires_at, "revoked_at": None,
        }
        return key_id, secret

    async def find_key(self, key_hash: str) -> dict | None:
        return self.keys.get(key_hash)

    async def list_keys(self, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(k) for k in self.keys.values() if (user_id is None or k["user_id"] == user_id) and (team is None or k["team"] == team)]

    async def get_key(self, key_id: str) -> dict | None:
        return next((dict(k) for k in self.keys.values() if k["id"] == key_id), None)

    async def revoke_key(self, key_id: str) -> bool:
        for k in self.keys.values():
            if k["id"] == key_id and k["revoked_at"] is None:
                k["revoked_at"] = datetime.now(UTC)
                return True
        return False

    async def record(self, row: dict) -> None:
        self.ledger.append(dict(row))

    async def spend_since(self, field: str, value: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["actual_cost"] for r in self.ledger if r.get(field) == value and r["ts"] >= since)

    def _key(self, r: dict, group_by: str) -> Any:
        m = _TAG.match(group_by)
        if m:
            return (r.get("tags") or {}).get(m.group(1)) or "(untagged)"
        if group_by == "none":
            return "total"
        if group_by in ("day", "hour", "month"):
            ts: datetime = r["ts"]
            if group_by == "hour":
                return ts.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0).isoformat()
            if group_by == "day":
                return ts.date().isoformat()
            return ts.strftime("%Y-%m")
        return r.get(GROUPS[group_by])

    async def summary(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, group_by: str, user_id: str | None = None,
                      team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        validate_group(group_by)
        groups: dict[Any, dict] = defaultdict(lambda: {"requests": 0, "errors": 0, "upgraded": 0, **{f: 0 for f in SUM_FIELDS}})
        for r in self.ledger:
            if not (start <= r["ts"] < end):
                continue
            if user_id and r.get("user_id") != user_id:
                continue
            if team and r.get("team") != team:
                continue
            g = groups[self._key(r, group_by)]
            g["requests"] += 1
            g["errors"] += 1 if (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400 else 0
            g["upgraded"] += 1 if r.get("upgraded") else 0
            for f in SUM_FIELDS:
                g[f] += r.get(f) or 0
        rows = [_finish_row({"key": k, **v}) for k, v in groups.items()]
        return sorted(rows, key=lambda x: str(x["key"]))

    async def recent(self, limit: int, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        rows = [r for r in self.ledger if (not user_id or r.get("user_id") == user_id) and (not team or r.get("team") == team)]
        return [_finish_row({k: (str(v) if isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) else v) for k, v in r.items()}) for r in rows[-limit:][::-1]]

    async def needed_demand(self, model: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["served_api_cost"] for r in self.ledger if r.get("served_model") == model and not r.get("upgraded") and r["ts"] >= since)

    async def demand_by_hour(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        groups: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for r in self.ledger:
            if r["ts"] < since or r.get("upgraded") or (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400:
                continue
            hour = r["ts"].replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            k = (hour, r.get("floor"), r.get("served_model"), r.get("requested_model"))
            g = groups.setdefault(k, {"hour": hour, "floor": k[1], "served_model": k[2], "requested_model": k[3], "cost": 0.0, "tokens": 0})
            g["cost"] += r.get("served_api_cost") or 0
            g["tokens"] += sum(r.get(f) or 0 for f in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        return list(groups.values())

    async def export_rows(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, team: str | None = None):
        for r in sorted(self.ledger, key=lambda x: x["ts"]):
            if start <= r["ts"] < end and (team is None or r.get("team") == team):
                yield {k: r.get(k) for k in LEDGER_FIELDS}

    async def demand_rows(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        """Spend and tokens since ``since`` grouped by (floor, served_model, requested_model), excluding free upgrades."""
        groups: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for r in self.ledger:
            if r["ts"] < since or r.get("upgraded") or (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400:
                continue
            k = (r.get("floor"), r.get("served_model"), r.get("requested_model"))
            g = groups.setdefault(k, {"floor": k[0], "served_model": k[1], "requested_model": k[2], "cost": 0.0, "tokens": 0})
            g["cost"] += r.get("served_api_cost") or 0  # API-equivalent: stable whether or not GPUs serve it
            g["tokens"] += sum(r.get(f) or 0 for f in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        return list(groups.values())

    async def rollup(self, full: bool = False) -> int:
        return 0

    # --- config versions (the in-memory store keeps them for the life of the process)
    async def save_config(self, body: dict, author: str, comment: str | None) -> int:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("configs", [])
        vid = len(self.configs) + 1
        self.configs.append({"id": vid, "created_at": datetime.now(UTC), "author": author, "comment": comment, "body": body})
        return vid

    async def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        return (self.__dict__.get("configs") or [None])[-1]

    async def config_versions(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return [{k: v for k, v in c.items() if k != "body"} for c in reversed(self.__dict__.get("configs") or [])][:limit]

    async def get_config(self, vid: int) -> dict | None:
        return next((c for c in self.__dict__.get("configs") or [] if c["id"] == vid), None)

    async def get_setting(self, key: str):
        return self.__dict__.setdefault("settings", {}).get(key)

    async def set_setting(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("settings", {})[key] = value

    async def ensure_partitions(self) -> None:
        return None

MIGRATIONS = [(1, SCHEMA_V1), (2, SCHEMA_V2), (3, SCHEMA_V3)]

_SUMS_SQL = ", ".join(f"coalesce(sum({f}), 0) AS {f}" for f in SUM_FIELDS)


class PostgresStore:
    kind = "postgres"

    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:
        self.dsn = dsn
        self.pool = None

    async def init(self) -> None:
        import asyncpg

        async def setup(conn):
            await conn.set_type_codec("jsonb", encoder=json.dumps, decoder=json.loads, schema="pg_catalog")

        # Reports group by day/hour/month in UTC regardless of the database server's timezone.
        self.pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(self.dsn, min_size=1, max_size=10, init=setup, server_settings={"timezone": "UTC"})

    async def close(self) -> None:
        if self.pool:
            await self.pool.close()

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("SELECT 1") == 1

    async def migrate(self) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version int PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())")
            applied = {r["version"] for r in await c.fetch("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations")}
            for version, sql in MIGRATIONS:
                if version in applied:
                    continue
                async with c.transaction():
                    await c.execute(sql)
                    await c.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ($1)", version)
        await self.ensure_partitions()

    async def ensure_partitions(self, months_ahead: int = 2) -> None:
        start = month_start()
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            for i in range(months_ahead + 1):
                lo = (start + timedelta(days=32 * i)).replace(day=1)
                hi = (lo + timedelta(days=32)).replace(day=1)
                name = f"requests_{lo:%Y_%m}"
                exists = await c.fetchval("SELECT to_regclass($1)", name)
                if exists:
                    continue
                # Rows that landed in the default partition for this range must move first.
                async with c.transaction():
                    await c.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {name} (LIKE requests INCLUDING DEFAULTS)")
                    await c.execute(
                        f"WITH moved AS (DELETE FROM requests_default WHERE ts >= $1 AND ts < $2 RETURNING *) "
                        f"INSERT INTO {name} SELECT * FROM moved", lo, hi)
                    await c.execute(f"ALTER TABLE requests ATTACH PARTITION {name} FOR VALUES FROM ('{lo.isoformat()}') TO ('{hi.isoformat()}')")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- users & keys

    async def upsert_user(self, user_id, team, role, email=None, display_name=None) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                """INSERT INTO users (id, team, role, email, display_name) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5)
                   ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET team=EXCLUDED.team, role=EXCLUDED.role,
                   email=coalesce(EXCLUDED.email, users.email), display_name=coalesce(EXCLUDED.display_name, users.display_name),
                   updated_at=now()""",
                user_id, team, role, email, display_name)

    async def create_key(self, user_id, team, role, name=None, tags=None, expires_at=None) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key_id, secret = new_api_key()
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO api_keys (id, key_hash, user_id, team, role, name, tags, expires_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8)",
                key_id, hash_key(secret), user_id, team, role, name, tags or {}, expires_at)
        return key_id, secret

    async def find_key(self, key_hash: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM api_keys WHERE key_hash=$1", key_hash)
            if row:
                await c.execute("UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND (last_used_at IS NULL OR last_used_at < now() - interval '5 minutes')", row["id"])
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def list_keys(self, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        where, args = [], []
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        sql = ("SELECT id, user_id, team, role, name, tags, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, last_used_at FROM api_keys "
               + ("WHERE " + " AND ".join(where) if where else "") + " ORDER BY created_at")
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def get_key(self, key_id: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT id, user_id, team, role, name, tags, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at FROM api_keys WHERE id=$1", key_id)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def revoke_key(self, key_id: str) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            res = await c.execute("UPDATE api_keys SET revoked_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND revoked_at IS NULL", key_id)
        return res.endswith("1")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- ledger

    async def record(self, row: dict) -> None:
        cols = ", ".join(LEDGER_FIELDS)
        params = ", ".join(f"${i + 1}" for i in range(len(LEDGER_FIELDS)))
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(f"INSERT INTO requests ({cols}) VALUES ({params})", *[row.get(f) for f in LEDGER_FIELDS])

    async def spend_since(self, field: str, value: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        if field not in ("user_id", "team"):
            raise ValueError(field)
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval(f"SELECT coalesce(sum(actual_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE {field}=$1 AND ts >= $2", value, since))

    async def summary(self, start, end, group_by, user_id=None, team=None) -> list[dict]:
        validate_group(group_by)
        tag = _TAG.match(group_by)
        use_rollup = not tag and (end - start) > timedelta(days=7)
        table, ts_col = ("usage_hourly", "hour") if use_rollup else ("requests", "ts")
        if tag:
            key_expr = f"coalesce(tags->>'{tag.group(1)}', '(untagged)')"
        elif group_by == "none":
            key_expr = "'total'"
        elif group_by in ("day", "hour", "month"):
            key_expr = f"date_trunc('{group_by}', {ts_col})"
        else:
            key_expr = GROUPS[group_by]
        if use_rollup:
            counts = "coalesce(sum(requests),0) AS requests, coalesce(sum(errors),0) AS errors, coalesce(sum(upgraded),0) AS upgraded"
        else:
            counts = "count(*) AS requests, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 400) AS errors, count(*) FILTER (WHERE upgraded) AS upgraded"
        where = [f"{ts_col} >= $1", f"{ts_col} < $2"]
        args: list[Any] = [start, end]
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        sql = f"SELECT {key_expr} AS key, {counts}, {_SUMS_SQL} FROM {table} WHERE {' AND '.join(where)} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1"
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [_finish_row({k: (float(v) if k in SUM_FIELDS else v) for k, v in dict(r).items()}) for r in rows]

    async def recent(self, limit: int, user_id=None, team=None) -> list[dict]:
        where, args = [], []
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        args.append(limit)
        sql = f"SELECT * FROM requests {'WHERE ' + ' AND '.join(where) if where else ''} ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ${len(args)}"
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [_finish_row({k: (str(v) if isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) else v) for k, v in dict(r).items()}) for r in rows]

    async def demand_rows(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT floor, served_model, requested_model, coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) AS cost,
                        coalesce(sum(input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens + output_tokens),0) AS tokens
                 FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND coalesce(status,0) < 400
                 GROUP BY 1,2,3"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, since)
        return [{**dict(r), "cost": float(r["cost"]), "tokens": int(r["tokens"])} for r in rows]

    async def demand_by_hour(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hour, floor, served_model, requested_model,
                        coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) AS cost,
                        coalesce(sum(input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens + output_tokens),0) AS tokens
                 FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND coalesce(status,0) < 400
                 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, since)
        return [{**dict(r), "cost": float(r["cost"]), "tokens": int(r["tokens"])} for r in rows]

    async def export_rows(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, team: str | None = None):
        """Stream ledger rows with a server-side cursor (constant memory for big ranges)."""
        cols = ", ".join(LEDGER_FIELDS)
        sql = f"SELECT {cols} FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND ts < $2" + (" AND team = $3" if team else "") + " ORDER BY ts"
        args = [start, end] + ([team] if team else [])
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            async with c.transaction():
                async for r in c.cursor(sql, *args, prefetch=2000):
                    yield dict(r)

    async def needed_demand(self, model: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval(
                "SELECT coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE served_model=$1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND ts >= $2",
                model, since))

    # --- config versions
    async def save_config(self, body: dict, author: str, comment: str | None) -> int:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("INSERT INTO config_versions (author, comment, body) VALUES ($1,$2,$3) RETURNING id",
                                    author, comment, body)

    async def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM config_versions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1")
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def config_versions(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT id, created_at, author, comment FROM config_versions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT $1", limit)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def get_config(self, vid: int) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM config_versions WHERE id=$1", vid)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def get_setting(self, key: str):
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key=$1", key)

    async def set_setting(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES ($1,$2) ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value=EXCLUDED.value, updated_at=now()",
                            key, value)

    async def rollup(self, full: bool = False) -> int:
        """Recompute hourly rollups from the raw ledger.

        Normally the last 3 hours (late rows land within that window). With ``full``,
        or when the rollup table is empty, everything is recomputed.
        """
        sums = ", ".join(f"coalesce(sum({f}),0)" for f in SUM_FIELDS)
        cols = ", ".join(SUM_FIELDS)
        updates = ", ".join(f"{f}=EXCLUDED.{f}" for f in ["requests", "errors", "upgraded", *SUM_FIELDS])
        sql = f"""
            INSERT INTO usage_hourly (hour, user_id, team, served_model, backend, requests, errors, upgraded, {cols})
            SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts), coalesce(user_id,''), coalesce(team,''), coalesce(served_model,''), coalesce(backend,''),
                   count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 400), count(*) FILTER (WHERE upgraded), {sums}
            FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1
            GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
            ON CONFLICT (hour, user_id, team, served_model, backend) DO UPDATE SET {updates}"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            if full or not await c.fetchval("SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM usage_hourly)"):
                since = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
            else:
                since = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=3)).replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            res = await c.execute(sql, since)
        return int(res.split()[-1]) if res else 0


def make_store(database_url: str | None):
    return PostgresStore(database_url) if database_url else MemoryStore()

def sse_events(text: str) -> list[tuple[str | None, str]]:
    out = []
    for block in text.strip().split("\n\n"):
        name, data = None, []
        for line in block.split("\n"):
            if line.startswith("event: "):
                name = line[7:]
            elif line.startswith("data: "):
                data.append(line[6:])
        out.append((name, "\n".join(data)))
    return out

"""Hot-path state: session metadata, spend counters, rate limits, GPU utilization.

Redis in real deployments; an in-memory version for development and tests.
Postgres (store.py) stays the source of truth for spend; these counters are a
fast cache of it, re-seeded from Postgres when missing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from collections import deque
from typing import Any

HEALTH_FIELDS = ("requests", "errors", "latency_ms", "ttft_ms", "ttft_n")


def _live_inflight(fields: dict, gateways: dict, within: float = 20) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
    """In-flight requests per gateway per backend, from gateways seen in the last ``within`` seconds."""
    cutoff = time.time() - within
    live = {g for g, t in gateways.items() if float(t) > cutoff}
    out: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
    for field_, n in fields.items():
        gw, _, backend = field_.partition("|")
        if gw in live and int(n):
            out.setdefault(gw, {})[backend] = int(n)
    return out


class MemoryState:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._kv: dict[str, tuple[Any, float]] = {}
        self._spend: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._util: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._events: deque = deque(maxlen=500)
        self._alerts: deque = deque(maxlen=200)
        self._health: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
        self._gateways: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._inflight: dict[str, int] = {}
        self._config_version: str | None = None

    def _get(self, key: str) -> Any:
        item = self._kv.get(key)
        if item is None:
            return None
        value, expires = item
        if expires and expires < time.time():
            self._kv.pop(key, None)
            return None
        return value

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def get_session(self, sid: str) -> dict | None:
        return self._get(f"sess:{sid}")

    async def put_session(self, sid: str, data: dict, ttl: int) -> None:
        self._kv[f"sess:{sid}"] = (data, time.time() + ttl)

    async def get_spend(self, key: str) -> float | None:
        return self._spend.get(key)

    async def seed_spend(self, key: str, amount: float) -> None:
        self._spend.setdefault(key, amount)

    async def add_spend(self, keys: list[str], amount: float) -> None:
        for k in keys:
            self._spend[k] = self._spend.get(k, 0.0) + amount

    async def admit(self, spend_keys: list[str], rates: list[tuple[str, int, int]], session_id: str | None,
                    thread_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
        state_id = thread_id or session_id
        return {
            "spend": {k: self._spend.get(k) for k in spend_keys},
            "rates": {key: await self.rate_hit(key, window, amount) for key, window, amount in rates},
            "session": await self.get_session(state_id) if state_id else None,
            "session_spend": self._spend.get(f"session:{session_id}") if session_id else None,
            "util": dict(self._util),
            "inflight": _live_inflight(self._inflight, self._gateways),
        }

    async def publish_inflight(self, gateway_id: str, counts: dict[str, int]) -> None:
        self._gateways[gateway_id] = time.time()
        self._inflight.update({f"{gateway_id}|{b}": n for b, n in counts.items()})

    async def record_request(self, event: dict | None, health: tuple | None, spend_keys: list[str], amount: float) -> None:
        if event is not None:
            await self.push_event(event)
        if health is not None:
            await self.record_backend(*health)
        if amount:
            await self.add_spend(spend_keys, amount)

    async def rate_hit(self, key: str, window_seconds: int, amount: int = 1) -> int:
        bucket = f"rate:{key}:{int(time.time() // window_seconds)}"
        count = (self._get(bucket) or 0) + amount
        self._kv[bucket] = (count, time.time() + window_seconds)
        return count

    async def utilization(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        return dict(self._util)

    async def set_utilization(self, backend: str, util: float) -> None:
        self._util[backend] = util

    async def set_json(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: int = 0) -> None:
        self._kv[key] = (value, time.time() + ttl if ttl else 0)

    async def get_json(self, key: str) -> Any:
        return self._get(key)

    # --- live telemetry for the console
    async def push_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
        self._events.appendleft(event)

    async def recent_events(self, limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
        return list(self._events)[:limit]

    async def push_alert(self, alert: dict) -> None:
        self._alerts.appendleft(alert)

    async def recent_alerts(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return list(self._alerts)[:limit]

    async def record_backend(self, backend: str, ok: bool, latency_ms: int | None, ttft_ms: int | None) -> None:
        minute = int(time.time() // 60)
        h = self._health.setdefault(f"{backend}:{minute}", dict.fromkeys(HEALTH_FIELDS, 0.0))
        h["requests"] += 1
        h["errors"] += 0 if ok else 1
        h["latency_ms"] += latency_ms or 0
        if ttft_ms:
            h["ttft_ms"] += ttft_ms
            h["ttft_n"] += 1

    async def backend_health(self, backends: list[str], minutes: int = 5) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
        now = int(time.time() // 60)
        out = {}
        for b in backends:
            agg = dict.fromkeys(HEALTH_FIELDS, 0.0)
            for m in range(now - minutes + 1, now + 1):
                for k, v in self._health.get(f"{b}:{m}", {}).items():
                    agg[k] += v
            out[b] = agg
        return out

    async def heartbeat(self, gateway_id: str) -> None:
        self._gateways[gateway_id] = time.time()

    async def live_gateways(self, within: int = 20) -> int:
        return sum(1 for t in self._gateways.values() if t > time.time() - within)

    async def get_config_token(self) -> str | None:
        return self._config_version

    async def set_config_token(self, token: str) -> None:
        self._config_version = token


class RedisState:
    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        import redis.asyncio as redis

        # A blocking pool waits for a free connection instead of failing under bursts.
        pool = redis.BlockingConnectionPool.from_url(url, decode_responses=True, timeout=10,
                                                     max_connections=int(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS", "200")))
        self.r = redis.Redis(connection_pool=pool)

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return bool(await self.r.ping())

    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self.r.aclose()

    async def get_session(self, sid: str) -> dict | None:
        raw = await self.r.get(f"mo:sess:{sid}")
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else None

    async def put_session(self, sid: str, data: dict, ttl: int) -> None:
        await self.r.set(f"mo:sess:{sid}", json.dumps(data), ex=ttl)

    async def get_spend(self, key: str) -> float | None:
        raw = await self.r.get(f"mo:spend:{key}")
        return float(raw) if raw is not None else None

    async def seed_spend(self, key: str, amount: float) -> None:
        await self.r.set(f"mo:spend:{key}", amount, nx=True, ex=40 * 86400)

    async def add_spend(self, keys: list[str], amount: float) -> None:
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        for k in keys:
            pipe.incrbyfloat(f"mo:spend:{k}", amount)
            pipe.expire(f"mo:spend:{k}", 40 * 86400)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def admit(self, spend_keys: list[str], rates: list[tuple[str, int, int]], session_id: str | None,
                    thread_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
        """Everything a request needs before routing, in one round trip: spend counters, rate-limit hits
        (counted now), the conversation's routing state (``thread_id``, or the session's), the session's spend,
        and GPU utilization."""
        state_id = thread_id or session_id
        pipe = self.r.pipeline(transaction=False)
        pipe.mget([f"mo:spend:{k}" for k in spend_keys] or ["mo:spend:-"])
        now = time.time()
        for key, window, amount in rates:
            bucket = f"mo:rate:{key}:{int(now // window)}"
            pipe.incrby(bucket, amount)
            pipe.expire(bucket, window * 2)
        pipe.get(f"mo:sess:{state_id}" if state_id else "mo:sess:-")
        pipe.get(f"mo:spend:session:{session_id}" if session_id else "mo:spend:-")
        pipe.hgetall("mo:util")
        pipe.hgetall("mo:inflight")
        pipe.hgetall("mo:gateways")
        res = await pipe.execute()
        spends = res[0]
        rate_counts = res[1:1 + 2 * len(rates):2]
        sess_raw, sess_spend, util, inflight, gateways = res[1 + 2 * len(rates):]
        return {
            "inflight": _live_inflight(inflight, gateways),
            "spend": {k: (float(v) if v is not None else None) for k, v in zip(spend_keys, spends)},
            "rates": {key: int(c) for (key, _, _), c in zip(rates, rate_counts)},
            "session": json.loads(sess_raw) if state_id and sess_raw else None,
            "session_spend": float(sess_spend) if session_id and sess_spend is not None else None,
            "util": {k: float(v) for k, v in util.items()},
        }

    async def record_request(self, event: dict | None, health: tuple | None, spend_keys: list[str], amount: float) -> None:
        """After a request: feed event, backend health, and spend counters in one round trip."""
        pipe = self.r.pipeline(transaction=False)
        if event is not None:
            pipe.lpush("mo:events", json.dumps(event, default=str))
            pipe.ltrim("mo:events", 0, 499)
        if health is not None:
            backend, ok, latency_ms, ttft_ms = health
            key = f"mo:bh:{backend}:{int(time.time() // 60)}"
            pipe.hincrby(key, "requests", 1)
            if not ok:
                pipe.hincrby(key, "errors", 1)
            if latency_ms:
                pipe.hincrby(key, "latency_ms", int(latency_ms))
            if ttft_ms:
                pipe.hincrby(key, "ttft_ms", int(ttft_ms))
                pipe.hincrby(key, "ttft_n", 1)
            pipe.expire(key, 1800)
        if amount:
            for k in spend_keys:
                pipe.incrbyfloat(f"mo:spend:{k}", amount)
                pipe.expire(f"mo:spend:{k}", 40 * 86400)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def publish_inflight(self, gateway_id: str, counts: dict[str, int]) -> None:
        """Heartbeat plus this gateway's in-flight requests per backend; forget gateways gone for 2 minutes."""
        now = time.time()
        pipe = self.r.pipeline(transaction=False)
        pipe.hset("mo:gateways", gateway_id, now)
        if counts:
            pipe.hset("mo:inflight", mapping={f"{gateway_id}|{b}": n for b, n in counts.items()})
        pipe.hgetall("mo:gateways")
        pipe.hkeys("mo:inflight")
        res = await pipe.execute()
        gateways, fields = res[-2], res[-1]
        dead = {g for g, t in gateways.items() if float(t) < now - 120}
        if dead:
            pipe = self.r.pipeline(transaction=False)
            pipe.hdel("mo:gateways", *dead)
            stale = [f for f in fields if f.split("|", 1)[0] in dead]
            if stale:
                pipe.hdel("mo:inflight", *stale)
            await pipe.execute()

    async def rate_hit(self, key: str, window_seconds: int, amount: int = 1) -> int:
        bucket = f"mo:rate:{key}:{int(time.time() // window_seconds)}"
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.incrby(bucket, amount)
        pipe.expire(bucket, window_seconds * 2)
        count, _ = await pipe.execute()
        return int(count)

    async def utilization(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        raw = await self.r.hgetall("mo:util")
        return {k: float(v) for k, v in raw.items()}

    async def set_utilization(self, backend: str, util: float) -> None:
        await self.r.hset("mo:util", backend, util)

    async def set_json(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: int = 0) -> None:
        await self.r.set(f"mo:{key}", json.dumps(value), ex=ttl or None)

    async def get_json(self, key: str) -> Any:
        raw = await self.r.get(f"mo:{key}")
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else None

    # --- live telemetry for the console (shared by every gateway)
    async def push_event(self, event: dict) -> None:
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.lpush("mo:events", json.dumps(event, default=str))
        pipe.ltrim("mo:events", 0, 499)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def recent_events(self, limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
        return [json.loads(x) for x in await self.r.lrange("mo:events", 0, limit - 1)]

    async def push_alert(self, alert: dict) -> None:
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.lpush("mo:alerts", json.dumps(alert, default=str))
        pipe.ltrim("mo:alerts", 0, 199)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def recent_alerts(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return [json.loads(x) for x in await self.r.lrange("mo:alerts", 0, limit - 1)]

    async def record_backend(self, backend: str, ok: bool, latency_ms: int | None, ttft_ms: int | None) -> None:
        key = f"mo:bh:{backend}:{int(time.time() // 60)}"
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hincrby(key, "requests", 1)
        if not ok:
            pipe.hincrby(key, "errors", 1)
        if latency_ms:
            pipe.hincrby(key, "latency_ms", int(latency_ms))
        if ttft_ms:
            pipe.hincrby(key, "ttft_ms", int(ttft_ms))
            pipe.hincrby(key, "ttft_n", 1)
        pipe.expire(key, 1800)
        await pipe.execute()

    async def backend_health(self, backends: list[str], minutes: int = 5) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
        now = int(time.time() // 60)
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        for b in backends:
            for m in range(now - minutes + 1, now + 1):
                pipe.hgetall(f"mo:bh:{b}:{m}")
        results = await pipe.execute()
        out, i = {}, 0
        for b in backends:
            agg = dict.fromkeys(HEALTH_FIELDS, 0.0)
            for _ in range(minutes):
                for k, v in (results[i] or {}).items():
                    agg[k] = agg.get(k, 0.0) + float(v)
                i += 1
            out[b] = agg
        return out

    async def heartbeat(self, gateway_id: str) -> None:
        await self.r.hset("mo:gateways", gateway_id, time.time())

    async def live_gateways(self, within: int = 20) -> int:
        raw = await self.r.hgetall("mo:gateways")
        return sum(1 for t in raw.values() if float(t) > time.time() - within)

    async def get_config_token(self) -> str | None:
        return await self.r.get("mo:config_token")

    async def set_config_token(self, token: str) -> None:
        await self.r.set("mo:config_token", token)


def make_state(redis_url: str | None):
    return RedisState(redis_url) if redis_url else MemoryState()

"""Profiles: named sets of settings (production, staging, dev)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .profiles import PROFILES
from .retry import RetryPolicy


@dataclass
class Profile:
    name: str
    bank_feed_url: str
    ledger_dsn: str
    http_timeout: float = 10.0
    retries: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def retry_policy(self, service: str) -> RetryPolicy:
        """The retry policy for calls to ``service``.

        Uses the service's own entry under ``retries`` when there is one, otherwise the ``default`` entry. Entries are
        not combined: a setting the chosen entry leaves out gets RetryPolicy's default value.
        """
        settings = self.retries.get(service, self.retries.get("default", {}))
        return RetryPolicy(**settings)


def load_profile(name: str) -> Profile:
    """The ``base`` settings with the named profile's settings on top.

    Each top-level key the profile sets replaces the base value as a whole.
    """
    if name == "base" or name not in PROFILES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown profile {name!r}")
    settings = {**PROFILES["base"], **PROFILES[name]}
    return Profile(name=name, **settings)
