# 10 — How it decides Every decision Merit Order makes, in the order it makes them, with the exact rules and defaults. Each rule names the setting that controls it. The code is the source of truth: `proxy.py` (request pipeline), `router.py` (model and backend choice), `gpu.py` and `controller.py` (GPU scaling). - [A request, start to finish](#a-request-start-to-finish) - [Which model](#which-model) - [Which backend: GPU or API](#which-backend-gpu-or-api) - [When a backend fails or a model refuses](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses) - [When GPUs start, scale, and stop](#when-gpus-start-scale-and-stop) - [What happens when…](#what-happens-when) - [Every threshold in one table](#every-threshold-in-one-table) ## A request, start to finish Checks run in this order. The first one that fails ends the request with the error shown. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> K{"Valid key?
person not disabled?"} K -- "no" --> E401["401"] K -- "yes" --> B{"Org, personal, and team
monthly budgets left?"} B -- "no" --> E429a["429: which budget, how much spent"] B -- "yes" --> RL{"Within requests/tokens
per minute?"} RL -- "no" --> E429b["429 + Retry-After"] RL -- "yes" --> SC{"Session under its
spend cap?"} SC -- "no" --> E429c["429: start a new session"] SC -- "yes" --> M["Pick the model
(next section)"] M --> BK["List and rank backends
(GPU or API)"] BK -- "nothing can serve it" --> E503["503 with the reason for each route"] BK --> MR{"Worst case under
max_request_usd?"} MR -- "no candidate fits" --> E400["400: what it could cost"] MR -- "yes" --> RC{"Response cache on
and a hit?"} RC -- "hit" --> HIT["Return the cached answer ($0)"] RC -- "miss / off" --> CP["Compress huge tool outputs
(deterministic, if on)"] CP --> TRY["Try candidates in order
(failures and refusals below)"] TRY --> OK["Stream the answer back
in the client's format"] OK --> LED["Record cost, baseline, savings;
update session and spend counters"] ``` ## Which model ```mermaid flowchart TD R{"What did the
client ask for?"} R -- "a model name" --> NAMED["That model, never swapped"] R -- "auto" --> SESS{"Existing session,
same task?"} SESS -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep the session's model"] SESS -- "no: new session, new human prompt,
or the harness compacted history" --> CL["Classify the task → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] CL --> CANDS["Every chat model the team may use
with quality ≥ floor"] CANDS -- "none meets the floor" --> BEST["The best models available"] KEEP -- "it has nowhere to run
(e.g. its GPUs were stopped)" --> CL NAMED -- "it has nowhere to run" --> SUB{"Team turned on
substitute_unavailable?"} SUB -- "no" --> E503["503: why, per route;
suggests auto"] SUB -- "yes" --> EQ["Models at least as good
for this task (never weaker);
response says which was replaced"] ``` **The classifier** (rules, no model call): | Request | Floor | |---|---| | Has tools or code-like text | `coding:3` | | …with 5+ tools (an agent) | `coding:4` | | …and "hard" wording (architecture, race condition, security, performance, migration, …) or > 60k tokens of context | +1 | | Anything else | `general:2` | | …short (< 400 tokens, no tools) | `general:1` | | …analysis wording (analyze, compare, trade-offs, plan, …) or > 20k tokens of context | `general:3` | | `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | −1 / +1 | | `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | exactly that, skipping the rules | Quality scores (1–5 per task type) come from config and can be measured with `meritorder eval`. **What the client can force** | Client sends | Effect | |---|---| | A model name | That model; only the backend varies | | `reasoning_effort` / `output_config.effort` | Passed through as-is. Merit Order only picks an effort for `auto` requests that don't set one | | `X-Route-Floor`, `X-Route-Hint` | Changes the floor for `auto` | | `X-MeritOrder-Backend` | Pins the backend (admins only) | | `X-MeritOrder-Cache: off` | Skips the response cache | Team policy (allowed models and backends) applies before any of this, so nothing above can escape it. ## Which backend: GPU or API Each candidate model lists its routes (backends that serve it). A route is dropped when: | Dropped when | Why | |---|---| | The backend isn't enabled (no key, no URL) or the team may not use it | Policy and credentials | | The backend is being skipped after failures (see [When a backend fails](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses)) | Bad credentials or a network-level outage: the whole backend. Retried when the wait is up | | This model is being skipped on this backend: over capacity (429/503/529), or its deployment doesn't exist there (404) | Only that model there; the backend's other models are unaffected. A busy route is kept as a **last resort** if nothing else can take the request | | It's a GPU deployment that isn't warm (not started, starting, or stopped now) | Nothing to send to | | It's draining and this session has no warm cache there | Draining only finishes sessions already there | | It's a GPU at 100% (see [When a GPU is full](#when-a-gpu-is-full)) | Saturated: new work spills to other routes. Kept as a **last resort** if nothing else can take the request | | It's a saturated GPU whose queue is also full | No room to wait either | | `auto` and the route has no known price | An unknown price must never look free | | The model's context window is too small (prompt > 95% of it) and other models fit | Avoid a guaranteed error | | `auto` and it's a mock backend while real ones exist | Mocks are for trying things out | The rest are ranked by **what this session will cost from here**: ``` cost = rebuild + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn rebuild = 0 if the backend holds this session's cache, else context × (cache-write − cache-read price) per_turn = cached context × cache-read + new tokens × cache-write (input price for OpenAI-format backends) + ~600 output tokens × output price turns = turns so far, clamped to 3…30 (a long session is expected to keep going) ``` A **GPU's price is a shadow price**: what one token "costs" given how busy the GPU is. ```mermaid flowchart LR U{"GPU utilization"} -- "≤ 60%" --> F["2% of the same model's API price
(nearly free: it's already paid for)"] U -- "60–100%" --> RISE["Rises toward 100% of API price
(quadratically)"] U -- "100% / queueing" --> OUT["Last resort only:
used when no other route can take it"] ``` So GPUs win whenever they have room, even for a **better** model than the task needs (a "free upgrade", sent at low vLLM priority so traffic that needs that model goes first). As they fill up, APIs win again. **Then the tie-breakers:** 1. **Close on price, then quality and speed.** The same model often costs the same everywhere (Claude on Anthropic, Bedrock, Foundry and OpenRouter), so price alone can't choose. Routes that cost at most the priority's premium more than the cheapest compete on speed instead: | Priority | A faster route may cost up to | Within that range | |---|---|---| | `cost` (default) | 2% more (a tie) | the higher-quality model (`auto`), then the faster route | | `balanced` | 20% more | the faster route, then the higher-quality model | | `speed` | 100% more | the faster route, then the higher-quality model | The organization default is `routing.priority`; a team can set its own (`priority`), and a request can send `X-MeritOrder-Priority: cost|balanced|speed`. Speed is the expected time for a typical reply (`routing.est_output_tokens`, 600 tokens): time to the first token plus the writing time, both moving averages of real replies on that route (backend + upstream model). Timing starts when the route is called, so a route that took over after a failure isn't charged for it. A route is trusted after 2 replies; until then it ranks after measured ones, keeping cost order. 2. **Measuring the alternatives.** Otherwise the first route measured would win forever. Every 10th new session (`routing.speed_check_every`; 0 turns it off) can go to a route in that price range that hasn't been measured, or not in the last 10 minutes. Never mid-session, so no cache is lost. 3. **Stickiness:** a session stays on its current backend unless the cheapest one saves more than 10% + $0.01 over the rest of the session, which is usually only true once its cache has expired (5 minutes by default, `cache_ttl_seconds` per backend). That's what stops a session bouncing between Bedrock and Anthropic and paying to rebuild its cache each time. Speed never moves a session either: a warm cache is cheaper, and usually faster, than any other route. Each gateway process learns speeds from its own traffic. The console's **Backends** page shows them per model (first token, tokens per second). ## When a backend fails or a model refuses ```mermaid flowchart TD S["Send to the top candidate"] --> R{"Result"} R -- "over capacity (429/503/529),
unknown model (404), 408/409/425/500" --> NEXTM["Count a failure against this model here;
skip it on this backend for this request;
try the next"] R -- "timeout, network error, 502/504,
bad key or no access (401/403)" --> NEXT["Count a failure against the backend;
skip every candidate on it;
try the next"] R -- "200, then an error before any content
(Anthropic's in-stream overload,
an OpenRouter error chunk or body)" --> NEXTM R -- "stream sends nothing within
first_byte_timeout_seconds" --> NEXT R -- "other 4xx (bad request)" --> STOP["Return the error:
another backend would reject it too"] R -- "200, but the model refused
(before any content)" --> REF{"auto and team allows
refusal_fallback?"} REF -- "yes" --> NM["Try the next model
(refused attempt is billed and logged)"] REF -- "no" --> PASS["Return the refusal"] R -- "200" --> DONE["Respond"] NEXT --> LIM{"Candidates left?"} NEXTM --> LIM NM --> LIM LIM -- "yes" --> S LIM -- "no" --> ERR["Return the last error
(with the provider's Retry-After)"] ``` The gateway reads the start of every stream, up to its first content, before passing it on. So an error that arrives after a `200` still goes to the next source, and nothing reaches the client twice. Once content has started, an error is passed through: switching then would repeat output. How long a failing backend or model is skipped: | Failure | Skipped | For | |---|---|---| | Over capacity (429, 503, 529) | That model on that backend | The provider's `Retry-After` if it sends one, else 10 s doubling to 5 min. Still tried as a last resort | | Model or deployment not found (404) | That model on that backend | 5 min, doubling to 1 hour while it stays missing (a model not deployed there yet is checked less and less often). Turn a backend off in `.env` (`MERITORDER_BEDROCK=false`, `MERITORDER_FOUNDRY_CLAUDE=false`) until its models exist | | Credentials rejected (401, 403) | The backend | 1 min doubling to 10 min | | Anything else (5xx, timeouts, network) | The model (500) or the backend (502, 504, network) | After 3 in a row: 5 s doubling to 60 s | When something starts being skipped, an alert goes to the console's "needs attention" list, the log, and `MERITORDER_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`. It says why and where its traffic goes meanwhile. That's at most once per backend and model every 30 minutes, with a second alert when it works again. The Backends page shows what's skipped and for how long. `meritorder_failovers_total{backend,status}` counts every failed attempt, and responses served after one carry `X-MeritOrder-Failed-Over: backend/model status`. At most `max_attempts` (3) models are tried for refusals. Once a stream has started sending content to the client, a failure can't be retried: the client gets an error event, and the partial usage is still recorded. ## When GPUs start, scale, and stop The capacity controller runs every 60 s (one active at a time) and wakes immediately when an admin changes a GPU control. ```mermaid flowchart TD C0["Add up what running replicas cost
since the last cycle"] --> C1["Addressable demand for each deployment:
traffic its model is good enough for,
valued at API prices (free upgrades excluded),
max of last hour and 4 × last 15 min"] C1 --> C2["Price of one replica:
cheapest SkyPilot catalog offer in allowed
clouds/regions, else gpu_cost_per_hour"] C2 --> C3["Wanted replicas = enough for the throughput
(at 70% load), but no more than demand pays for
with a 20% margin; within min/max_replicas"] C3 --> P1{"Stop all GPUs
is on?"} P1 -- "yes" --> OFF["Stop every deployment"] P1 -- "no" --> P2{"Admin control

# 05 — GPU autoscaling Only open-weight models (Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Llama, …) can be self-hosted. Every self-hostable model is also configured with **at least one API route serving the same weights** (Bedrock, Vertex, Together, Fireworks, …). APIs are the floor; GPUs are an optimization. ## Lifecycle of a self-hosted model ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> APIOnly APIOnly --> Provisioning: forecast savings > threshold Provisioning --> Warm: health check passes, model loaded Provisioning --> APIOnly: provisioning failed / timed out Warm --> Warm: add or remove replicas Warm --> Draining: savings below threshold for hold period Draining --> Warm: demand returns Draining --> APIOnly: sessions moved or idle, GPUs released note right of APIOnly All traffic on API routes. Controller watches demand. end note note right of Provisioning 10–20+ min for big MoE models. Traffic stays on API meanwhile. end note note right of Draining No new sessions. Existing ones finish or move at free re-route moments. end note ``` ## Controller loop (every 60 s) ```mermaid flowchart TD L["Read the ledger
last 1 h and last 15 min"] --> A["Addressable demand for this model:
traffic whose quality floor it meets,
valued at API prices, free upgrades excluded"] A --> R["Desired replicas =
enough for throughput,
but each must pay for itself"] R --> SM{"State machine
api_only · provisioning · warm · draining"} SM -- "up / scale / down" --> P["Provisioner
SkyPilot (sky serve) or static"] SM --> PUB["Publish state, endpoint,
vLLM utilization → Redis"] PUB --> GW["Gateways pick it up
within 5 s"] ``` Why *addressable* demand: if the controller only counted traffic already sent to a model, a model that isn't running would never look worth starting, because `auto` routes its traffic elsewhere. So it counts what you currently pay for all traffic this model *could* serve (its quality meets the request's floor), at API-equivalent prices. That value doesn't drop when the GPUs start serving, so the controller doesn't flap. ## The break-even test ``` demand_per_hour = addressable API-equivalent spend per hour (max of the 1 h and 4 × 15 min windows) throughput = addressable tokens per second (same windows) by_load = ceil(throughput / (capacity_tokens_per_second × target_utilization)) affordable = floor(demand_per_hour / (gpu_cost_per_hour × (1 + margin))) desired_replicas = clamp(min(by_load ≥ 1, affordable), min_replicas, max_replicas) ``` State machine (`src/meritorder/gpu.py`, pure and unit-tested): | From | To | When | |---|---|---| | api_only | provisioning | `desired ≥ 1` continuously for `scale_up_after_minutes` (or `min_replicas > 0`) | | provisioning | warm | replicas answer `/v1/models` | | provisioning | api_only | failed or `provision_timeout_minutes` passed; 30-minute cooldown | | warm | warm | replica count follows `desired` | | warm | draining | `desired = 0` for `scale_up_after_minutes`, and warm for at least `hold_minutes` | | draining | warm | demand returns | | draining | api_only | after `drain_minutes`; GPUs released | Key details: - **Free upgrades don't count.** Traffic running above its floor because a GPU had headroom is excluded, so idle capacity can't keep itself alive by attracting traffic. - **Measured capacity, not benchmarks.** `capacity_tokens_per_second` should be what one replica sustains at your latency target on real agent traffic (prefill-heavy). - **Hysteresis everywhere.** Margins, minimum hold time, and the scale-up delay stop flapping. A 20-minute cold start is expensive to waste. - **Spot where it's safe.** SkyServe handles spot preemption; overflow to the API covers the gap. ## Configuring a self-hosted model ```yaml backends: gpu-qwen-coder: kind: self_hosted format: openai gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0 # one replica (here 4× H100) capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000 serve: provisioner: skypilot # or `static` for a server you already run model: qwen3-coder-next # its hf_id is what vLLM serves accelerators: "H100:4" use_spot: true clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda] image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144" max_replicas: 4 ``` The SkyPilot provisioner writes a SkyServe service (vLLM with `--enable-prefix-caching` and `--scheduling-policy priority`, fixed replica count, readiness probe on `/v1/models`) and drives `sky serve up / update / down`. It needs the `sky` CLI and cloud credentials (`sky check`). Set `HF_TOKEN` for gated models. ## Controls and safeguards The console's **GPUs** page shows, for every deployment: where each replica runs (cloud, region, zone, instance, spot or on-demand, from SkyPilot), how long it has been up, its burn rate, what this run and this month have cost, what demand would pay for it at API prices, and why the controller is doing what it's doing. An activity log records every state change, scale, and admin action with who did it. Admins can override the controller: | Control | Effect | |---|---| | **Stop** (drain first) | No new sessions; warm ones finish for up to `drain_minutes`, then the replicas go down. Skips the usual hold time | | **Stop now** | Replicas go down at once; their sessions continue on APIs (caches rebuild there) | | **Pin N replicas** | Runs N regardless of demand, skipping the scale-up wait and any failure cooldown | | **Back to automatic** | Demand decides again | | **Stop all GPUs** | Every deployment stops and none start until someone resumes the fleet | Stops and pins can expire after a set number of hours, and every one takes a reason. Gateways stop routing to a stopped deployment within seconds, before the controller acts; the controller wakes up as soon as a control changes. For a static server, Merit Order can only stop sending it traffic. Organization safeguards apply on top, to pins as well ([06](06-auth-and-spend.md#organization-wide-safeguards)): a monthly GPU budget, a fleet burn-rate cap, and a replica cap. ### What GPUs cost Prices come from **SkyPilot's catalog**, the same list prices its optimizer uses to pick a cloud: - **Before launching**, the break-even test uses the cheapest catalog offer for the deployment's accelerators within its allowed clouds and regions (spot or on-demand, per `use_spot`). - **While running**, each replica is priced for its actual cloud, region, instance type, and spot/on-demand, so a replica that lands in a pricier region costs what it really costs. - `gpu_cost_per_hour` is only a fallback, used for static servers (your own hardware) and when SkyPilot isn't installed where the controller runs. Cost is accrued every cycle from the moment provisioning starts until the replicas are down, and stored per hour (`gpu_usage`). Self-hosted tokens are charged back at the same live price. These are **list prices**, not your bill: they don't include negotiated discounts, reservations, or credits, and they leave out disks, egress, and the SkyServe controller VM. Spot prices in the catalog are refreshed periodically, not live. Reconciling against the cloud bill is on the roadmap. SkyPilot runs in its own Python environment (the `-gpu` image, built with `--build-arg SKYPILOT=`), so its dependencies never mix with the gateway's. Merit Order calls it through the `sky` CLI and, for prices, SkyPilot's Python (`MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON`, found from the `sky` command when unset). If the controller stops running while GPUs are up, the console flags it: nothing would scale them down. If a stop fails at the cloud, the deployment stays marked as running and the controller keeps retrying, so a GPU that may still be billing is never shown as off. ## Overflow ```mermaid flowchart LR REQ["New session for qwen3-coder"] --> H{"Self-hosted pool
has headroom?"} H -- "yes" --> SELF["Self-hosted replica
(cache-aware pick)"] H -- "no" --> API["Same model via API
e.g. Bedrock / Together"] API -.-> SIG["Signal controller:
saturation"] ``` Overflow applies to **new sessions** first. Existing sessions stay put unless their replica is gone or truly saturated — then they move to the cheapest warm-ish option (see [03](03-routing.md)). ## Inside the GPU pool - **Continuous batching** is the engine's job (vLLM / SGLang). The gateway sends concurrently and never serializes requests per replica. - **Cache-aware replica routing** sends a session back to the replica holding its KV cache. - **Priority scheduling**: normal traffic > opportunistic (free-upgrade) traffic. - **Engine knobs per model**: `max-num-seqs`, `max-num-batched-tokens`, chunked prefill, prefix caching (on), optional speculative decoding.

"""Durable storage: users, API keys, the per-request ledger, and report queries.

Postgres in real deployments (ledger partitioned by month, hourly rollups);
an in-memory version for development and tests. The ledger holds metadata
only, never prompt or response content.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import secrets
import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

LEDGER_FIELDS = [
    "id", "ts", "user_id", "team", "key_id", "session_id", "tags", "client_format", "requested_model", "floor",
    "served_model", "upstream_model", "backend", "backend_kind", "status", "error", "stream", "upgraded", "proxy_cache",
    "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens", "latency_ms", "ttft_ms",
    "actual_cost", "served_api_cost", "baseline_cost", "list_cost",
    "savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache",
]
SUM_FIELDS = [
    "input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens",
    "actual_cost", "served_api_cost", "baseline_cost", "list_cost",
    "savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache",
]
SAVINGS_FIELDS = ["savings_routing", "savings_caching", "savings_self_hosting", "savings_compression", "savings_response_cache"]
GROUPS = {"user": "user_id", "team": "team", "model": "served_model", "backend": "backend", "day": "day", "hour": "hour", "month": "month", "none": None}
_TAG = re.compile(r"^tag:([A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64})$")


def hash_key(key: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()


def new_api_key() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Returns (key_id, secret). The secret is shown once and stored only as a hash."""
    return f"key_{secrets.token_hex(6)}", f"mo-{secrets.token_urlsafe(32)}"


def month_start(now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime:
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    return now.replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)


def validate_group(group_by: str) -> str:
    if group_by in GROUPS or _TAG.match(group_by):
        return group_by
    raise ValueError(f"group_by must be one of {', '.join(GROUPS)} or tag:<name>")


def complete_row(row: dict) -> dict:
    """Fill what a ledger row left out with the schema's defaults: a new id, now, no tags, zero counts."""
    out = {f: row.get(f) for f in LEDGER_FIELDS}
    out["id"] = out["id"] or uuid.uuid4()
    out["ts"] = out["ts"] or datetime.now(UTC)
    out["tags"] = out["tags"] or {}
    for f in SUM_FIELDS:
        out[f] = out[f] or 0
    for f in ("stream", "upgraded", "proxy_cache"):
        out[f] = bool(out[f])
    return {**row, **out}


def _finish_row(row: dict) -> dict:
    row["savings_total"] = sum(row.get(f) or 0 for f in SAVINGS_FIELDS)
    for k, v in list(row.items()):
        if isinstance(v, float):
            row[k] = round(v, 6)
        elif isinstance(v, datetime):
            row[k] = v.isoformat()
    return row


# ====================================================================== memory


KEEP = object()  # update_user: leave this field as it is (None clears a person's monthly limit)


class MemoryStore:
    kind = "memory"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.keys: dict[str, dict] = {}
        self.ledger: list[dict] = []

    async def init(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def migrate(self) -> None:
        return None

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def upsert_user(self, user_id: str, team: str, role: str, email: str | None = None, display_name: str | None = None,
                          source: str = "idp") -> None:
        """source="idp": a login refreshes team/role unless an admin pinned them; "ensure": only create if missing."""
        u = self.users.get(user_id)
        if u is None:
            self.users[user_id] = {"id": user_id, "team": team, "role": role, "email": email, "display_name": display_name,
                                   "managed": "idp", "disabled_at": None, "budget_usd_month": None, "created_at": datetime.now(UTC)}
            return
        if source == "idp" and u.get("managed", "idp") == "idp":
            u.update(team=team, role=role)
        if email:
            u["email"] = email
        if display_name:
            u["display_name"] = display_name

    async def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> dict | None:
        u = self.users.get(user_id)
        return dict(u) if u else None

    async def update_user(self, user_id: str, team: str | None = None, role: str | None = None, disabled: bool | None = None,
                          managed: str | None = None, budget_usd_month=KEEP) -> dict | None:
        u = self.users.get(user_id)
        if u is None:
            return None
        if budget_usd_month is not KEEP:
            u["budget_usd_month"] = budget_usd_month
        if team is not None or role is not None:
            u["managed"] = "local"
        if team is not None:
            u["team"] = team
        if role is not None:
            u["role"] = role
        if managed is not None:
            u["managed"] = managed
        if disabled is not None:
            u["disabled_at"] = datetime.now(UTC) if disabled else None
        return dict(u)

    async def find_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> dict | None:
        return next((dict(u) for u in self.users.values() if (u.get("email") or "").lower() == email.lower()), None)

    async def scim_groups(self) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(g) for g in self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {}).values()]

    async def scim_group(self, gid: str) -> dict | None:
        g = self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {}).get(gid)
        return dict(g) if g else None

    async def save_scim_group(self, group: dict) -> None:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {})[group["id"]] = dict(group)

    async def delete_scim_group(self, gid: str) -> bool:
        return self.__dict__.setdefault("groups", {}).pop(gid, None) is not None

    async def list_users(self, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        out = []
        for u in self.users.values():
            if team and u["team"] != team:
                continue
            keys = [k for k in self.keys.values() if k["user_id"] == u["id"]]
            out.append({**u, "active_keys": sum(1 for k in keys if not k["revoked_at"]),
                        "last_seen": max((k.get("last_used_at") for k in keys if k.get("last_used_at")), default=None)})
        return out

    async def create_key(self, user_id: str, team: str, role: str, name: str | None = None, tags: dict | None = None,
                         expires_at: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key_id, secret = new_api_key()
        self.keys[hash_key(secret)] = {
            "id": key_id, "user_id": user_id, "team": team, "role": role, "name": name, "tags": tags or {},
            "created_at": datetime.now(UTC), "expires_at": expires_at, "revoked_at": None,
        }
        return key_id, secret

    async def find_key(self, key_hash: str) -> dict | None:
        return self.keys.get(key_hash)

    async def list_keys(self, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(k) for k in self.keys.values() if (user_id is None or k["user_id"] == user_id) and (team is None or k["team"] == team)]

    async def get_key(self, key_id: str) -> dict | None:
        return next((dict(k) for k in self.keys.values() if k["id"] == key_id), None)

    async def revoke_key(self, key_id: str) -> bool:
        for k in self.keys.values():
            if k["id"] == key_id and k["revoked_at"] is None:
                k["revoked_at"] = datetime.now(UTC)
                return True
        return False

    async def record(self, row: dict) -> None:
        self.ledger.append(complete_row(row))

    async def spend_since(self, field: str, value: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["actual_cost"] for r in self.ledger if r.get(field) == value and r["ts"] >= since)

    async def spend_all_since(self, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["actual_cost"] or 0 for r in self.ledger if r["ts"] >= since)

    # GPU time (cost of running replicas, accrued by the capacity controller) and the GPU activity log.

    async def add_gpu_usage(self, backend: str, ts: datetime, seconds: float, cost: float) -> None:
        hour = ts.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        u = self.__dict__.setdefault("_gpu_usage", {}).setdefault((hour, backend), [0.0, 0.0])
        u[0] += seconds
        u[1] += cost

    async def gpu_spend_since(self, since: datetime) -> dict[str, float]:
        out: dict[str, float] = {}
        for (hour, backend), (_, cost) in self.__dict__.get("_gpu_usage", {}).items():
            if hour >= since.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0):
                out[backend] = out.get(backend, 0.0) + cost
        return out

    async def gpu_daily(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        days: dict = {}
        for (hour, backend), (secs, cost) in self.__dict__.get("_gpu_usage", {}).items():
            if hour >= since:
                d = days.setdefault((hour.date().isoformat(), backend), [0.0, 0.0])
                d[0] += secs / 3600
                d[1] += cost
        return [{"day": k[0], "backend": k[1], "replica_hours": v[0], "cost": v[1]} for k, v in sorted(days.items())]

    async def gpu_event(self, kind: str, backend: str | None = None, actor: str | None = None, detail: dict | None = None) -> None:
        ev = self.__dict__.setdefault("_gpu_events", [])
        ev.append({"id": len(ev) + 1, "ts": datetime.now(UTC), "backend": backend, "kind": kind, "actor": actor, "detail": detail or {}})

    async def gpu_events(self, limit: int = 100, backend: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        ev = [e for e in self.__dict__.get("_gpu_events", []) if backend is None or e["backend"] == backend]
        return list(reversed(ev))[:limit]

    def _key(self, r: dict, group_by: str) -> Any:
        m = _TAG.match(group_by)
        if m:
            return (r.get("tags") or {}).get(m.group(1)) or "(untagged)"
        if group_by == "none":
            return "total"
        if group_by in ("day", "hour", "month"):
            ts: datetime = r["ts"]
            if group_by == "hour":
                return ts.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0).isoformat()
            if group_by == "day":
                return ts.date().isoformat()
            return ts.strftime("%Y-%m")
        return r.get(GROUPS[group_by])

    async def summary(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, group_by: str, user_id: str | None = None,
                      team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        validate_group(group_by)
        groups: dict[Any, dict] = defaultdict(lambda: {"requests": 0, "errors": 0, "upgraded": 0, **{f: 0 for f in SUM_FIELDS}})
        for r in self.ledger:
            if not (start <= r["ts"] < end):
                continue
            if user_id and r.get("user_id") != user_id:
                continue
            if team and r.get("team") != team:
                continue
            g = groups[self._key(r, group_by)]
            g["requests"] += 1
            g["errors"] += 1 if (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400 else 0
            g["upgraded"] += 1 if r.get("upgraded") else 0
            for f in SUM_FIELDS:
                g[f] += r.get(f) or 0
        rows = [_finish_row({"key": k, **v}) for k, v in groups.items()]
        return sorted(rows, key=lambda x: str(x["key"]))

    async def recent(self, limit: int, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        rows = [r for r in self.ledger if (not user_id or r.get("user_id") == user_id) and (not team or r.get("team") == team)]
        return [_finish_row({k: (str(v) if isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) else v) for k, v in r.items()}) for r in rows[-limit:][::-1]]

    async def needed_demand(self, model: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        return sum(r["served_api_cost"] for r in self.ledger if r.get("served_model") == model and not r.get("upgraded") and r["ts"] >= since)

    async def demand_by_hour(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        groups: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for r in self.ledger:
            if r["ts"] < since or r.get("upgraded") or (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400:
                continue
            hour = r["ts"].replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            k = (hour, r.get("floor"), r.get("served_model"), r.get("requested_model"))
            g = groups.setdefault(k, {"hour": hour, "floor": k[1], "served_model": k[2], "requested_model": k[3], "cost": 0.0, "tokens": 0})
            g["cost"] += r.get("served_api_cost") or 0
            g["tokens"] += sum(r.get(f) or 0 for f in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        return list(groups.values())

    async def export_rows(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, team: str | None = None):
        for r in sorted(self.ledger, key=lambda x: x["ts"]):
            if start <= r["ts"] < end and (team is None or r.get("team") == team):
                yield {k: r.get(k) for k in LEDGER_FIELDS}

    async def demand_rows(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        """Spend and tokens since ``since`` grouped by (floor, served_model, requested_model), excluding free upgrades."""
        groups: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for r in self.ledger:
            if r["ts"] < since or r.get("upgraded") or (r.get("status") or 0) >= 400:
                continue
            k = (r.get("floor"), r.get("served_model"), r.get("requested_model"))
            g = groups.setdefault(k, {"floor": k[0], "served_model": k[1], "requested_model": k[2], "cost": 0.0, "tokens": 0})
            g["cost"] += r.get("served_api_cost") or 0  # API-equivalent: stable whether or not GPUs serve it
            g["tokens"] += sum(r.get(f) or 0 for f in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_tokens", "cache_write_tokens", "output_tokens"))
        return list(groups.values())

    async def rollup(self, full: bool = False) -> int:
        return 0

    # --- config versions (the in-memory store keeps them for the life of the process)
    async def save_config(self, body: dict, author: str, comment: str | None) -> int:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("configs", [])
        vid = len(self.configs) + 1
        self.configs.append({"id": vid, "created_at": datetime.now(UTC), "author": author, "comment": comment, "body": body})
        return vid

    async def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        return (self.__dict__.get("configs") or [None])[-1]

    async def config_versions(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        return [{k: v for k, v in c.items() if k != "body"} for c in reversed(self.__dict__.get("configs") or [])][:limit]

    async def get_config(self, vid: int) -> dict | None:
        return next((c for c in self.__dict__.get("configs") or [] if c["id"] == vid), None)

    async def get_setting(self, key: str):
        return self.__dict__.setdefault("settings", {}).get(key)

    async def set_setting(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        self.__dict__.setdefault("settings", {})[key] = value

    async def ensure_partitions(self) -> None:
        return None

class PostgresStore:
    kind = "postgres"

    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:
        self.dsn = dsn
        self.pool = None

    async def init(self) -> None:
        import asyncpg

        async def setup(conn):
            await conn.set_type_codec("jsonb", encoder=json.dumps, decoder=json.loads, schema="pg_catalog")

        # Reports group by day/hour/month in UTC regardless of the database server's timezone.
        # Per process. Behind many gateway processes, put PgBouncer in front so the total stays within max_connections.
        size = int(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DB_POOL_SIZE", "10"))
        self.pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(self.dsn, min_size=1, max_size=size, init=setup, server_settings={"timezone": "UTC"})

    async def close(self) -> None:
        if self.pool:
            await self.pool.close()

    async def ping(self) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("SELECT 1") == 1

    async def migrate(self) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version int PRIMARY KEY, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())")
            applied = {r["version"] for r in await c.fetch("SELECT version FROM schema_migrations")}
            for version, sql in MIGRATIONS:
                if version in applied:
                    continue
                async with c.transaction():
                    await c.execute(sql)
                    await c.execute("INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES ($1)", version)
        await self.ensure_partitions()

    async def ensure_partitions(self, months_ahead: int = 2) -> None:
        start = month_start()
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            for i in range(months_ahead + 1):
                lo = (start + timedelta(days=32 * i)).replace(day=1)
                hi = (lo + timedelta(days=32)).replace(day=1)
                name = f"requests_{lo:%Y_%m}"
                exists = await c.fetchval("SELECT to_regclass($1)", name)
                if exists:
                    continue
                # Rows that landed in the default partition for this range must move first.
                async with c.transaction():
                    await c.execute(f"CREATE TABLE {name} (LIKE requests INCLUDING DEFAULTS)")
                    await c.execute(
                        f"WITH moved AS (DELETE FROM requests_default WHERE ts >= $1 AND ts < $2 RETURNING *) "
                        f"INSERT INTO {name} SELECT * FROM moved", lo, hi)
                    await c.execute(f"ALTER TABLE requests ATTACH PARTITION {name} FOR VALUES FROM ('{lo.isoformat()}') TO ('{hi.isoformat()}')")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- users & keys

    async def upsert_user(self, user_id, team, role, email=None, display_name=None, source: str = "idp") -> None:
        """source="idp": a login refreshes team/role unless an admin pinned them; "ensure": only create if missing."""
        refresh = "team=EXCLUDED.team, role=EXCLUDED.role," if source == "idp" else ""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                """INSERT INTO users (id, team, role, email, display_name) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5)
                   ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
                   team=CASE WHEN users.managed='idp' AND $6 THEN EXCLUDED.team ELSE users.team END,
                   role=CASE WHEN users.managed='idp' AND $6 THEN EXCLUDED.role ELSE users.role END,
                   email=coalesce(EXCLUDED.email, users.email), display_name=coalesce(EXCLUDED.display_name, users.display_name),
                   updated_at=now()""",
                user_id, team, role, email, display_name, bool(refresh))

    async def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=$1", user_id)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def update_user(self, user_id, team=None, role=None, disabled=None, managed=None, budget_usd_month=KEEP) -> dict | None:
        sets, args = [], [user_id]
        if budget_usd_month is not KEEP:
            args.append(budget_usd_month)
            sets.append(f"budget_usd_month=${len(args)}")
        if team is not None:
            args.append(team)
            sets.append(f"team=${len(args)}")
        if role is not None:
            args.append(role)
            sets.append(f"role=${len(args)}")
        if (team is not None or role is not None) and managed is None:
            sets.append("managed='local'")  # an admin's edit sticks across IdP logins, unless told to follow the IdP
        if managed is not None:
            args.append(managed)
            sets.append(f"managed=${len(args)}")
        if disabled is not None:
            sets.append("disabled_at=now()" if disabled else "disabled_at=NULL")
        if not sets:
            return await self.get_user(user_id)
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow(f"UPDATE users SET {', '.join(sets)}, updated_at=now() WHERE id=$1 RETURNING *", *args)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def find_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM users WHERE lower(email)=lower($1) LIMIT 1", email)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def scim_groups(self) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return [dict(r) for r in await c.fetch("SELECT * FROM scim_groups ORDER BY display_name")]

    async def scim_group(self, gid: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM scim_groups WHERE id=$1", gid)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def save_scim_group(self, group: dict) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                """INSERT INTO scim_groups (id, display_name, external_id, members) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)
                   ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET display_name=EXCLUDED.display_name, external_id=EXCLUDED.external_id,
                   members=EXCLUDED.members, updated_at=now()""",
                group["id"], group["display_name"], group.get("external_id"), group.get("members") or [])

    async def delete_scim_group(self, gid: str) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return (await c.execute("DELETE FROM scim_groups WHERE id=$1", gid)).endswith("1")

    async def list_users(self, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT u.*, count(k.id) FILTER (WHERE k.revoked_at IS NULL) AS active_keys, max(k.last_used_at) AS last_seen
                 FROM users u LEFT JOIN api_keys k ON k.user_id = u.id""" + (" WHERE u.team = $1" if team else "") + """
                 GROUP BY u.id ORDER BY u.id"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *([team] if team else []))
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def create_key(self, user_id, team, role, name=None, tags=None, expires_at=None) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key_id, secret = new_api_key()
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO api_keys (id, key_hash, user_id, team, role, name, tags, expires_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8)",
                key_id, hash_key(secret), user_id, team, role, name, tags or {}, expires_at)
        return key_id, secret

    async def find_key(self, key_hash: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM api_keys WHERE key_hash=$1", key_hash)
            if row:
                await c.execute("UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND (last_used_at IS NULL OR last_used_at < now() - interval '5 minutes')", row["id"])
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def list_keys(self, user_id: str | None = None, team: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        where, args = [], []
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        sql = ("SELECT id, user_id, team, role, name, tags, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, last_used_at FROM api_keys "
               + ("WHERE " + " AND ".join(where) if where else "") + " ORDER BY created_at")
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def get_key(self, key_id: str) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT id, user_id, team, role, name, tags, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at FROM api_keys WHERE id=$1", key_id)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def revoke_key(self, key_id: str) -> bool:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            res = await c.execute("UPDATE api_keys SET revoked_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND revoked_at IS NULL", key_id)
        return res.endswith("1")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- ledger

    async def record(self, row: dict) -> None:
        cols = ", ".join(LEDGER_FIELDS)
        params = ", ".join(f"${i + 1}" for i in range(len(LEDGER_FIELDS)))
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = complete_row(row)
            await c.execute(f"INSERT INTO requests ({cols}) VALUES ({params})", *[row[f] for f in LEDGER_FIELDS])

    async def spend_since(self, field: str, value: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        if field not in ("user_id", "team"):
            raise ValueError(field)
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval(f"SELECT coalesce(sum(actual_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE {field}=$1 AND ts >= $2", value, since))

    async def spend_all_since(self, since: datetime) -> float:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval("SELECT coalesce(sum(actual_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1", since))

    async def add_gpu_usage(self, backend: str, ts: datetime, seconds: float, cost: float) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO gpu_usage (hour, backend, replica_seconds, cost) VALUES (date_trunc('hour', $1::timestamptz), $2, $3, $4) "
                "ON CONFLICT (hour, backend) DO UPDATE SET replica_seconds = gpu_usage.replica_seconds + EXCLUDED.replica_seconds, "
                "cost = gpu_usage.cost + EXCLUDED.cost", ts, backend, seconds, cost)

    async def gpu_spend_since(self, since: datetime) -> dict[str, float]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT backend, sum(cost) AS cost FROM gpu_usage WHERE hour >= date_trunc('hour', $1::timestamptz) GROUP BY backend", since)
        return {r["backend"]: float(r["cost"]) for r in rows}

    async def gpu_daily(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT date_trunc('day', hour)::date AS day, backend, sum(replica_seconds)/3600 AS replica_hours, sum(cost) AS cost "
                                 "FROM gpu_usage WHERE hour >= $1 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2", since)
        return [{"day": r["day"].isoformat(), "backend": r["backend"], "replica_hours": float(r["replica_hours"]), "cost": float(r["cost"])} for r in rows]

    async def gpu_event(self, kind: str, backend: str | None = None, actor: str | None = None, detail: dict | None = None) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("INSERT INTO gpu_events (kind, backend, actor, detail) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)", kind, backend, actor, detail or {})

    async def gpu_events(self, limit: int = 100, backend: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT * FROM gpu_events WHERE ($2::text IS NULL OR backend = $2) ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT $1", limit, backend)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def summary(self, start, end, group_by, user_id=None, team=None) -> list[dict]:
        validate_group(group_by)
        tag = _TAG.match(group_by)
        use_rollup = not tag and (end - start) > timedelta(days=7)
        table, ts_col = ("usage_hourly", "hour") if use_rollup else ("requests", "ts")
        if tag:
            key_expr = f"coalesce(tags->>'{tag.group(1)}', '(untagged)')"
        elif group_by == "none":
            key_expr = "'total'"
        elif group_by in ("day", "hour", "month"):
            key_expr = f"date_trunc('{group_by}', {ts_col})"
        else:
            key_expr = GROUPS[group_by]
        if use_rollup:
            counts = "coalesce(sum(requests),0) AS requests, coalesce(sum(errors),0) AS errors, coalesce(sum(upgraded),0) AS upgraded"
        else:
            counts = "count(*) AS requests, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 400) AS errors, count(*) FILTER (WHERE upgraded) AS upgraded"
        where = [f"{ts_col} >= $1", f"{ts_col} < $2"]
        args: list[Any] = [start, end]
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        sql = f"SELECT {key_expr} AS key, {counts}, {_SUMS_SQL} FROM {table} WHERE {' AND '.join(where)} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1"
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [_finish_row({k: (float(v) if k in SUM_FIELDS else v) for k, v in dict(r).items()}) for r in rows]

    async def recent(self, limit: int, user_id=None, team=None) -> list[dict]:
        where, args = [], []
        if user_id:
            args.append(user_id)
            where.append(f"user_id = ${len(args)}")
        if team:
            args.append(team)
            where.append(f"team = ${len(args)}")
        args.append(limit)
        sql = f"SELECT * FROM requests {'WHERE ' + ' AND '.join(where) if where else ''} ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ${len(args)}"
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, *args)
        return [_finish_row({k: (str(v) if isinstance(v, uuid.UUID) else v) for k, v in dict(r).items()}) for r in rows]

    async def demand_rows(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT floor, served_model, requested_model, coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) AS cost,
                        coalesce(sum(input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens + output_tokens),0) AS tokens
                 FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND coalesce(status,0) < 400
                 GROUP BY 1,2,3"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, since)
        return [{**dict(r), "cost": float(r["cost"]), "tokens": int(r["tokens"])} for r in rows]

    async def demand_by_hour(self, since: datetime) -> list[dict]:
        sql = """SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hour, floor, served_model, requested_model,
                        coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) AS cost,
                        coalesce(sum(input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens + output_tokens),0) AS tokens
                 FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND coalesce(status,0) < 400
                 GROUP BY 1,2,3,4"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch(sql, since)
        return [{**dict(r), "cost": float(r["cost"]), "tokens": int(r["tokens"])} for r in rows]

    async def export_rows(self, start: datetime, end: datetime, team: str | None = None):
        """Stream ledger rows with a server-side cursor (constant memory for big ranges)."""
        cols = ", ".join(LEDGER_FIELDS)
        sql = f"SELECT {cols} FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1 AND ts < $2" + (" AND team = $3" if team else "") + " ORDER BY ts"
        args = [start, end] + ([team] if team else [])
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            async with c.transaction():
                async for r in c.cursor(sql, *args, prefetch=2000):
                    yield dict(r)

    async def needed_demand(self, model: str, since: datetime) -> float:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return float(await c.fetchval(
                "SELECT coalesce(sum(served_api_cost),0) FROM requests WHERE served_model=$1 AND NOT coalesce(upgraded,false) AND ts >= $2",
                model, since))

    # --- config versions
    async def save_config(self, body: dict, author: str, comment: str | None) -> int:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("INSERT INTO config_versions (author, comment, body) VALUES ($1,$2,$3) RETURNING id",
                                    author, comment, body)

    async def active_config(self) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM config_versions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1")
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def config_versions(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            rows = await c.fetch("SELECT id, created_at, author, comment FROM config_versions ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT $1", limit)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    async def get_config(self, vid: int) -> dict | None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            row = await c.fetchrow("SELECT * FROM config_versions WHERE id=$1", vid)
        return dict(row) if row else None

    async def get_setting(self, key: str):
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            return await c.fetchval("SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key=$1", key)

    async def set_setting(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            await c.execute("INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES ($1,$2) ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value=EXCLUDED.value, updated_at=now()",
                            key, value)

    async def rollup(self, full: bool = False) -> int:
        """Recompute hourly rollups from the raw ledger.

        Normally the last 3 hours (late rows land within that window). With ``full``,
        or when the rollup table is empty, everything is recomputed.
        """
        sums = ", ".join(f"coalesce(sum({f}),0)" for f in SUM_FIELDS)
        cols = ", ".join(SUM_FIELDS)
        updates = ", ".join(f"{f}=EXCLUDED.{f}" for f in ["requests", "errors", "upgraded", *SUM_FIELDS])
        sql = f"""
            INSERT INTO usage_hourly (hour, user_id, team, served_model, backend, requests, errors, upgraded, {cols})
            SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts), coalesce(user_id,''), coalesce(team,''), coalesce(served_model,''), coalesce(backend,''),
                   count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 400), count(*) FILTER (WHERE upgraded), {sums}
            FROM requests WHERE ts >= $1
            GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
            ON CONFLICT (hour, user_id, team, served_model, backend) DO UPDATE SET {updates}"""
        async with self.pool.acquire() as c:
            if full or not await c.fetchval("SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM usage_hourly)"):
                since = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
            else:
                since = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=3)).replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            res = await c.execute(sql, since)
        return int(res.split()[-1]) if res else 0


def make_store(database_url: str | None):
    return PostgresStore(database_url) if database_url else MemoryStore()

# Merit Order

An open-source LLM gateway that cuts LLM spend for day-to-day use, without changing how
people work.

Power grids dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest marginal cost first, with expensive
peaker plants switched on only when demand requires them. Merit Order does the same with tokens:

- **Routes** every session to the cheapest model and backend that meets the task's quality bar,
  counting what it would cost to rebuild the prompt cache somewhere else.
- **Runs open-weight models on your own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when steady load makes that cheaper
  than paying per token, and turns them off when it doesn't. APIs (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex,
  Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, ...) are always there for overflow.
- **Saves tokens**: automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, cache-safe compression of huge tool
  outputs, and an optional response cache.
- **Shows the money**: every request is recorded with what it cost and what it would have cost
  without Merit Order, broken down by cause, per user, team, project, and day.

Point Claude Code, pi, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or anything that speaks either API at it.

## Quickstart (no keys needed)

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env            # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY (and any provider keys you have)
uv run meritorder serve         # http://localhost:8080; console at /ui/ once built (see Development)
```

```bash
curl localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $MERITORDER_DEV_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}'
```

With no provider keys, requests go to built-in mock backends. `uv run meritorder check` shows
which backends and models are live with the keys you've set. Without `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`,
storage is in memory; use Docker Compose for the real thing.

## Run the full stack with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add at least one provider key
docker compose up -d            # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080
docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin
```

Bedrock with your AWS profile (including SSO): `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d`.
Kubernetes: `helm install mo charts/meritorder` (see [docs/07-deployment.md](docs/07-deployment.md)).
No image is published yet, so push your own build and set `image.repository` and `image.tag`.

## Point your harness at it

```bash
meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com   # Entra sign-in; or: meritorder use-key <key>
meritorder setup pi                                    # adds a "meritorder" provider to pi
meritorder setup claude-code                           # gateway URL, key helper, model auto, context window
meritorder setup claude-code --config-dir ~/.claude-meritorder   # same, in a separate Claude Code profile
```

Or by hand: OpenAI-compatible clients use base URL `<gateway>/v1`; Claude Code uses
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>` (plus `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` for a model name it doesn't know,
and `CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1`). Use `model: "auto"` to let Merit Order choose, or name a model
(`claude-sonnet`, `kimi-k3.1`, `qwen3-coder`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, ...) to pin it. Each tool keeps
its own API format; Merit Order translates when the chosen model speaks the other one. How it all fits
together: [docs/00-how-it-all-works.md](docs/00-how-it-all-works.md).

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Session-Id` | Groups requests into a session (pi sends it; Claude Code's own session id is used; otherwise inferred) |
| `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | Minimum quality for `auto` routing |
| `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges `auto` routing down or up |
| `X-MeritOrder-Priority: cost` / `balanced` / `speed` | How much more a faster route may cost (2%, 20%, 100%) |
| `X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=foo` | Cost-allocation tags for reports |
| `X-MeritOrder-Cache: on` / `off` | Use or bypass the response cache |
| `X-MeritOrder-Backend: <name>` | Admins only: pin a backend (testing, debugging) |

Responses carry `x-meritorder-model`, `x-meritorder-backend`, and (non-streaming)
`x-meritorder-cost-usd` / `x-meritorder-savings-usd`. A model you name is never swapped for
another unless your team opted in to substitution when it can't run; reasoning effort you set is
always passed through. Every routing and scaling rule, as diagrams:
[docs/10-how-it-decides.md](docs/10-how-it-decides.md).

## What's in the box

| Area | Built |
|---|---|
| APIs | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (stateless), Anthropic Messages, and embeddings; streaming and not; pass-through when formats match, translation when they don't |
| Backends | Anthropic, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Vertex AI (Claude and Gemini), Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, xAI, OpenRouter (incl. opt-in free tier), DeepSeek, Mistral, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, any OpenAI-compatible server |
| Models | Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, and an open-weight catalog: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen3-Coder, MiniMax, MiMo, Muse, Llama, Mistral/Devstral, Gemma, Nemotron, gpt-oss; embedding models |
| Routing | Rule-based classifier → quality floor; marginal-cost router with cache rebuild cost, context-window checks (a session that outgrows its model moves to one with room), sticky sessions, fallback across backends and on refusals; live prices (OpenRouter's catalog and LiteLLM's price list, every 15 minutes); quality scores from Epoch AI's benchmark data by default, refreshed daily, or measured on your own tasks with `meritorder eval` |
| GPUs | Break-even controller (addressable demand, hysteresis), SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM provisioner, static servers, utilization from vLLM metrics, spill to API when saturated (live in-flight counts; a GPU that's the only route queues, bounded); console shows where each replica runs, uptime, burn rate, and cost, with stop / drain / pin / stop-all controls and an activity log |
| Savings | Automatic prompt caching, lower reasoning effort for simple `auto` tasks (stable per session), deterministic tool-output compression, opt-in response cache |
| Identity | Virtual API keys, Entra/OIDC device-code login with group → team/role mapping, SCIM provisioning, roles (user, team lead, finance, admin), People page to move, pin, or disable anyone (applies to existing keys within a minute) |
| Spend | Organization, team, and user monthly budgets, GPU budget and fleet caps, a per-request cost ceiling, per-session spend caps (stops runaway agents), requests/tokens-per-minute limits, policy allow/deny lists for models and backends; all editable on the console's Controls page |
| Control panel | Web console at `/ui/` (Mantine, dark by default): live Dispatch view (merit-order stack from real traffic, live request feed, backend health, GPU fleet, needs-attention), Reports, GPUs (incl. what-if and controls), Controls (budgets and safeguards against spend), Backends, Models (incl. Evals and GPU break-even by quality level and model), Teams, People, Keys, and Config (forms for teams, models, backends, routing, and access plus raw YAML; validate, version history, restore; hot-reloads every gateway) |
| Reporting | Ledger with savings by cause, reports API, CSV, JSONL/CSV ledger export to a file or S3, `meritorder usage`, Prometheus metrics, budget/spike alerts, weekly digests |
| Deployment | Docker Compose, Helm chart, CI (tests, audits, Helm lint, Compose smoke test), a release workflow for signed multi-arch images (no release tagged yet) |

Not yet: reconciliation against provider and cloud bills (OpenRouter costs already come from what it
billed), Kubernetes-native GPU provisioning (llm-d/KServe), a learned router, Parquet export. See
[docs/](docs/README.md) for the design, [how it decides](docs/10-how-it-decides.md), and
[the decisions](docs/09-decisions.md).

## Development

```bash
uv sync && uv run pytest                     # gateway (in-memory state and storage)
cd ui && npm ci && npm run build             # console (served at /ui/)
cd ui && npx playwright install chromium && E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://… npm run e2e   # console browser tests
uv run python scripts/fake_vllm.py           # a stand-in vLLM server for the GPU path
uv run python scripts/smoke_providers.py     # test every enabled provider through a running gateway
```

To also run the gateway, storage, and state tests against real Redis and Postgres (CI does, with a
95% coverage floor), point these at a throwaway Redis database and Postgres database; both are
wiped before each test:

```bash
MERITORDER_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/15 \
MERITORDER_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:pw@localhost:5432/motest \
uv run pytest --cov
```

"""Reports API (docs/08-reporting.md). Metadata only; never prompt content.

Who sees what:
* user       -> their own usage
* team_lead  -> their team
* finance    -> everything, aggregated (no per-request detail)
* admin      -> everything
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import json
from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, timedelta

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, Response, StreamingResponse

from .auth import AuthError, Principal
from .store import SUM_FIELDS, month_start, validate_group

COUNT_FIELDS = ["requests", "errors", "upgraded"]


def _parse_day(value: str | None, default: datetime) -> datetime:
    if not value:
        return default
    try:
        return datetime.combine(date.fromisoformat(value), datetime.min.time(), tzinfo=UTC)
    except ValueError:
        raise HTTPException(400, f"dates must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {value!r}")


def _scope(p: Principal, user: str | None, team: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Clamp the requested filters to what this principal may see."""
    if p.at_least("finance"):
        return user, team
    if p.role == "team_lead":
        return user, p.team
    return p.user_id, None


def _totals(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    t = {f: 0 for f in COUNT_FIELDS + SUM_FIELDS + ["savings_total"]}
    for r in rows:
        for f in t:
            t[f] += r.get(f) or 0
    return {k: round(v, 6) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in t.items()}


def build_router(gateway) -> APIRouter:
    router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1/reports", tags=["reports"])

    async def principal(request: Request) -> Principal:
        try:
            return await gateway.authn.authenticate({k.lower(): v for k, v in request.headers.items()})
        except AuthError as e:
            raise HTTPException(e.status, e.message)

    async def summary_rows(p, start, end, group_by, user, team):
        try:
            validate_group(group_by)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise HTTPException(400, str(e))
        user, team = _scope(p, user, team)
        rows = await gateway.store.summary(start, end, group_by, user_id=user, team=team)
        return rows, user, team

    @router.get("/summary")
    async def summary(
        request: Request,
        start: str | None = Query(None, description="YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (default: first of this month)"),
        end: str | None = Query(None, description="YYYY-MM-DD, exclusive (default: tomorrow)"),
        group_by: str = Query("model", description="user, team, model, backend, day, hour, month, none, or tag:<name>"),
        user: str | None = None,
        team: str | None = None,
    ):
        p = await principal(request)
        s = _parse_day(start, month_start())
        e = _parse_day(end, datetime.now(UTC).replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(days=1))
        rows, user, team = await summary_rows(p, s, e, group_by, user, team)
        return {"start": s.isoformat(), "end": e.isoformat(), "group_by": group_by, "user": user, "team": team,
                "rows": rows, "totals": _totals(rows)}

    @router.get("/summary.csv")
    async def summary_csv(request: Request, start: str | None = None, end: str | None = None, group_by: str = "model",
                          user: str | None = None, team: str | None = None):
        p = await principal(request)
        s = _parse_day(start, month_start())
        e = _parse_day(end, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1))
        rows, _, _ = await summary_rows(p, s, e, group_by, user, team)
        buf = io.StringIO()
        fields = ["key"] + COUNT_FIELDS + SUM_FIELDS + ["savings_total"]
        w = csv.DictWriter(buf, fieldnames=fields, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
        return Response(buf.getvalue(), media_type="text/csv",
                        headers={"content-disposition": f'attachment; filename="meritorder-{group_by.replace(":", "-")}.csv"'})

    @router.get("/me")
    async def me(request: Request):
        p = await principal(request)
        team_cfg = gateway.cfg.team(p.team)
        start = month_start()
        rows = await gateway.store.summary(start, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1), "model", user_id=p.user_id)
        totals = _totals(rows)
        return {
            "user": p.user_id,
            "team": p.team,
            "role": p.role,
            "month": start.strftime("%Y-%m"),
            "spend_usd": round(await gateway.spend("user", p.user_id), 6),
            "budget_usd": team_cfg.user_budget_usd_month,
            "team_spend_usd": round(await gateway.spend("team", p.team), 6) if p.at_least("team_lead") else None,
            "team_budget_usd": team_cfg.budget_usd_month,
            "baseline_usd": totals["baseline_cost"],
            "savings_usd": totals["savings_total"],
            "requests": totals["requests"],
            "by_model": rows,
        }

"""Capacity controller (docs/05-gpu-autoscaling.md).

Every interval, for each self-hosted backend with a ``serve:`` section:

1. Measure addressable demand: what traffic this model could serve costs per hour
   at API prices, and its token throughput. Free upgrades are excluded, so idle
   capacity can't keep GPUs alive by attracting traffic.
2. Size replicas: enough for throughput, but each replica must pay for itself.
3. Advance the state machine (gpu.decide) and act through the provisioner.
4. Publish state, endpoint, and vLLM utilization to Redis for the gateways.

Only one controller is active at a time (Postgres advisory lock).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

from .alerts import notify
from .config import Config
from .gpu import API_ONLY, Deployment, Demand, Status, addressable, decide, desired_replicas, fetch_utilization, make_provisioner
from .state import make_state
from .store import make_store

log = logging.getLogger("meritorder.controller")
LOCK_ID = 0x4D45524954  # "MERIT"


def deployments(cfg: Config) -> list[Deployment]:
    out = []
    for b in cfg.backends:
        if b.kind != "self_hosted" or b.serve is None or not b.enabled:
            continue
        model = cfg.model(b.serve.model)
        if model is None:
            log.warning("backend %s serves unknown model %r; skipping", b.name, b.serve.model)
            continue
        out.append(Deployment(backend=b, model=model, provisioner=make_provisioner(b, cfg)))
    return out


async def tick(cfg: Config, store, state, deps: list[Deployment], now: float | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    now = now or time.time()
    wall = datetime.fromtimestamp(now, UTC)
    rows_1h = await store.demand_rows(wall - timedelta(hours=1))
    rows_15m = await store.demand_rows(wall - timedelta(minutes=15))
    published = []
    for dep in deps:
        b, serve = dep.backend, dep.backend.serve
        cost_1h, tok_1h = addressable(dep.model, rows_1h, cfg)
        cost_15, tok_15 = addressable(dep.model, rows_15m, cfg)
        demand = Demand(usd_per_hour=max(cost_1h, cost_15 * 4), tokens_per_second=max(tok_1h / 3600, tok_15 / 900))
        desired = desired_replicas(serve, b.gpu_cost_per_hour, b.capacity_tokens_per_second, demand)

        key = f"deploy:{b.name}"
        rec = await state.get_json(key) or {}
        if rec.get("state", API_ONLY) == API_ONLY and serve.provisioner != "static":
            status = Status()  # don't poll the cloud for something that isn't running
        else:
            status = await dep.provisioner.status()
        new, action = decide(rec, serve, desired, status, now)
        if action is not None:
            try:
                if action.kind == "up":
                    await dep.provisioner.up(action.replicas)
                elif action.kind == "scale":
                    await dep.provisioner.scale(action.replicas)
                elif action.kind == "down":
                    await dep.provisioner.down()
            except Exception as e:
                log.error("%s: %s failed: %s", b.name, action.kind, e)
                new.update(state=API_ONLY, since=now, endpoint=None, replicas=0, cooldown_until=now + 1800, reason=f"{action.kind} failed: {e}"[:300])
            else:
                if action.kind == "up":
                    # A server that is already running (static) or comes up fast goes warm this cycle.
                    status = await dep.provisioner.status()
                    if status.ready:
                        new, _ = decide(new, serve, desired, status, now)
        if new.get("endpoint"):
            util = await fetch_utilization(new["endpoint"])
            if util is not None:
                await state.set_utilization(b.name, util)
                new["utilization"] = round(util, 3)
        new.update(
            backend=b.name,
            model=dep.model.name,
            desired=desired,
            demand_usd_per_hour=round(demand.usd_per_hour, 4),
            demand_tokens_per_second=round(demand.tokens_per_second, 1),
            gpu_usd_per_hour=b.gpu_cost_per_hour,
            updated=wall.isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        )
        if new.get("state") != rec.get("state", API_ONLY):
            await notify(f"GPU tier: {b.name} ({dep.model.name}) {rec.get('state', API_ONLY)} -> {new['state']}: {new.get('reason', '')}. "
                         f"Demand ${demand.usd_per_hour:,.2f}/h at API prices vs ${b.gpu_cost_per_hour:,.2f}/h per replica.",
                         state=state, title=f"GPU {b.name}: {new['state'].replace('_', ' ')}", level="info", page="gpus")
        await state.set_json(key, new)
        published.append(new)
        log.info("%s (%s): %s, demand $%.2f/h at API prices, %.0f tok/s, desired %d replica(s) at $%.2f/h each",
                 b.name, dep.model.name, new["state"], demand.usd_per_hour, demand.tokens_per_second, desired, b.gpu_cost_per_hour)
    return published


async def run_controller(cfg: Config, once: bool = False, interval: int = 60) -> None:
    store = make_store(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL"))
    state = make_state(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_REDIS_URL"))
    if store.kind != "postgres":
        raise SystemExit("the controller needs Postgres: set MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL")
    deps = deployments(cfg)
    if not deps:
        log.warning("no self-hosted backends with a `serve:` section are enabled; nothing to control")
    await store.init()
    lock_conn = await store.pool.acquire()
    try:
        while not await lock_conn.fetchval("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)", LOCK_ID):
            log.info("another controller is active; standing by")
            if once:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)
        log.info("controller is active for: %s", ", ".join(d.backend.name for d in deps) or "(none)")
        while True:
            try:
                await tick(cfg, store, state, deps)
            except Exception:
                log.exception("controller cycle failed")
            if once:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)
    finally:
        await store.pool.release(lock_conn)
        await store.close()
        await state.close()
