"""Quality scores from published benchmarks: Epoch AI's ability scale (or the Artificial Analysis index), each model's
chance on a reference task, the best-anchored or worst-to-best scale, overrides, and the worker keeping them live."""

import copy
import io
import json
import math
import zipfile

import httpx
import pytest
from conftest import ADMIN_KEY, TEST_CONFIG, auth

from meritorder import catalog, cli, live_prices, quality_data as qd
from meritorder.config import build_config
from meritorder.state import MemoryState
from meritorder.store import MemoryStore


@pytest.fixture
def durable(gateway):
    """The admin refresh needs a durable store; the in-memory one behaves the same here."""
    kind = gateway.store.kind
    gateway.store.kind = "postgres"
    yield gateway
    gateway.store.kind = kind


def epoch_zip(**extra) -> bytes:
    files = {
        "epoch_capabilities_index/eci_scores.csv": "Model,Display name,eci,eci_ci_low,eci_ci_high\nx,Claude Top 1,170,167,173\nx,Claude Mid 1,165,162,168\n"
                                                   "x,Cheap Model,150,148,152\n",
        "epoch_capabilities_index/edi_scores.csv": "benchmark_name,is_anchor,benchmark_release_date,edi,estimated_slope_scaled\nFrontierSWE,False,2026-09-02,165,0.16\n"
                                                   "FrontierCode,False,2026-06-08,164,0.086\n",
        "frontierswe_external.csv": "Model version,Harness,Score\nclaude-top-1_max,h,0.70\nclaude-top-1_high,h,0.66\nclaude-mid-1_max,h,0.62\n",
        "frontiercode_external.csv": "Model version,Main score,Harness\nclaude-mid-1_medium,0.40,h\nnot a number,x,h\n",
        **extra,
    }
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as z:
        for name, text in files.items():
            z.writestr(name, text)
    return buf.getvalue()


def config(**quality):
    raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
    raw["models"] = {
        **raw["models"],
        "top": {"quality": {"coding": 3, "general": 3}, "routes": [{"backend": "mock-anthropic", "model": "claude-top-1"}]},
        "mid": {"aliases": ["Claude Mid 1"], "routes": [{"backend": "mock-anthropic", "model": "claude-mid-1-20260101"}]},
        "cheap": {"benchmark_name": "Cheap Model", "quality": {"coding": 2}, "quality_override": {"general": 4.5}, "routes": [{"backend": "mock-openai", "model": "c-1"}]},
    }
    raw["quality"] = {"source": "epoch", "scale": "best", **quality}
    return build_config(raw, prices_data={}, quiet=True)


def test_epoch_data_becomes_chances_on_the_reference_task():
    data = qd.parse_epoch(epoch_zip())
    assert data["eci"]["claude-top-1"] == 170 and data["difficulty"]["FrontierSWE"] == (165.0, 0.16)
    assert sorted(data["results"]["FrontierSWE"]["claude-top-1"]) == [("high", 0.66), ("max", 0.70)]
    assert data["results"]["FrontierCode"] == {"claude-mid-1": [("medium", 0.40)]}  # "Main score"; junk rows skipped

    cfg = config()
    m = qd.epoch_measures(cfg, data, "high")
    top = m["top"]["coding"]
    assert top["evidence"]["FrontierSWE"]["variant"] == "high"  # the effort it's routed with, when published
    assert top["ability"] == pytest.approx(165 + math.log(0.66 / 0.34) / 0.16, abs=0.01) and top["basis"] == "results on FrontierSWE"
    assert m["top"]["general"]["basis"] == "Epoch Capabilities Index" and m["top"]["general"]["chance"] == pytest.approx(1 / (1 + math.exp(-0.16 * 5)), abs=1e-3)
    mid = m["mid"]["coding"]  # two benchmarks of different difficulty: averaged on the ability scale
    assert set(mid["evidence"]) == {"FrontierSWE", "FrontierCode"}
    assert mid["ability"] == pytest.approx((mid["evidence"]["FrontierSWE"]["ability"] + mid["evidence"]["FrontierCode"]["ability"]) / 2, abs=0.01)
    assert "cheap" in m and "small" not in m  # matched by benchmark_name; unknown models aren't guessed
    assert qd.model_keys(cfg.model("mid")) >= {"claude-mid-1-20260101", "claude-mid-1"}

    best = qd.scores(m, "best")
    assert best["top"]["general"] == 5.0 and best["cheap"]["general"] == 1.0  # floor of 1: any model may take level-1 work
    assert 1.0 < best["mid"]["general"] < 5.0
    spread = qd.scores(m, "range")
    assert spread["top"]["general"] == 5.0 and spread["cheap"]["general"] == 1.0
    assert qd.scores({"a": {"coding": {"chance": 0.3}}}, "range") == {"a": {"coding": 5.0}}  # one model: it's the best


def test_scores_reach_the_models_with_overrides_and_fallbacks():
    cfg = config()
    q = qd.refresh_quality(cfg, epoch=qd.parse_epoch(epoch_zip()))
    assert q["status"]["ok"] and q["attribution"].startswith("Epoch AI") and "big" in q["missing"] and "mock-large" not in q["missing"]
    loaded = config()
    from meritorder.config import apply_quality
    apply_quality(loaded, {"quality": q})
    top, cheap, big = loaded.model("top"), loaded.model("cheap"), loaded.model("big")
    assert top.quality["general"] == 5.0 and top.quality_sources == {"coding": "epoch", "general": "epoch"}
    assert cheap.quality["general"] == 4.5 and cheap.quality_sources["general"] == "override"  # set by hand: always wins
    assert big.quality == {"coding": 5, "general": 5} and big.quality_sources == {"coding": "config", "general": "config"}  # not covered

    other = config(scale="range")  # scores worked out on another scale aren't used until they're redone
    apply_quality(other, {"quality": q})
    assert other.model("top").quality == {"coding": 3, "general": 3} and other.model("top").quality_sources["coding"] == "config"
    by_hand = config(source="config")
    apply_quality(by_hand, {"quality": q})
    assert by_hand.model("top").quality == {"coding": 3, "general": 3}


def test_artificial_analysis_and_failures(monkeypatch):
    cfg = config(source="artificial_analysis")
    assert qd.refresh_quality(cfg)["status"]["error"].startswith("ValueError: set ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY")
    pages = {1: {"data": [{"slug": "claude-top-1", "name": "Claude Top 1", "evaluations": {"artificial_analysis_intelligence_index": 70}},
                          {"slug": "x", "name": "X", "evaluations": {"artificial_analysis_intelligence_index": None}}], "pagination": {"has_more": True}},
             2: {"data": [{"slug": "cheap-model", "name": "Cheap Model", "evaluations": {"artificial_analysis_intelligence_index": 35}}], "pagination": {"has_more": False}}}
    seen = []

    def fake_get(url, params=None, headers=None, timeout=None, **kw):
        seen.append((url, params, headers))
        return httpx.Response(200, json=pages[params["page"]], request=httpx.Request("GET", url))
    monkeypatch.setattr(qd.httpx, "get", fake_get)
    q = qd.refresh_quality(cfg, aa_key="k")
    assert seen[0][2] == {"x-api-key": "k"} and len(seen) == 2
    assert q["scores"]["top"] == {"coding": 5.0, "general": 5.0} and q["scores"]["cheap"]["coding"] == 2.5  # half the best's index
    assert q["measures"]["top"]["general"]["basis"] == "Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index"

    def down(*a, **k):
        raise httpx.ConnectError("offline")
    monkeypatch.setattr(qd.httpx, "get", down)
    failed = qd.refresh_quality(config())
    assert not failed["status"]["ok"] and "offline" in failed["status"]["error"] and failed["scores"] == {}
    assert qd.refresh_quality(config(source="config"))["missing"] == []


async def test_the_worker_keeps_scores_live():
    cfg, store, state = config(), MemoryStore(), MemoryState()
    data = {"zip": epoch_zip()}

    def fetch(c, epoch, aa, key):
        return qd.refresh_quality(c, epoch=qd.parse_epoch(data["zip"]))
    assert (await qd.refresh_quality_once(cfg, store, state, fetch))["stored"] is False  # no live catalog yet: prices first
    await store.set_setting("prices", {"updated": "p1", "prices": {"mock-openai:small-1": {"input": 1, "output": 2}}})
    first = await qd.refresh_quality_once(cfg, store, state, fetch)
    doc = await store.get_setting("prices")
    assert first["stored"] and doc["prices"] and doc["quality"]["scores"]["top"]["general"] == 5.0  # prices kept alongside
    assert await state.get_config_token() == f"file:p1:{doc['quality']['updated']}"

    data["zip"] = epoch_zip(**{"epoch_capabilities_index/eci_scores.csv": "Model,Display name,eci\nx,Claude Top 1,170\nx,Claude Mid 1,169\nx,Cheap Model,150\n"})
    moved = await qd.refresh_quality_once(cfg, store, state, fetch)
    assert any(c.startswith("mid general") for c in moved["changed"]) and any(a["title"] == "Quality scores changed" for a in await state.recent_alerts())

    def broken(c, epoch, aa, key):
        return {**qd.refresh_quality(config(source="config")), "source": "epoch", "status": {"ok": False, "error": "HTTP 503"}}
    kept = await qd.refresh_quality_once(cfg, store, state, broken)
    assert not kept["ok"] and (await store.get_setting("prices"))["quality"]["scores"]["top"]["general"] == 5.0  # the last good ones
    assert any(a["title"] == "Quality scores not refreshed" for a in await state.recent_alerts())

    refresher, calls = qd.QualityRefresher(), []

    def counting(c, epoch, aa, key):
        calls.append(1)
        return fetch(c, epoch, aa, key)
    await refresher.maybe(cfg, store, state, 100.0, counting)
    assert await refresher.maybe(cfg, store, state, 200.0, counting) is None  # not due for a day
    await refresher.maybe(config(scale="range"), store, state, 300.0, counting)  # the settings changed: right away
    assert len(calls) == 2

    def boom(c, epoch, aa, key):
        raise RuntimeError("bug")
    assert await qd.QualityRefresher().maybe(cfg, store, state, 1.0, boom) is None

    def prices_fetch(c, path, write):
        return catalog.refresh_prices(c, {"data": []}, write=False, litellm={})
    await live_prices.refresh_once(cfg, store, state, prices_fetch)
    assert (await store.get_setting("prices"))["quality"]["scores"]  # a price refresh keeps the scores


def test_the_cli_writes_scores_into_prices_json(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
    raw["models"]["top"] = {"routes": [{"backend": "mock-anthropic", "model": "claude-top-1"}]}
    (tmp_path / "meritorder.yaml").write_text(json.dumps(raw))
    (tmp_path / "prices.json").write_text(json.dumps({"quality": {"source": "epoch", "scale": "best", "scores": {"top": {"coding": 1.0}}}}))
    monkeypatch.setattr(catalog.httpx, "get", lambda url, **k: httpx.Response(200, json={"data": []}, request=httpx.Request("GET", url)))
    monkeypatch.setattr(qd, "fetch_epoch", lambda: qd.parse_epoch(epoch_zip()))
    cli.main(["prices", "refresh", "--config", str(tmp_path / "meritorder.yaml")])
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    data = json.loads((tmp_path / "prices.json").read_text())
    assert "Quality scores for 1 models from epoch" in out and data["quality"]["scores"]["top"]["coding"] == 5.0
    assert build_config(raw, tmp_path, quiet=True).model("top").quality_sources == {"general": "epoch", "coding": "epoch"}

    monkeypatch.setattr(qd, "fetch_epoch", lambda: (_ for _ in ()).throw(httpx.ConnectError("offline")))
    cli.main(["prices", "refresh", "--config", str(tmp_path / "meritorder.yaml")])
    assert "Quality scores not refreshed" in capsys.readouterr().out
    assert json.loads((tmp_path / "prices.json").read_text())["quality"]["scores"]["top"]["coding"] == 5.0  # kept


async def test_admin_api_shows_and_refreshes_scores(durable, client, monkeypatch):
    def fake(c, epoch=None, aa=None, aa_key=None):
        return {"updated": "u1", "source": "epoch", "scale": "best", "reference": dict(c.quality.reference), "status": {"ok": True},
                "attribution": qd.ATTRIBUTION["epoch"], "scores": {"small": {"coding": 2.4}}, "measures": {"small": {"coding": {"chance": 0.3, "basis": "b", "evidence": {}}}},

# 07 — Deployment Goal: **clone, add one API key, `docker compose up`, point pi at it.** Everything else is an opt-in layer. ## Two supported ways to run it The same container images run under **Docker Compose** or **Kubernetes (Helm chart)**. Each organization picks one. | | Docker Compose | Kubernetes (Helm) | |---|---|---| | **For** | Trying it out, small teams, a single VM | Production at organizations with real spend | | **Setup** | `docker compose up`, minutes | Needs a cluster and Helm | | **High availability** | One machine | Multiple gateways, restarts, rolling upgrades | | **Scaling** | Manual | Gateway autoscales | | **Postgres / Redis** | Containers in the compose file | Usually managed cloud services | | **Secrets** | `.env` | A Secret synced from your cloud's store by External Secrets ([Secrets](#secrets)) | What keeps supporting both cheap: - **No Kubernetes-specific code in the app.** Config is env vars plus one YAML file, health checks are plain HTTP (`/healthz`, `/readyz`), logs go to stdout. - **One active controller, enforced by a Postgres advisory lock.** Works the same under both. - **Migrations are a command** (`meritorder migrate`): a one-off service in Compose, a pre-install / pre-upgrade hook in Helm. - **CI checks both** on every change: a Compose smoke test (build, start, send requests) and a Helm lint plus schema validation of the rendered manifests (kubeconform). - Nomad, ECS, Docker Swarm, etc. can be community recipes; they aren't officially supported. Where GPUs run is a separate choice. SkyPilot can start GPU VMs on clouds and neoclouds, or target an existing Kubernetes cluster with GPUs, from either deployment style. ## Containers One image, `ghcr.io/therick/meritorder`, runs every Merit Order process; the command picks which. | Service | Image and command | Required? | |---|---|---| | gateway | `meritorder serve`: APIs, console at `/ui/`, reports, admin, SCIM | Yes | | worker | `meritorder worker`: rollups, partitions, alerts, digests | Yes, for reports and alerts | | migrate | `meritorder migrate`, once per upgrade | Yes | | controller | `meritorder controller` on the **`-gpu` image variant**, which adds SkyPilot in its own environment (`--build-arg SKYPILOT=`) | Only for the GPU tier | | postgres | People, keys, config versions, ledger, GPU cost | Yes | | redis | Sessions, counters, GPU state, live feed | Yes | | caddy (profile: tls) | HTTPS for single-machine installs | No | The SkyPilot controller needs cloud credentials and keeps state in `~/.sky`: mount them into the controller (commented example in `compose.yaml`) or point it at a SkyPilot API server. For local testing without a cloud, `scripts/fake_vllm.py` stands in for a GPU server (`provisioner: static`). ## Topology: laptop / single VM ```mermaid flowchart LR pi["pi / Claude Code"] --> gw subgraph compose["docker compose"] gw["gateway"] pg[("postgres")] rd[("redis")] wk["worker"] ctl["controller
(profile: gpu, -gpu image)"] gw --> pg gw --> rd wk --> pg ctl --> pg ctl --> rd end gw --> own["Your own vLLM server
(provisioner: static)"] gw --> apis["API backends
Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry / OpenRouter"] ctl --> sky["SkyPilot → cloud GPUs"] gw --> sky ``` ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/therick/meritorder && cd meritorder cp .env.example .env # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY and at least one provider key docker compose up -d # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080, UI at /ui/ docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin ``` Turning on more: ```bash docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d # use your ~/.aws profile (incl. SSO) for Bedrock docker compose --profile gpu up -d # adds the GPU capacity controller docker compose --profile tls up -d # adds Caddy for HTTPS on one machine ``` Entra: set `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`. ## Topology: production (Kubernetes) ```mermaid flowchart LR users["Harnesses / apps"] --> ing["Ingress / LB"] subgraph k8s["Kubernetes (Helm chart)"] ing --> gw1["gateway"] ing --> gw2["gateway"] ing --> gw3["gateway"] ctl["controller, -gpu image
(1 active: Postgres lock)"] end gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> rd[("Managed Redis")] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> pg[("Managed Postgres")] ctl --> pg ctl --> skyapi["SkyPilot API server"] skyapi --> gpus["GPU clusters
any cloud / neocloud"] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> gpus gw1 & gw2 & gw3 --> apis["API backends"] gw1 & gw2 & gw3 -.-> otel["OpenTelemetry →
Grafana / Datadog / ..."] ``` - Gateways are stateless; scale with HPA on CPU. - One controller is active at a time, enforced by a Postgres advisory lock; a standby is fine. - Same images as Compose. ## Performance and scaling Measured against zero-latency mock backends with real Postgres and Redis (one laptop, Apple M4 Max), so the numbers are Merit Order's own work. The benchmark is in `scripts/bench_gateway.py`. **Added latency per call** (before the request goes upstream; the same for time to first token on streams): | Request | Merit Order's own time | |---|---| | Chat with a short or 2k-token prompt | ~0.6 ms | | Agent turn: 30k tokens of history + tools | ~2 ms | | Agent turn: 120k tokens of history + tools | ~6.5 ms (mostly parsing and hashing a ~500 KB body) | Add the network hop to the gateway, and **two Redis round trips** (one pipeline for budgets, rate limits, session, and GPU load and in-flight counts; one to save the session). With a managed Redis in the same zone, that's about 0.5–2 ms. Ledger writes, spend counters, and telemetry happen after the response, in one more pipeline. For comparison, models take 0.3–2 s to first token, and many seconds to prefill 120k tokens. **Throughput:** about **1,100 requests/s per process** (one CPU core); it scales nearly linearly with processes (7,100 requests/s with 8 on one machine that was also running Redis, Postgres, and the load generator). Gateways share nothing but Redis and Postgres, so add pods or `--workers` (`MERITORDER_WORKERS`) to scale. Long streams are cheap to hold open: what limits a process is CPU per request, not open connections. A rough sizing for 10,000 requests/s: 10–16 gateway cores, one Redis node (~20 commands per request in three pipelines), and Postgres taking 10,000 ledger inserts/s, the first part that would need work (batched inserts) at that scale. For perspective, an organization spending $300k a month on LLMs makes about 5–50 requests/s. Connection pools, all per process: | Pool | Default | Setting | |---|---|---| | Upstream, per backend (each stream holds one connection) | 500 | `MERITORDER_UPSTREAM_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `MERITORDER_UPSTREAM_KEEPALIVE` (100) | | Redis (waits for a free connection rather than failing) | 200 | `MERITORDER_REDIS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | | Postgres | 10 | `MERITORDER_DB_POOL_SIZE`; with many processes, put PgBouncer in front | Request bodies are capped at 32 MB (`MERITORDER_MAX_BODY_MB`; Anthropic's own limit), 64 KB for sign-in, and 1 MB for SCIM; larger ones get a 413 before anything reads them. ## Ingress and TLS Merit Order is a plain HTTP service. It runs behind whatever the organization already uses: a cloud load balancer, an existing ingress controller, NGINX, Envoy. We don't ship or require a proxy in front of it. Single-machine installs that want HTTPS can enable the Caddy profile. What's exposed: Docker Compose publishes the gateway on `127.0.0.1` (set `MERITORDER_BIND=0.0.0.0` to open it to your network). Behind a public ingress, `/metrics` is reachable too; it shows spend and traffic totals, not prompts or users, but set `MERITORDER_METRICS_TOKEN` (and Helm `metrics.tokenKey`) to require a token. The console is served with a strict Content-Security-Policy and refuses to be framed. ## Configuration `config/meritorder.yaml` (plus `include:`d files and environment variables for secrets) describes everything. The image ships the default config; override files with a volume (Compose) or `--set-file configFiles.=...` (Helm). ```yaml baseline_model: claude-sonnet # counterfactual for savings reports include: [models-open.yaml] # open-weight catalog, direct vendor APIs backends: bedrock: format: anthropic base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"} models: claude-sonnet: aliases: ["claude-sonnet-*"] quality: {coding: 5, general: 4} routes: - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}} - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}} teams: platform: budget_usd_month: 20000 user_budget_usd_month: 500 allowed_models: ["*"] allowed_backends: ["*", "!openrouter-free"] compression: {enabled: true} ``` Useful commands: | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `meritorder check` | Which backends and models are usable with the current credentials | | `meritorder prices refresh` | Write the live prices, context windows and output limits to `prices.json` (the worker keeps the stored ones current on its own) | | `meritorder models discover` | List the model IDs each enabled backend serves | | `meritorder keys create / list / revoke` | Manage API keys | | `meritorder login`, `meritorder setup pi` / `claude-code` | Sign in with Entra and point a harness at the gateway | | `meritorder usage` | Your own spend | | `meritorder eval --models a,b [--apply]` | Measure quality scores with graded tasks (asks before spending) | | `meritorder export --out file.csv` or `s3://…` | Export the ledger | | `meritorder worker --backfill` | Rebuild hourly report rollups from the raw ledger | | `meritorder controller [--once] [--interval 60]` | Run the GPU capacity controller | Once the first configuration is saved from the console, the stored version (in Postgres) is what gateways, the worker, and the controller use; the YAML file is the starting point and the format for import and export. ## Secrets Merit Order never stores provider keys. It reads them from the environment (`value_env`) or from a file (`value_file`), and a configuration saved from the console is refused if it contains a literal key, so keys never reach Postgres or the config history. What it does store: | Secret | Where | How | |---|---|---| | Provider keys | Environment or a mounted file | Supplied by the platform from your secret store | | `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`, `MERITORDER_REDIS_URL` | Environment | Same Secret as the provider keys | | Merit Order keys (`mo-…`) for people and harnesses | Postgres | Shown once; stored only as a SHA-256 hash (random 256-bit tokens, so a slow hash isn't needed) | | Entra / OIDC tokens | Not stored | Verified against the issuer's signing keys, then exchanged for a short-lived `mo-` key | **The best key is no key.** For each cloud's own models, use the workload's identity instead: | Models | Config | Identity | |---|---|---| | Claude in Bedrock | `auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: …}` | IRSA or EKS Pod Identity: a role allowed to invoke the Bedrock models you route to | | Claude on Vertex | `auth: {type: google}` | GKE Workload Identity: a Google service account with `roles/aiplatform.user` | | Azure OpenAI, Foundry | `auth: {type: azure_ad}` | AKS Workload Identity: a managed identity with *Cognitive Services OpenAI User* (or the Foundry equivalent) on the resource | The image includes the Google and Azure identity libraries. In Helm, put the identity on the service account (`serviceAccount.annotations`; AKS also needs the pod label `podLabels: {azure.workload.identity/use: "true"}`). Third-party providers (Anthropic direct, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, Mistral) always need a key. ### Kubernetes: three ways to provide the Secret Every component reads its environment from one Secret. Set exactly one of these (the chart refuses more than one): | Value | What it does | Use for | |---|---|---| | `externalSecret.enabled` | The chart creates an `ExternalSecret`; [External Secrets Operator](https://external-secrets.io) syncs it from AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Vault, … | Production (recommended) | | `existingSecret` | Use a Secret you create and manage some other way (Sealed Secrets, SOPS, CSI sync, by hand) | Production | | `secretEnv` | The chart creates the Secret from Helm values | Trying it out only: the values end up in Helm's release history (one Secret per revision) and in whatever values file you passed | The `ExternalSecret` is a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook, because the migration hook needs `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL` before anything else starts. Its synced Secret is kept across upgrades; delete it by hand after `helm uninstall`. ### Rotating keys | Approach | Values | What happens when a key changes | |---|---|---| | **Rolling restart** (default) | `secrets.reloadOnChange: true` and [Stakater Reloader](https://github.com/stakater/Reloader) installed in the cluster | Reloader rolls the gateways, worker, and controller; pods start with the new environment. Works for every secret, including the database and Redis URLs | | **No restart** | `secrets.mountAsFiles: true`, and `value_file:` on each backend's `auth` | The Secret is also mounted as files under `/run/secrets/meritorder/`; Kubernetes refreshes them about a minute after the Secret changes, and the next request uses the new key. Provider keys only | With External Secrets, a rotation in the cloud store reaches the Secret within `externalSecret.refreshInterval` (default 1 h; lower it, or annotate the ExternalSecret with `force-sync` to pull at once). For zero-restart rotation of provider keys: ```yaml # values.yaml secrets: {mountAsFiles: true, reloadOnChange: false} ``` ```yaml # meritorder.yaml: the file when it's there, the environment otherwise (so the same config works locally) backends: openrouter: auth: {type: api_key, value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/OPENROUTER_API_KEY, value_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY} ``` Keep the old key valid until the new one is everywhere (most providers allow two keys at once), then revoke it. ### AWS: Secrets Manager One JSON secret holding every variable: ```bash aws secretsmanager create-secret --name meritorder/prod --secret-string '{ "MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://…", "MERITORDER_REDIS_URL": "rediss://…", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "…", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY": "…"}' ``` ```yaml # Once per cluster. ESO's own service account has an IRSA role allowed to read meritorder/*. apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1 kind: ClusterSecretStore metadata: {name: aws-secrets-manager} spec: provider: aws: {service: SecretsManager, region: us-east-1} --- # values.yaml externalSecret: enabled: true secretStoreRef: {kind: ClusterSecretStore, name: aws-secrets-manager} dataFrom: - extract: {key: meritorder/prod} # every JSON key becomes an environment variable serviceAccount: annotations: {eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/meritorder} # keyless Bedrock ``` Without Kubernetes (ECS), put the same secret ARNs in the task definition's `secrets` (`valueFrom`) and give the task role the Bedrock permissions. ### GCP: Secret Manager Secret Manager holds one value per secret, so map each one: ```bash printf '%s' "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | gcloud secrets create meritorder-anthropic-api-key --data-file=- ``` ```yaml apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1 kind: ClusterSecretStore metadata: {name: gcp-secret-manager} spec: provider: gcpsm: {projectID: my-project} # ESO authenticates with its own Workload Identity --- # values.yaml externalSecret: enabled: true secretStoreRef: {kind: ClusterSecretStore, name: gcp-secret-manager} data: - {secretKey: MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-database-url}} - {secretKey: MERITORDER_REDIS_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-redis-url}} - {secretKey: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-anthropic-api-key}} serviceAccount: annotations: {iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: meritorder@my-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com} # keyless Vertex env: {GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT: my-project} ``` Without Kubernetes (Cloud Run), use `--set-secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=meritorder-anthropic-api-key:latest` and run the service as a service account with `roles/aiplatform.user`. ### Azure: Key Vault Key Vault secret names allow only letters, digits, and dashes, so map them to variable names: ```bash az keyvault secret set --vault-name my-vault --name anthropic-api-key --value "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ``` ```yaml apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1 kind: ClusterSecretStore metadata: {name: azure-key-vault} spec: provider: azurekv: vaultUrl: https://my-vault.vault.azure.net authType: WorkloadIdentity serviceAccountRef: {name: external-secrets, namespace: external-secrets} --- # values.yaml externalSecret: enabled: true secretStoreRef: {kind: ClusterSecretStore, name: azure-key-vault} data: - {secretKey: MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-database-url}} - {secretKey: MERITORDER_REDIS_URL, remoteRef: {key: meritorder-redis-url}} - {secretKey: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, remoteRef: {key: anthropic-api-key}} serviceAccount: annotations: {azure.workload.identity/client-id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000} # keyless Azure OpenAI podLabels: {azure.workload.identity/use: "true"} ``` Without Kubernetes (Container Apps), add each secret as a Key Vault reference (`--secrets name=keyvaultref:,identityref:`) and map it to an environment variable. ### Locally `.env` (git-ignored) is plain text on your disk: fine for development, not for shared machines. Compose reads it into every container. ## Helm values worth knowing | Value | Default | Notes | |---|---|---| | `externalSecret` | off | Sync the env Secret from a cloud secret store via External Secrets Operator ([Secrets](#secrets)) | | `existingSecret` | `""` | A Secret you manage with provider keys, `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`, `MERITORDER_REDIS_URL` | | `secretEnv` | `{}` | Chart-made Secret from values: for trying it out only | | `secrets.reloadOnChange` | `true` | Reloader annotation: roll pods when the Secret changes | | `secrets.mountAsFiles` | `false` | Also mount the Secret as files, for `value_file:` keys that rotate without a restart | | `configFiles` | `{}` | Files mounted over `/app/config/` | | `gateway.autoscaling` | on, 2–10 | HPA on CPU | | `controller.enabled` | `false` | Turn on with self-hosted backends; extra replicas stand by | | `controller.imageSuffix` | `-gpu` | The controller runs the image variant with SkyPilot | | `migrations.enabled` | `true` | `meritorder migrate` as a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook | | `serviceAccount.annotations`, `podLabels` | `{}` | Workload identity (IRSA, GKE, AKS) for keyless Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure OpenAI | | `metrics.serviceMonitor` | `false` | Prometheus Operator scraping `/metrics` | ## Open-source hygiene - AGPL-3.0-only license. - Images published to GHCR, multi-arch (amd64 / arm64). - No telemetry phone-home. All metrics go to the operator's own OpenTelemetry endpoint. - Works with zero cloud accounts beyond one API key; every cloud integration is a plugin. ## Supply-chain security A gateway holds every provider credential an organization has, so it is a prime target. Supply-chain security is a feature, not an afterthought. | Area | Policy | |---|---| | **Dependencies** | Small, well-maintained set: FastAPI, uvicorn, httpx, pydantic, PyYAML, redis, asyncpg, PyJWT + cryptography, botocore; optional extras for google-auth, azure-identity, OpenTelemetry. SkyPilot (~150 packages) lives only in the controller's `-gpu` image, in its own environment. Adding a dependency needs a written justification in the PR. | | **Lockfile** | `uv.lock` with hashes. `exclude-newer` keeps us off releases published in the last few days, the window in which most malicious releases are caught and pulled. | | **Updates** | Renovate waits 7 days before proposing a new version; `pip-audit` and `npm audit` in CI. The UI's npm dependencies are pinned exactly and install scripts are disabled. | | **Our releases** | Multi-arch images (`` and `-gpu`) signed with Sigstore/cosign, with an SBOM and provenance per release. PyPI publishing is not set up yet. | | **Images** | Minimal (distroless or slim) base images, non-root user, read-only filesystem. | | **Reporting issues** | `SECURITY.md` with a private disclosure address. |

"""The weekly on-call hours export for payroll."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from .overrides import Override, on_call
from .rotation import Rotation
from .timeutil import hours_between, week_start


def weekly_hours(rotation: Rotation, overrides: list[Override], start: datetime, end: datetime) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
    """Hours on call per member per calendar week, counting each whole hour in [start, end).

    Returns {week: {member: hours}}, where week is the ISO date of the Monday that starts the calendar week (Monday 00:00
    to Monday 00:00 UTC) containing the hour, e.g. '2026-03-02'. Weeks follow the calendar, not the rotation's
    handoffs. Members without hours in a week, and weeks without hours, are left out.
    """
    out: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    for hour in hours_between(start, end):
        # week_start() gives the Sunday before; step forward a day to get the Monday.
        monday = week_start(hour) + timedelta(days=1)
        out[monday.date().isoformat()][on_call(rotation, overrides, hour)] += 1
    return {week: dict(members) for week, members in out.items()}

import json

from conftest import LEAD_KEY, auth

def sse_events(text: str) -> list[tuple[str | None, str]]:
    out = []
    for block in text.strip().split("\n\n"):
        name, data = None, []
        for line in block.split("\n"):
            if line.startswith("event: "):
                name = line[7:]
            elif line.startswith("data: "):
                data.append(line[6:])
        out.append((name, "\n".join(data)))
    return out


async def test_requires_key(client):
    r = await client.post("/v1/messages", json={"model": "big", "max_tokens": 10, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]})
    assert r.status_code == 401
    assert r.json()["type"] == "error"

    assert body["type"] == "message"

"""The ``meritorder`` command."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from .harness import CREDENTIALS, KEY_FILE, save_key, saved


def load_dotenv(path: str | Path = ".env") -> None:
    """Load KEY=VALUE lines from .env without overriding variables already set."""
    try:
        lines = Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return
    for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key, value = key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        if key and value and key not in os.environ:
            os.environ[key] = value


def _setup_logging(level: str = "INFO") -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(level=level, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")


def _store():
    from .store import make_store

    store = make_store(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL"))
    if store.kind != "postgres":
        raise SystemExit("this command needs Postgres: set MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL")
    return store


def _saved() -> dict:
    return saved()


def _gateway(args) -> str:
    return (getattr(args, "gateway", None) or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_URL") or _saved().get("gateway") or "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")


def _key(args) -> str:
    key = getattr(args, "key", None) or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_API_KEY") or _saved().get("api_key")

def cmd_login(args) -> None:
    gateway = (args.gateway or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_URL") or "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")
    with httpx.Client(timeout=30) as c:
        oidc = c.get(f"{gateway}/auth/config").json().get("oidc")
        if not oidc:
            raise SystemExit("this gateway has no OIDC login configured; ask an admin for an API key")
        disc = c.get(oidc["issuer"].rstrip("/") + "/.well-known/openid-configuration").json()
        dev = c.post(disc["device_authorization_endpoint"], data={"client_id": oidc["client_id"], "scope": " ".join(oidc["scopes"])}).json()
        print(dev.get("message") or f"Open {dev['verification_uri']} and enter code {dev['user_code']}")
        interval = int(dev.get("interval", 5))
        deadline = time.time() + int(dev.get("expires_in", 900))
        while time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(interval)
            tok = c.post(disc["token_endpoint"], data={
                "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
                "device_code": dev["device_code"],
                "client_id": oidc["client_id"],
            }).json()
            if "id_token" in tok:
                break
            err = tok.get("error")
            if err == "slow_down":
                interval += 5
            elif err != "authorization_pending":
                raise SystemExit(f"login failed: {tok.get('error_description') or err}")
        else:
            raise SystemExit("login timed out")
        resp = c.post(f"{gateway}/auth/exchange", json={"id_token": tok["id_token"]})
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"key exchange failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}")
        result = resp.json()
    save_key(gateway, result["api_key"], {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "api_key"})
    print(f"\nLogged in as {result['user']} (team {result['team']}); key expires {result['expires_at'][:10]}.")
    print(f"Key saved to {KEY_FILE}\n")
    print("Next: `meritorder setup pi` and/or `meritorder setup claude-code`.")

"""Marginal-cost router (docs/03-routing.md).

For each candidate backend b over the session's expected remaining turns:

    cost(b) = rebuild(b) + expected_remaining_turns * per_turn(b)

* per_turn uses API prices, or for self-hosted backends a shadow price that is
  near zero while the replica has headroom and rises toward the API price as it fills.
* rebuild is zero when b already holds a warm cache for this session, otherwise
  the extra cost of re-processing the whole prefix there.

Routes within the priority's premium of the cheapest are then ranked by measured speed (speed.py): with the
default `cost` priority that only decides between routes that cost the same (2%), so the faster one wins.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .backends import Backend, describe
from .classifier import Floor, classify, parse_floor
from .config import PRIORITIES, Config, ModelConfig, Price, Route, TeamConfig
from .sessions import Session
from .speed import Speeds


class RoutingError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int, message: str, kind: str = "invalid_request_error", headers: dict | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.message = message
        self.kind = kind
        self.headers = headers or {}


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    model: ModelConfig
    route: Route
    backend: Backend
    cost: float
    warm: bool
    quality: int
    upgraded: bool = False
    queued: bool = False  # sent to a saturated backend because nothing else could take it

    @property
    def self_hosted(self) -> bool:
        return self.backend.kind == "self_hosted"


@dataclass
class Decision:
    requested: str
    auto: bool
    floor: Floor | None
    candidates: list[Candidate] = field(default_factory=list)
    reason: str = ""
    substituted_for: str | None = None  # the named model that couldn't run (team opted in to substitution)
    priority: str = "cost"


def shadow_multiplier(util: float, knee: float, floor: float) -> float | None:
    """Fraction of API price a self-hosted token "costs" at this utilization. None = full."""
    if util >= 1.0:
        return None
    if util <= knee:
        return floor
    return floor + (1.0 - floor) * ((util - knee) / (1.0 - knee)) ** 2


def _scaled(price: Price, m: float) -> Price:
    return Price(input=price.input * m, output=price.output * m, cache_read=price.read() * m, cache_write=price.write() * m)


class Router:
    def __init__(self, cfg: Config, backends: dict[str, Backend], speeds: Speeds | None = None):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.backends = backends
        self.speeds = speeds if speeds is not None else Speeds()

    def priority(self, team: TeamConfig, headers: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """The request's X-MeritOrder-Priority, else the team's, else routing.priority."""
        asked = (headers.get("x-meritorder-priority") or "").strip().lower()
        if asked:
            if asked not in PRIORITIES:
                raise RoutingError(400, f"X-MeritOrder-Priority must be one of {', '.join(PRIORITIES)}, not '{asked}'",
                                   "invalid_request_error")
            return asked
        return team.priority or self.cfg.routing.priority

    def _seconds(self, c: Candidate) -> float:
        e = self.speeds.expected(c.backend.name, c.route.model, self.cfg.routing.est_output_tokens)
        return math.inf if e is None else e

    def _speed_note(self, c: Candidate) -> str:
        s = self._seconds(c)
        return f"~{s:.1f}s" if s != math.inf else "not measured yet"

    def _needs_check(self, c: Candidate, now: float) -> bool:
        s = self.speeds.get(c.backend.name, c.route.model)
        return s is None or s.stale(now)

    def rank(self, cands: list[Candidate], priority: str, new_session: bool, now: float) -> tuple[list[Candidate], str]:
        """Order cost-sorted candidates by the priority. Routes within its premium of the cheapest compete on
        speed (and, for `auto`, quality); the rest stay in cost order behind them."""
        r = self.cfg.routing
        limit = cands[0].cost * (1 + r.priority_premium_pct[priority] / 100) + 1e-9
        group = [c for c in cands if c.cost <= limit]
        rest = [c for c in cands if c.cost > limit]
        if len(group) < 2:
            return cands, ""
        if priority == "cost":
            # Close enough on price: the better model first (for `auto`), then the faster route.
            ranked = sorted(group, key=lambda c: (-c.quality, self._seconds(c)))
        else:
            ranked = sorted(group, key=lambda c: (self._seconds(c), -c.quality))
        lead, cheapest = ranked[0], group[0]
        note = ""
        if lead is not cheapest and lead.quality == cheapest.quality and self._seconds(lead) < self._seconds(cheapest):
            extra = (lead.cost / cheapest.cost - 1) * 100 if cheapest.cost > 0 else 0.0
            note = (f"; {priority} priority: {lead.backend.name} ({self._speed_note(lead)}) over {cheapest.backend.name} "
                    f"({self._speed_note(cheapest)})" + (f" for {extra:.0f}% more" if extra >= 1 else ""))

        if new_session and r.speed_check_every:
            # Keep measuring the alternatives, or the first route measured would win forever. Only new
            # sessions (no cache to lose) and only routes the priority already allows.
            self.speeds.decisions += 1
            pool = [c for c in ranked[1:] if priority != "cost" or c.quality == lead.quality]
            stale = [c for c in pool if self._needs_check(c, now)]
            if stale and self.speeds.decisions >= r.speed_check_every:
                self.speeds.decisions = 0

                def oldest(c: Candidate) -> tuple[bool, float]:
                    s = self.speeds.get(c.backend.name, c.route.model)
                    return (s is not None and s.measured, s.last if s else 0.0)

                pick = min(stale, key=oldest)  # never measured first, then the longest ago
                ranked.remove(pick)
                ranked.insert(0, pick)
                note = f"; checking {pick.backend.name}'s speed ({self._speed_note(pick)})"
        return ranked + rest, note

    def resolve(self, requested: str) -> ModelConfig | None:
        return self.cfg.model(requested)

    def _expected_turns(self, session: Session | None) -> int:
        r = self.cfg.routing
        turns = session.turns if session else 0
        return max(r.min_expected_turns, min(r.max_expected_turns, turns or r.min_expected_turns))

    def estimate(
        self, price: Price, backend: Backend, prompt_tokens: int, session: Session | None, warm: bool, turns: int
    ) -> float:
        r = self.cfg.routing
        new = r.est_new_tokens_per_turn
        if session and session.prefix_tokens:
            new = max(prompt_tokens - session.prefix_tokens, 200)
        cached = max(prompt_tokens - new, 0)
        # Steady state: the prefix is read from cache, new tokens are written to it.
        write_price = price.write()  # input price unless the route charges a write premium
        per_turn = (cached * price.read() + new * write_price + r.est_output_tokens * price.output) / 1e6
        rebuild = 0.0 if warm else cached * max(write_price - price.read(), 0.0) / 1e6
        return rebuild + turns * per_turn

    def decide(
        self,
        requested: str,
        team: TeamConfig,
        body: dict,
        headers: dict[str, str],
        session: Session | None,
        prompt_tokens: int,
        boundary: bool,
        utilization: dict[str, float],
        now: float,
        queue_full: frozenset[str] | set[str] = frozenset(),
    ) -> Decision:
        """Pick and rank candidates. ``queue_full`` names saturated backends that also have no room left
        to queue requests; other saturated backends are kept as a last resort."""
        r = self.cfg.routing
        auto = requested == r.auto_model or requested == ""
        floor: Floor | None = None
        priority = self.priority(team, headers)

        if auto:
            if session and session.model and not boundary and team.allows_model(session.model) and self.cfg.model(session.model):
                models = [self.cfg.model(session.model)]
                floor = parse_floor(session.floor or "")
                reason = f"mid-task: keeping session model {session.model}"
            else:
                floor = classify(body, headers, prompt_tokens)
                models = [m for m in self.cfg.models
                          if m.kind == "chat" and m.q(floor.task) >= floor.level and team.allows_model(m.name)]
                reason = f"classified {floor} ({floor.reason})"
                if not models:
                    # Nothing meets the floor: fall back to the best allowed models.
                    allowed = [m for m in self.cfg.models if m.kind == "chat" and team.allows_model(m.name)]
                    best = max((m.q(floor.task) for m in allowed), default=0)
                    models = [m for m in allowed if m.q(floor.task) == best]
                    reason += f"; no model meets the floor, using best available (level {best})"
        else:
            model = self.resolve(requested)
            if model is None:
                raise RoutingError(404, f"model '{requested}' is not configured", "not_found_error")
            if model.kind != "chat":
                raise RoutingError(400, f"'{model.name}' is an embedding model; use /v1/embeddings", "invalid_request_error")
            if not team.allows_model(model.name):
                raise RoutingError(403, f"model '{model.name}' is not allowed for team '{team.name}'", "permission_error")
            models = [model]
            reason = f"harness requested {model.name}"

        turns = self._expected_turns(session)
        task = floor.task if floor else "general"
        cands: list[Candidate] = []
        too_small = [m.name for m in models if m.context_window and prompt_tokens > m.context_window * 0.95]
        if too_small and len(too_small) < len(models):
            models = [m for m in models if m.name not in too_small]
            reason += f"; skipped {', '.join(too_small)} (context window too small)"
        saturated: list[Candidate] = []
        cooling: list[Candidate] = []  # the model is over capacity on this backend: a last resort
        for m in models:
            for route in m.routes:
                backend = self.backends.get(route.backend)
                if backend is None or not backend.available or not backend.healthy(now) or not team.allows_backend(route.backend):
                    continue
                busy = backend.skipped(now, route.model)
                if busy is not None and not busy.capacity:
                    continue  # e.g. the deployment doesn't exist there
                if backend.draining and not (session and session.warm(backend.name, now)):
                    continue  # draining: only finish sessions whose cache is already there
                if auto and not route.priced:
                    continue  # an unknown price must never look free
                price = route.cost_price().at(prompt_tokens)  # long prompts can cost more per token
                full = False
                if backend.kind == "self_hosted":
                    mult = shadow_multiplier(utilization.get(backend.name, 0.0), r.shadow_knee, r.shadow_floor)
                    if mult is None:
                        # Saturated: new work spills to other routes. If none can take it, the request queues
                        # here (in vLLM) rather than failing, unless that queue is full too.
                        if backend.name in queue_full:
                            continue
                        full = True
                    else:
                        price = _scaled(price, mult)
                warm = bool(session and session.warm(backend.name, now))
                quality = m.q(task)
                (cooling if busy else saturated if full else cands).append(
                    Candidate(
                        model=m,
                        route=route,
                        backend=backend,
                        cost=self.estimate(price, backend, prompt_tokens, session, warm, turns),
                        warm=warm,
                        quality=quality,
                        upgraded=bool(auto and floor and quality > floor.level and backend.kind == "self_hosted"),
                        queued=full,
                    )
                )
        if not cands and saturated and auto and session and session.model and not boundary:
            # The session's GPUs are full: another model with room beats waiting in a queue.
            again = self.decide(requested, team, body, headers, session, prompt_tokens, True, utilization, now, queue_full)
            if not any(c.queued for c in again.candidates):
                again.reason = f"session model {session.model} is saturated; re-routed: {again.reason}"
                return again
        if not cands and saturated:
            saturated.sort(key=lambda c: (c.cost, -c.quality))
            names = ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(c.backend.name for c in saturated))
            return Decision(requested=requested, auto=auto, floor=floor, candidates=saturated,
                            reason=f"{reason}; every route is saturated, queued on {names}")
        if not cands and cooling:
            # Every route is over capacity right now. Try the one that should free up first rather than refuse:
            # the alternative is an error the client would retry anyway.
            cooling.sort(key=lambda c: c.backend.skipped(now, c.route.model).until)
            names = ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(c.backend.name for c in cooling))
            return Decision(requested=requested, auto=auto, floor=floor, candidates=cooling,
                            reason=f"{reason}; every route is over capacity, trying {names} anyway")
        if not cands:
            if auto and session and session.model and not boundary:
                # The session's model has nowhere to run (e.g. its GPUs were stopped): pick again.
                again = self.decide(requested, team, body, headers, session, prompt_tokens, True, utilization, now, queue_full)
                again.reason = f"session model {session.model} is unavailable; re-routed: {again.reason}"
                return again
            if not auto and team.substitute_unavailable and len(models) == 1:
                sub = self._substitute(models[0], team, body, headers, session, prompt_tokens, utilization, now, queue_full)
                if sub is not None:
                    return sub
            message, wait = self._unavailable_message(models, team, now, auto)
            raise RoutingError(503, message, "overloaded_error", {"retry-after": str(wait)} if wait else None)
        if auto and any(c.backend.kind != "mock" for c in cands):
            # Mocks are for trying things out; never let them win against real backends.
            cands = [c for c in cands if c.backend.kind != "mock"]

        cands.sort(key=lambda c: (c.cost, -c.quality))
        if len(cands) > 1:
            cands, note = self.rank(cands, priority, session is None or not session.backend, now)
            reason += note

        # Stickiness: only move a session off its current backend if it's clearly cheaper.
        if session and session.backend:
            current = next((c for c in cands if c.backend.name == session.backend and c.model.name == session.model), None)
            if current is not None and current is not cands[0]:
                margin = current.cost * r.switch_margin_pct / 100.0 + r.switch_margin_usd
                if cands[0].cost + margin >= current.cost:
                    cands.remove(current)
                    cands.insert(0, current)
                    reason += f"; staying on {current.backend.name} (move would not pay for cache rebuild)"

        return Decision(requested=requested, auto=auto, floor=floor, candidates=cands, reason=reason, priority=priority)

    def _substitute(self, named: ModelConfig, team: TeamConfig, body: dict, headers: dict[str, str], session: Session | None,
                    prompt_tokens: int, utilization: dict[str, float], now: float,
                    queue_full: frozenset[str] | set[str] = frozenset()) -> Decision | None:
        """Route a named model that can't run to models at least as good for this task (never a weaker one)."""
        task = classify(body, headers, prompt_tokens).task
        level = max(1, named.q(task))
        try:
            sub = self.decide(self.cfg.routing.auto_model, team, body, {**headers, "x-route-floor": f"{task}:{level}"},
                              session, prompt_tokens, True, utilization, now, queue_full)
        except RoutingError:
            return None
        sub.candidates = [c for c in sub.candidates if c.model.name != named.name and c.model.q(task) >= level]
        if not sub.candidates:
            return None
        for c in sub.candidates:
            c.upgraded = False
        sub.auto = False  # the client named a model: no automatic effort changes or refusal retries
        sub.requested = named.name
        sub.substituted_for = named.name
        sub.reason = f"{named.name} has nowhere to run; substituted a model at least as good for {task} (level {level}): {sub.reason}"
        return sub

    def _unavailable_message(self, models: list[ModelConfig], team: TeamConfig, now: float, auto: bool) -> tuple[str, int | None]:
        """Say why nothing can serve the request, route by route, so people know what to fix or switch to. Also
        returns the seconds until a skipped route is tried again (for Retry-After), if any is."""
        waits = [o.until - now for m in models for r in m.routes
                 if (b := self.backends.get(r.backend)) is not None and (o := b.skipped(now, r.model)) is not None]
        wait = max(1, int(min(waits))) if waits else None
        if auto or len(models) != 1:
            return "no healthy backend is available for this request", wait
        why = []
        for route in models[0].routes:
            b = self.backends.get(route.backend)
            bc = self.cfg.backend(route.backend)
            out = b.skipped(now, route.model) if b is not None else None
            if b is None:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: {(bc.disabled_reason if bc else None) or 'not enabled'}")
            elif not team.allows_backend(route.backend):
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: not allowed for team '{team.name}'")
            elif not b.available:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: {getattr(b, 'unavailable_reason', None) or 'not running'}")
            elif out is not None:
                what = describe(out.status) if out.status else "failing"
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: {what}, trying again in {max(1, int(out.until - now))}s")
            elif b.draining:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: draining, only finishing existing sessions")
            else:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: saturated and its queue is full")
        return (f"'{models[0].name}' has nowhere to run right now ({'; '.join(why)}). "
                f"Use model '{self.cfg.routing.auto_model}' to let Merit Order pick another model, or try again later."), wait

async def real_store() -> PostgresStore:
    store = PostgresStore(DATABASE_URL)
    await store.init()
    await store.migrate()
    async with store.pool.acquire() as c:
        tables = [r["tablename"] for r in await c.fetch(
            "SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename <> 'schema_migrations' "
            "AND tablename NOT IN (SELECT inhrelid::regclass::text FROM pg_inherits)")]
        if tables:
            await c.execute(f"TRUNCATE {', '.join(tables)} RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE")
    return store


async def real_state() -> RedisState:
    state = RedisState(REDIS_URL)
    await state.r.flushdb()
    return state

    return complete_row({"id": uuid.uuid4(), "ts": datetime.now(UTC), "user_id": "alice", "team": "default",

async def ledger(gateway) -> list[dict]:
    """Every ledger row, oldest first, on either store."""
    await gateway.drain()
    return (await gateway.store.recent(100_000))[::-1]


async def last_row(gateway) -> dict:
    """The newest ledger row, on either store."""
    await gateway.drain()
    return (await gateway.store.recent(1))[0]

# Merit Order configuration.
#
# Strings support ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Secrets come from the
# environment (see .env.example), never from this file.
#
# Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are switched off automatically,
# so this file works with whatever provider keys you have. Run `meritorder check`
# to see what is usable.
#
# PRICES are dollars per million tokens. Anthropic prices are from published
# rates on 2026-11-09; routes without a price use prices.json, which
# `meritorder prices refresh` updates from OpenRouter's catalog; AWS, Azure, and GCP set their
# own prices and you may have negotiated discounts, so verify before trusting
# the savings numbers. QUALITY scores (1-5) are starting points; tune them with
# your own evals.

# "What you'd use without Merit Order": the counterfactual for savings reports.
baseline_model: claude-sonnet

# Open-weight models, direct vendor APIs, and OpenRouter's free tier.
include:
  - models-open.yaml
  - models-embeddings.yaml

default_max_tokens: 16000

routing:
  auto_model: auto              # clients send model="auto" to let the router choose
  switch_margin_pct: 10         # only move a session if it's this much cheaper (after cache rebuild)
  est_output_tokens: 600
  # Among routes that cost about the same, the faster one wins. cost: only ties (2%); balanced: a faster
  # route may cost 20% more; speed: up to 100% more. Teams (priority:) and X-MeritOrder-Priority override it.
  priority: cost

backends:
  # Keys come from the environment (value_env). In Kubernetes you can also add
  # value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/<NAME> so a rotated key works without a restart
  # (docs/07-deployment.md#secrets). Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure can run keyless on workload identity.
  # --- always available: in-process mocks for trying things out and for tests
  mock-anthropic:
    kind: mock
    format: anthropic
    mock_min_cache_tokens: 1024   # like Anthropic: shorter prompts aren't cached
  mock-openai:
    kind: mock
    format: openai

  # --- Anthropic Messages API family
  anthropic:
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://api.anthropic.com
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}

  bedrock:                      # Claude in Amazon Bedrock (Messages API, SigV4 or bearer token)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_BEDROCK:-true}   # false until the account can use the models (quotas, model access)
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic
    anthropic_version: "2026-10-21"
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}", profile: "${AWS_PROFILE:-}"}

  foundry-claude:               # Claude in Microsoft Foundry
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_FOUNDRY_CLAUDE:-true}   # false until the Claude deployments exist
    format: anthropic
    base_url: ${AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT}/anthropic
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY}

  vertex:                       # Claude on Vertex AI (needs: uv sync --extra gcp)
    enabled: false
    format: anthropic
    flavor: vertex
    project: ${GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT}
    region: global
    auth: {type: google}

  # --- OpenAI-compatible family
  azure-openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: ${AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT}/openai/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, header: api-key, value_env: AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openai:

# 02 — Request flow One turn of a pi session using `model="auto"` (`meritorder setup pi` points pi at the OpenAI Chat Completions API). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant H as Harness (pi) participant G as Gateway participant R as Redis participant P as Postgres participant B as Chosen backend H->>G: POST /v1/chat/completions
key, X-Session-Id, model=auto, full history G->>G: Validate key (in-process cache for 60 s, Postgres on miss) G->>R: Check budgets (org, team, person), rate limits, session spend cap G->>R: Load the conversation's routing state (the session's, or its thread for a subagent
or side requests): model, backend, cache warm-until, prefix hash (same round trip) alt New session, new human prompt, the harness compacted history, or it outgrew its model G->>G: Classify task → quality floor (an outgrown session keeps its floor) G->>G: Candidate models: quality ≥ floor, with room for the conversation else Mid-task (tool results coming back) and it still fits G->>G: Keep the session's model end G->>G: Score backends: rebuild + turns × per-turn cost, stickiness G->>G: Compress huge tool outputs (if the team turned it on: deterministic, nothing stored) G->>G: Translate to the backend's API format, shape prompt: cache marker, stable prefix G->>B: Forward Note over G,B: On 5xx / 429 / timeout / bad key: next backend.
On a refusal or "prompt too long" (auto): next model (with a bigger window). B-->>G: Response starts G->>R: Update the conversation's routing state before replying, so the next turn sees it:
model, backend, warm-until, prefix hash B-->>G: Stream tokens + usage (cached vs uncached tokens) G-->>H: Stream tokens (in the harness's API format) G-)P: Ledger row: actual cost, baseline cost, savings by cause G-)R: Spend counters, live feed event ``` ## Hot-path budget The gateway should add **single-digit milliseconds** before the first byte goes upstream. Everything on the hot path is in-memory or one Redis round trip: | Step | Where it reads from | |---|---| | Key validation | In-process cache (60 s), Postgres on miss | | Rate limit / budget | Redis counters (a missing spend counter is seeded from the Postgres ledger) | | Session lookup | Redis, in the same round trip as the counters | | GPU state and headroom | Published to Redis by the controller; each gateway reloads deployment state every 5 s and reads utilization with the session | | Classifier | Rules; only on new sessions and task boundaries | | Compression | Deterministic and in-memory; the same output always compresses the same way | Writes to Postgres (usage, ledger) are **async** and never block the response. ## What the harness sees Nothing unusual. Same API it already speaks, streamed tokens, usage numbers. Response headers tell curious users what happened: ``` x-meritorder-model: qwen3-coder-next # the model that answered x-meritorder-backend: gpu-qwen-coder # where it ran x-meritorder-floor: coding:3 # what the classifier decided (auto) x-meritorder-session: 3f9c… # the session it was counted under x-meritorder-request-id: 6b1e… # find it in the ledger x-meritorder-cost-usd: 0.000400 # non-streaming responses: cost, x-meritorder-baseline-usd: 0.031000 # what it would have cost without Merit Order, x-meritorder-savings-usd: 0.030600 # and the difference x-meritorder-max-tokens: 128000 # the reply's output allowance, x-meritorder-max-tokens-source: model # and where it came from (client, model, context, …) x-meritorder-failed-over: openai/gpt-6.1-terra 429 # only when a source failed first x-meritorder-refused-by: claude-opus # only when a model refused and another answered x-meritorder-substituted-for: qwen3-coder # only when a named model couldn't run (opt-in) x-meritorder-queued: 1 # only when it waited in a full GPU deployment's queue ``` The whole decision, rule by rule, is in [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md).

from datetime import UTC, datetime

import yaml

from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, Config, ModelConfig, Route, ServeConfig
from meritorder.controller import tick
from meritorder.gpu import (
    API_ONLY, DRAINING, PROVISIONING, WARM, Demand, Deployment, SkyPilotProvisioner, Status, addressable, decide,
    desired_replicas, parse_vllm_metrics,
)
from meritorder.state import MemoryState
from meritorder.store import MemoryStore

SERVE = ServeConfig(model="ow", scale_up_after_minutes=10, hold_minutes=30, drain_minutes=15, max_replicas=4)


def test_desired_replicas_must_pay_for_themselves():
    # $50/h of API spend can pay for 2 replicas at $20/h (with 20% margin), throughput needs 3.
    d = desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=50, tokens_per_second=2000))
    assert d == 2
    assert desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=10, tokens_per_second=2000)) == 0
    warm = ServeConfig(model="ow", min_replicas=1)
    assert desired_replicas(warm, 20.0, 1000, Demand(0, 0)) == 1


def test_state_machine_full_cycle():
    t = 1_000_000.0
    rec, act = decide({}, SERVE, desired=2, status=Status(), now=t)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act is None  # must be justified for 10 minutes first
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + 601)
    assert rec["state"] == PROVISIONING and act.kind == "up" and act.replicas == 2
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM and rec["endpoint"] == "http://gpu/v1"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 3, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1600)
    assert act.kind == "scale" and act.replicas == 3
    # demand disappears, but GPUs are held for 30 minutes after warming
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1700)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801)
    assert rec["state"] == DRAINING
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801 + 901)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"


def test_provisioning_timeout_cools_down():
    t = 0.0
    rec = {"state": PROVISIONING, "since": t}
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 1)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 700)
    assert act is None  # still cooling down


def test_addressable_demand_uses_quality_floor():
    cfg = Config(backends=[], models=[ModelConfig(name="ow", quality={"coding": 4}, routes=[Route(backend="x", model="y")])])
    rows = [
        {"floor": "coding:3", "served_model": "sonnet", "requested_model": "auto", "cost": 10.0, "tokens": 100},

vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc{model_name="m"} 0.42
vllm:num_requests_waiting{model_name="m"} 0.0
"""

def test_skypilot_task_yaml():
    model = ModelConfig(name="ow", hf_id="Org/Model-7B", routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="org-model")])
    backend = BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai",

class FakeProvisioner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
        self.ready = False

    async def status(self):
        return Status(ready=self.ready, endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1" if self.ready else None)

    async def up(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("up", n))

    async def scale(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("scale", n))

    async def down(self):
        self.calls.append(("down",))

    backend = BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai", gpu_cost_per_hour=10.0,
                            serve=ServeConfig(model="ow", scale_up_after_minutes=0))
    cfg = Config(backends=[backend], models=[model])
    store, state = MemoryStore(), MemoryState()
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    for _ in range(30):  # $30 of coding:3 traffic in the last hour, served by an API model
        await store.record({"ts": now, "floor": "coding:3", "served_model": "sonnet", "requested_model": "auto",
                            "served_api_cost": 1.0, "actual_cost": 1.0, "status": 200, "upgraded": False,

    [rec] = await tick(cfg, store, state, deps)

    prov.ready = True
    [rec] = await tick(cfg, store, state, deps)

def test_sky_python_found_next_to_sky_even_with_spaces_and_symlinks(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import os

    from meritorder.gpu import _shebang_python, sky_python

    monkeypatch.delenv("MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON", raising=False)
    venv = tmp_path / "Example LLC" / "sky-venv" / "bin"
    venv.mkdir(parents=True)
    py = venv / "python"
    py.write_text("#!/bin/sh\n")
    py.chmod(0o755)
    sky = venv / "sky"
    sky.write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\n'''exec' \"{py}\" \"$0\" \"$@\"\n' '''\n")

# Merit Order

An open-source LLM gateway that cuts LLM spend for day-to-day use, without changing how
people work.

Power grids dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest marginal cost first, with expensive
peaker plants switched on only when demand requires them. Merit Order does the same with tokens:

- **Routes** every session to the cheapest model and backend that meets the task's quality bar,
  counting what it would cost to rebuild the prompt cache somewhere else.
- **Runs open-weight models on your own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when steady load makes that cheaper
  than paying per token, and turns them off when it doesn't. APIs (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex,
  Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, ...) are always there for overflow.
- **Saves tokens**: automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, cache-safe compression of huge tool
  outputs, and an optional response cache.
- **Shows the money**: every request is recorded with what it cost and what it would have cost
  without Merit Order, broken down by cause, per user, team, project, and day.

Point Claude Code, pi, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or anything that speaks either API at it.

## Quickstart (no keys needed)

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env            # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY (and any provider keys you have)
uv run meritorder serve         # http://localhost:8080, reports UI at /ui/
```

```bash
curl localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $MERITORDER_DEV_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}'
```

With no provider keys, requests go to built-in mock backends. `uv run meritorder check` shows
which backends and models are live with the keys you've set. Without `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`,
storage is in memory; use Docker Compose for the real thing.

## Run the full stack with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add at least one provider key
docker compose up -d            # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080
docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin
```

Bedrock with your AWS profile (including SSO): `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d`.
Kubernetes: `helm install mo charts/meritorder` (see [docs/07-deployment.md](docs/07-deployment.md)).

## Point your harness at it

```bash
meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com   # Entra sign-in; or: meritorder use-key <key>
meritorder setup pi                                    # adds a "meritorder" provider to pi
meritorder setup claude-code                           # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + apiKeyHelper
```

Or by hand: OpenAI-compatible clients use base URL `<gateway>/v1`; Claude Code uses
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>`. Use `model: "auto"` to let Merit Order choose, or name a model
(`claude-sonnet`, `kimi-k3.1`, `qwen3-coder`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, ...) to pin it.

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Session-Id` | Groups requests into a session (pi sends it; otherwise inferred) |
| `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | Minimum quality for `auto` routing |
| `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges `auto` routing down or up |
| `X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=foo` | Cost-allocation tags for reports |
| `X-MeritOrder-Cache: on` / `off` | Use or bypass the response cache |
| `X-MeritOrder-Backend: <name>` | Admins only: pin a backend (testing, debugging) |

Responses carry `x-meritorder-model`, `x-meritorder-backend`, and (non-streaming)
`x-meritorder-cost-usd` / `x-meritorder-savings-usd`. A model you name is never swapped for
another unless your team opted in to substitution when it can't run; reasoning effort you set is
always passed through. Every routing and scaling rule, as diagrams:
[docs/10-how-it-decides.md](docs/10-how-it-decides.md).

## What's in the box

| Area | Built |
|---|---|
| APIs | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (stateless), Anthropic Messages, and embeddings; streaming and not; pass-through when formats match, translation when they don't |
