# 04 — Caching & sessions ## Who owns what ```mermaid flowchart LR H["Harness
owns the conversation
history, compaction"] G["Gateway
owns session metadata
backend, hashes, timestamps"] B["Backend
owns the prompt / KV cache
per provider, region, replica"] H -- "full history every turn" --> G G -- "same backend + byte-stable prefix" --> B B -- "cached vs uncached token counts" --> G ``` LLM APIs are stateless: pi resends the whole conversation every turn. Caching happens **on the backend**, which recognizes a prefix it processed recently and bills it at a discount. The gateway's job is to make cache hits *likely* — not to hold the conversation. ## Caches are per backend ```mermaid flowchart TB S["Session 7f3a
120k-token prefix"] S -- "warm ✓" --> A["Bedrock us-east-1
Claude"] S -. "cold — full price to move" .-> B["Bedrock us-west-2
Claude"] S -. "cold" .-> C["Anthropic direct
Claude"] S -. "cold" .-> D["Self-hosted replica-2"] ``` Each provider, region, account, and replica has its own cache. That's why sessions are sticky and why the router prices moves (see [03](03-routing.md)). | Backend | How caching works | What the gateway does | |---|---|---| | Anthropic / Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry (Claude) | Explicit `cache_control` breakpoints, 5 min or 1 h TTL | Turns on automatic caching (top-level `cache_control`) if the client set no breakpoints; TTL from `cache_ttl_seconds` | | Claude through OpenRouter | Cached only when asked; a client's own breakpoints are lost when its Anthropic request is translated | Turns on automatic caching unless the forwarded request already has breakpoints (an OpenAI-format client's survive), so translated Anthropic requests always get it. Counted as a Merit Order saving only if the client hadn't asked for caching | | OpenAI / Azure | Automatic above ~1k tokens | On backends with `supports_prompt_cache_key` (OpenAI's API in the shipped config), sets `prompt_cache_key` to the conversation's thread ID (the session, or a subagent or side requests within it) | | Gemini (Vertex AI, OpenRouter) | Implicit caching + explicit context caches | Keeps prefix stable; explicit caches later | | vLLM / SGLang | Automatic prefix caching per replica | Keeps the session on the same deployment; SkyServe's load balancer picks the replica (cache-aware replica routing and LMCache are not built) | ## Keeping the prefix byte-stable Any change early in the prompt invalidates everything after it. The gateway: - Adds nothing to the system prompt or messages: cache markers and keys, output limits and effort are top-level request fields. - Serializes tool definitions deterministically (stable key order). - Never injects timestamps, request IDs, or per-request text into the prompt. - Passes Anthropic thinking blocks (with their signatures) through untouched when client and backend both speak Anthropic Messages. Translating to the other format drops them, and OpenAI reasoning items aren't carried between turns. ## The session table (Redis) Metadata only. No conversation content. | Field | Used for | |---|---| | `id` | The session id: from `X-Session-Id`, `X-MeritOrder-Session` or Claude Code's `x-claude-code-session-id`, else Claude Code's session in request metadata, else a hash of user + system prompt + first user message | | `thread` | Which conversation in the session this is (below); empty for the main one | | `model`, `backend` | Stickiness | | `floor` | The level a mid-task turn keeps, and an outgrown session is re-routed at | | `effort` | The reasoning effort chosen for the session, kept so the cache stays valid | | `msg_count`, `prefix_hash`, `prefix_tokens` | Detect compaction / divergence (hash mismatch ⇒ cache is dead ⇒ free re-route); estimate new tokens per turn | | `warm_until{backend}` | Which backends still hold a warm cache (now + the backend's `cache_ttl_seconds`, after each turn) | | `turns`, `last_seen` | Estimate remaining turns | Entries are keyed by user, so another caller sending the same session id can't read or change them, and expire 6 hours after the last turn. The per-session spend cap (`max_session_usd`) uses a separate spend counter for the session. ### Several conversations in one session A coding agent can run several conversations under one session id. Claude Code sends its subagents' turns (with `x-claude-code-agent-id`) and its side requests (titles, summaries; request class `auxiliary`) with the main session's id, but each has its own history and its own cache. If they shared routing state, every subagent turn would overwrite the main conversation's model, prefix hash and warm caches, so the next main turn would look compacted, re-route, and pay to rebuild its cache. So the routing state above is kept per **thread**: the session id, plus `/agent:` for a subagent and `/aux` for side requests. Spend limits (`max_session_usd`), the ledger's `session_id` and reports still use the session id, so a session's cost includes its subagents. ## Compression without storing anything Problem: if we compress a big tool output on turn 5, the harness resends the **original** on turn 6. If we compress it differently, the prefix changes and the cache misses. Solution: compression is **deterministic**. The same tool output always compresses to the same text, so applying it to every tool result in the history, on every turn, sends the provider an identical prefix each time. No map of compressed text needs to be stored. ```mermaid flowchart LR H["History from the harness
(original tool outputs)"] --> C["Deterministic rules
strip ANSI codes, collapse repeated lines,
keep head + tail of huge outputs"] C --> S["Same compressed history
every turn"] S --> P["Provider prefix unchanged
→ cache keeps hitting"] ``` Rules: - Only **tool results** above a size threshold. User and assistant text is never touched. - Off by default; enabled per team (`compression: {enabled: true, min_chars: 4000, max_chars: 24000}`). - Changing the settings mid-session changes the history once (one cache miss). - Savings are counted per request: removed tokens in the newest tool result at the input price, removed tokens in older results at the cache-read price (that's what they would have cost). - A model-based compressor (LLMLingua-2) could be added later behind the same interface; because it isn't deterministic across versions, it would need a content-hash cache. ## Stateful APIs OpenAI's Responses API can store conversation server-side (`previous_response_id`). Merit Order supports only `store: false`: it rejects `previous_response_id` (400) and sends `store: false` to OpenAI. """Sizing a GPU replica to a model, priced from SkyPilot's catalog.

- **What a model needs** comes from Hugging Face: its weights' size in bytes as published (the safetensors files'
  sizes; their metadata says how many parameters are in 16 bits, 8 bits, or packed 4 bits), and for
  mixture-of-experts models the parameters active per token (its config.json, or a name such as "A3B"), which is
  what sets throughput.
- **Quantizing** (``quantized``) serves weights published in 16 bits at 8 (FP8), or anything above 4 bits at 4
  (AWQ, GPTQ, NVFP4, MXFP4: about 4.25 bits a weight with their scales). It changes what fits and what the GPUs
  compute in, not the quality scores, which are for the weights as published.
- **What GPUs cost** comes from SkyPilot's catalog, through SkyPilot itself (in its own environment, as the
  controller uses it): on-demand and spot prices for every instance with GPUs, by cloud and region. SkyPilot keeps
  its catalogs current on its own schedule; a refresh downloads them again first. Lookups never use cloud
  credentials (none are needed for prices).
- **A replica** is a setup (GPU type and count, 1-8 on one machine) where the weights fill at most ``FIT`` of the
  GPUs' memory, leaving the rest for the KV cache. ``replica_options`` lists the ones worth considering (cheapest per
  hour first, each faster than the cheaper ones); the break-even picks the one that pays from the least traffic.
- **Its throughput** is an estimate: a share of the GPUs' peak dense compute at the precision they compute the
  weights in (``compute_precision``), at two operations per active parameter per token. Input read from the prompt
  cache isn't computed again, so it doesn't count against it. A deployment's configured
  ``capacity_tokens_per_second`` (measured) replaces the estimate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger("meritorder.gpu_sizing")

DEFAULT_CLOUDS = ("aws", "gcp", "azure", "lambda", "runpod", "nebius")
HF_API = "https://huggingface.co/api/models/{id}?blobs=true&expand[]=safetensors&expand[]=siblings"
HF_CONFIG = "https://huggingface.co/{id}/resolve/main/config.json"
FIT = 0.7  # the weights may fill this share of the GPUs' memory; the rest is the KV cache's
CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 6  # the report fetches prices again when they're older than this
SIZES_MAX_AGE_HOURS = 24 * 7
SIZES_VERSION = 2  # stored sizes from an older version are fetched again
FOUR_BIT = 4.25  # bits a 4-bit weight takes with its scales (one 8-bit scale per 32 weights, as MXFP4 and Kimi's checkpoints)
WEIGHTS = ("published", "fp8", "4bit")  # how the weights are served: as published, or quantized to 8 or 4 bits


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Accelerator:
    memory_gb: float
    bf16_tflops: float  # dense, from the vendor's spec sheet
    fp8_tflops: float | None = None  # GPUs with FP8 tensor cores (Ada, Hopper, Blackwell, MI300)
    fp4: bool = False  # FP4 tensor cores (Blackwell): 4-bit weights are computed with 8-bit activations, at the FP8 rate


# Datacenter GPUs vLLM serves on, by SkyPilot's names for them. Peak dense tensor throughput from the spec sheets.
ACCELERATORS = {
    "L4": Accelerator(24, 121, 242),
    "A10G": Accelerator(24, 70),
    "A10": Accelerator(24, 125),
    "L40S": Accelerator(48, 362, 733),
    "A100": Accelerator(40, 312),
    "A100-80GB": Accelerator(80, 312),
    "A100-80GB-SXM": Accelerator(80, 312),
    "H100": Accelerator(80, 989, 1979),
    "H100-SXM": Accelerator(80, 989, 1979),
    "H100-MEGA": Accelerator(80, 989, 1979),
    "H100-NVL": Accelerator(94, 835, 1671),
    "GH200": Accelerator(96, 989, 1979),
    "H200": Accelerator(141, 989, 1979),
    "H200-SXM": Accelerator(141, 989, 1979),
    "B200": Accelerator(180, 2250, 4500, fp4=True),
    "B300": Accelerator(288, 2250, 4500, fp4=True),
    "MI300X": Accelerator(192, 1307, 2615),
}

DTYPE_BYTES = {"F64": 8, "I64": 8, "F32": 4, "I32": 4, "U32": 4, "BF16": 2, "F16": 2, "I16": 2, "U16": 2,
               "F8_E4M3": 1, "F8_E5M2": 1, "I8": 1, "U8": 1, "BOOL": 1}
BITS_NAME = {16: "16-bit", 8: "FP8", 4: "4-bit"}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ what a model needs

def _name_params(hf_id: str) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    """(total, active) parameters from a name like "Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B" or "Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E"."""
    name = hf_id.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    active = (re.search(r"(?:^|[-_])A(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)B(?![a-z])", name, re.I)  # "...-A52B"
              or re.search(r"(?:^|[-_])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)B-\d+E(?![a-z])", name, re.I))  # "...-17B-128E": 17B active
    totals = [float(m.group(1)) * (1e12 if m.group(2).upper() == "T" else 1e9)
              for m in re.finditer(r"(?:^|[-_])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)([BT])(?![a-z])(?!-\d+E)", name, re.I)]
    return (totals[-1] if totals else None), (float(active.group(1)) * 1e9 if active else None)


def active_from_config(config: dict) -> float | None:
    """Parameters each token goes through in a mixture-of-experts model, from its layer sizes: attention, the experts
    it's routed to plus any shared expert, dense layers, and the output head. None when the config describes no
    experts (a dense model) or not enough to work it out. Counted from the shapes, not the stored weights, which
    for 4-bit experts hold two parameters per byte."""
    c = {**config, **(config.get("text_config") if isinstance(config.get("text_config"), dict) else {})}
    experts = c.get("n_routed_experts") or c.get("num_experts") or c.get("num_local_experts") or c.get("moe_num_experts")
    per_token = c.get("num_experts_per_tok") or c.get("moe_topk") or c.get("num_experts_per_token")
    h, layers = c.get("hidden_size"), c.get("num_hidden_layers")
    width = c.get("moe_intermediate_size") or c.get("intermediate_size")
    if not (experts and per_token and h and layers and width) or experts <= per_token:
        return None
    heads = c.get("num_attention_heads")
    head_dim = c.get("head_dim") or (h // heads if heads else None)
    if heads and head_dim:
        kv = c.get("num_key_value_heads") or heads
        attention = 2 * h * heads * head_dim + 2 * h * kv * head_dim  # q and o, k and v
    else:
        attention = 4 * h * h
    freq = c.get("moe_layer_freq")
    moe_layers = sum(1 for x in freq if x) if isinstance(freq, list) else layers - int(c.get("first_k_dense_replace") or 0)
    dense_width = c.get("dense_intermediate_size") or c.get("intermediate_size") or width
    shared = (c.get("shared_expert_intermediate_size") or c.get("shared_intermediate_size")
              or (int(c.get("n_shared_experts") or 0) * width))
    ffn = moe_layers * (per_token * width + shared) * 3 * h + (layers - moe_layers) * dense_width * 3 * h
    return float(layers * attention + ffn + (c.get("vocab_size") or 0) * h)


def _hf_headers() -> dict:
    token = os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN")
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"} if token else {}


async def _get(client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str) -> httpx.Response:
    """GET from Hugging Face, waiting out a rate limit or a hiccup twice before giving up."""
    for attempt in range(3):
        r = await client.get(url, headers=_hf_headers(), follow_redirects=True)
        if r.status_code not in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) or attempt == 2:
            return r
        await asyncio.sleep(1.0 * (attempt + 1))
    return r


def _root_safetensors_bytes(siblings: list[dict]) -> int | None:
    """The model's weights on disk: its top-level .safetensors files (not copies such as gpt-oss's original/), of one
    format where a repository has two (Mistral's ship consolidated-* for mistral-inference and model-* for
    transformers and vLLM: the same weights twice)."""
    files = [f for f in siblings or [] if str(f.get("rfilename", "")).endswith(".safetensors") and "/" not in f["rfilename"]]
    if not files or any(f.get("size") is None for f in files):
        return None
    hf_format = [f for f in files if not f["rfilename"].startswith("consolidated")]
    return sum(int(f["size"]) for f in hf_format or files)


def _bucket(bytes_per_param: float) -> int:
    return 16 if bytes_per_param >= 1.5 else 8 if bytes_per_param >= 0.75 else 4


def _dominant(params_by_bits: dict) -> int:
    """The precision most of the parameters are in, which is what the GPUs compute in."""
    return max((16, 8, 4), key=lambda b: (params_by_bits.get(str(b)) or 0, -b))


def _breakdown(params: dict, files: int | None) -> tuple[int, dict, dict, str]:
    """(weight bytes, bytes by bits, parameters by bits, how) from Hugging Face's parameter counts by dtype and the
    files' size. Packed 4-bit weights (gpt-oss's and Kimi's MXFP4, DeepSeek's FP4 experts) are stored as U8 or I8
    with about half a byte per parameter; the files' size tells them apart from real 8-bit ones."""
    p16 = sum(n for k, n in params.items() if k in ("BF16", "F16"))
    p8 = sum(n for k, n in params.items() if k.startswith("F8"))
    packed = sum(n for k, n in params.items() if k in ("I8", "U8"))
    other = sum(n * DTYPE_BYTES.get(k, 2) for k, n in params.items() if k not in ("BF16", "F16", "I8", "U8") and not k.startswith("F8"))
    known = 2 * p16 + p8 + other
    if files and files < known:  # fewer bytes than the parameters need: the file list isn't the whole model
        files = None
    four = 0
    if files and packed and files > known and (files - known) / packed < 0.75:
        four, how = files - known, "weights from Hugging Face (file sizes; packed 4-bit where stored as bytes)"
    else:
        p8 += packed
        how = "weights from Hugging Face (file sizes)" if files else "weights from Hugging Face (parameter counts)"
    weight = files or known + four
    return (weight, {"16": 2 * p16, "8": p8, "4": four}, {"16": p16, "8": p8, "4": packed if four else 0}, how)


async def fetch_model_size(hf_id: str, client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> dict:
    """{weight_bytes, bytes_by_bits, params_by_bits, bits, total_params, active_params, basis}: the weights as
    published, by precision (16, 8 or 4 bits); ``error`` instead when nothing is known."""
    total = weight = None
    by_bits = params_by_bits = None
    basis = []
    try:
        r = await _get(client, HF_API.format(id=hf_id))
        info = r.json() if r.status_code == 200 else {}
        st = info.get("safetensors") or {}
        params = st.get("parameters") or {}
        files = _root_safetensors_bytes(info.get("siblings") or [])
        if params:
            weight, by_bits, params_by_bits, how = _breakdown(params, files)
            total = float(st.get("total") or sum(params.values()))
            basis.append(how)
        elif files:
            weight = files  # no metadata (a format Hugging Face doesn't parse): the parameters from its name, below
    except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as e:
        log.debug("%s: model info failed: %s", hf_id, e)
    name_total, name_active = _name_params(hf_id)
    if total is None and name_total:
        total = name_total
        if weight:  # file sizes and a parameter count in the name: their ratio says the precision
            bits = _bucket(weight / total)
            basis.append(f"weights from Hugging Face (file sizes), parameters from its name ({BITS_NAME[bits]})")
        else:
            bits, weight = 16, name_total * 2
            basis.append("size from its name, at 16 bits")
        by_bits = {str(b): (weight if b == bits else 0) for b in (16, 8, 4)}
        params_by_bits = {str(b): (total if b == bits else 0) for b in (16, 8, 4)}
    if total is None:
        return {"error": "no size published (gated, or no weights on Hugging Face)"}
    active = name_active
    if active:
        basis.append("active parameters from its name")
    else:
        try:
            r = await _get(client, HF_CONFIG.format(id=hf_id))
            if r.status_code == 200:
                moe = active_from_config(r.json())
                active = min(moe, total) if moe else total
                basis.append("active parameters estimated from its config" if moe else "dense")
        except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as e:
            log.debug("%s: config failed: %s", hf_id, e)
    if not active:
        active = total
        basis.append("assumed dense (no config to read)")
    bits = _dominant(params_by_bits)
    return {"weight_bytes": int(weight), "bytes_by_bits": {k: int(v) for k, v in by_bits.items()},
            "params_by_bits": {k: int(v) for k, v in params_by_bits.items()}, "bits": bits, "published_bits": bits,
            "total_params": int(total), "active_params": int(active), "basis": "; ".join(basis)}


def quantized(size: dict, weights: str) -> dict:
    """The model served with its weights quantized: ``fp8`` serves a 16-bit checkpoint in FP8 (vLLM's
    --quantization fp8, which doesn't apply to a checkpoint that's already quantized); ``4bit`` serves everything
    above 4 bits in 4 (a 4-bit checkpoint made from it: AWQ, GPTQ, NVFP4), at FOUR_BIT bits a weight. Weights
    already at or below the target stay as they are. ``published`` changes nothing."""
    if weights == "published" or "error" in size or "bytes_by_bits" not in size:
        return size
    target = 8 if weights == "fp8" else 4
    by_bits, params = dict(size["bytes_by_bits"]), dict(size["params_by_bits"])
    if target == 8 and (by_bits.get("8") or by_bits.get("4")):
        return {**size, "basis": size["basis"] + "; published already quantized, so served as published"}
    new_bits, saved = (8 if target == 8 else FOUR_BIT), 0.0
    for k in ("16", "8"):
        if int(k) <= target or not by_bits.get(k):
            continue
        shrunk = by_bits[k] * new_bits / int(k)
        saved += by_bits[k] - shrunk
        by_bits[str(target)] = by_bits.get(str(target), 0) + shrunk
        params[str(target)] = params.get(str(target), 0) + params.get(k, 0)
        by_bits[k] = params[k] = 0
    if not saved:
        return {**size, "basis": size["basis"] + f"; already {BITS_NAME[size['bits']]} as published"}
    return {**size, "weight_bytes": int(size["weight_bytes"] - saved), "bytes_by_bits": {k: int(v) for k, v in by_bits.items()},
            "params_by_bits": params, "bits": _dominant(params),
            "basis": size["basis"] + f"; served at {BITS_NAME[target]}" + (f" (about {FOUR_BIT} bits a weight with its scales)" if target == 4 else "")}


async def fetch_model_sizes(hf_ids: list[str], client: httpx.AsyncClient) -> dict:
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(8)

    async def one(i: str):
        async with sem:
            return i, await fetch_model_size(i, client)

    return dict(await asyncio.gather(*(one(i) for i in sorted(set(hf_ids)))))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ what GPUs cost

class SkyPilotMissing(RuntimeError):
    pass


async def fetch_catalog(clouds: list[str], refresh: bool = False) -> dict:
    """GPU offers in these clouds from SkyPilot's catalog (see ``gpu.catalog_offers``)."""
    from .gpu import catalog_offers, sky_available

    if not sky_available():
        raise SkyPilotMissing("SkyPilot isn't installed where the gateway runs: build its image with --build-arg SKYPILOT=0.14.2, "
                              "or point MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON at SkyPilot's Python")
    found = await asyncio.to_thread(catalog_offers, clouds, refresh)
    if not found:
        raise RuntimeError("SkyPilot's catalog lookup failed (see the gateway log)")
    return found


def catalog_clouds(cfg) -> list[str]:
    """The clouds to price: SkyPilot deployments' own clouds first, then the common GPU clouds."""
    own = [c.lower() for b in cfg.backends if b.serve and b.serve.provisioner == "skypilot" for c in b.serve.clouds]
    return list(dict.fromkeys(own + list(DEFAULT_CLOUDS)))


async def refresh(cfg, store, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None, sizes: bool = True, download: bool = False,
                  catalog: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Fetch GPU prices from SkyPilot (``download``: its catalogs too, rather than on its own schedule) and, with
    ``sizes``, every open-weight model's size, and keep them in the store."""
    own = client is None
    client = client or httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60, headers={"User-Agent": "merit-order"})
    try:
        now = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
        clouds = catalog_clouds(cfg)
        failed: Exception | None = None
        out: dict = {}
        try:
            if catalog:
                found = {**await fetch_catalog(clouds, download), "fetched_at": now, "clouds": clouds}
                await store.set_setting("gpu_catalog", found)
                out = {"catalog": {k: found.get(k) for k in ("fetched_at", "clouds", "catalog_updated", "skypilot")}, "offers": len(found["offers"])}
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (sizes are still worth fetching; the caller hears about it below)
            failed = e
        if sizes:
            ids = [m.hf_id for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat" and m.hf_id]
            found = await fetch_model_sizes(ids, client)
            await store.set_setting("model_sizes", {"fetched_at": now, "version": SIZES_VERSION, "models": found})
            out["models"] = len(found)
            out["unsized"] = sorted(i for i, s in found.items() if "error" in s)
        if failed:
            raise failed
        return out
    finally:
        if own:
            await client.aclose()


def _age_hours(stamp: str | None) -> float:
    if not stamp:
        return float("inf")
    return (datetime.now(UTC) - datetime.fromisoformat(stamp)).total_seconds() / 3600


async def current(cfg, store, client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """The stored catalog and model sizes, fetched again first when stale or missing (at the time of the report).
    Prices come through SkyPilot where the gateway has it; otherwise the GPU controller publishes them
    (controller.publish_gpu_prices), and a stale catalog is reported as a problem."""
    from .gpu import sky_available

    catalog = await store.get_setting("gpu_catalog") or {}
    sizes = await store.get_setting("model_sizes") or {}
    ids = {m.hf_id for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat" and m.hf_id}
    stale_sizes = (_age_hours(sizes.get("fetched_at")) > SIZES_MAX_AGE_HOURS or not ids <= set(sizes.get("models") or {})
                   or sizes.get("version") != SIZES_VERSION)
    stale_catalog = _age_hours(catalog.get("fetched_at")) > CATALOG_MAX_AGE_HOURS
    here = sky_available()
    problem = None
    if (stale_catalog and here) or stale_sizes:
        try:
            await refresh(cfg, store, client, sizes=stale_sizes, catalog=stale_catalog and here)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 (a source that's down: the last prices stand, and the report says how old they are)
            log.warning("GPU prices or model sizes couldn't be fetched: %s", e)
            problem = str(e)
        catalog = await store.get_setting("gpu_catalog") or catalog
        sizes = await store.get_setting("model_sizes") or sizes
    if stale_catalog and not here and not problem:
        problem = ("SkyPilot isn't installed where the gateway runs, so GPU prices come from the GPU controller, which "
                   + ("hasn't published any in the last 6 hours" if catalog.get("fetched_at") else "hasn't published any yet")
                   + ": run it (compose --profile gpu, or controller.enabled in the Helm chart), or install SkyPilot in the gateway's image")
    return {**catalog, "problem": problem} if problem else catalog, sizes


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ a replica for a model

def compute_precision(acc: Accelerator, bits: int) -> str:
    """What the GPU computes weights mostly in ``bits`` in: FP8 weights at FP8 where it has FP8 tensor cores (Ada,
    Hopper, Blackwell, MI300); 4-bit weights at FP8 on Blackwell, whose FP4 kernels take 8-bit activations (vLLM's
    for MXFP4; full FP4 needs 4-bit activations too); everything else at 16 bits (Hopper's 4-bit kernels, and every
    GPU without FP8, dequantize the weights)."""
    if acc.fp8_tflops and (bits == 8 or (bits == 4 and acc.fp4)):
        return "FP8"
    return "16-bit"


def peak_tflops(acc: Accelerator, bits: int) -> float:
    """Dense compute per GPU for weights mostly in ``bits``, at the precision it computes them in."""
    return acc.fp8_tflops if compute_precision(acc, bits) == "FP8" else acc.bf16_tflops


def size_replica(size: dict, offers: list[dict], clouds: set[str], spot: bool, fit: float = FIT,
                 accelerators: str | None = None, regions: list[str] | None = None) -> dict:
    """The replica for a model: the cheapest per hour among the offers in ``clouds`` whose memory holds its weights at
    ``fit``, on 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs (how vLLM splits a model), the faster one on a tie. ``accelerators`` ("H100:4")
    fixes the GPU, as a deployment does. Spot prices where asked for and offered, else on-demand."""
    found = replica_options(size, offers, clouds, spot, fit, accelerators, regions)
    return found[0] if isinstance(found, list) else found


def replica_options(size: dict, offers: list[dict], clouds: set[str], spot: bool, fit: float = FIT,
                    accelerators: str | None = None, regions: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict] | dict:
    """Every machine worth considering for a model, cheapest per hour first, each with more compute than the cheaper
    ones (a pricier machine that's no faster never helps): the cheapest takes the least traffic to pay for, a faster
    one may be the only one that pays at all. ``{error}`` when none holds the weights (see ``size_replica``)."""
    if "error" in size and not accelerators:
        return {"error": size["error"]}
    need_gb = size.get("weight_bytes", 0) / 1e9 / fit
    want = None
    if accelerators:
        name, _, n = accelerators.partition(":")
        want = (name.upper() if name.upper() in ACCELERATORS else name, int(n or 1))
    found = []
    for o in offers:
        acc = ACCELERATORS.get(o["accelerator"])
        if acc is None or o["cloud"] not in clouds or o["count"] not in (1, 2, 4, 8) \
                or (want and (o["accelerator"].upper(), o["count"]) != (want[0].upper(), want[1])):
            continue
        if not want and acc.memory_gb * o["count"] < need_gb:
            continue
        price, used_spot = (o["spot"], True) if spot and o["spot"] else (o["on_demand"], False)
        if price is None or (regions and price.get("region") not in regions):
            continue
        tflops = peak_tflops(acc, size.get("bits", 16)) * o["count"]
        found.append(((price["usd_per_hour"], -tflops), {
            "accelerator": o["accelerator"], "count": o["count"], "memory_gb": acc.memory_gb * o["count"], "tflops": tflops,
            "computes_in": compute_precision(acc, size.get("bits", 16)),
            "cloud": o["cloud"], "region": price.get("region"), "instance_type": price.get("instance_type"),
            "spot": used_spot, "usd_per_hour": price["usd_per_hour"],
            "on_demand_usd_per_hour": (o["on_demand"] or {}).get("usd_per_hour"),
            "spot_usd_per_hour": (o["spot"] or {}).get("usd_per_hour")}))
    if not found:
        largest = max((ACCELERATORS[o["accelerator"]].memory_gb * o["count"] for o in offers
                       if o["cloud"] in clouds and o["accelerator"] in ACCELERATORS and o["count"] in (1, 2, 4, 8)), default=0)
        if want:
            return {"error": f"no {accelerators} offer in {', '.join(sorted(clouds))}"}
        return {"error": f"needs {need_gb:,.0f} GB of GPU memory; the largest machine on offer has {largest:,.0f} GB"
                if largest and need_gb > largest else "no offer in the chosen clouds"}
    frontier, fastest = [], 0.0
    for _, replica in sorted(found, key=lambda x: x[0]):
        if replica["tflops"] > fastest:
            frontier.append(replica)
            fastest = replica["tflops"]
    return frontier


def capacity_tps(replica: dict, size: dict, efficiency: float, cache_read_share: float) -> float:
    """Estimated tokens per second one replica serves: ``efficiency`` of its peak compute at 2 operations per active
    parameter per token, for the tokens it has to compute (cache reads are served from the prefix cache)."""
    computed = efficiency * replica["tflops"] * 1e12 / (2 * size["active_params"])
    return computed / max(1.0 - cache_read_share, 0.1)


def replica_plans(cfg, catalog: dict, sizes: dict, clouds: set[str], spot: bool, weights: str = "published",
                  replica_prices: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Per open-weight chat model, the replica its break-even is worked out for: its own deployment's (its GPUs,
    clouds and spot setting, priced from the catalog or at the controller's current price, and its configured
    capacity), else one sized to it, with its weights served as ``weights`` (see ``quantized``). Each is
    {deployment, replica, size, capacity_tps} or {error}; a sized one also has ``options`` (``replica_options``),
    for the break-even to pick the machine that pays from the least traffic."""
    from .gpu import deployment_for

    offers = catalog.get("offers") or []
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for m in cfg.models:
        if m.kind != "chat" or not m.hf_id:
            continue
        options = None
        size = (sizes.get("models") or {}).get(m.hf_id) or {"error": "its size hasn't been fetched yet"}
        size = quantized(size, weights)
        dep = deployment_for(cfg, m)
        sized = "error" not in size
        if dep and dep.serve and dep.serve.provisioner == "skypilot":
            s = dep.serve
            replica = size_replica(size, offers, {c.lower() for c in s.clouds} or clouds, s.use_spot, accelerators=s.accelerators,
                                   regions=s.regions or None)
            if "error" in replica:  # not in the catalog: the configured price
                replica = {"accelerator": s.accelerators.partition(":")[0], "count": int(s.accelerators.partition(":")[2] or 1),
                           "usd_per_hour": dep.gpu_cost_per_hour, "spot": s.use_spot, "source": "configured"}
            else:
                replica["source"] = "catalog"
        elif dep:  # a server you run: its configured price
            replica = {"usd_per_hour": dep.gpu_cost_per_hour, "source": "configured"}
        else:
            found = replica_options(size, offers, clouds, spot)
            if isinstance(found, dict):
                out[m.name] = {"error": found["error"], "size": size if sized else None}
                continue
            for r in found:
                r["source"] = "catalog"
            replica, options = found[0], found
        if dep and (replica_prices or {}).get(dep.name):  # what the controller is paying, or would
            replica = {**replica, "usd_per_hour": replica_prices[dep.name], "source": "controller"}
        configured = dep.capacity_tokens_per_second if dep and dep.capacity_tokens_per_second else None
        if not replica.get("usd_per_hour") or not (configured or (sized and replica.get("tflops"))):
            out[m.name] = {"error": "no price or capacity for its deployment", "size": size if sized else None}
            continue
        out[m.name] = {"deployment": dep.name if dep else None, "replica": replica, "size": size if sized else None, "capacity_tps": configured,
                       **({"options": options} if options else {})}
    return out

"""Switching to another source when a provider fails: errors that arrive after a 200, streams that never
start, Retry-After, busy models versus broken backends, last resorts, alerts, and what people see."""

import asyncio
import time

import httpx
from conftest import ADMIN_KEY
from test_http_backend import CHAT, OPENAI_OK, Upstream, chunks, collect, http_gateway, post, stream_response

from meritorder.backends.base import Backend
from meritorder.backends.http import retry_after
from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, ModelConfig, Route
from meritorder.failover import error_in
from meritorder.formats.sse import iter_sse

OK_STREAM = (b'data: {"id":"c","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""}}]}\n\n'
             b'data: {"id":"c","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"from b"}}]}\n\n'
             b'data: {"id":"c","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":3,"completion_tokens":2}}\n\n'
             b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
OVERLOADED = (b'event: message_start\ndata: {"type":"message_start","message":{"id":"m","type":"message","role":"assistant",'
              b'"content":[],"model":"m-a","usage":{"input_tokens":3,"output_tokens":0}}}\n\n'
              b'event: error\ndata: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"Overloaded"}}\n\n')


async def stream_text(r) -> str:
    out = ""
    for e in await collect(iter_sse(chunks(r.content))):
        d = e.json() or {}
        for c in d.get("choices") or []:
            out += (c.get("delta") or {}).get("content") or ""
    return out


def second_model(gw, name="y", route_model="y-a"):
    gw.cfg.models.append(ModelConfig(name=name, quality={"coding": 4, "general": 4},
                                     routes=[Route(backend="up-a", model=route_model, price={"input": 1, "output": 2})]))


async def test_anthropic_overload_inside_a_200_stream_goes_to_the_next_source(monkeypatch):
    a = Upstream(lambda req: stream_response(OVERLOADED))
    b = Upstream(lambda req: stream_response(OK_STREAM))
    gw = http_gateway(monkeypatch, a, b, primary_format="anthropic")
    r = await post(gw, {**CHAT, "stream": True})
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.headers["x-meritorder-backend"] == "up-b"
    assert r.headers["x-meritorder-failed-over"] == "up-a/m-a 529"
    assert await stream_text(r) == "from b"
    now = time.time()
    assert not gw.backends["up-a"].healthy(now, "m-a") and gw.backends["up-a"].healthy(now)  # only that model is skipped
    await gw.drain()
    alerts = await gw.state.recent_alerts()
    assert alerts and "up-a (m-a) is failing: overloaded" in alerts[0]["text"] and "Traffic goes to up-b" in alerts[0]["text"]
    assert gw.inflight.count("up-a") == 0

    a = Upstream(lambda req: stream_response(b'data: {"id":"c","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""}}]}\n\n', chunk))
    gw = http_gateway(monkeypatch, a, Upstream(lambda req: stream_response(OK_STREAM)))
    r = await post(gw, {**CHAT, "stream": True})
    assert r.headers["x-meritorder-backend"] == "up-b" and await stream_text(r) == "from b"

    a2 = Upstream(httpx.Response(200, json={"error": {"message": "upstream timed out", "code": 504}}))

    async def hang():
        await asyncio.sleep(30)
        yield b""

    a = Upstream(lambda req: httpx.Response(200, headers={"content-type": "text/event-stream"}, content=hang()))
    gw = http_gateway(monkeypatch, a, Upstream(lambda req: stream_response(OK_STREAM)))

    assert BackendConfig(name="g", format="openai", kind="self_hosted", first_byte_timeout_seconds=300).first_byte_timeout() == 300
    assert BackendConfig(name="n", format="openai", first_byte_timeout_seconds=None).first_byte_timeout() is None


def test_error_shapes():
    assert error_in({"type": "error", "error": {"type": "rate_limit_error", "message": "x"}}, "anthropic") == (429, "x")
    assert error_in({"type": "message_start"}, "anthropic") is None
    assert error_in({"error": "plain text"}, "openai") == (502, "plain text")
    assert error_in({"error": {"code": "503", "message": "busy"}}, "openai") == (503, "busy")
    assert error_in({"error": {"type": "insufficient_quota", "message": "q"}}, "openai") == (429, "q")
    assert error_in({"error": {"type": "tokens", "code": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "r"}}, "openai") == (429, "r")
    assert error_in({"error": {"type": "api_error", "code": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "r"}}, "openai") == (429, "r")
    assert error_in({"choices": [{"delta": {"content": "hi"}}]}, "openai") is None
    assert error_in({"data": [{"embedding": [0.1]}], "error": None}, "openai") is None
    assert error_in(None, "openai") is None

# Merit Order — how it works

An open-source, self-hostable LLM gateway whose job is to **cut LLM spend for day-to-day use**
(coding agents like pi and Claude Code, internal apps, SDKs) without users changing how they work.

The name comes from power grids. Operators dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest
marginal cost first, with expensive "peaker" plants switched on only when demand requires them.
Merit Order does the same with tokens. When steady load justifies it, your own GPUs become the
cheap baseload. API endpoints are always available as the peakers that cover spikes and everything
else. The router dispatches every session to the cheapest capacity that meets its quality bar.

It does three things:

1. **Routes** each session to the cheapest model/backend that meets the task's quality bar.
2. **Runs open-weight models on its own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when sustained load makes that cheaper
   than paying per token — and turns them off when it doesn't. API endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex,
   Foundry, …) are always on, as the fallback and the overflow.
3. **Saves tokens** with provider prompt caching, cache-aware routing, and careful compression.

Around that: enterprise auth (Entra first, generic OIDC, SCIM), budgets and hard safeguards, a
**savings ledger** that shows what every request would have cost without the proxy, and a web
console to watch and control all of it: spend, savings, where every GPU runs and what it costs,
and the switches to stop it.

## Read in this order

| Doc | What you'll understand |
|---|---|
| [00 — How it all works](00-how-it-all-works.md) | **Start here.** How your tools connect, how a request gets a level, how models get scores, why the cheapest qualifying route wins, how long conversations are handled, when your GPUs start and stop, and setting up Claude Code, with real numbers ([also as a standalone page](html/how-it-all-works.html)) |
| [01 — Architecture](01-architecture.md) | The boxes and what each one owns |
| [02 — Request flow](02-request-flow.md) | What happens to one request, start to finish |
| [03 — Routing](03-routing.md) | How a model/backend is picked: marginal cost + switching cost |
| [04 — Caching & sessions](04-caching-and-sessions.md) | Who owns what state; why caches don't move between backends |
| [05 — GPU autoscaling](05-gpu-autoscaling.md) | When GPUs come up/down, and overflow to APIs |
| [06 — Auth & spend](06-auth-and-spend.md) | Entra login → virtual keys, budgets, the ledger |
| [07 — Deployment](07-deployment.md) | Compose or Kubernetes, `docker compose up`, supply-chain security |
| [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md) | Spend and savings reports by user, team, project, and time |
| [09 — Decisions](09-decisions.md) | What we decided, why, and what's still open |
| [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md) | **Every rule, as diagrams:** which model, GPU or API, retries, when GPUs start and stop, and what happens when things go wrong |
| [11 — Evals](11-evals.md) | Model quality: scores from published benchmarks, running evals from the console or CLI, the task kinds, judges, the sandbox, and how results become scores |

Every doc is also a web page in [`html/`](html/): one page per doc (`html/routing.html`, …; this
file is `html/overview.html`), all of them on one page (`html/index.html`), and the start-here
explainer with diagrams (`html/how-it-all-works.html`, written by hand).
`python scripts/build_docs_html.py` rebuilds the generated pages from these files; it needs the
`markdown` package (`uv run --with markdown python scripts/build_docs_html.py`).

## Six ideas that drive every design decision

1. **Marginal cost, not list price.** A GPU that is already running is a sunk cost for that hour,
   so its spare capacity is ~free. Use it — even for a *better* model than the task needs.
2. **Moving a session costs money.** Prompt caches live on the backend. Switching backends means
   re-paying for the whole context, so the router counts that before moving anything.
3. **The harness owns the conversation.** The proxy stores routing *metadata* (hashes, timestamps,
   which backend), never conversation content.
4. **APIs are the floor, GPUs are an optimization.** Every model that runs on our GPUs should also
   have an API route, so GPUs never become a single point of failure. The console warns about any
   model that doesn't before anyone stops its GPUs.
5. **Clone and run.** One `docker compose up` with one API key gives you a working gateway. GPUs,
   Entra, and Kubernetes are opt-in layers.
6. **Every cost is visible next to the switch that controls it.** Anything that spends money (a
   team, a GPU, the whole organization) shows what it's costing and can be capped or stopped from
   the console.

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Harness** | The client driving the model: pi, Claude Code, Cursor, an SDK app |
| **Session** | One conversation/agent run; the unit of stickiness and caching |
| **Backend** | A configured place models run: `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `openrouter`, or your own GPUs (`gpu-qwen-coder`) |
| **Quality floor** | Minimum capability the classifier says a task needs (e.g. `coding:3`) |
| **Headroom** | Spare capacity on a running GPU replica before it misses its latency target |
| **Shadow price** | Internal price for self-hosted tokens: ~0 when idle, rising toward API price as it fills |
| **Rebuild cost** | Cost to re-process a session's context on a backend whose cache is cold |
| **Counterfactual cost** | What a request would have cost on the baseline model (`baseline_model`, set for the organization or a team) at its API price |

## Status

| Area | Built | Not yet |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway | OpenAI Chat + Responses, Anthropic Messages, embeddings; pass-through and translation; Anthropic, Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex (Claude, and Gemini through Vertex's OpenAI-compatible endpoint), Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, OpenRouter, direct open-model vendors, any OpenAI-compatible server | Gemini native API |
| Routing | Rule classifier, marginal-cost router with rebuild cost, stickiness, re-routing sessions that outgrow their model's context window, refusal fallback, opt-in substitution, automatic reasoning effort, live prices (OpenRouter, LiteLLM; every 15 minutes), quality scores from published benchmarks (Epoch AI by default; daily) or measured (`meritorder eval`) | A learned router |
| GPUs | Break-even controller, SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM, static servers, SkyPilot catalog prices, stop / drain / pin / stop-all, fleet safeguards, activity log | Kubernetes-native provisioning (llm-d / KServe) |
| Token savings | Automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, deterministic compression, opt-in response cache | Model-based compression (LLMLingua) |
| Identity and spend | Keys, Entra/OIDC login, SCIM, roles, People page, team/user/org/GPU budgets, rate limits, per-session and per-request caps | Google sign-in (works as generic OIDC, untested) |
| Reporting | Ledger, savings by cause, reports API, console, CSV/JSONL export to S3, Prometheus with a Grafana dashboard, OpenTelemetry, alerts and weekly digests to a webhook; OpenRouter costs taken from what it billed | Reconciliation with other providers' bills, Parquet |

# Merit Order configuration.
#
# Strings support ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Secrets come from the
# environment (see .env.example), never from this file.
#
# Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are switched off automatically,
# so this file works with whatever provider keys you have. Run `meritorder check`
# to see what is usable.
#
# PRICES are dollars per million tokens. Anthropic prices are from published
# rates on 2026-11-09; routes without a price use prices.json, which
# `meritorder prices refresh` updates from OpenRouter's catalog; AWS, Azure, and GCP set their
# own prices and you may have negotiated discounts, so verify before trusting
# the savings numbers. QUALITY scores (1-5) are starting points; tune them with
# your own evals.

# "What you'd use without Merit Order": the counterfactual for savings reports.
baseline_model: claude-sonnet

# Open-weight models, direct vendor APIs, and OpenRouter's free tier.
include:
  - models-open.yaml
  - models-embeddings.yaml

default_max_tokens: 16000

routing:
  auto_model: auto              # clients send model="auto" to let the router choose
  switch_margin_pct: 10         # only move a session if it's this much cheaper (after cache rebuild)
  est_output_tokens: 600

backends:
  # Keys come from the environment (value_env). In Kubernetes you can also add
  # value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/<NAME> so a rotated key works without a restart
  # (docs/07-deployment.md#secrets). Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure can run keyless on workload identity.
  # --- always available: in-process mocks for trying things out and for tests
  mock-anthropic:
    kind: mock
    format: anthropic
    mock_min_cache_tokens: 1024   # like Anthropic: shorter prompts aren't cached
  mock-openai:
    kind: mock
    format: openai

  # --- Anthropic Messages API family
  anthropic:
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://api.anthropic.com
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}

  bedrock:                      # Claude in Amazon Bedrock (Messages API, SigV4 or bearer token)
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic
    anthropic_version: "2026-10-21"
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}", profile: "${AWS_PROFILE:-}"}

  foundry-claude:               # Claude in Microsoft Foundry
    format: anthropic
    base_url: ${AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT}/anthropic
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY}

  vertex:                       # Claude on Vertex AI (needs: uv sync --extra gcp)
    enabled: false
    format: anthropic
    flavor: vertex
    project: ${GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT}
    region: global
    auth: {type: google}

  # --- OpenAI-compatible family
  azure-openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: ${AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT}/openai/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, header: api-key, value_env: AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENAI_API_KEY}
    supports_prompt_cache_key: true
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openrouter:                   # one key for open-weight and Chinese models (and most others)
    format: openai
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY}

  local-vllm:                   # a vLLM/SGLang server you already run (always used while it's up)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_LOCAL_VLLM:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 8.0          # per replica; used for chargeback and break-even
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 2500
    max_concurrency: 64             # vLLM --max-num-seqs (or what the KV cache fits): saturation seen within seconds
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: static
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      static_url: ${LOCAL_VLLM_URL:-http://localhost:8000/v1}
      min_replicas: 1

  gpu-qwen-coder:               # SkyPilot starts this on cloud GPUs when demand pays for it
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_SKYPILOT:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0         # fallback only: with SkyPilot installed, prices come from its catalog per cloud/region/instance
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000
    max_concurrency: 64             # per replica; at full, requests spill to APIs or wait (max_waiting, default 32)
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: skypilot
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      accelerators: "H100:4"
      use_spot: true
      clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda]
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
      vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144"
      max_replicas: 4
      scale_up_after_minutes: 10
      hold_minutes: 30

models:

    aliases: ["claude-opus-*", "anthropic/claude-opus*", "opus"]

  claude-haiku:

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

from ..config import BackendConfig
from ..formats.sse import SSEEvent

RETRYABLE_STATUS = {408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529}
CAPACITY_STATUS = {429, 503, 529}  # this model is busy here; others on the same backend usually aren't
# Failures that say something about one model on a backend (its capacity, its deployment) rather than the
# backend as a whole (its credentials, its network). Only these skip just that model.
MODEL_SCOPED_STATUS = CAPACITY_STATUS | {404, 408, 409, 425, 500}
MAX_CAPACITY_WAIT = 300.0


class BackendError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int, message: str, body: dict | None = None, retryable: bool = False,
                 retry_after: float | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.message = message
        self.body = body
        self.retryable = retryable
        self.retry_after = retry_after  # seconds, from the provider's Retry-After header


def describe(status: int) -> str:
    """A failure in words, for logs, alerts, and error messages."""
    return {429: "rate limited", 529: "overloaded", 503: "unavailable", 404: "model or deployment not found",
            401: "credentials rejected", 403: "access denied", 504: "timed out", 502: "unreachable or bad response",
            500: "server error", 408: "request timeout"}.get(status, f"HTTP {status}")


@dataclass
class Outage:
    """Why a backend, or one model on it, is being skipped and until when."""

    until: float
    status: int
    message: str
    capacity: bool  # busy rather than broken: still worth trying when nothing else can serve the request


@dataclass
class UpstreamResponse:
    status: int
    headers: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    body: dict | None = None
    events: AsyncIterator[SSEEvent] | None = None
    _close: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | None = None

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        if self._close is not None:
            await self._close()
            self._close = None


class Backend:
    """A place a model runs. Subclasses implement ``send``."""

    def __init__(self, cfg: BackendConfig):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.name = cfg.name
        self.format = cfg.format
        self.kind = cfg.kind
        self._failures = 0
        self._open_until = 0.0
        self._model_failures: dict[str, int] = {}
        self._model_open: dict[str, Outage] = {}
        self.outage: Outage | None = None  # the whole backend's, while it's being skipped
        # Self-hosted deployments managed by the controller: set from published state.
        self.available = not (cfg.kind == "self_hosted" and cfg.serve is not None)
        self.draining = False
        self.unavailable_reason: str | None = None  # shown when a request has nowhere else to go
        self.live_cost_per_hour: float | None = None  # per replica, from the controller (SkyPilot catalog) when known
        self.replicas: int | None = None  # running replicas, from the controller
        self.reported_waiting: int | None = None  # requests waiting in vLLM at the controller's last sample
        self.deploy: dict | None = None  # the controller's published record for this deployment

    # Circuit breaker, per backend and per model on it.
    #   capacity (429/503/529): skip that model here for Retry-After, else 10 s doubling to 5 min
    #   model or deployment missing (404): skip that model here for 5 minutes, doubling to an hour while it stays missing
    #   credentials rejected (401/403): skip the backend for 1 minute doubling to 10
    #   anything else (5xx, timeouts, network): after 3 in a row, skip the backend for 5 s doubling to 60 s
    def healthy(self, now: float, model: str | None = None) -> bool:
        if now < self._open_until:
            return False
        if model is None:
            return True
        o = self._model_open.get(model)
        return o is None or now >= o.until

    def skipped(self, now: float, model: str | None = None) -> Outage | None:
        """The outage this backend (or model on it) is being skipped for right now, if any."""
        if now < self._open_until:
            return self.outage or Outage(self._open_until, 0, "repeated failures", capacity=False)
        o = self._model_open.get(model) if model else None
        return o if o and now < o.until else None

    def cooling_models(self, now: float) -> dict[str, Outage]:
        return {m: o for m, o in self._model_open.items() if now < o.until}

    def record_failure(self, now: float, model: str | None = None, status: int = 0, retry_after: float | None = None,
                       message: str = "") -> Outage | None:
        """Count a failure. Returns the outage if this one started skipping the backend or model (for alerts)."""
        scoped = model is not None and status in MODEL_SCOPED_STATUS
        n = (self._model_failures.get(model, 0) if scoped else self._failures) + 1
        if scoped:
            self._model_failures[model] = n
        else:
            self._failures = n
        if status in CAPACITY_STATUS or (retry_after and status in RETRYABLE_STATUS):
            wait = min(retry_after if retry_after else 10.0 * 2 ** (n - 1), MAX_CAPACITY_WAIT)
        elif scoped and status == 404:
            wait = min(300.0 * 2 ** (n - 1), 3600.0)  # not deployed there yet: check back less and less often
        elif status in (401, 403):
            wait = min(60.0 * 2 ** (n - 1), 600.0)
        elif n >= 3:
            wait = min(60.0, 5.0 * 2 ** (n - 3))
        else:
            return None
        was_healthy = self.healthy(now, model if scoped else None)
        outage = Outage(now + wait, status, message, capacity=status in CAPACITY_STATUS)
        if scoped:
            self._model_open[model] = outage
        else:
            self._open_until, self.outage = now + wait, outage
        return outage if was_healthy else None

    def record_success(self, model: str | None = None) -> bool:
        """A request worked. Returns True if the backend or model was being skipped (it has recovered)."""
        recovered = self._failures >= 3 or self.outage is not None or (model is not None and model in self._model_open)
        self._failures = 0
        self._open_until = 0.0
        self.outage = None
        if model is not None:
            self._model_failures.pop(model, None)
            self._model_open.pop(model, None)
        return recovered

    async def send(self, body: dict, stream: bool, headers: dict[str, str]) -> UpstreamResponse:
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def count_tokens(self, body: dict, headers: dict[str, str]) -> dict | None:
        return None

    async def close(self) -> None:
        return None

"""Configuration: one YAML file plus environment variables for secrets.

Strings in the YAML may reference environment variables as ``${NAME}`` or
``${NAME:-default}``. Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are
disabled automatically, so one config file works with whatever keys you have.
"""

class PriceTier(BaseModel):
    """Prices for requests whose prompt is longer than ``above`` tokens (e.g. Claude Haiku 5.5 above 100K,
    OpenAI's GPT-6.x above 272K). Dollars per million tokens."""

    above: int
    input: float
    output: float
    cache_read: float | None = None
    cache_write: float | None = None


class Price(BaseModel):
    """Dollars per million tokens."""

    input: float = 0.0
    output: float = 0.0
    cache_read: float | None = None  # default: 0.1 x input
    cache_write: float | None = None  # default: input (no write premium)
    # Server-side tools billed per call, on top of tokens: Anthropic web search is $10 per 1,000.
    # (Web fetch adds only tokens. Code-execution container time isn't modeled.)
    web_search_per_1k: float = 10.0
    tiers: list[PriceTier] = []  # long-prompt prices, which replace the ones above when they apply
    # Where the price came from: "openrouter" or "litellm" (live lists, refreshed by the worker), or "config"
    # (written into the configuration: an override such as a negotiated discount, or a price no list has).
    source: str | None = None

    def read(self) -> float:
        return self.cache_read if self.cache_read is not None else self.input * 0.1

    def write(self) -> float:
        return self.cache_write if self.cache_write is not None else self.input

    def at(self, prompt_tokens: int) -> "Price":
        """The price for a request with this many prompt tokens (cached ones included), long-context tiers applied."""
        tier = max((t for t in self.tiers if prompt_tokens > t.above), key=lambda t: t.above, default=None)
        if tier is None:
            return self
        return self.model_copy(update={"input": tier.input, "output": tier.output, "tiers": [],
                                       "cache_read": tier.cache_read if tier.cache_read is not None else (
                                           None if self.cache_read is None else self.cache_read * tier.input / self.input if self.input else None),
                                       "cache_write": tier.cache_write if tier.cache_write is not None else (
                                           None if self.cache_write is None else self.cache_write * tier.input / self.input if self.input else None)})


class BackendAuth(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["none", "api_key", "aws_sigv4", "azure_ad", "google"] = "none"
    header: str = "authorization"  # api_key: header to put the key in
    prefix: str | None = None  # api_key: defaults to "Bearer " for the authorization header
    value_env: str | None = None  # api_key: env var holding the key
    # api_key: file holding the key (e.g. a mounted Kubernetes Secret). Re-read when it changes, so a
    # rotated key takes effect without a restart. Falls back to value_env if the file is missing or empty.
    value_file: str | None = None
    value: str | None = None  # api_key: literal key (prefer value_env)
    service: str | None = None  # aws_sigv4
    region: str | None = None  # aws_sigv4
    profile: str | None = None  # aws_sigv4
    scope: str | None = None  # azure_ad

    def key(self) -> str | None:
        if self.value:
            return self.value
        if self.value_file:
            key = read_secret_file(self.value_file)
            if key:
                return key
        if self.value_env:
            return os.environ.get(self.value_env) or None
        return None

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """Where the key is expected, for "not set" messages."""
        where = [w for w in (self.value_file, self.value_env) if w]
        return " or ".join(where) or "api key"


_SECRET_FILES: dict[str, tuple[tuple[int, int], str | None]] = {}


def read_secret_file(path: str) -> str | None:
    """The file's contents, stripped; cached until its modification time or size changes.

    Kubernetes updates a mounted Secret by swapping a symlink, so ``stat`` (which follows it) sees the change.
    """
    try:
        st = os.stat(path)
    except OSError:
        _SECRET_FILES.pop(path, None)
        return None
    sig = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
    cached = _SECRET_FILES.get(path)
    if cached and cached[0] == sig:
        return cached[1]
    try:
        value = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() or None
    except OSError:
        value = None
    _SECRET_FILES[path] = (sig, value)
    return value

    effort_format: Literal["auto", "anthropic", "openai", "openrouter", "none"] = "auto"

    # from the URL. price_prefix is the provider's prefix in LiteLLM's list (e.g. "vertex_ai/"); None picks it.
    price_source: Literal["auto", "openrouter", "litellm", "none"] = "auto"

    api: Literal["chat", "responses"] = "chat"
    # What a request cost: "reported" uses the amount the backend bills and returns with the response
    # (OpenRouter's usage.cost, which reflects whichever provider it picked); "catalog" prices the tokens
    # from the catalog. "auto" picks reported for OpenRouter and catalog otherwise.
    billed_cost: Literal["auto", "reported", "catalog"] = "auto"
    cache_ttl_seconds: int = 300
    timeout_seconds: float = 600.0
    # Streams only: give up on this backend (and try the next one) if it hasn't started answering by then: response
    # headers plus the first event (not the first token, so slow reasoning models are fine). None: wait timeout_seconds.
    # Default 120 s for APIs; off for self-hosted GPUs, where a request may wait in vLLM's queue on purpose.
    first_byte_timeout_seconds: float | None = Field(default=120.0, gt=0)

    def first_byte_timeout(self) -> float | None:
        if self.kind == "self_hosted" and "first_byte_timeout_seconds" not in self.model_fields_set:
            return None
        return self.first_byte_timeout_seconds
    extra_headers: dict[str, str] = {}
    # self-hosted economics
    gpu_cost_per_hour: float = 0.0  # per replica
    capacity_tokens_per_second: float = 2000.0  # per replica, measured at your latency target

    max_concurrency: int | None = None
    # When this backend is saturated and no other route can take a request, the request still goes here and
    # waits in vLLM's queue, up to this many waiting per replica. Beyond that the gateway answers 503.
    max_waiting: int = 32
    serve: ServeConfig | None = None  # set: the controller provisions this backend on demand
    disabled_reason: str | None = None  # set at load time when credentials or URL are missing
    # mock
    mock_latency_ms: int = 15
    mock_min_cache_tokens: int = 0  # prompts shorter than this aren't cached (Anthropic: 1024 on most models)

class ModelConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str = ""
    kind: Literal["chat", "embedding"] = "chat"
    aliases: list[str] = []
    # 1-5 per task type (decimals allowed). Used with `quality.source: config`, or until a live source has been
    # fetched; once it has, a task type it doesn't cover scores 0 and `auto` won't pick the model for it.
    # quality_override always wins.
    quality: dict[str, float] = {}
    quality_override: dict[str, float] = {}
    benchmark_name: str | None = None  # the model's name in benchmark data, when its route ids don't match it
    quality_sources: dict[str, str] = {}  # set when loaded: where each score came from (epoch, artificial_analysis, config, override)
    hf_id: str | None = None  # Hugging Face repo, used when self-hosting the weights
    context_window: int | None = None  # tokens; filled from prices.json when not set
    # The most output (thinking plus reply) the model can write in one response; filled from prices.json when not set.
    # Requests that don't set max_tokens get this, so nothing is cut short by a limit the model doesn't have.
    max_output_tokens: int | None = None
    effort_levels: list[str] = []  # reasoning effort levels the model accepts; empty = don't set effort
    license: str | None = None
    routes: list[Route]

    def matches(self, requested: str) -> bool:
        if requested == self.name:
            return True
        return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(requested, pattern) for pattern in self.aliases)

    def q(self, task: str) -> float:
        return self.quality.get(task, self.quality.get("general", 0))

def _allowed(name: str, patterns: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Glob allow-list with ``!pattern`` exclusions, e.g. ["*", "!openrouter-free", "!deepseek"]."""
    if any(p.startswith("!") and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, p[1:]) for p in patterns):
        return False
    return any(not p.startswith("!") and fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, p) for p in patterns)

class RoutingConfig(BaseModel):
    auto_model: str = "auto"
    switch_margin_pct: float = 10.0
    switch_margin_usd: float = 0.01
    est_output_tokens: int = 600
    est_new_tokens_per_turn: int = 2000
    min_expected_turns: int = 3
    max_expected_turns: int = 30
    shadow_knee: float = 0.6  # self-hosted utilization where the shadow price starts rising
    shadow_floor: float = 0.02  # shadow price below the knee, as a fraction of API price
    max_attempts: int = 3
    # Reasoning effort for `auto` requests by quality-floor level (levels not listed keep the model default).
    # Set for every level so a model runs the same way whichever it is (Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium,
    # most others to high), and evals measure each level at the effort it's served with.
    effort_by_floor: dict[int, str] = {1: "low", 2: "low", 3: "medium", 4: "high", 5: "high"}
    # The highest level `auto` gives a Claude Code request of each class (the x-claude-code-request-class header).
    # Side requests (session titles, summaries, permission checks) are small jobs; a compaction summary needs a
    # capable model, not the conversation's top level. Classes not listed (main, subagent, workflow) aren't capped.
    request_class_levels: dict[str, int] = {"auxiliary": 1, "compaction": 3}
    # What decides among routes that cost about the same. Each priority is how much more (%) a route may cost
    # than the cheapest and still win by being faster: `cost` only breaks ties, `speed` pays up to double.
    # Teams (`priority`) and requests (X-MeritOrder-Priority) can choose another one.
    priority: Priority = "cost"
    priority_premium_pct: dict[str, float] = {"cost": 2.0, "balanced": 20.0, "speed": 100.0}
    # Every Nth new session can go to a route within that range whose speed is unknown or out of date, so
    # the router keeps measuring the alternatives. 0 never does.
    speed_check_every: int = Field(default=10, ge=0)

    @field_validator("request_class_levels")
    @classmethod
    def _class_levels(cls, v: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, int]:
        bad = {k: n for k, n in v.items() if not 1 <= int(n) <= 5}
        if bad:
            raise ValueError(f"request class levels must be 1-5: {bad}")
        return {k.lower(): int(n) for k, n in v.items()}

    @field_validator("priority_premium_pct", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _all_priorities(cls, v):
        """A partial map (just `balanced: 30`) keeps the other defaults."""
        merged = {"cost": 2.0, "balanced": 20.0, "speed": 100.0, **(v or {})}
        unknown = set(merged) - set(PRIORITIES)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown priorities {sorted(unknown)}; use {', '.join(PRIORITIES)}")
        if any(float(x) < 0 for x in merged.values()):
            raise ValueError("a priority's premium can't be negative")
        return merged

    backends: list[BackendConfig]

    auth: AuthConfig = AuthConfig()

    # Only for models whose output limit isn't known (max_output_tokens unset and not in prices.json): what to
    # send to Anthropic-format backends, which require a limit, when the client doesn't set one.
    default_max_tokens: int = 16000
    prices_file: str = "prices.json"
