    # they must be current; a refresh that changes nothing changes nothing.
    prices_refresh_minutes: float = Field(default=15.0, gt=0)
    config_dir: str = "."

    def team(self, name: str) -> TeamConfig:
        for t in self.teams:
            if t.name == name:
                return t
        for t in self.teams:
            if t.name == "default":
                return t
        return TeamConfig(name=name)

    def model(self, name: str | None) -> ModelConfig | None:
        if not name:
            return None
        for m in self.models:
            if m.name == name:
                return m
        for m in self.models:
            if m.matches(name):
                return m
        return None

    def backend(self, name: str) -> BackendConfig | None:
        for b in self.backends:
            if b.name == name:
                return b
        return None


_ENV_RE = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)(?::-([^}]*))?\}")


def _interpolate(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return _ENV_RE.sub(lambda m: os.environ.get(m.group(1)) or (m.group(2) or ""), value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_interpolate(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: _interpolate(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    return value


def _named(section: Any) -> list[dict]:
    """Accept either a mapping of name -> settings or a list of settings with names."""
    if section is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(section, dict):
        return [{**(v or {}), "name": k} for k, v in section.items()]
    return list(section)


def default_config_path() -> Path:
    env = os.environ.get("MERITORDER_CONFIG")
    if env:
        return Path(env)
    for candidate in (Path("meritorder.yaml"), Path("config/meritorder.yaml")):
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    return Path("config/meritorder.yaml")


def _load_raw(path: Path, seen: set[Path]) -> dict:
    """Read one YAML file plus anything it lists under ``include:`` (merged in order)."""
    path = path.resolve()
    if path in seen:
        return {}
    seen.add(path)
    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}
    merged: dict = {}
    for inc in raw.pop("include", None) or []:
        sub = _load_raw((path.parent / inc), seen)
        for section in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
            if section in sub:
                merged.setdefault(section, {}).update(_as_mapping(sub[section]))
        for k, v in sub.items():
            if k not in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
                merged.setdefault(k, v)
    for section in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
        if section in raw:
            merged.setdefault(section, {}).update(_as_mapping(raw[section]))
    for k, v in raw.items():
        if k not in ("backends", "models", "teams"):
            merged[k] = v
    return merged


def _as_mapping(section: Any) -> dict:
    if isinstance(section, dict):
        return section
    return {item["name"]: item for item in section or []}


def parse_prices(data: dict) -> tuple[dict[str, Price], dict[str, int], set[str], dict[str, int]]:
    """prices.json: route prices, context windows, models that take a reasoning effort, and output limits."""
    prices = {k: Price.model_validate(v) for k, v in (data.get("prices") or {}).items()}
    return (prices, {k: int(v) for k, v in (data.get("context") or {}).items()}, set(data.get("reasoning") or []),
            {k: int(v) for k, v in (data.get("max_output") or {}).items()})


def load_catalog(path: Path) -> dict:
    """prices.json: the live catalog (prices, limits, and the `quality` section), as last refreshed."""
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}
    return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}


def load_prices(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Price], dict[str, int], set[str], dict[str, int]]:
    return parse_prices(load_catalog(path))


def apply_quality(cfg: "Config", catalog: dict) -> None:
    """Each model's quality: the live source's scores where it has them (if it's the configured source and scale);
    quality_override always wins. A task type the live source doesn't cover gets 0 ("unmeasured"): `auto` won't pick
    the model for it on a score nobody measured, though requests that name it still work. Without live data at all
    (never fetched), the configured scores stand. Records where each came from in ``quality_sources``."""
    section = catalog.get("quality") or {}
    same = section.get("source") == cfg.quality.source and section.get("scale") == cfg.quality.scale
    live = (section.get("scores") or {}) if cfg.quality.source != "config" and same else {}
    mock = {b.name for b in cfg.backends if b.kind == "mock"}
    for m in cfg.models:
        m.quality_sources = {t: "config" for t in m.quality}
        if live and m.kind == "chat" and not all(r.backend in mock for r in m.routes):
            for task in list(m.quality):
                if task not in (live.get(m.name) or {}):
                    m.quality[task] = 0.0
                    m.quality_sources[task] = "unmeasured"
        for task, v in (live.get(m.name) or {}).items():
            m.quality[task] = float(v)
            m.quality_sources[task] = cfg.quality.source
        for task, v in m.quality_override.items():
            m.quality[task] = float(v)
            m.quality_sources[task] = "override"


def effort_format(b: "BackendConfig") -> str:
    if b.effort_format != "auto":
        return b.effort_format
    if b.format == "anthropic":
        return "anthropic"
    host = b.base_url.lower()
    if "openrouter.ai" in host:
        return "openrouter"
    if "api.openai.com" in host or ".openai.azure.com" in host:
        return "openai"
    return "none"


def uses_reported_cost(b: "BackendConfig") -> bool:
    if b.billed_cost != "auto":
        return b.billed_cost == "reported"
    return b.kind == "api" and "openrouter.ai" in b.base_url.lower()


def load_raw_config(path: str | Path | None = None) -> dict:
    """The merged config document (includes resolved, ${ENV} references left as written)."""
    path = Path(path) if path else default_config_path()
    return _load_raw(path, set())


def build_config(raw: dict, config_dir: str | Path = ".", prices_data: dict | None = None, quiet: bool = False) -> Config:
    """Validate a merged config document and resolve environment references, prices, and capabilities.

    ``prices_data`` (the prices.json structure) overrides the file in ``config_dir``; the
    database-backed config passes the prices it stores.
    """
    import copy

    raw = _interpolate(copy.deepcopy(raw))
    oidc = (raw.get("auth") or {}).get("oidc")
    if isinstance(oidc, dict) and not (oidc.get("issuer") and oidc.get("client_id")):
        raw["auth"]["oidc"] = None
    raw["backends"] = _named(raw.get("backends"))
    raw["models"] = _named(raw.get("models"))
    if "teams" in raw:
        raw["teams"] = _named(raw.get("teams"))
    cfg = Config.model_validate(raw)
    _disable_unusable_backends(cfg, quiet)
    cfg.config_dir = str(Path(config_dir).resolve())
    catalog = prices_data if prices_data is not None else load_catalog(Path(config_dir) / cfg.prices_file)
    prices, contexts, reasoning, outputs = parse_prices(catalog)
    apply_quality(cfg, catalog)
    unpriced = []
    for m in cfg.models:
        if m.context_window is None:
            m.context_window = contexts.get(m.name)
        if m.max_output_tokens is None:
            m.max_output_tokens = outputs.get(m.name)
        if not m.effort_levels and m.name in reasoning and m.kind == "chat":
            m.effort_levels = ["low", "medium", "high"]
        for r in m.routes:
            if r.price is None:
                r.price = prices.get(f"{r.backend}:{r.model}")
                if r.price is None:
                    unpriced.append(f"{m.name}@{r.backend}")
            elif r.price.source is None:
                r.price.source = "config"
    unknown = sorted({r.backend for m in cfg.models for r in m.routes} - {b.name for b in cfg.backends})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"routes refer to backends that aren't defined: {', '.join(unknown)}")
    # Savings are measured against the baseline model: a typo there would silently zero them.
    chat = {m.name for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat"}
    for where, name in [("baseline_model", cfg.baseline_model)] + [(f"teams.{t.name}.baseline_model", t.baseline_model) for t in cfg.teams]:
        if name and name not in chat:
            raise ValueError(f"{where} is '{name}', which isn't a configured chat model")
    if unpriced and not quiet:
        log.info("routes without a known price (excluded from auto routing): %s", ", ".join(unpriced))
    return cfg


def load_config(path: str | Path | None = None) -> Config:
    path = Path(path) if path else default_config_path()
    return build_config(load_raw_config(path), path.parent)


_AZURE_PROJECT = re.compile(r"(\.services\.ai\.azure\.com)/api/projects/[^/]+", re.IGNORECASE)


def normalize_base_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Accept the endpoint forms people actually have in their environment.

    * Azure AI Foundry project URLs (``.../api/projects/<name>``): Claude and the
      OpenAI v1 API live at the resource root, so the project path is dropped.
    * An endpoint that already ends in the API path the config appends
      (``.../openai/v1/openai/v1``) is collapsed.
    """
    url = _AZURE_PROJECT.sub(r"\1", url.rstrip("/"))
    for suffix in ("/openai/v1", "/anthropic", "/v1"):
        while url.endswith(suffix + suffix):
            url = url[: -len(suffix)]
    return url


def _disable_unusable_backends(cfg: Config, quiet: bool = False) -> None:
    for b in cfg.backends:
        b.base_url = normalize_base_url(b.base_url)
        if not b.enabled:
            continue
        reason = None
        if b.kind == "self_hosted" and b.serve is not None:
            pass  # endpoint is published by the capacity controller at runtime
        elif b.kind != "mock":
            if b.flavor == "vertex":
                if not b.project:
                    reason = "no GCP project configured"
            elif not b.base_url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                reason = f"base_url {b.base_url!r} is not a URL"
            if b.auth.type == "api_key" and not b.auth.key():
                reason = f"{b.auth.describe()} is not set"
        if reason:
            b.enabled = False
            b.disabled_reason = reason
            if not quiet:
                log.info("backend %s disabled: %s", b.name, reason)

"""Hidden tests for c5-lisp."""

import sys
import threading

from solution import LispError, run


def raises(src):
    try:
        run(src)
    except LispError:
        return True
    return False


def peak_depth(src):
    """run(src) and the deepest Python call stack reached while it ran (counted with a profiler, in every thread)."""
    depth, peak = {}, [0]

    def prof(frame, event, arg):
        if event == "call":
            t = threading.get_ident()
            depth[t] = depth.get(t, 0) + 1
            peak[0] = max(peak[0], depth[t])
        elif event == "return":
            t = threading.get_ident()
            depth[t] = depth.get(t, 0) - 1

    sys.setprofile(prof)
    threading.setprofile(prof)
    try:
        out = run(src)
    finally:
        sys.setprofile(None)
        threading.setprofile(None)
    return out, peak[0]


def constant_depth(template, small=10, big=1000):
    """Outputs for N=small and N=big, and whether the Python stack depth stayed the same (within a small slack)."""
    out1, d1 = peak_depth(template.replace("N", str(small)))
    out2, d2 = peak_depth(template.replace("N", str(big)))
    return out1, out2, d2 - d1 <= 50


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- proper tail calls

def test_tail_call_in_if():
    small, big, ok = constant_depth("(define (loop i acc) (if (= i 0) acc (loop (- i 1) (+ acc 2)))) (loop N 0)")
    assert (small, big) == ("20", "2000")
    assert ok


def test_tail_call_in_cond_clauses():
    src = """(define c 0)
             (define (f n) (cond ((< n 0) 'neg)
                                 ((= n 0) (list 'done c))
                                 ((odd? n) (set! c (+ c 1)) (f (- n 1)))
                                 (else (f (- n 1)))))
             (define (odd? n) (= (remainder n 2) 1))
             (f N)"""
    small, big, ok = constant_depth(src)
    assert (small, big) == ("(done 5)", "(done 500)")
    assert ok


def test_tail_call_as_last_operand_of_and():
    small, big, ok = constant_depth("(define (f n) (if (= n 0) 'end (and #t 1 (f (- n 1))))) (f N)")
    assert (small, big) == ("end", "end")
    assert ok


def test_tail_call_as_last_operand_of_or():
    small, big, ok = constant_depth("(define (g n) (or (= n 0) #f (g (- n 1)))) (g N)")
    assert (small, big) == ("#t", "#t")
    assert ok

    assert ok

def _client(routes: dict) -> httpx.AsyncClient:
    calls: dict[str, int] = {}

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        url = str(request.url)
        calls[url] = calls.get(url, 0) + 1
        for prefix, answer in routes.items():
            if url.startswith(prefix):
                status, body = answer(calls[url]) if callable(answer) else answer
                return httpx.Response(status, json=body)
        return httpx.Response(404, json={})

    return httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))


async def test_model_size_from_hugging_face(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(gs.asyncio, "sleep", lambda s: _done())
    api = "https://huggingface.co/api/models/"
    conf = "https://huggingface.co/"
    async with _client({
        api + "org/moe": lambda n: (429, {}) if n == 1 else (200, {"safetensors": {"parameters": {"BF16": 1_000_000_000, "F8_E4M3": 3_000_000_000},
                                                                                       "total": 4_000_000_000}}),
        conf + "org/moe/resolve": (200, GPT_OSS_120B),
        api + "org/dense": (200, {"safetensors": {"parameters": {"BF16": 8_000_000_000}, "total": 8_000_000_000}}),
        conf + "org/dense/resolve": (200, {"hidden_size": 4096, "num_hidden_layers": 32}),
        api + "org/Big-1T-A50B": (401, {}),
        api + "org/gated-dense": (200, {"safetensors": {"parameters": {"BF16": 1_000_000_000}, "total": 1_000_000_000}}),
        conf + "org/gated-dense/resolve": (401, {}),
    }) as c:
        moe = await gs.fetch_model_size("org/moe", c)  # rate-limited once, then answered
        assert moe["weight_bytes"] == 2_000_000_000 + 3_000_000_000 and moe["fp8_share"] == 0.75 and moe["sixteen_bit_bytes"] == 2_000_000_000
        assert moe["active_params"] == 4_000_000_000  # capped at the total the weights hold
        assert "estimated from its config" in moe["basis"]

def test_sizing_a_replica_to_a_model():
    small = {"weight_bytes": 16e9, "active_params": 14e9, "fp8_share": 0.0}
    r = gs.size_replica(small, OFFERS, {"aws", "runpod"}, spot=True)
    # 16 GB of weights at 70% of memory needs 23 GB: one L4, at its spot price. Three L40S are cheaper but vLLM splits 1, 2, 4 or 8 ways.
    assert (r["accelerator"], r["count"], r["usd_per_hour"], r["spot"], r["region"]) == ("L4", 1, 0.2, True, "us-west-2")
    assert r["on_demand_usd_per_hour"] == 0.8 and r["tflops"] == 121
    mid = {"weight_bytes": 100e9, "active_params": 10e9, "fp8_share": 1.0}
    on_demand = gs.size_replica(mid, OFFERS, {"aws", "runpod"}, spot=False)
    assert (on_demand["accelerator"], on_demand["count"], on_demand["cloud"], on_demand["usd_per_hour"]) == ("H100", 2, "runpod", 5.0)
    assert on_demand["tflops"] == 2 * 1979  # FP8 weights on a GPU with FP8
    assert gs.size_replica(mid, OFFERS, {"aws"}, spot=True)["count"] == 8  # aws only has 1 or 8
    too_big = gs.size_replica({"weight_bytes": 600e9, "active_params": 1e9, "fp8_share": 0}, OFFERS, {"aws"}, spot=True)
    assert too_big == {"error": "needs 857 GB of GPU memory; the largest machine on offer has 640 GB"}
    assert gs.size_replica(small, OFFERS, {"gcp"}, spot=True) == {"error": "no offer in the chosen clouds"}
    fixed = gs.size_replica(small, OFFERS, {"aws"}, spot=False, accelerators="H100:8")
    assert (fixed["accelerator"], fixed["count"], fixed["usd_per_hour"]) == ("H100", 8, 55.0)
    assert gs.size_replica({"error": "x"}, OFFERS, {"aws"}, True, accelerators="H100:1")["count"] == 1  # a deployment needs no size
    assert gs.size_replica({"error": "unknown"}, OFFERS, {"aws"}, True) == {"error": "unknown"}
    assert "no H100:4 offer" in gs.size_replica(small, OFFERS, {"aws"}, True, accelerators="H100:4")["error"]
    assert gs.size_replica(small, OFFERS, {"aws"}, True, regions=["eu-north-1"])["count"] == 8  # the only spot offer there

async def test_prices_are_fetched_at_report_time_when_stale(monkeypatch):

    store = MemoryStore()
    calls = []

    async def catalog(clouds, refresh=False):

        return {"offers": OFFERS, "catalog_updated": {"aws": "2026-11-11T17:00:00+00:00"}, "skypilot": "0.14.2"}

    async def sizes(ids, client):
        calls.append(("sizes", tuple(ids)))
        return {i: {"error": "x"} for i in ids}

    monkeypatch.setattr(gs, "fetch_catalog", catalog)
    monkeypatch.setattr(gs, "fetch_model_sizes", sizes)
    cfg = _cfg()
    cat, found = await gs.current(cfg, store)  # nothing stored: fetched now
    assert cat["offers"] == OFFERS and cat["skypilot"] == "0.14.2" and set(found["models"]) == {"org/deployed", "org/boxed", "org/small", "org/unsized"}
    assert calls[0] == ("catalog", ("aws", "gcp", "azure", "lambda", "runpod", "nebius"), False)  # its deployment's clouds first
    calls.clear()
    await gs.current(cfg, store)
    assert calls == []  # fresh: as stored
    old = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=7)).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    await store.set_setting("gpu_catalog", {**cat, "fetched_at": old})
    await gs.current(cfg, store)
    assert [c[0] for c in calls] == ["catalog"]  # prices again; sizes are good for a week
    out = await gs.refresh(cfg, store, download=True)
    assert out["offers"] == len(OFFERS) and calls[-2][2] is True and out["unsized"] == sorted(found["models"])

    async def broken(clouds, refresh=False):
        raise gs.SkyPilotMissing("SkyPilot isn't installed")

    monkeypatch.setattr(gs, "fetch_catalog", broken)

    await store.set_setting("model_sizes", {})
    calls.clear()
    cat, found = await gs.current(cfg, store)
    assert cat["problem"] == "SkyPilot isn't installed" and cat["offers"] == OFFERS  # the last prices stand
    assert calls[0][0] == "sizes" and found["models"]  # sizes are fetched all the same

    from meritorder.state import MemoryState

    store, state = MemoryStore(), MemoryState()
    calls = []

    async def catalog(clouds, refresh=False):
        calls.append(("catalog", refresh))
        return {"offers": OFFERS, "skypilot": "0.14.2"}

    async def sizes(ids, client):

    assert calls == [("sizes",)] and found["models"] and "hasn't published any yet" in cat["problem"]
    # The controller (which has SkyPilot) publishes them when they're stale...

    await publish_gpu_prices(cfg, store, state)

    # ...and right away, catalogs downloaded again, when someone asks for the latest.
    await state.set_json(PRICES_REQUESTED, {"by": "root"})
    await publish_gpu_prices(cfg, store, state)
    assert calls == [("catalog", True)] and await state.get_json(PRICES_REQUESTED) is None
    old = (datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=7)).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    await store.set_setting("gpu_catalog", {**cat, "fetched_at": old})
    cat, _ = await gs.current(cfg, store)
    assert "hasn't published any in the last 6 hours" in cat["problem"] and cat["offers"] == OFFERS

    async def broken(clouds, refresh=False):
        raise RuntimeError("catalog down")

    monkeypatch.setattr(gs, "fetch_catalog", broken)
    await publish_gpu_prices(cfg, store, state)  # logged; the controller carries on

# Merit Order configuration.
#
# Strings support ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Secrets come from the
# environment (see .env.example), never from this file.
#
# Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are switched off automatically,
# so this file works with whatever provider keys you have. Run `meritorder check`
# to see what is usable.
#
# PRICES are dollars per million tokens. Anthropic prices are from published
# rates on 2026-11-09; routes without a price use prices.json, which
# `meritorder prices refresh` updates from OpenRouter's catalog; AWS, Azure, and GCP set their
# own prices and you may have negotiated discounts, so verify before trusting
# the savings numbers. QUALITY scores (1-5) are starting points; tune them with
# your own evals.

# "What you'd use without Merit Order": the counterfactual for savings reports.
baseline_model: claude-sonnet

# Open-weight models, direct vendor APIs, and OpenRouter's free tier.
include:
  - models-open.yaml
  - models-embeddings.yaml

default_max_tokens: 16000

routing:
  auto_model: auto              # clients send model="auto" to let the router choose
  switch_margin_pct: 10         # only move a session if it's this much cheaper (after cache rebuild)
  est_output_tokens: 600

  # route may cost 20% more; speed: up to 100% more. Teams (priority:) and X-MeritOrder-Priority override it.
  priority: cost

from datetime import UTC, datetime

import yaml

from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, Config, ModelConfig, Route, ServeConfig
from meritorder.controller import tick
from meritorder.gpu import (
    API_ONLY, DRAINING, PROVISIONING, WARM, Demand, Deployment, SkyPilotProvisioner, Status, addressable, decide,
    desired_replicas, parse_vllm_metrics,
)
from meritorder.state import MemoryState
from meritorder.store import MemoryStore

SERVE = ServeConfig(model="ow", scale_up_after_minutes=10, hold_minutes=30, drain_minutes=15, max_replicas=4)


def test_desired_replicas_must_pay_for_themselves():
    # $50/h of API spend can pay for 2 replicas at $20/h (with 20% margin), throughput needs 3.
    d = desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=50, tokens_per_second=2000))
    assert d == 2
    assert desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=10, tokens_per_second=2000)) == 0
    warm = ServeConfig(model="ow", min_replicas=1)
    assert desired_replicas(warm, 20.0, 1000, Demand(0, 0)) == 1


def test_state_machine_full_cycle():
    t = 1_000_000.0
    rec, act = decide({}, SERVE, desired=2, status=Status(), now=t)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act is None  # must be justified for 10 minutes first
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + 601)
    assert rec["state"] == PROVISIONING and act.kind == "up" and act.replicas == 2
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM and rec["endpoint"] == "http://gpu/v1"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 3, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1600)
    assert act.kind == "scale" and act.replicas == 3
    # demand disappears, but GPUs are held for 30 minutes after warming
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1700)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801)
    assert rec["state"] == DRAINING
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801 + 901)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"


def test_provisioning_timeout_cools_down():
    t = 0.0
    rec = {"state": PROVISIONING, "since": t}
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 1)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 700)
    assert act is None  # still cooling down


def test_addressable_demand_uses_quality_floor():
    cfg = Config(backends=[], models=[ModelConfig(name="ow", quality={"coding": 4}, routes=[Route(backend="x", model="y")])])
    rows = [
        {"floor": "coding:3", "served_model": "sonnet", "requested_model": "auto", "cost": 10.0, "tokens": 100},
        {"floor": "coding:5", "served_model": "opus", "requested_model": "auto", "cost": 50.0, "tokens": 500},
        {"floor": None, "served_model": "ow", "requested_model": "ow", "cost": 2.0, "tokens": 20},
    ]
    assert addressable(cfg.models[0], rows, cfg) == (12.0, 120)


def test_parse_vllm_metrics():
    text = """# HELP vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc KV-cache usage
vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc{model_name="m"} 0.42
vllm:num_requests_waiting{model_name="m"} 0.0
"""
    assert parse_vllm_metrics(text) == 0.42
    assert parse_vllm_metrics(text.replace("waiting{model_name=\"m\"} 0.0", "waiting{model_name=\"m\"} 4")) > 0.85


def test_skypilot_task_yaml():
    model = ModelConfig(name="ow", hf_id="Org/Model-7B", routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="org-model")])
    backend = BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai",
                            serve=ServeConfig(model="ow", accelerators="L4:2", clouds=["aws", "gcp"], use_spot=True, vllm_args="--max-model-len 32768"))
    cfg = Config(backends=[backend], models=[model])
    task = yaml.safe_load(SkyPilotProvisioner(backend, cfg).task_yaml(2))
    assert task["service"]["replicas"] == 2
    assert task["resources"]["accelerators"] == "L4:2" and task["resources"]["use_spot"] is True
    assert {c["cloud"] for c in task["resources"]["any_of"]} == {"aws", "gcp"}
    assert "vllm serve Org/Model-7B" in task["run"]
    assert "--served-model-name org-model" in task["run"] and "--tensor-parallel-size 2" in task["run"]
    assert "--enable-prefix-caching" in task["run"] and task["run"].endswith("--max-model-len 32768")


class FakeProvisioner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
        self.ready = False

    async def status(self):
        return Status(ready=self.ready, endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1" if self.ready else None)

    async def up(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("up", n))

    async def scale(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("scale", n))

    async def down(self):
        self.calls.append(("down",))


async def test_controller_tick_scales_up_on_addressable_demand():
    model = ModelConfig(name="ow", quality={"coding": 4}, hf_id="o/m", routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="m")])
    backend = BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai", gpu_cost_per_hour=10.0,
                            serve=ServeConfig(model="ow", scale_up_after_minutes=0))
    cfg = Config(backends=[backend], models=[model])
    store, state = MemoryStore(), MemoryState()
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    for _ in range(30):  # $30 of coding:3 traffic in the last hour, served by an API model
        await store.record({"ts": now, "floor": "coding:3", "served_model": "sonnet", "requested_model": "auto",
                            "served_api_cost": 1.0, "actual_cost": 1.0, "status": 200, "upgraded": False,
                            "input_tokens": 1000, "output_tokens": 100})
    prov = FakeProvisioner()
    deps = [Deployment(backend=backend, model=model, provisioner=prov)]
    [rec] = await tick(cfg, store, state, deps)
    assert rec["state"] == PROVISIONING and prov.calls == [("up", 1)]  # ~9 tok/s fits one replica
    prov.ready = True
    [rec] = await tick(cfg, store, state, deps)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM and rec["endpoint"].startswith("http://127.0.0.1")


def test_simulate_whatif():
    from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

    from meritorder.gpu import simulate

    model = ModelConfig(name="ow", quality={"coding": 4}, routes=[Route(backend="x", model="y")])
    cfg = Config(backends=[], models=[model])
    t0 = datetime(2026, 11, 2, 9, tzinfo=UTC)
    rows = []
    for h in range(10):  # 8 busy hours at $50/h of coding:3 traffic, 2 quiet hours at $2/h
        cost = 50.0 if h < 8 else 2.0
        rows.append({"hour": t0 + timedelta(hours=h), "floor": "coding:3", "served_model": "sonnet", "requested_model": "auto",
                     "cost": cost, "tokens": 3_600_000 if h < 8 else 10_000})
        rows.append({"hour": t0 + timedelta(hours=h), "floor": "coding:5", "served_model": "opus", "requested_model": "auto",
                     "cost": 100.0, "tokens": 1})  # too hard for this model: never counted
    r = simulate(model, cfg, rows, gpu_cost_per_hour=16.0, capacity_tps=4000)
    assert r["hours_gpus_would_run"] == 8 and r["peak_replicas"] == 1
    assert r["addressable_api_cost"] == 404.0
    assert r["net_savings"] == 8 * (50 - 16)


def test_sky_python_found_next_to_sky_even_with_spaces_and_symlinks(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    import os

    from meritorder.gpu import _shebang_python, sky_python

    monkeypatch.delenv("MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON", raising=False)
    venv = tmp_path / "Example LLC" / "sky-venv" / "bin"
    venv.mkdir(parents=True)
    py = venv / "python"
    py.write_text("#!/bin/sh\n")
    py.chmod(0o755)
    sky = venv / "sky"
    sky.write_text(f"#!/bin/sh\n'''exec' \"{py}\" \"$0\" \"$@\"\n' '''\n")
    sky.chmod(0o755)
    links = tmp_path / "bin"
    links.mkdir()
    os.symlink(sky, links / "sky")  # like ~/.local/bin/sky -> the tool's venv
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(links))
    assert sky_python() == str(py)
    monkeypatch.setenv("MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON", "/explicit/python")
    assert sky_python() == "/explicit/python"
    # Without a python next to it, the launcher itself says which interpreter it runs.
    assert _shebang_python(sky.read_text().splitlines()) == str(py)
    assert _shebang_python(["#!/usr/local/bin/python3.12"]) == "/usr/local/bin/python3.12"
    assert _shebang_python(["#!/bin/bash", "echo"]) is None and _shebang_python([]) is None

import time

import pytest

from meritorder.backends.base import Backend
from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, Config, ModelConfig, Price, Route, TeamConfig
from meritorder.pricing import Usage, attribute
from meritorder.router import Router, RoutingError, shadow_multiplier
from meritorder.sessions import Session

SONNET = Price(input=3, output=15, cache_read=0.3, cache_write=3.75)
CHEAP = Price(input=0.2, output=1.0, cache_read=0.02)


def test_savings_add_up():
    u = Usage(input_tokens=1_000, cache_read_tokens=90_000, cache_write_tokens=2_000, output_tokens=500)
    c = attribute(u, served_price=CHEAP, baseline_price=SONNET, proxy_cache=True)
    assert c.savings_total == pytest.approx(c.baseline - c.actual)
    assert c.savings_routing > 0 and c.savings_caching > 0 and c.savings_self_hosting == 0


def test_client_caching_is_not_claimed():
    u = Usage(input_tokens=1_000, cache_read_tokens=90_000, output_tokens=500)
    c = attribute(u, served_price=SONNET, baseline_price=SONNET, proxy_cache=False)
    assert c.savings_caching == 0
    assert c.savings_total == pytest.approx(0)


def test_self_hosting_savings():
    u = Usage(input_tokens=10_000, output_tokens=1_000)
    c = attribute(u, served_price=CHEAP, baseline_price=CHEAP, proxy_cache=False, self_hosted_cost=0.0001)
    assert c.actual == 0.0001
    assert c.savings_self_hosting == pytest.approx(c.served_api - 0.0001)


def test_shadow_price_curve():
    assert shadow_multiplier(0.1, 0.6, 0.02) == 0.02
    assert 0.02 < shadow_multiplier(0.8, 0.6, 0.02) < 1.0
    assert shadow_multiplier(1.0, 0.6, 0.02) is None


def _router(extra_backends=()):
    backends_cfg = [
        BackendConfig(name="api-a", format="anthropic", base_url="https://a"),
        BackendConfig(name="api-b", format="anthropic", base_url="https://b"),
        BackendConfig(name="api-o", format="openai", base_url="https://o"),
        BackendConfig(name="gpu", format="openai", kind="self_hosted", base_url="http://gpu"),
        *extra_backends,
    ]
    models = [
        ModelConfig(name="frontier", quality={"coding": 5, "general": 5},
                    routes=[Route(backend="api-a", model="f", price=SONNET), Route(backend="api-b", model="f", price=SONNET)]),
        ModelConfig(name="cheap", quality={"coding": 3, "general": 3}, routes=[Route(backend="api-o", model="c", price=CHEAP)]),
        ModelConfig(name="openweight", quality={"coding": 4, "general": 4}, routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="ow", price=Price(input=1, output=4))]),
    ]
    cfg = Config(backends=backends_cfg, models=models, teams=[TeamConfig(name="default")])
    backends = {b.name: Backend(b) for b in backends_cfg}
    return Router(cfg, backends), cfg


def coding_body(n_tools=1):
    return {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "fix this bug in app.py"}], "tools": [{"name": f"t{i}"} for i in range(n_tools)]}


def test_auto_prefers_idle_gpu_even_for_better_model():
    router, cfg = _router()
    d = router.decide("auto", cfg.team("default"), coding_body(), {}, None, 5_000, True, {"gpu": 0.1}, time.time())
    assert d.floor.level == 3
    assert d.candidates[0].model.name == "openweight"  # quality 4 at ~zero marginal cost
    assert d.candidates[0].upgraded


def test_saturated_gpu_spills_to_api():
    router, cfg = _router()
    d = router.decide("auto", cfg.team("default"), coding_body(), {}, None, 5_000, True, {"gpu": 1.0}, time.time())
    assert d.candidates[0].model.name == "cheap"
    assert all(c.backend.name != "gpu" for c in d.candidates)


def test_explicit_model_is_never_substituted():
    router, cfg = _router()
    d = router.decide("frontier", cfg.team("default"), coding_body(), {}, None, 5_000, True, {}, time.time())
    assert {c.model.name for c in d.candidates} == {"frontier"}
    with pytest.raises(RoutingError):
        router.decide("nope", cfg.team("default"), coding_body(), {}, None, 5_000, True, {}, time.time())


def test_warm_cache_keeps_session_on_its_backend():
    router, cfg = _router()
    now = time.time()
    sess = Session(id="s", model="frontier", backend="api-b", turns=10, prefix_tokens=100_000, warm_until={"api-b": now + 200})
    d = router.decide("frontier", cfg.team("default"), coding_body(), {}, sess, 102_000, False, {}, now)
    assert d.candidates[0].backend.name == "api-b"

"""Marginal-cost router (docs/03-routing.md).

For each candidate backend b over the session's expected remaining turns:

    cost(b) = rebuild(b) + expected_remaining_turns * per_turn(b)

* per_turn uses API prices, or for self-hosted backends a shadow price that is
  near zero while the replica has headroom and rises toward the API price as it fills.
* rebuild is zero when b already holds a warm cache for this session, otherwise
  the extra cost of re-processing the whole prefix there.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .backends import Backend
from .classifier import Floor, classify, parse_floor
from .config import Config, ModelConfig, Price, Route, TeamConfig
from .sessions import Session


class RoutingError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int, message: str, kind: str = "invalid_request_error"):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.message = message
        self.kind = kind


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    model: ModelConfig
    route: Route
    backend: Backend
    cost: float
    warm: bool
    quality: int
    upgraded: bool = False
    queued: bool = False  # sent to a saturated backend because nothing else could take it

    @property
    def self_hosted(self) -> bool:
        return self.backend.kind == "self_hosted"


@dataclass
class Decision:
    requested: str
    auto: bool
    floor: Floor | None
    candidates: list[Candidate] = field(default_factory=list)
    reason: str = ""
    substituted_for: str | None = None  # the named model that couldn't run (team opted in to substitution)


def shadow_multiplier(util: float, knee: float, floor: float) -> float | None:
    """Fraction of API price a self-hosted token "costs" at this utilization. None = full."""
    if util >= 1.0:
        return None
    if util <= knee:
        return floor
    return floor + (1.0 - floor) * ((util - knee) / (1.0 - knee)) ** 2


def _scaled(price: Price, m: float) -> Price:
    return Price(input=price.input * m, output=price.output * m, cache_read=price.read() * m, cache_write=price.write() * m)


class Router:
    def __init__(self, cfg: Config, backends: dict[str, Backend]):
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.backends = backends

    def resolve(self, requested: str) -> ModelConfig | None:
        return self.cfg.model(requested)

    def _expected_turns(self, session: Session | None) -> int:
        r = self.cfg.routing
        turns = session.turns if session else 0
        return max(r.min_expected_turns, min(r.max_expected_turns, turns or r.min_expected_turns))

    def estimate(
        self, price: Price, backend: Backend, prompt_tokens: int, session: Session | None, warm: bool, turns: int
    ) -> float:
        r = self.cfg.routing
        new = r.est_new_tokens_per_turn
        if session and session.prefix_tokens:
            new = max(prompt_tokens - session.prefix_tokens, 200)
        cached = max(prompt_tokens - new, 0)
        # Steady state: the prefix is read from cache, new tokens are written to it.
        write_price = price.write()  # input price unless the route charges a write premium
        per_turn = (cached * price.read() + new * write_price + r.est_output_tokens * price.output) / 1e6
        rebuild = 0.0 if warm else cached * max(write_price - price.read(), 0.0) / 1e6
        return rebuild + turns * per_turn

    def decide(
        self,
        requested: str,
        team: TeamConfig,
        body: dict,
        headers: dict[str, str],
        session: Session | None,
        prompt_tokens: int,
        boundary: bool,
        utilization: dict[str, float],
        now: float,
        queue_full: frozenset[str] | set[str] = frozenset(),
    ) -> Decision:
        """Pick and rank candidates. ``queue_full`` names saturated backends that also have no room left
        to queue requests; other saturated backends are kept as a last resort."""
        r = self.cfg.routing
        auto = requested == r.auto_model or requested == ""
        floor: Floor | None = None

        if auto:
            if session and session.model and not boundary and team.allows_model(session.model) and self.cfg.model(session.model):
                models = [self.cfg.model(session.model)]
                floor = parse_floor(session.floor or "")
                reason = f"mid-task: keeping session model {session.model}"
            else:
                floor = classify(body, headers, prompt_tokens)
                models = [m for m in self.cfg.models
                          if m.kind == "chat" and m.q(floor.task) >= floor.level and team.allows_model(m.name)]
                reason = f"classified {floor} ({floor.reason})"
                if not models:
                    # Nothing meets the floor: fall back to the best allowed models.
                    allowed = [m for m in self.cfg.models if m.kind == "chat" and team.allows_model(m.name)]
                    best = max((m.q(floor.task) for m in allowed), default=0)
                    models = [m for m in allowed if m.q(floor.task) == best]
                    reason += f"; no model meets the floor, using best available (level {best})"
        else:
            model = self.resolve(requested)
            if model is None:
                raise RoutingError(404, f"model '{requested}' is not configured", "not_found_error")
            if model.kind != "chat":
                raise RoutingError(400, f"'{model.name}' is an embedding model; use /v1/embeddings", "invalid_request_error")
            if not team.allows_model(model.name):
                raise RoutingError(403, f"model '{model.name}' is not allowed for team '{team.name}'", "permission_error")
            models = [model]
            reason = f"harness requested {model.name}"

        turns = self._expected_turns(session)
        task = floor.task if floor else "general"
        cands: list[Candidate] = []
        too_small = [m.name for m in models if m.context_window and prompt_tokens > m.context_window * 0.95]
        if too_small and len(too_small) < len(models):
            models = [m for m in models if m.name not in too_small]
            reason += f"; skipped {', '.join(too_small)} (context window too small)"
        saturated: list[Candidate] = []
        for m in models:
            for route in m.routes:
                backend = self.backends.get(route.backend)
                if backend is None or not backend.available or not backend.healthy(now) or not team.allows_backend(route.backend):
                    continue
                if backend.draining and not (session and session.warm(backend.name, now)):
                    continue  # draining: only finish sessions whose cache is already there
                if auto and not route.priced:
                    continue  # an unknown price must never look free
                price = route.cost_price()
                full = False
                if backend.kind == "self_hosted":
                    mult = shadow_multiplier(utilization.get(backend.name, 0.0), r.shadow_knee, r.shadow_floor)
                    if mult is None:
                        # Saturated: new work spills to other routes. If none can take it, the request queues
                        # here (in vLLM) rather than failing, unless that queue is full too.
                        if backend.name in queue_full:
                            continue
                        full = True
                    else:
                        price = _scaled(price, mult)
                warm = bool(session and session.warm(backend.name, now))
                quality = m.q(task)
                (saturated if full else cands).append(
                    Candidate(
                        model=m,
                        route=route,
                        backend=backend,
                        cost=self.estimate(price, backend, prompt_tokens, session, warm, turns),
                        warm=warm,
                        quality=quality,
                        upgraded=bool(auto and floor and quality > floor.level and backend.kind == "self_hosted"),
                        queued=full,
                    )
                )
        if not cands and saturated and auto and session and session.model and not boundary:
            # The session's GPUs are full: another model with room beats waiting in a queue.
            again = self.decide(requested, team, body, headers, session, prompt_tokens, True, utilization, now, queue_full)
            if not any(c.queued for c in again.candidates):
                again.reason = f"session model {session.model} is saturated; re-routed: {again.reason}"
                return again
        if not cands and saturated:
            saturated.sort(key=lambda c: (c.cost, -c.quality))
            names = ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(c.backend.name for c in saturated))
            return Decision(requested=requested, auto=auto, floor=floor, candidates=saturated,
                            reason=f"{reason}; every route is saturated, queued on {names}")
        if not cands:
            if auto and session and session.model and not boundary:
                # The session's model has nowhere to run (e.g. its GPUs were stopped): pick again.
                again = self.decide(requested, team, body, headers, session, prompt_tokens, True, utilization, now, queue_full)
                again.reason = f"session model {session.model} is unavailable; re-routed: {again.reason}"
                return again
            if not auto and team.substitute_unavailable and len(models) == 1:
                sub = self._substitute(models[0], team, body, headers, session, prompt_tokens, utilization, now, queue_full)
                if sub is not None:
                    return sub
            raise RoutingError(503, self._unavailable_message(models, team, now, auto), "overloaded_error")
        if auto and any(c.backend.kind != "mock" for c in cands):
            # Mocks are for trying things out; never let them win against real backends.
            cands = [c for c in cands if c.backend.kind != "mock"]

        cands.sort(key=lambda c: (c.cost, -c.quality))
        if auto and len(cands) > 1:
            # Near-ties go to the higher-quality model.
            cheapest = cands[0].cost
            near = [c for c in cands if c.cost <= cheapest * 1.02 + 1e-9]
            best = max(near, key=lambda c: c.quality)
            cands.remove(best)
            cands.insert(0, best)

        # Stickiness: only move a session off its current backend if it's clearly cheaper.
        if session and session.backend:
            current = next((c for c in cands if c.backend.name == session.backend and c.model.name == session.model), None)
            if current is not None and current is not cands[0]:
                margin = current.cost * r.switch_margin_pct / 100.0 + r.switch_margin_usd
                if cands[0].cost + margin >= current.cost:
                    cands.remove(current)
                    cands.insert(0, current)
                    reason += f"; staying on {current.backend.name} (move would not pay for cache rebuild)"

        return Decision(requested=requested, auto=auto, floor=floor, candidates=cands, reason=reason)

    def _substitute(self, named: ModelConfig, team: TeamConfig, body: dict, headers: dict[str, str], session: Session | None,
                    prompt_tokens: int, utilization: dict[str, float], now: float,
                    queue_full: frozenset[str] | set[str] = frozenset()) -> Decision | None:
        """Route a named model that can't run to models at least as good for this task (never a weaker one)."""
        task = classify(body, headers, prompt_tokens).task
        level = max(1, named.q(task))
        try:
            sub = self.decide(self.cfg.routing.auto_model, team, body, {**headers, "x-route-floor": f"{task}:{level}"},
                              session, prompt_tokens, True, utilization, now, queue_full)
        except RoutingError:
            return None
        sub.candidates = [c for c in sub.candidates if c.model.name != named.name and c.model.q(task) >= level]
        if not sub.candidates:
            return None
        for c in sub.candidates:
            c.upgraded = False
        sub.auto = False  # the client named a model: no automatic effort changes or refusal retries
        sub.requested = named.name
        sub.substituted_for = named.name
        sub.reason = f"{named.name} has nowhere to run; substituted a model at least as good for {task} (level {level}): {sub.reason}"
        return sub

    def _unavailable_message(self, models: list[ModelConfig], team: TeamConfig, now: float, auto: bool) -> str:
        """Say why nothing can serve the request, route by route, so people know what to fix or switch to."""
        if auto or len(models) != 1:
            return "no healthy backend is available for this request"
        why = []
        for route in models[0].routes:
            b = self.backends.get(route.backend)
            bc = self.cfg.backend(route.backend)
            if b is None:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: {(bc.disabled_reason if bc else None) or 'not enabled'}")
            elif not team.allows_backend(route.backend):
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: not allowed for team '{team.name}'")
            elif not b.available:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: {getattr(b, 'unavailable_reason', None) or 'not running'}")
            elif not b.healthy(now):
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: failing, retrying shortly")
            elif b.draining:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: draining, only finishing existing sessions")
            else:
                why.append(f"{route.backend}: saturated and its queue is full")
        return (f"'{models[0].name}' has nowhere to run right now ({'; '.join(why)}). "
                f"Use model '{self.cfg.routing.auto_model}' to let Merit Order pick another model, or try again later.")

# Merit Order

An open-source LLM gateway that cuts LLM spend for day-to-day use, without changing how
people work.

Power grids dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest marginal cost first, with expensive
peaker plants switched on only when demand requires them. Merit Order does the same with tokens:

- **Routes** every session to the cheapest model and backend that meets the task's quality bar,
  counting what it would cost to rebuild the prompt cache somewhere else.
- **Runs open-weight models on your own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when steady load makes that cheaper
  than paying per token, and turns them off when it doesn't. APIs (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex,
  Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, ...) are always there for overflow.
- **Saves tokens**: automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, cache-safe compression of huge tool
  outputs, and an optional response cache.
- **Shows the money**: every request is recorded with what it cost and what it would have cost
  without Merit Order, broken down by cause, per user, team, project, and day.

Point Claude Code, pi, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or anything that speaks either API at it.

## Quickstart (no keys needed)

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env            # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY (and any provider keys you have)
uv run meritorder serve         # http://localhost:8080, reports UI at /ui/
```

```bash
curl localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $MERITORDER_DEV_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}'
```

With no provider keys, requests go to built-in mock backends. `uv run meritorder check` shows
which backends and models are live with the keys you've set. Without `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`,
storage is in memory; use Docker Compose for the real thing.

## Run the full stack with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add at least one provider key
docker compose up -d            # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080
docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin
```

Bedrock with your AWS profile (including SSO): `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d`.
Kubernetes: `helm install mo charts/meritorder` (see [docs/07-deployment.md](docs/07-deployment.md)).

## Point your harness at it

```bash
meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com   # Entra sign-in; or: meritorder use-key <key>
meritorder setup pi                                    # adds a "meritorder" provider to pi
meritorder setup claude-code                           # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + apiKeyHelper
```

Or by hand: OpenAI-compatible clients use base URL `<gateway>/v1`; Claude Code uses
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>`. Use `model: "auto"` to let Merit Order choose, or name a model
(`claude-sonnet`, `kimi-k3.1`, `qwen3-coder`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, ...) to pin it.

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Session-Id` | Groups requests into a session (pi sends it; otherwise inferred) |
| `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | Minimum quality for `auto` routing |
| `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges `auto` routing down or up |
| `X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=foo` | Cost-allocation tags for reports |
| `X-MeritOrder-Cache: on` / `off` | Use or bypass the response cache |
| `X-MeritOrder-Backend: <name>` | Admins only: pin a backend (testing, debugging) |

Responses carry `x-meritorder-model`, `x-meritorder-backend`, and (non-streaming)
`x-meritorder-cost-usd` / `x-meritorder-savings-usd`.

## What's in the box

| Area | Built |
|---|---|
| APIs | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (stateless), Anthropic Messages, and embeddings; streaming and not; pass-through when formats match, translation when they don't |
| Backends | Anthropic, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, OpenRouter (incl. opt-in free tier), DeepSeek, Mistral, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, any OpenAI-compatible server |
| Models | Claude, GPT, and an open-weight catalog: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen3-Coder, MiniMax, MiMo, Muse, Mistral/Devstral, Gemma, Nemotron, gpt-oss |
| Routing | Rule-based classifier → quality floor; marginal-cost router with cache rebuild cost, context-window checks, sticky sessions, fallback across backends |
| GPUs | Break-even controller (addressable demand, hysteresis), SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM provisioner, static servers, utilization from vLLM metrics, spill to API when saturated |
| Savings | Automatic prompt caching, lower reasoning effort for simple `auto` tasks (stable per session), deterministic tool-output compression, opt-in response cache |
| Identity | Virtual API keys, Entra/OIDC device-code login, roles (user, team lead, finance, admin) |
| Spend | Team and user monthly budgets, per-session spend caps (stops runaway agents), requests/tokens-per-minute limits, policy allow/deny lists for models and backends |
| Reporting | Ledger with savings by cause, reports API, CSV, JSONL/CSV ledger export to a file or S3, web UI (incl. key management), `meritorder usage`, Prometheus metrics, budget/spike alerts, weekly digests |
| Deployment | Docker Compose, Helm chart, CI (tests, audits, Helm lint, Compose smoke test), signed multi-arch releases |

Not yet: billing reconciliation against provider invoices, Kubernetes-native GPU provisioning
(llm-d/KServe), a learned router, OpenTelemetry traces. See [docs/](docs/README.md) for the design.

## Development

```bash
uv sync && uv run pytest                     # gateway
cd ui && npm ci && npm run build             # reporting UI (served at /ui/)
uv run python scripts/fake_vllm.py           # a stand-in vLLM server for the GPU path
uv run python scripts/smoke_providers.py     # test every enabled provider through a running gateway
```

# 03 — Routing The router answers: **which model, on which backend, for this request?** It optimizes **marginal cost** — what this request adds to the bill *right now* — subject to a quality floor and team policy. ## Decision flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> B{"Harness pinned
a model?"} B -- "yes" --> FIX["Model is fixed
(only the backend can vary)"] B -- "no, model=auto" --> C{"Existing session,
mid-task, cache warm?"} C -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep session's model"] C -- "no" --> D["Classifier → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] D --> E["Candidates = models allowed for team
with quality ≥ floor"] FIX --> S KEEP --> S E --> S["Score every backend of every candidate
cost = rebuild + turns × per-turn"] S --> T{"Cheapest beats current
by more than hysteresis margin?"} T -- "yes" --> MOVE["Route to cheapest
(ties → higher quality)"] T -- "no" --> STAY["Stay on current backend"] MOVE --> PRI{"Running above floor
only because it's free?"} STAY --> PRI PRI -- "yes" --> LOW["Send with low priority
(paid traffic preempts it)"] PRI -- "no" --> NORM["Send with normal priority"] ``` ## The cost function For each candidate backend `b`, over the session's expected remaining turns: ``` cost(b) = rebuild(b) + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn(b) ``` **Per-turn cost by backend type** | Backend state | `per_turn(b)` | |---|---| | API | uncached tokens × input price + cached tokens × cache-read price + output × output price | | Self-hosted, plenty of headroom | ≈ 0 (shadow price near zero) | | Self-hosted, filling up | shadow price rises toward the same model's API price | | Self-hosted, at latency target | unavailable (or priced as the API version of the same model) | **Rebuild cost** | Situation | `rebuild(b)` | |---|---| | `b` already holds a warm cache for this session | 0 | | API, cold | prefix tokens × (cache-write price − cache-read price) | | Self-hosted, cold | prefix tokens × shadow price + latency penalty for the prefill | Illustrative (check real prices): a 120k-token Claude session costs ~$0.04/turn in cache reads to stay. Moving it to another Claude backend costs ~$0.45 to rewrite the cache. A move has to save more than ~$0.41 over the rest of the session to be worth it. ## Shadow price Self-hosted tokens aren't literally free — capacity is finite. The shadow price makes spare capacity attractive while protecting latency: ![Shadow price vs replica utilization](img/shadow-price.svg) ## Free upgrades (and why they're safe) If a strong open model is running with headroom and the task only needs a medium model, the user gets the strong model at ~zero cost. Three guardrails keep this from backfiring: 1. **Low priority.** Opportunistic requests use vLLM priority scheduling, so traffic that *needs* that model always goes first. 2. **Doesn't keep GPUs alive.** The controller values upgraded traffic at its *floor* model's API price, so free traffic can't make a GPU look worth keeping. (See [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md).) 3. **Only at boundaries.** Upgrades/downgrades happen at session start or task boundaries — never mid-task — so tool-calling behavior and caches stay stable. ## Free moments to re-route Moving costs nothing when the session's cache is already gone: - Session idle longer than the cache TTL. - The harness compacted history (prefix hash no longer matches). - The replica evicted the session's KV cache (from vLLM / llm-d KV events). - A natural task boundary. ## When a model refuses Some models decline requests through safety classifiers (Claude returns HTTP 200 with `stop_reason: "refusal"`; OpenAI-style APIs use `finish_reason: "content_filter"`). For `auto` requests, Merit Order retries on the next eligible model: - Streams are buffered only until the first content arrives, so a refusal before any content is retried invisibly; one that arrives after content has started streams through. - The refused attempt is recorded in the ledger (it cost tokens), and the response carries `x-meritorder-refused-by`. - A model the client named is never substituted. Teams can turn this off (`refusal_fallback: false`). ## Harness overrides | Harness sends | Behavior | |---|---| | `model: "claude-sonnet-4-5"` (explicit) | No model substitution. def _then(close, release):
    """A stream's close callback that also releases its in-flight slot, exactly once."""
    async def wrapped() -> None:
        try:

                await close()
        finally:

def parse_tags(value: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    tags: dict[str, str] = {}

        if m:
