# 08 — Reporting Merit Order exists to save money, so reporting is a core feature: what was spent, what was saved, why, by whom, and when. ## Data flow ```mermaid flowchart LR gw["Gateway"] -- "one row per request (async)" --> ledger[("Ledger
Postgres, monthly partitions")] ctl["Capacity controller"] -- "GPU hours, utilization" --> roll ledger --> roll["Rollup worker"] roll --> agg[("Hourly + daily rollups
by user, team, tag,
model, backend")] roll --> alerts["Alerts
budgets, spend spikes,
break-even changes"] agg --> api["Reports API"] ledger --> api api --> ui["Web UI"] api --> cli["meritorder usage"] api --> exp["CSV / Parquet exports"] api --> dig["Scheduled digests
email, Slack, Teams"] bills["Provider billing exports
AWS, GCP, Azure"] --> recon["Monthly reconciliation"] agg --> recon gw -. "Prometheus / OpenTelemetry" .-> mon["Grafana, Datadog, ..."] ``` Reports never contain prompt or response content. The ledger holds metadata only. ## Savings numbers have to stand up to scrutiny If finance finds one inflated number, they stop trusting the whole dashboard. So: **1. A baseline per team.** "What you'd have done without Merit Order", set in config: ```yaml teams: platform: baseline_model: claude-sonnet # API at list price, no proxy-added caching pricing_overrides: bedrock: { discount_pct: 12 } # negotiated / committed-spend discount ``` **2. Savings broken down by cause, never one blended number.** Causes are computed in a fixed order, each against the result of the previous step, so they add up exactly to the total with no double counting: | Order | Cause | How it's counted | |---|---|---| | 1 | **Routing** | Baseline model's API cost − served model's API cost | | 2 | **Self-hosting** | Served model's API cost − chargeback cost on our GPUs | | 3 | **Prompt caching** | Discount from cache breakpoints *we added*, minus cache-write premiums we paid. Caching the harness set up itself would have happened anyway and isn't counted. | | 4 | **Compression** | Tokens removed × served model's input price | | 5 | **Response cache** | Full cost of each request answered from cache | **3. Two headline numbers, side by side:** savings against list price, and savings caused by Merit Order. **4. Negotiated prices.** Per-provider discounts and price overrides, so costs match what the organization actually pays. **5. Monthly reconciliation.** Compare our computed cost with providers' billing exports (AWS Cost and Usage Reports, GCP billing export, Azure Cost Management) and report the difference. ## What's tracked | Area | Metrics | |---|---| | **Spend** | Actual cost by user, team, project tag, API key, model, provider, backend, time; burn rate; month-end forecast | | **Savings** | Total and by cause (above), over time | | **GPU fleet** | Where each replica runs (cloud, region, instance, spot), uptime, burn rate, cost per run and per month (SkyPilot catalog prices), replica-hours, utilization, demand at API prices vs GPU cost, every state change and admin action | | **Routing** | Model mix, free-upgrade rate, quality floor distribution, harness overrides | | **Caching** | Cache hit rate per backend, sessions that switched backends, rebuild cost paid | | **Operations** | Time to first token, tokens/s, error rate per backend | | **Budgets** | Users and teams near limits, soft and hard limit events | ## Views (console pages) | Page | Audience | Shows | |---|---|---| | **Dispatch** | Admins, finance, team leads | Live: the merit-order stack from real traffic, request feed, backend health, GPU fleet, what needs attention | | **Reports** | Everyone (scoped to their role) | Spend vs baseline over time, savings by cause, breakdowns by team, person, model, backend, or tag; recent requests; CSV | | **GPUs** | Admins, finance, team leads | Each deployment: where it runs, uptime, burn rate, run and month cost, demand coverage; stop / pin / stop-all (admins); activity log; what-if for models you don't host yet | | **Controls** | Admins, finance | Org, GPU, and team spend against budgets with month-end pace; safeguards and budgets (editable by admins) | | **Backends, Models** | Admins | Health, latency, errors; prices, routes, configured vs measured quality | | **Teams, People, Keys** | Admins, team leads | Budgets and usage by team; who's in which team; API keys | | **My usage** | Everyone | Own spend, models used, budget remaining | ## Who sees what Roles come from Entra (or OIDC) group membership, with exceptions pinned on the People page. | Role | Can see | |---|---| | User | Their own usage | | Team lead | Their team's usage, per user | | Finance | All spend and savings, no per-request detail | | Admin | Everything | ## Ways to get reports - **Web console** with the pages above. - **Reports API.** The console is built on it, so anyone can build their own views. - **CLI:** `meritorder usage` for a quick look at your own spend. - **Exports:** CSV and JSONL of the ledger, to a file or S3, for data warehouses and BI tools. - **Weekly digests** per team, to a webhook (Slack, Teams, or anything that accepts JSON). - **Alerts** to the same webhook and the console: team, personal, org, and GPU budget thresholds, **spend spikes** (a person suddenly at 5× normal usually means an agent stuck in a loop), GPU state changes, and every admin GPU action. - **Metrics:** Prometheus `/metrics` and OpenTelemetry traces. ## Cost allocation tags Requests can carry tags, and API keys can have default tags: ``` X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=checkout-rewrite,ticket=PLAT-1234 ``` Tags flow into the ledger and every report can group by them. ## Storage and scale - The ledger is a Postgres table partitioned by month. - A rollup worker keeps hourly and daily summary tables current. Dashboards read the summaries, not the raw ledger. - Postgres comfortably handles the millions of requests per month a $100k+/month organization generates. ClickHouse can be an optional backend for very large deployments. - We don't build a general-purpose BI tool. Ad-hoc analysis goes through the exports. ## What's built and what isn't yet | Piece | Status | |---|---| | Ledger, hourly rollups (`meritorder worker`, `--backfill`) | Built | | Savings by cause, baseline per team, negotiated prices (`price:` per route) | Built | | Reports API (`/v1/reports/summary`, `summary.csv`, `me`, `requests`, `gpu`) with role scoping | Built | | Console at `/ui/` (Mantine): Dispatch (live), Reports, GPUs (with controls and what-if), Controls, Backends, Models, Teams, People, Keys, Config, My usage | Built | | GPU cost per hour (`gpu_usage`) from SkyPilot catalog prices, GPU activity log (`gpu_events`) | Built | | Measured model quality (`meritorder eval`), shown on Models | Built | | `meritorder usage` | Built | | Prometheus `/metrics` (requests, tokens, cost, baseline, savings by cause, latency histogram) | Built | | OpenTelemetry traces: a span per LLM call in GenAI conventions plus cost, savings, backend; joins the client's `traceparent` (set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`) | Built | | Alerts (team/person/org/GPU budgets at 80%/100%, spend spikes, GPU state changes and admin actions) and Monday digests to a webhook | Built (`MERITORDER_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`) | | Ledger export: `/v1/reports/export.jsonl`, `meritorder export --out file.csv` or `s3://bucket/key` | Built | | Parquet export | Not yet (JSONL/CSV load into every warehouse) | | Monthly reconciliation against provider billing exports (API and GPU) | Not yet | | Grafana dashboard | Not yet | | ClickHouse backend for very large deployments | Not yet | The UI is a small React/TypeScript app (no charting library; hand-written SVG) built into the Python package and served by the gateway. It signs in with a Merit Order API key and shows what that key's role may see.

import copy

import pytest
from conftest import TEST_CONFIG

from meritorder.configstore import ConfigError, parse_and_validate


@pytest.mark.parametrize("where", ["org", "team"])
def test_unknown_baseline_model_is_rejected(tmp_path, where):
    doc = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
    doc["auth"] = {}
    if where == "org":
        doc["baseline_model"] = "no-such-model"
    else:
        doc["teams"]["default"]["baseline_model"] = "embed-small"  # exists, but isn't a chat model
    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="isn't a configured chat model"):
        parse_and_validate(None, str(tmp_path), None, document=doc)
    doc["baseline_model"], doc["teams"]["default"]["baseline_model"] = "big", "small"
    parse_and_validate(None, str(tmp_path), None, document=doc)

"""Admin API: who may mint and revoke keys, people management, evals, and config versions."""

import copy

import pytest
import yaml
from conftest import ADMIN_KEY, LEAD_KEY, TEST_CONFIG, auth, ledger_row


@pytest.fixture
def durable(gateway):
    """Key and config management need a durable store; the in-memory one behaves the same for these tests."""
    kind = gateway.store.kind
    gateway.store.kind = "postgres"
    yield gateway
    gateway.store.kind = kind


async def mint(client, body, key=LEAD_KEY):
    return await client.post("/v1/admin/keys", json=body, headers=auth(key))


async def test_lead_cannot_mint_a_key_that_acts_as_an_admin_or_another_team(client, durable):
    """Regression: a key acts as its user's record, so a lead minting a key for an existing admin got admin access."""
    await durable.store.upsert_user("boss", "ops", "admin")
    await durable.store.upsert_user("carol", "ops", "user")
    await durable.store.upsert_user("dana", "default", "team_lead")
    for user in ("boss", "carol", "dana"):
        r = await mint(client, {"user": user})
        assert r.status_code == 403 and "only an admin" in r.text, user
    assert not await durable.store.list_keys(user_id="boss")
    # Their own team's users, new people, and themselves are fine.
    await durable.store.upsert_user("erin", "default", "user")
    for user in ("erin", "newcomer@example.com", "lee"):
        assert (await mint(client, {"user": user})).status_code == 201, user
    # An admin can mint for anyone; the key acts as the user's record, and the response says so.
    r = await mint(client, {"user": "boss", "role": "user"}, ADMIN_KEY)
    assert r.status_code == 201 and r.json()["role"] == "admin" and r.json()["team"] == "ops" and "kept" in r.json()["note"]
    p = await durable.authn.authenticate({"authorization": f"Bearer {r.json()['api_key']}"})
    assert (p.user_id, p.team, p.role) == ("boss", "ops", "admin")


async def test_key_lifecycle_and_scoping(client, durable):
    r = await mint(client, {"user": "zed", "name": "ci", "tags": {"project": "x"}, "expires_days": 7})
    assert r.status_code == 201 and r.json()["expires_at"] and "Shown once" in r.json()["note"]
    lead_key = r.json()["id"]
    r = await mint(client, {"user": "olga", "team": "ops"}, ADMIN_KEY)
    ops_key = r.json()["id"]
    lead_view = {k["id"] for k in (await client.get("/v1/admin/keys", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).json()["keys"]}
    assert lead_key in lead_view and ops_key not in lead_view
    admin_view = (await client.get("/v1/admin/keys?user=olga", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()["keys"]
    assert [k["id"] for k in admin_view] == [ops_key] and admin_view[0]["status"] == "active"
    r = await client.delete(f"/v1/admin/keys/{ops_key}", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))
    assert r.status_code == 403 and "your own team" in r.text
    assert (await client.delete("/v1/admin/keys/key_nope", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).status_code == 404
    assert (await client.delete(f"/v1/admin/keys/{ops_key}", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()["revoked"] is True
    statuses = {k["id"]: k["status"] for k in (await client.get("/v1/admin/keys", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()["keys"]}
    assert statuses[ops_key] == "revoked"
    _, fin = await durable.store.create_key("fin", "ops", "finance")
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/keys", headers=auth(fin))).status_code == 403  # finance isn't a lead
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/keys")).status_code == 401


async def test_expired_key_status(client, durable):
    from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

    key_id, _ = await durable.store.create_key("old", "default", "user", expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1))
    keys = {k["id"]: k for k in (await client.get("/v1/admin/keys", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()["keys"]}
    assert keys[key_id]["status"] == "expired" and "key_hash" not in keys[key_id]


async def test_key_and_config_management_need_a_durable_store(client, gateway):
    if gateway.store.kind != "memory":
        pytest.skip("only the in-memory store refuses")
    for method, path, body in (("post", "/v1/admin/keys", {"user": "x"}), ("delete", "/v1/admin/keys/k", None),
                               ("patch", "/v1/admin/users/x", {"team": "default"}), ("put", "/v1/admin/config", {"yaml": "x: 1"}),
                               ("post", "/v1/admin/config/versions/1/restore", None), ("post", "/v1/admin/prices/refresh", None)):
        kwargs = {"json": body} if body is not None else {}
        r = await client.request(method, path, headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY), **kwargs)
        assert r.status_code == 409 and "Postgres" in r.text, path


async def test_people(client, durable):
    await durable.store.upsert_user("alice", "default", "user", email="alice@example.com")
    await durable.store.upsert_user("carol", "ops", "user")
    await durable.store.record(ledger_row(user_id="alice", actual_cost=2.5))
    await durable.store.rollup()
    lead = (await client.get("/v1/admin/users", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).json()
    assert [u["id"] for u in lead["users"]] == ["alice"] and lead["users"][0]["spend_month"] == 2.5
    admin = (await client.get("/v1/admin/users", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()
    assert {u["id"] for u in admin["users"]} == {"alice", "carol"} and admin["teams"] == ["default"]
    assert admin["oidc"] is False and admin["scim"] is False

    patch = lambda uid, body, key=ADMIN_KEY: client.patch(f"/v1/admin/users/{uid}", json=body, headers=auth(key))  # noqa: E731
    assert (await patch("alice", {"team": "default"}, LEAD_KEY)).status_code == 403
    r = await patch("root", {"disabled": True})
    assert r.status_code == 400 and "yourself" in r.text
    assert (await patch("root", {"role": "user"})).status_code == 400
    r = await patch("alice", {"team": "nowhere"})
    assert r.status_code == 400 and "isn't defined" in r.text
    assert (await patch("ghost", {"role": "user"})).status_code == 404
    r = (await patch("alice", {"role": "team_lead"})).json()
    assert r["role"] == "team_lead" and r["managed"] == "local"
    r = (await patch("alice", {"follow_idp": True})).json()
    assert r["managed"] == "idp"
    r = (await patch("alice", {"role": "user", "follow_idp": True})).json()  # both in one save (Postgres used to fail)
    assert r["role"] == "user" and r["managed"] == "idp"
    r = (await patch("alice", {"disabled": True})).json()
    assert r["disabled"] is True


async def test_evals_storage(client, gateway):
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/evals", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).json() == {"models": {}}
    run = {"suite": "starter", "ran_at": "2026-11-10T00:00:00Z", "models": {"small": {"score": 0.7}, "big": {"score": 0.9}}}
    assert (await client.put("/v1/admin/evals", json=run, headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).status_code == 403
    await client.put("/v1/admin/evals", json=run, headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    later = {"suite": "starter", "ran_at": "2026-11-11T00:00:00Z", "models": {"small": {"score": 0.75}}}
    out = (await client.put("/v1/admin/evals", json=later, headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()
    assert out["models"]["small"] == {"score": 0.75, "suite": "starter", "ran_at": "2026-11-11T00:00:00Z"}
    assert out["models"]["big"]["score"] == 0.9  # the latest result per model is kept


async def test_config_overview(client, gateway):
    c = (await client.get("/v1/admin/config", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()
    assert c["baseline_model"] == "big" and {b["name"] for b in c["backends"]} >= {"mock-anthropic", "mock-openai"}
    big = next(m for m in c["models"] if m["name"] == "big")
    assert big["routes"][0]["live"] is True and big["routes"][0]["price"]["input"] == 3
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/config", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).status_code == 403


async def test_config_source_without_a_file_or_version(client, gateway):
    gateway.file_raw = None
    r = await client.get("/v1/admin/config/source", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    assert r.status_code == 409


async def test_config_save_validate_and_restore_errors(client, durable, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("T_USER", "mo-test-key")
    monkeypatch.setenv("T_ADMIN", "mo-admin-key")
    doc = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
    doc["auth"]["static_keys"] = [{"key_env": "T_USER", "user": "alice", "team": "default"},
                                  {"key_env": "T_ADMIN", "user": "root", "team": "ops", "role": "admin"}]
    v = await client.post("/v1/admin/config/validate", json={"document": {"models": "not a mapping"}}, headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    assert v.json()["ok"] is False
    r = await client.put("/v1/admin/config", json={"yaml": "models: [unclosed"}, headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    assert r.status_code == 422
    r = await client.put("/v1/admin/config", json={"document": doc, "comment": "first"}, headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["version"] == 1
    src = (await client.get("/v1/admin/config/source", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()
    assert src["source"] == "database" and src["version"] == 1 and yaml.safe_load(src["yaml"])["baseline_model"] == "big"
    one = (await client.get("/v1/admin/config/versions/1", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).json()
    assert one["author"] == "root" and one["comment"] == "first"
    assert (await client.get("/v1/admin/config/versions/99", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).status_code == 404
    assert (await client.post("/v1/admin/config/versions/99/restore", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).status_code == 404
    # A stored version that no longer validates (e.g. it names a key variable that's gone) can't be restored.
    bad = copy.deepcopy(doc)
    bad["baseline_model"] = "a-model-that-was-removed"
    vid = await durable.store.save_config(bad, "root", "broken")
    r = await client.post(f"/v1/admin/config/versions/{vid}/restore", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    assert r.status_code == 422 and "no longer validates" in r.text


async def test_prices_refresh(client, durable, monkeypatch):
    import meritorder.catalog as catalog

    def fake_refresh(cfg, path, write):
        return None, 3, ["small"], {"updated": "2026-11-10", "prices": {}}

    monkeypatch.setattr(catalog, "refresh_prices", fake_refresh)
    r = await client.post("/v1/admin/prices/refresh", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json() == {"priced_routes": 3, "missing": ["small"], "updated": "2026-11-10", "by": "root"}
    assert (await durable.store.get_setting("prices"))["updated"] == "2026-11-10"
    assert (await client.post("/v1/admin/prices/refresh", headers=auth(LEAD_KEY))).status_code == 403

from datetime import UTC, datetime

import yaml

from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, Config, ModelConfig, Route, ServeConfig
from meritorder.controller import tick
from meritorder.gpu import (
    API_ONLY, DRAINING, PROVISIONING, WARM, Demand, Deployment, SkyPilotProvisioner, Status, addressable, decide,
    desired_replicas, parse_vllm_metrics,
)
from meritorder.state import MemoryState
from meritorder.store import MemoryStore

SERVE = ServeConfig(model="ow", scale_up_after_minutes=10, hold_minutes=30, drain_minutes=15, max_replicas=4)


def test_desired_replicas_must_pay_for_themselves():
    # $50/h of API spend can pay for 2 replicas at $20/h (with 20% margin), throughput needs 3.
    d = desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=50, tokens_per_second=2000))
    assert d == 2
    assert desired_replicas(SERVE, 20.0, 1000, Demand(usd_per_hour=10, tokens_per_second=2000)) == 0
    warm = ServeConfig(model="ow", min_replicas=1)
    assert desired_replicas(warm, 20.0, 1000, Demand(0, 0)) == 1


def test_state_machine_full_cycle():
    t = 1_000_000.0
    rec, act = decide({}, SERVE, desired=2, status=Status(), now=t)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act is None  # must be justified for 10 minutes first
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + 601)
    assert rec["state"] == PROVISIONING and act.kind == "up" and act.replicas == 2
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM and rec["endpoint"] == "http://gpu/v1"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 3, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1600)
    assert act.kind == "scale" and act.replicas == 3
    # demand disappears, but GPUs are held for 30 minutes after warming
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1700)
    assert rec["state"] == WARM
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801)
    assert rec["state"] == DRAINING
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 0, Status(ready=True, endpoint="http://gpu/v1"), t + 1500 + 1801 + 901)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"


def test_provisioning_timeout_cools_down():
    t = 0.0
    rec = {"state": PROVISIONING, "since": t}
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 1)
    assert rec["state"] == API_ONLY and act.kind == "down"
    rec, act = decide(rec, SERVE, 2, Status(), t + SERVE.provision_timeout_minutes * 60 + 700)
    assert act is None  # still cooling down


def test_addressable_demand_uses_quality_floor():
    cfg = Config(backends=[], models=[ModelConfig(name="ow", quality={"coding": 4}, routes=[Route(backend="x", model="y")])])
    rows = [
        {"floor": "coding:3", "served_model": "sonnet", "requested_model": "auto", "cost": 10.0, "tokens": 100},
        {"floor": "coding:5", "served_model": "opus", "requested_model": "auto", "cost": 50.0, "tokens": 500},
        {"floor": None, "served_model": "ow", "requested_model": "ow", "cost": 2.0, "tokens": 20},
    ]
    assert addressable(cfg.models[0], rows, cfg) == (12.0, 120)


def test_parse_vllm_metrics():
    text = """# HELP vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc KV-cache usage
vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc{model_name="m"} 0.42
vllm:num_requests_waiting{model_name="m"} 0.0
"""
    assert parse_vllm_metrics(text) == 0.42
    assert parse_vllm_metrics(text.replace("waiting{model_name=\"m\"} 0.0", "waiting{model_name=\"m\"} 4")) > 0.85


def test_skypilot_task_yaml():
    model = ModelConfig(name="ow", hf_id="Org/Model-7B", routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="org-model")])
    backend = BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai",
                            serve=ServeConfig(model="ow", accelerators="L4:2", clouds=["aws", "gcp"], use_spot=True, vllm_args="--max-model-len 32768"))
    cfg = Config(backends=[backend], models=[model])
    task = yaml.safe_load(SkyPilotProvisioner(backend, cfg).task_yaml(2))
    assert task["service"]["replicas"] == 2
    assert task["resources"]["accelerators"] == "L4:2" and task["resources"]["use_spot"] is True
    assert {c["cloud"] for c in task["resources"]["any_of"]} == {"aws", "gcp"}
    assert "vllm serve Org/Model-7B" in task["run"]
    assert "--served-model-name org-model" in task["run"] and "--tensor-parallel-size 2" in task["run"]
    assert "--enable-prefix-caching" in task["run"] and task["run"].endswith("--max-model-len 32768")


class FakeProvisioner:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
        self.ready = False

    async def status(self):
        return Status(ready=self.ready, endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1" if self.ready else None)

    async def up(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("up", n))

    async def scale(self, n):
        self.calls.append(("scale", n))

    async def down(self):
        self.calls.append(("down",))


async def test_controller_tick_scales_up_on_addressable_demand():
    model = ModelConfig(name="ow", quality={"coding": 4}, hf_id="o/m", routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="m")])

The memo below argues for a company-wide four-day week. It contains **exactly three** substantive flaws in its reasoning or its use of evidence. Everything else in it (the facts it reports, the measurement process it describes, and its arithmetic) is accurate.

Identify the three flaws. For each one:

1. say what the flaw is and quote or point to the part of the memo it affects,
2. explain why it undermines the recommendation, quantifying the problem with the memo's own numbers wherever they allow it, and
3. say what evidence or analysis would fix it.

Then give a one-sentence verdict on whether the memo's recommendation is supported. Do not pad the list with minor or speculative concerns; we want the three real flaws.

---

**MEMO**

**To:** Executive Committee
**From:** People Analytics
**Date:** 22 April 2025
**Subject:** Four-day week pilot: results and recommendation

**Summary.** Our 13-week pilot of a four-day week in Customer Engineering raised productivity by 18% and cut attrition by almost two thirds, with no loss of customer satisfaction. We recommend rolling the four-day week out to all 1,240 engineers from the start of Q3 2025.

**1. Pilot design**

The pilot ran for the 13 weeks from 6 January to 4 April 2025. Pilot engineers worked 32 hours over four days at unchanged pay. In November 2024 every team in Customer Engineering was invited to apply, and all seven teams that applied were accepted: 61 engineers in total. The applicants were an enthusiastic group and included all three teams that won last year's Delivery Excellence award. The remaining 12 teams (174 engineers) kept the usual five-day week and serve as the comparison group.

Both groups were measured over exactly the same 13 calendar weeks, so seasonality, holidays and release cycles affected them equally.

Customer Engineering is a fair proxy for engineering as a whole: the 2024 work-mix study found that every engineering organisation uses the same ticketing process and has a similar mix of feature, maintenance and support work, and similar on-call duties.

**2. How we measured productivity**

Our productivity measure is tickets closed per engineer per week, taken directly from the ticketing system. The definition of "closed" and the script that counts closed tickets were identical for both groups, and Internal Audit reviewed both before the pilot began. Tickets reopened within 14 days were not counted as closed for either group.

To help pilot teams adapt to the shorter week, their agile coaches encouraged them to split work into smaller tickets that fit within four days. Over the pilot, the average size of a pilot team's ticket fell from 5.0 story points to 3.4 story points. The comparison group's average ticket size stayed at 5.0 story points throughout.

**3. Results**

*Productivity.* Pilot engineers closed an average of 9.2 tickets per week, against 7.8 for the comparison group: 18% more. The effect was stable across the pilot rather than a short-lived burst of enthusiasm: the pilot's weekly average was 9.1 in weeks 1–4, 9.3 in weeks 5–9 and 9.2 in weeks 10–13. A test on weekly team-level averages puts the difference well outside what chance would produce (p = 0.01).

*Customer satisfaction.* The average customer satisfaction (CSAT) score on tickets handled by pilot teams was 4.5 out of 5 (from 1,900 survey responses), against 4.4 for the comparison group (5,200 responses). The four-day week did not hurt customers.

*Attrition.* Only 2 of the 61 pilot engineers resigned during the pilot, an attrition rate of 3.3%. The company's attrition rate for 2024 was 9% per year. The four-day week therefore cut attrition by almost two thirds, which matters because each departure costs us roughly $90,000 in recruiting and ramp-up time.

*Engagement.* In the end-of-pilot survey, 57 of the 61 pilot engineers (93%) said they would like to keep the four-day week.

**4. Recommendation**

Because the pilot raised productivity by 18% and cut attrition by almost two thirds, we recommend extending the four-day week to all 1,240 engineers from 1 July 2025. An 18% productivity gain across 1,240 engineers is equivalent to adding about 223 engineers of capacity at no extra salary cost. We propose a review after two quarters, with the option to return any team to a five-day week if its results fall short.

# 03 — Routing The router answers: **which model, on which backend, for this request?** It optimizes **marginal cost** — what this request adds to the bill *right now* — subject to a quality floor and team policy. ## Decision flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> B{"Harness pinned
a model?"} B -- "yes" --> FIX["Model is fixed
(only the backend can vary)"] B -- "no, model=auto" --> C{"Existing session,
mid-task, cache warm?"} C -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep session's model"] C -- "no" --> D["Classifier → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] D --> E["Candidates = models allowed for team
with quality ≥ floor"] FIX --> S KEEP --> S E --> S["Score every backend of every candidate
cost = rebuild + turns × per-turn"] S --> T{"Cheapest beats current
by more than hysteresis margin?"} T -- "yes" --> MOVE["Route to cheapest
(ties → higher quality)"] T -- "no" --> STAY["Stay on current backend"] MOVE --> PRI{"Running above floor
only because it's free?"} STAY --> PRI PRI -- "yes" --> LOW["Send with low priority
(paid traffic preempts it)"] PRI -- "no" --> NORM["Send with normal priority"] ``` ## The cost function For each candidate backend `b`, over the session's expected remaining turns: ``` cost(b) = rebuild(b) + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn(b) ``` **Per-turn cost by backend type** | Backend state | `per_turn(b)` | |---|---| | API | uncached tokens × input price + cached tokens × cache-read price + output × output price | | Self-hosted, plenty of headroom | ≈ 0 (shadow price near zero) | | Self-hosted, filling up | shadow price rises toward the same model's API price | | Self-hosted, at latency target | unavailable (or priced as the API version of the same model) | **Rebuild cost** | Situation | `rebuild(b)` | |---|---| | `b` already holds a warm cache for this session | 0 | | API, cold | prefix tokens × (cache-write price − cache-read price) | | Self-hosted, cold | prefix tokens × shadow price + latency penalty for the prefill | Illustrative (check real prices): a 120k-token Claude session costs ~$0.04/turn in cache reads to stay. Moving it to another Claude backend costs ~$0.45 to rewrite the cache. A move has to save more than ~$0.41 over the rest of the session to be worth it. ## Shadow price Self-hosted tokens aren't literally free — capacity is finite. The shadow price makes spare capacity attractive while protecting latency: ![Shadow price vs replica utilization](img/shadow-price.svg) ## Free upgrades (and why they're safe) If a strong open model is running with headroom and the task only needs a medium model, the user gets the strong model at ~zero cost. Three guardrails keep this from backfiring: 1. **Low priority.** Opportunistic requests use vLLM priority scheduling, so traffic that *needs* that model always goes first. 2. **Doesn't keep GPUs alive.** The controller values upgraded traffic at its *floor* model's API price, so free traffic can't make a GPU look worth keeping. (See [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md).) 3. **Only at boundaries.** Upgrades/downgrades happen at session start or task boundaries — never mid-task — so tool-calling behavior and caches stay stable. ## Free moments to re-route Moving costs nothing when the session's cache is already gone: - Session idle longer than the cache TTL. - The harness compacted history (prefix hash no longer matches). - The replica evicted the session's KV cache (from vLLM / llm-d KV events). - A natural task boundary. ## Harness overrides | Harness sends | Behavior | |---|---| | `model: "claude-sonnet-4-5"` (explicit) | No model substitution. Router picks the cheapest *backend* for that model. | | `model: "auto"` | Classifier + router choose. | | `model: "auto"` + `X-Route-Floor: coding:3` | Harness sets the floor; router chooses above it. | | `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges the classifier's floor down / up. | Team policy (allowed models, allowed providers, data-residency rules) is applied **before** scoring, so an override can never escape policy.

# 05 — GPU autoscaling Only open-weight models (Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Llama, …) can be self-hosted. Every self-hostable model should also have **at least one API route serving the same weights** (OpenRouter, the vendor, Bedrock, …). APIs are the floor; GPUs are an optimization. The console warns about models without one before anyone stops their GPUs. The full decision logic, with every rule and default, is in [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md#when-gpus-start-scale-and-stop). ## Lifecycle of a self-hosted model ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> APIOnly APIOnly --> Provisioning: demand pays for a replica for 10 min,
or pinned by an admin Provisioning --> Warm: replicas answer /v1/models Provisioning --> APIOnly: failed / timed out (30 min cooldown),
or stopped Warm --> Warm: add or remove replicas Warm --> Draining: below break-even 10 min (and warm 30 min),
or stopped with drain Warm --> APIOnly: stopped now Warm --> Provisioning: lost readiness (e.g. spot preemption) Draining --> Warm: demand returns (unless stopped) Draining --> APIOnly: after 15 min, GPUs released note right of APIOnly All traffic on API routes. Controller watches demand. end note note right of Provisioning 10–20+ min for big MoE models. Traffic stays on API meanwhile. end note note right of Draining No new sessions. Warm sessions finish there. end note ``` ## Controller loop (every 60 s) ```mermaid flowchart TD L["Read the ledger
last 1 h and last 15 min"] --> A["Addressable demand for this model:
traffic whose quality floor it meets,
valued at API prices, free upgrades excluded"] A --> R["Desired replicas =
enough for throughput,
but each must pay for itself"] R --> CT["Admin controls and safeguards
stop all · stop · pin · GPU budget · fleet caps"] CT --> SM{"State machine
api_only · provisioning · warm · draining"} SM -- "up / scale / down" --> P["Provisioner
SkyPilot (sky serve) or static"] SM --> PUB["Publish state, endpoint,
vLLM utilization → Redis"] PUB --> GW["Gateways pick it up
within 5 s"] ``` Why *addressable* demand: if the controller only counted traffic already sent to a model, a model that isn't running would never look worth starting, because `auto` routes its traffic elsewhere. So it counts what you currently pay for all traffic this model *could* serve (its quality meets the request's floor), at API-equivalent prices. That value doesn't drop when the GPUs start serving, so the controller doesn't flap. ## The break-even test ``` demand_per_hour = addressable API-equivalent spend per hour (max of the 1 h and 4 × 15 min windows) throughput = addressable tokens per second (same windows) by_load = ceil(throughput / (capacity_tokens_per_second × target_utilization)) affordable = floor(demand_per_hour / (replica_price × (1 + margin))) replica_price = cheapest SkyPilot catalog offer in the allowed clouds/regions, else gpu_cost_per_hour desired_replicas = clamp(min(by_load ≥ 1, affordable), min_replicas, max_replicas) ``` State machine (`src/meritorder/gpu.py`, pure and unit-tested): | From | To | When | |---|---|---| | api_only | provisioning | `desired ≥ 1` continuously for `scale_up_after_minutes` (or `min_replicas > 0`) | | provisioning | warm | replicas answer `/v1/models` | | provisioning | api_only | failed or `provision_timeout_minutes` passed; 30-minute cooldown | | warm | warm | replica count follows `desired` | | warm | draining | `desired = 0` for `scale_up_after_minutes`, and warm for at least `hold_minutes` | | warm | provisioning | replicas stop answering (e.g. spot preemption); traffic goes to APIs until they're back | | draining | warm | demand returns | | draining | api_only | after `drain_minutes`; GPUs released | | any | api_only / draining | an admin stops it, Stop all GPUs, or the GPU budget runs out (see [Controls](#controls-and-safeguards)) | | api_only | provisioning | an admin pins replicas: at once, skipping the wait and any cooldown | Key details: - **Free upgrades don't count.** Traffic running above its floor because a GPU had headroom is excluded, so idle capacity can't keep itself alive by attracting traffic. - **Measured capacity, not benchmarks.** `capacity_tokens_per_second` should be what one replica sustains at your latency target on real agent traffic (prefill-heavy). - **Hysteresis everywhere.** Margins, minimum hold time, and the scale-up delay stop flapping. A 20-minute cold start is expensive to waste. - **Spot where it's safe.** SkyServe handles spot preemption; overflow to the API covers the gap. ## Configuring a self-hosted model ```yaml backends: gpu-qwen-coder: kind: self_hosted format: openai gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0 # one replica (here 4× H100) capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000 serve: provisioner: skypilot # or `static` for a server you already run model: qwen3-coder-next # its hf_id is what vLLM serves accelerators: "H100:4" use_spot: true clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda] image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0 vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144" max_replicas: 4 ``` The SkyPilot provisioner writes a SkyServe service (vLLM with `--enable-prefix-caching` and `--scheduling-policy priority`, fixed replica count, readiness probe on `/v1/models`) and drives `sky serve up / update / down`. It needs the `sky` CLI and cloud credentials (`sky check`). Set `HF_TOKEN` for gated models. ## Controls and safeguards The console's **GPUs** page shows, for every deployment: where each replica runs (cloud, region, zone, instance, spot or on-demand, from SkyPilot), how long it has been up, its burn rate, what this run and this month have cost, what demand would pay for it at API prices, and why the controller is doing what it's doing. An activity log records every state change, scale, and admin action with who did it. Admins can override the controller: | Control | Effect | |---|---| | **Stop** (drain first) | No new sessions; warm ones finish for up to `drain_minutes`, then the replicas go down. Skips the usual hold time | | **Stop now** | Replicas go down at once; their sessions continue on APIs (caches rebuild there) | | **Pin N replicas** | Runs N regardless of demand, skipping the scale-up wait and any failure cooldown | | **Back to automatic** | Demand decides again | | **Stop all GPUs** | Every deployment stops and none start until someone resumes the fleet | Stops and pins can expire after a set number of hours, and every one takes a reason. Gateways stop routing to a stopped deployment within seconds, before the controller acts; the controller wakes up as soon as a control changes. For a static server, Merit Order can only stop sending it traffic. Organization safeguards apply on top, to pins as well ([06](06-auth-and-spend.md#organization-wide-safeguards)): a monthly GPU budget, a fleet burn-rate cap, and a replica cap. ### What GPUs cost Prices come from **SkyPilot's catalog**, the same list prices its optimizer uses to pick a cloud: - **Before launching**, the break-even test uses the cheapest catalog offer for the deployment's accelerators within its allowed clouds and regions (spot or on-demand, per `use_spot`). - **While running**, each replica is priced for its actual cloud, region, instance type, and spot/on-demand, so a replica that lands in a pricier region costs what it really costs. - `gpu_cost_per_hour` is only a fallback, used for static servers (your own hardware) and when SkyPilot isn't installed where the controller runs. Cost is accrued every cycle from the moment provisioning starts until the replicas are down, and stored per hour (`gpu_usage`). Self-hosted tokens are charged back at the same live price. These are **list prices**, not your bill: they don't include negotiated discounts, reservations, or credits, and they leave out disks, egress, and the SkyServe controller VM. Spot prices in the catalog are refreshed periodically, not live. Reconciling against the cloud bill is on the roadmap. SkyPilot runs in its own Python environment (the `-gpu` image, built with `--build-arg SKYPILOT=`), so its dependencies never mix with the gateway's. Merit Order calls it through the `sky` CLI and, for prices, SkyPilot's Python (`MERITORDER_SKY_PYTHON`, found from the `sky` command when unset). If the controller stops running while GPUs are up, the console flags it: nothing would scale them down. If a stop fails at the cloud, the deployment stays marked as running and the controller keeps retrying, so a GPU that may still be billing is never shown as off. ## Overflow ```mermaid flowchart LR REQ["New session for qwen3-coder"] --> H{"Self-hosted pool
has headroom?"} H -- "yes" --> SELF["Self-hosted replica
(cache-aware pick)"] H -- "no" --> API{"Another route?
e.g. Bedrock / Together"} API -- "yes" --> SPILL["Same model via API"] API -- "no" --> Q["Waits in vLLM's queue,
up to max_waiting per replica;
then 503"] SPILL -.-> SIG["Controller sees the demand:
adds replicas"] ``` Below 100%, rising load raises the GPU's shadow price, so new sessions drift to APIs before it's full. At 100%, nothing new goes there while any other route can take it; sessions already there move too. A saturated GPU that's a model's only route still takes requests, which wait in vLLM, until `max_waiting` per replica are waiting. Set `max_concurrency` so gateways see saturation within seconds instead of at the controller's next sample. Details: [When a GPU is full](10-how-it-decides.md#when-a-gpu-is-full). ## Inside the GPU pool - **Continuous batching** is the engine's job (vLLM / SGLang). The gateway sends concurrently and never serializes requests per replica. - **Cache-aware replica routing** sends a session back to the replica holding its KV cache. - **Priority scheduling**: normal traffic > opportunistic (free-upgrade) traffic. - **Engine knobs per model**: `max-num-seqs`, `max-num-batched-tokens`, chunked prefill, prefix caching (on), optional speculative decoding.

# Merit Order

An open-source LLM gateway that cuts LLM spend for day-to-day use, without changing how
people work.

Power grids dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest marginal cost first, with expensive
peaker plants switched on only when demand requires them. Merit Order does the same with tokens:

- **Routes** every session to the cheapest model and backend that meets the task's quality bar,
  counting what it would cost to rebuild the prompt cache somewhere else.
- **Runs open-weight models on your own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when steady load makes that cheaper
  than paying per token, and turns them off when it doesn't. APIs (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex,
  Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, ...) are always there for overflow.
- **Saves tokens**: automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, cache-safe compression of huge tool
  outputs, and an optional response cache.
- **Shows the money**: every request is recorded with what it cost and what it would have cost
  without Merit Order, broken down by cause, per user, team, project, and day.

Point Claude Code, pi, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or anything that speaks either API at it.

## Quickstart (no keys needed)

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env            # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY (and any provider keys you have)
uv run meritorder serve         # http://localhost:8080, reports UI at /ui/
```

```bash
curl localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $MERITORDER_DEV_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}'
```

With no provider keys, requests go to built-in mock backends. `uv run meritorder check` shows
which backends and models are live with the keys you've set. Without `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`,
storage is in memory; use Docker Compose for the real thing.

## Run the full stack with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add at least one provider key
docker compose up -d            # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080
docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin
```

Bedrock with your AWS profile (including SSO): `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d`.
Kubernetes: `helm install mo charts/meritorder` (see [docs/07-deployment.md](docs/07-deployment.md)).

## Point your harness at it

```bash
meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com   # Entra sign-in; or: meritorder use-key <key>
meritorder setup pi                                    # adds a "meritorder" provider to pi
meritorder setup claude-code                           # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + apiKeyHelper
```

Or by hand: OpenAI-compatible clients use base URL `<gateway>/v1`; Claude Code uses
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>`. Use `model: "auto"` to let Merit Order choose, or name a model
(`claude-sonnet`, `kimi-k3.1`, `qwen3-coder`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, ...) to pin it.

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Session-Id` | Groups requests into a session (pi sends it; otherwise inferred) |
| `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | Minimum quality for `auto` routing |
| `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges `auto` routing down or up |
| `X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=foo` | Cost-allocation tags for reports |
| `X-MeritOrder-Cache: on` / `off` | Use or bypass the response cache |
| `X-MeritOrder-Backend: <name>` | Admins only: pin a backend (testing, debugging) |

Responses carry `x-meritorder-model`, `x-meritorder-backend`, and (non-streaming)
`x-meritorder-cost-usd` / `x-meritorder-savings-usd`. A model you name is never swapped for
another unless your team opted in to substitution when it can't run; reasoning effort you set is
always passed through. Every routing and scaling rule, as diagrams:
[docs/10-how-it-decides.md](docs/10-how-it-decides.md).

## What's in the box

| Area | Built |
|---|---|
| APIs | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (stateless), Anthropic Messages, and embeddings; streaming and not; pass-through when formats match, translation when they don't |
| Backends | Anthropic, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, OpenRouter (incl. opt-in free tier), DeepSeek, Mistral, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, any OpenAI-compatible server |
| Models | Claude, GPT, and an open-weight catalog: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen3-Coder, MiniMax, MiMo, Muse, Mistral/Devstral, Gemma, Nemotron, gpt-oss |
| Routing | Rule-based classifier → quality floor; marginal-cost router with cache rebuild cost, context-window checks, sticky sessions, fallback across backends and on refusals; `meritorder eval` measures each model's quality scores with graded tasks |
| GPUs | Break-even controller (addressable demand, hysteresis), SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM provisioner, static servers, utilization from vLLM metrics, spill to API when saturated (live in-flight counts; a GPU that's the only route queues, bounded); console shows where each replica runs, uptime, burn rate, and cost, with stop / drain / pin / stop-all controls and an activity log |
| Savings | Automatic prompt caching, lower reasoning effort for simple `auto` tasks (stable per session), deterministic tool-output compression, opt-in response cache |
| Identity | Virtual API keys, Entra/OIDC device-code login with group → team/role mapping, roles (user, team lead, finance, admin), People page to move, pin, or disable anyone (applies to existing keys within a minute) |
| Spend | Organization, team, and user monthly budgets, GPU budget and fleet caps, a per-request cost ceiling, per-session spend caps (stops runaway agents), requests/tokens-per-minute limits, policy allow/deny lists for models and backends; all editable on the console's Controls page |
| Control panel | Web console at `/ui/` (Mantine, dark by default): live Dispatch view (merit-order stack from real traffic, live request feed, backend health, GPU fleet, needs-attention), Reports, GPUs (incl. what-if and controls), Controls (budgets and safeguards against spend), Backends, Models, Teams, People, Keys, and Config (forms for teams, models, backends, routing, and access plus raw YAML; validate, version history, restore; hot-reloads every gateway) |
| Reporting | Ledger with savings by cause, reports API, CSV, JSONL/CSV ledger export to a file or S3, `meritorder usage`, Prometheus metrics, budget/spike alerts, weekly digests |
| Deployment | Docker Compose, Helm chart, CI (tests, audits, Helm lint, Compose smoke test), signed multi-arch releases |

Not yet: reconciliation against provider and cloud bills, Kubernetes-native GPU provisioning
(llm-d/KServe), a learned router, Parquet export. See [docs/](docs/README.md)
for the design, [how it decides](docs/10-how-it-decides.md), and [the decisions](docs/09-decisions.md).

## Development

```bash
uv sync && uv run pytest                     # gateway (in-memory state and storage)
cd ui && npm ci && npm run build             # reporting UI (served at /ui/)
cd ui && npx playwright install chromium && E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://… npm run e2e   # console browser tests
uv run python scripts/fake_vllm.py           # a stand-in vLLM server for the GPU path
uv run python scripts/smoke_providers.py     # test every enabled provider through a running gateway
```

To also run every test against real Redis and Postgres (CI does, with a 90% coverage floor), point
these at a throwaway Redis database and Postgres database; both are wiped before each test:

```bash
MERITORDER_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/15 \
MERITORDER_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:pw@localhost:5432/motest \
uv run pytest --cov
```

# 08 — Reporting Merit Order exists to save money, so reporting is a core feature: what was spent, what was saved, why, by whom, and when. ## Data flow ```mermaid flowchart LR gw["Gateway"] -- "one row per request (async)" --> ledger[("Ledger
Postgres, monthly partitions")] ctl["Capacity controller"] -- "GPU hours, utilization" --> roll ledger --> roll["Rollup worker"] roll --> agg[("Hourly + daily rollups
by user, team, tag,
model, backend")] roll --> alerts["Alerts
budgets, spend spikes,
break-even changes"] agg --> api["Reports API"] ledger --> api api --> ui["Web UI"] api --> cli["meritorder usage"] api --> exp["CSV / Parquet exports"] api --> dig["Scheduled digests
email, Slack, Teams"] bills["Provider billing exports
AWS, GCP, Azure"] --> recon["Monthly reconciliation"] agg --> recon gw -. "Prometheus / OpenTelemetry" .-> mon["Grafana, Datadog, ..."] ``` Reports never contain prompt or response content. The ledger holds metadata only. ## Savings numbers have to stand up to scrutiny If finance finds one inflated number, they stop trusting the whole dashboard. So: **1. A baseline per team.** "What you'd have done without Merit Order", set in config: ```yaml teams: platform: baseline_model: claude-sonnet # API at list price, no proxy-added caching pricing_overrides: bedrock: { discount_pct: 12 } # negotiated / committed-spend discount ``` **2. Savings broken down by cause, never one blended number.** Causes are computed in a fixed order, each against the result of the previous step, so they add up exactly to the total with no double counting: | Order | Cause | How it's counted | |---|---|---| | 1 | **Routing** | Baseline model's API cost − served model's API cost | | 2 | **Self-hosting** | Served model's API cost − chargeback cost on our GPUs | | 3 | **Prompt caching** | Discount from cache breakpoints *we added*, minus cache-write premiums we paid. Caching the harness set up itself would have happened anyway and isn't counted. | | 4 | **Compression** | Tokens removed × served model's input price | | 5 | **Response cache** | Full cost of each request answered from cache | **3. Two headline numbers, side by side:** savings against list price, and savings caused by Merit Order. **4. Negotiated prices.** Per-provider discounts and price overrides, so costs match what the organization actually pays. **5. Monthly reconciliation.** Compare our computed cost with providers' billing exports (AWS Cost and Usage Reports, GCP billing export, Azure Cost Management) and report the difference. ## What's tracked | Area | Metrics | |---|---| | **Spend** | Actual cost by user, team, project tag, API key, model, provider, backend, time; burn rate; month-end forecast | | **Savings** | Total and by cause (above), over time | | **GPU fleet** | GPU hours and cost, utilization, effective $/M tokens vs API equivalent, break-even status per model, cold starts, overflow rate | | **Routing** | Model mix, free-upgrade rate, quality floor distribution, harness overrides | | **Caching** | Cache hit rate per backend, sessions that switched backends, rebuild cost paid | | **Operations** | Time to first token, tokens/s, error rate per backend | | **Budgets** | Users and teams near limits, soft and hard limit events | ## Views | View | Audience | Shows | |---|---|---| | **Executive summary** | Leadership, finance | Spend vs savings over time, savings by cause, forecast | | **Team chargeback** | Finance, team leads | Monthly cost per team and project tag, exportable | | **My usage** | Every user | Own spend, models used, budget remaining | | **GPU fleet** | Platform team | Per-model break-even, utilization, cost per token | | **Routing and caching** | Platform team | Where traffic went and why, cache efficiency | ## Who sees what Roles come from Entra (or OIDC) group membership. | Role | Can see | |---|---| | User | Their own usage | | Team lead | Their team's usage, per user | | Finance | All spend and savings, no per-request detail | | Admin | Everything | ## Ways to get reports - **Web UI** with the views above. - **Reports API.** The UI is built on it, so anyone can build their own views. - **CLI:** `meritorder usage` for a quick look at your own spend. - **Exports:** CSV, and Parquet to S3 / GCS / Blob storage for data warehouses and BI tools. - **Scheduled digests** to email, Slack, or Teams (e.g. weekly per team). - **Alerts:** budget thresholds, **spend spikes** (a user suddenly at 5× normal usually means an agent stuck in a loop), and a model's GPU break-even status flipping. - **Metrics:** Prometheus and OpenTelemetry, plus a ready-made Grafana dashboard. ## Cost allocation tags Requests can carry tags, and API keys can have default tags: ``` X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=checkout-rewrite,ticket=PLAT-1234 ``` Tags flow into the ledger and every report can group by them. ## Storage and scale - The ledger is a Postgres table partitioned by month. - A rollup worker keeps hourly and daily summary tables current. Dashboards read the summaries, not the raw ledger. - Postgres comfortably handles the millions of requests per month a $100k+/month organization generates. ClickHouse can be an optional backend for very large deployments. - We don't build a general-purpose BI tool. Ad-hoc analysis goes through the exports. ## What's built and what isn't yet | Piece | Status | |---|---| | Ledger, hourly rollups (`meritorder worker`, `--backfill`) | Built | | Savings by cause, baseline per team, negotiated prices (`price:` per route) | Built | | Reports API (`/v1/reports/summary`, `summary.csv`, `me`, `requests`, `gpu`) with role scoping | Built | | Web UI at `/ui/` (React/TypeScript): Overview, Breakdown (team, user, model, backend, tag), Requests, GPUs, My usage | Built | | `meritorder usage` | Built | | Prometheus `/metrics` (requests, tokens, cost, baseline, savings by cause, latency histogram) | Built | | Alerts (budget 80%/100%, spend spikes, GPU state changes) and Monday digests to a webhook | Built (`MERITORDER_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`) | | Parquet export to object storage | Not yet | | Monthly reconciliation against provider billing exports | Not yet | | ClickHouse backend for very large deployments | Not yet | The UI is a small React/TypeScript app (no charting library; hand-written SVG) built into the Python package and served by the gateway. It signs in with a Merit Order API key and shows what that key's role may see.

"""OpenAI backends with `api: responses`: Chat Completions requests go to /responses and come back as Chat
Completions. Found live: GPT-5.6 rejects function tools with reasoning on /chat/completions."""

import copy
import json

import httpx
from conftest import TEST_CONFIG
from test_http_backend import Upstream, chunks, collect, post, stream_response

from meritorder.app import build_gateway
from meritorder.config import build_config
from meritorder.formats.responses_upstream import ResponsesToChatStream, chat_to_responses_request, responses_to_chat_completion
from meritorder.formats.sse import event, iter_sse
from meritorder.state import MemoryState
from meritorder.store import MemoryStore

TOOL = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "description": "Weather",
                                         "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}}}


def test_request_conversion_covers_roles_tools_limits_and_effort():
    body = {"model": "gpt-x", "max_completion_tokens": 300, "reasoning_effort": "high", "temperature": 0.2, "prompt_cache_key": "s1",
            "tools": [TOOL], "tool_choice": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather"}}, "stream": True,
            "stop": ["x"], "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": "be brief"},
                {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "look"}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,AA"}}]},
                {"role": "assistant", "content": "checking", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function",
                                                                              "function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"}}]},
                {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "sunny"}]},
            ]}
    out = chat_to_responses_request(body)
    assert out["store"] is False and out["stream"] is True and out["max_output_tokens"] == 300
    assert out["reasoning"] == {"effort": "high"} and out["temperature"] == 0.2 and out["prompt_cache_key"] == "s1" and "stop" not in out
    assert out["tools"] == [{"type": "function", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Weather",
                             "parameters": TOOL["function"]["parameters"], "strict": False}]
    assert out["tool_choice"] == {"type": "function", "name": "get_weather"}
    assert out["input"] == [
        {"type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": "be brief"},
        {"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "look"},
                                                        {"type": "input_image", "image_url": "data:image/png;base64,AA", "detail": "auto"}]},
        {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "checking"}]},
        {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"},
        {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": "sunny"},
    ]
    schema = chat_to_responses_request({"messages": [], "max_tokens": 5, "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "r", "schema": {"type": "object"}, "strict": True}}})
    assert schema["max_output_tokens"] == 5 and schema["text"] == {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "r", "schema": {"type": "object"}, "strict": True}}
    assert chat_to_responses_request({"messages": [], "response_format": {"type": "json_object"}})["text"] == {"format": {"type": "json_object"}}


USAGE = {"input_tokens": 100, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 60}, "output_tokens": 20,
         "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 12}, "total_tokens": 120}


def test_response_conversion_text_calls_refusals_and_limits():
    resp = {"id": "resp_1", "created_at": 5, "model": "gpt-x", "status": "completed", "usage": USAGE, "output": [
        {"type": "reasoning", "summary": []},
        {"type": "message", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "hi "}, {"type": "output_text", "text": "there"}]},
        {"type": "function_call", "id": "fc_1", "call_id": "call_9", "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{}"}]}
    out = responses_to_chat_completion(resp)
    choice = out["choices"][0]
    assert out["object"] == "chat.completion" and out["id"] == "resp_1" and choice["finish_reason"] == "tool_calls"
    assert choice["message"]["content"] == "hi there" and choice["message"]["tool_calls"][0]["id"] == "call_9"
    assert out["usage"] == {"prompt_tokens": 100, "completion_tokens": 20, "total_tokens": 120,
                            "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 60}, "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 12}}
    cut = responses_to_chat_completion({"status": "incomplete", "incomplete_details": {"reason": "max_output_tokens"}, "output": []})
    assert cut["choices"][0]["finish_reason"] == "length" and cut["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] is None and "usage" not in cut
    no = responses_to_chat_completion({"status": "completed", "output": [{"type": "message", "content": [{"type": "refusal", "refusal": "no"}]}]})
    assert no["choices"][0]["message"]["refusal"] == "no" and no["choices"][0]["finish_reason"] == "stop"


def ev(d):
    return event(d, d["type"])


def test_stream_conversion_text_then_tool_call_then_usage():
    conv = ResponsesToChatStream()
    out = []
    for d in [{"type": "response.created", "response": {"id": "resp_1", "model": "gpt-x", "created_at": 5}},
              {"type": "response.reasoning_summary_text.delta", "delta": "thinking"},
              {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": "he"}, {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": "llo"},
              {"type": "response.output_item.added", "output_index": 1, "item": {"type": "function_call", "id": "fc_1", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "get_weather"}},
              {"type": "response.function_call_arguments.delta", "item_id": "fc_1", "delta": "{\"city\":"},
              {"type": "response.function_call_arguments.delta", "item_id": "fc_1", "delta": "\"Paris\"}"},
              {"type": "response.function_call_arguments.delta", "item_id": "unknown", "delta": "x"},
              {"type": "response.completed", "response": {"status": "completed", "usage": USAGE}},
              {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": "after the end"}]:
        out += conv.feed(ev(d))
    data = [e.json() for e in out if e.data != "[DONE]"]
    assert out[-1].data == "[DONE]" and all(d["id"] == "resp_1" for d in data)
    assert data[0]["choices"][0]["delta"] == {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}
    assert "".join(d["choices"][0]["delta"].get("content") or "" for d in data if d["choices"]) == "hello"
    args = "".join(tc["function"].get("arguments") or "" for d in data if d["choices"] for tc in d["choices"][0]["delta"].get("tool_calls") or [])
    assert args == "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"
    assert data[-2]["choices"][0]["finish_reason"] == "tool_calls" and data[-1]["usage"]["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"] == 60


def test_stream_errors_become_an_error_chunk():
    conv = ResponsesToChatStream()
    out = conv.feed(ev({"type": "response.failed", "response": {"error": {"message": "overloaded"}}}))
    assert out[0].json() == {"error": {"message": "overloaded", "type": "api_error"}} and out[1].data == "[DONE]"
    assert ResponsesToChatStream().feed(ev({"type": "error", "message": "bad"}))[0].json()["error"]["message"] == "bad"
    assert ResponsesToChatStream().feed(event("not json")) == []


def gateway(monkeypatch, upstream: Upstream):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MO_TEST_OAI", "key-oai")
    raw = copy.deepcopy(TEST_CONFIG)
    raw["backends"] = {"oai": {"kind": "api", "format": "openai", "base_url": "https://api.openai.example/v1", "api": "responses",
                               "max_tokens_field": "max_completion_tokens", "auth": {"type": "api_key", "value_env": "MO_TEST_OAI"}}}
    raw["models"] = {"g": {"quality": {"coding": 4, "general": 4}, "routes": [{"backend": "oai", "model": "gpt-x", "price": {"input": 1, "output": 8}}]}}
    raw["baseline_model"] = "g"
    gw = build_gateway(build_config(raw, quiet=True), store=MemoryStore(), state=MemoryState())
    gw.backends["oai"].client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(upstream))
    return gw


async def test_gateway_sends_chat_requests_to_responses_and_records_usage(monkeypatch):
    up = Upstream(httpx.Response(200, json={"id": "resp_1", "status": "completed", "model": "gpt-x", "usage": USAGE, "output": [
        {"type": "function_call", "id": "fc_1", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"}]}))
    gw = gateway(monkeypatch, up)
    r = await post(gw, {"model": "g", "max_tokens": 64, "tools": [TOOL], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "weather?"}]})
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["name"] == "get_weather"
    sent = up.body()
    assert str(up.requests[0].url).endswith("/v1/responses") and sent["max_output_tokens"] == 64 and sent["tools"][0]["strict"] is False
    assert "messages" not in sent and "max_completion_tokens" not in sent
    await gw.drain()
    row = (await gw.store.recent(1))[0]
    assert row["input_tokens"] == 40 and row["cache_read_tokens"] == 60 and row["output_tokens"] == 20


async def test_claude_code_style_stream_through_responses(monkeypatch):
    sse = "".join(f"event: {d['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(d)}\n\n" for d in [
        {"type": "response.created", "response": {"id": "resp_2", "model": "gpt-x", "created_at": 1}},
        {"type": "response.output_item.added", "output_index": 0, "item": {"type": "function_call", "id": "fc_1", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "Write"}},
        {"type": "response.function_call_arguments.delta", "item_id": "fc_1", "delta": "{\"path\":\"a.py\"}"},
        {"type": "response.completed", "response": {"status": "completed", "usage": USAGE}}]).encode()
    up = Upstream(lambda req: stream_response(sse[:40], sse[40:]))
    gw = gateway(monkeypatch, up)
    r = await post(gw, {"model": "g", "max_tokens": 64, "stream": True, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "write it"}],
                        "tools": [{"name": "Write", "description": "w", "input_schema": {"type": "object"}}]}, path="/v1/messages")
    assert r.status_code == 200 and up.body()["stream"] is True
    evs = await collect(iter_sse(chunks(r.content)))
    kinds = [e.event for e in evs]
    assert kinds[0] == "message_start" and kinds[-1] == "message_stop"
    starts = [e.json() for e in evs if e.event == "content_block_start"]
    assert starts and starts[0]["content_block"]["type"] == "tool_use" and starts[0]["content_block"]["name"] == "Write"
    assert any((e.json() or {}).get("delta", {}).get("stop_reason") == "tool_use" for e in evs)
    await gw.drain()
    assert (await gw.store.recent(1))[0]["cache_read_tokens"] == 60

# Merit Order configuration.
#
# Strings support ${ENV_VAR} and ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Secrets come from the
# environment (see .env.example), never from this file.
#
# Backends whose credentials or URLs are missing are switched off automatically,
# so this file works with whatever provider keys you have. Run `meritorder check`
# to see what is usable.
#
# PRICES are dollars per million tokens. Anthropic prices are from published
# rates on 2026-11-09; routes without a price use prices.json, which
# `meritorder prices refresh` updates from OpenRouter's catalog; AWS, Azure, and GCP set their
# own prices and you may have negotiated discounts, so verify before trusting
# the savings numbers. QUALITY scores (1-5) are starting points; tune them with
# your own evals.

# "What you'd use without Merit Order": the counterfactual for savings reports.
baseline_model: claude-sonnet

# Open-weight models, direct vendor APIs, and OpenRouter's free tier.
include:
  - models-open.yaml
  - models-embeddings.yaml

default_max_tokens: 16000

routing:
  auto_model: auto              # clients send model="auto" to let the router choose
  switch_margin_pct: 10         # only move a session if it's this much cheaper (after cache rebuild)
  est_output_tokens: 600
  # Among routes that cost about the same, the faster one wins. cost: only ties (2%); balanced: a faster
  # route may cost 20% more; speed: up to 100% more. Teams (priority:) and X-MeritOrder-Priority override it.
  priority: cost

backends:
  # Keys come from the environment (value_env). In Kubernetes you can also add
  # value_file: /run/secrets/meritorder/<NAME> so a rotated key works without a restart
  # (docs/07-deployment.md#secrets). Bedrock, Vertex, and Azure can run keyless on workload identity.
  # --- always available: in-process mocks for trying things out and for tests
  mock-anthropic:
    kind: mock
    format: anthropic
    mock_min_cache_tokens: 1024   # like Anthropic: shorter prompts aren't cached
  mock-openai:
    kind: mock
    format: openai

  # --- Anthropic Messages API family
  anthropic:
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://api.anthropic.com
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}

  bedrock:                      # Claude in Amazon Bedrock (Messages API, SigV4 or bearer token)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_BEDROCK:-true}   # false until the account can use the models (quotas, model access)
    format: anthropic
    base_url: https://bedrock-mantle.${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}.api.aws/anthropic
    anthropic_version: "2026-10-21"
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: aws_sigv4, service: bedrock-mantle, region: "${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}", profile: "${AWS_PROFILE:-}"}

  foundry-claude:               # Claude in Microsoft Foundry
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_FOUNDRY_CLAUDE:-true}   # false until the Claude deployments exist
    format: anthropic
    base_url: ${AZURE_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT}/anthropic
    forward_anthropic_beta: false
    auth: {type: api_key, header: x-api-key, value_env: AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY}

  vertex:                       # Claude on Vertex AI (needs: uv sync --extra gcp)
    enabled: false
    format: anthropic
    flavor: vertex
    project: ${GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT}
    region: global
    auth: {type: google}

  # --- OpenAI-compatible family
  azure-openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: ${AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT}/openai/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, header: api-key, value_env: AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY}
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens

  openai:
    format: openai
    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENAI_API_KEY}
    supports_prompt_cache_key: true
    max_tokens_field: max_completion_tokens
    api: responses                # GPT-5.6 and later take function tools with reasoning only on the Responses API

  openrouter:                   # one key for open-weight and Chinese models (and most others)
    format: openai
    base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
    auth: {type: api_key, value_env: OPENROUTER_API_KEY}

  local-vllm:                   # a vLLM/SGLang server you already run (always used while it's up)
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_LOCAL_VLLM:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 8.0          # per replica; used for chargeback and break-even
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 2500
    max_concurrency: 64             # vLLM --max-num-seqs (or what the KV cache fits): saturation seen within seconds
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: static
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      static_url: ${LOCAL_VLLM_URL:-http://localhost:8000/v1}
      min_replicas: 1

  gpu-qwen-coder:               # SkyPilot starts this on cloud GPUs when demand pays for it
    enabled: ${MERITORDER_SKYPILOT:-false}
    kind: self_hosted
    format: openai
    gpu_cost_per_hour: 16.0         # fallback only: with SkyPilot installed, prices come from its catalog per cloud/region/instance
    capacity_tokens_per_second: 4000
    max_concurrency: 64             # per replica; at full, requests spill to APIs or wait (max_waiting, default 32)
    cache_ttl_seconds: 600
    serve:
      provisioner: skypilot
      model: qwen3-coder-next
      accelerators: "H100:4"
      use_spot: true
      clouds: [aws, gcp, lambda]
      image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.0
      vllm_args: "--max-model-len 262144"
      max_replicas: 4
      scale_up_after_minutes: 10
      hold_minutes: 30

models:
  # --- frontier
  claude-fable:                  # Anthropic's most capable tier; priced above Opus, so `auto` only picks it when it scores higher
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-fable-*", "anthropic/claude-fable*", "fable"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 5}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-fable-5-2, price: {input: 8, output: 40, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 10}}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-fable-5-2, price: {input: 8, output: 40, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 10}}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-fable-5-2, price: {input: 8, output: 40, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 10}}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-fable-5-2, price: {input: 8, output: 40, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 10}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-fable-5.2, price: {input: 8, output: 40, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 10}}

  claude-opus:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-opus-*", "anthropic/claude-opus*", "opus"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 5}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-opus-5-5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}
      - {backend: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, price: {input: 4, output: 20, cache_read: 0.20, cache_write: 5}}

  claude-sonnet:
    effort_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
    aliases: ["claude-sonnet-*", "anthropic/claude-sonnet*", "sonnet"]
    quality: {coding: 5, general: 4}
    routes:
      - {backend: anthropic, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: bedrock, model: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: foundry-claude, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}}
      - {backend: vertex, model: claude-sonnet-5-5, price: {input: 2, output: 10, cache_read: 0.10, cache_write: 2.5}}

def reply(text="", calls=()):
    msg = {"role": "assistant", "content": text}
    if calls:
        msg["tool_calls"] = [{"id": f"c{i}", "type": "function", "function": {"name": n, "arguments": a}} for i, (n, a) in enumerate(calls)]
    return {"choices": [{"index": 0, "message": msg, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}


def gateway_of(answer):
    """A fake gateway: ``answer(body)`` returns a reply dict (or an httpx.Response)."""
    seen = []

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        seen.append(body)
        out = answer(body)
        if isinstance(out, httpx.Response):
            return out
        return httpx.Response(200, json=out, headers={"x-meritorder-cost-usd": "0.001"})
    return httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)), seen

def write_task(root, tid, **fields):
    d = root / tid
    d.mkdir(parents=True)
    files = fields.pop("files", {})
    (d / "task.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump({"id": tid, "task": "coding", "level": 3, **fields}))
    for name, text in files.items():
        (d / name).write_text(text)
    return d

               files={"prompt.md": "Write add(a, b).", "tests.py": "from solution import add\ndef test_add():\n    assert add(2, 3) == 5\n"})
    write_task(root, "g3-gen", task="general", generate="test_eval_harness:generated", generate_args={"n": 7})
    return root

class CountEnv(Env):
    """Count to a target with an `add` tool, then report the total."""

    tools = [tool("add", "Add n to the counter", {"n": {"type": "integer"}})]

    def __init__(self, sandbox=None, target=3, **args):
        super().__init__(sandbox, **args)
        self.total, self.target = 0, target

    def call(self, name, arguments):
        if not isinstance(arguments.get("n"), int):
            return json.dumps({"error": "n must be an integer"})
        self.total += arguments["n"]
        return json.dumps({"total": self.total, "padding": "x" * 30_000})

    def grade(self, final_answer):
        ok = self.total == self.target and str(self.target) in final_answer
        return ok, [] if ok else [f"total {self.total}, wanted {self.target}"]
