# 09 — Decisions

What we decided, why, and what would make us revisit it. Newest decisions go at the bottom.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Python for the core | Accepted |
| 2 | Our own backend adapters; no LiteLLM dependency | Accepted |
| 3 | No Envoy | Accepted |
| 4 | Docker Compose and Kubernetes both supported | Accepted |
| 5 | The harness owns the conversation; no content stored | Accepted |
| 6 | Route by marginal cost, including cache rebuild cost | Accepted |
| 7 | SkyPilot for GPUs, provisioning as a plugin | Accepted |
| 8 | Generic OIDC, Entra first | Accepted |
| 9 | Postgres and Redis are the only state | Accepted |
| 10 | Continuous batching only; async batch APIs out of scope | Accepted |
| 11 | AGPL-3.0-only license | Accepted |
| 12 | Reporting UI in React/TypeScript | Accepted |
| 13 | Opt-in response cache may store responses | Accepted |
| 14 | Open-weight catalog with prices from OpenRouter | Accepted |
| 15 | GPU scaling on addressable demand at API prices | Accepted |
| 16 | Deterministic, rule-based compression first | Accepted |
| 17 | Configuration versions in Postgres, YAML as the starting point | Accepted |
| 18 | Control panel in Mantine, monitoring first | Accepted |
| 19 | The IdP owns identity; Merit Order owns teams; user records decide team and role | Accepted |

## 1. Python for the core

**Why:** The team prefers it, the ML and inference ecosystem (SkyPilot, vLLM, classifiers,
compression) is Python, and gateway overhead is a few milliseconds against model latency measured
in seconds. We scale by running more gateway copies.

**Revisit if:** a real deployment hits gateway CPU limits that more replicas can't fix.

## 2. Our own backend adapters; no LiteLLM dependency

**Why:**
- LiteLLM converts everything to the OpenAI format internally. That's lossy for `cache_control`,
  thinking signatures, and other provider fields, and prompt caching is our biggest savings lever.
- It has had supply-chain incidents, a large dependency tree, and SSO in a commercially licensed
  directory.
- The rest of what it offers (keys, budgets, spend tracking, routing, UI) we'd replace anyway,
  because our ledger, router, and reporting work differently.
- Almost every backend speaks the Anthropic or OpenAI format, so pass-through plus one pair of
  translators covers them in a few thousand lines we fully control.

**What we still take:** LiteLLM's MIT-licensed pricing data, copied in with attribution, and its
code as a reference for provider quirks. Anyone needing a niche provider can run LiteLLM themselves
as an OpenAI-compatible backend.

**Revisit if:** keeping our adapters current with provider API changes becomes a significant
ongoing burden.

## 3. No Envoy

**Why:** Envoy AI Gateway is strong as a proxy layer, but all of our product logic (routing,
shaping, sessions, budgets, ledger) would still be Python, called by Envoy over gRPC on every
request. That adds a second system to operate and debug, assumes Kubernetes, narrows the
contributor pool, and solves a performance problem we don't have. Merit Order runs behind whatever
load balancer or ingress an organization already uses.

**Revisit if:** large deployments ask for it. The routing and shaping code could be packaged as an
Envoy external-processing service without being rewritten. Separately, an optional plugin could use
Kubernetes inference-routing tools (llm-d) inside a customer's own GPU cluster.

## 4. Docker Compose and Kubernetes both supported

**Why:** Compose gives the clone-and-run experience an open-source project needs; Kubernetes is
what enterprises at our target spend run in production. Same images, no Kubernetes-specific code in
the app. Details in [07 — Deployment](07-deployment.md).

## 5. The harness owns the conversation; no content stored

**Why:** Harnesses already resend history and compact it. Storing conversations would make the
proxy a retention, eDiscovery, and breach liability. The gateway stores routing metadata (hashes,
timestamps, backends) only. Compression stays cache-safe through a content-hash map, not stored
conversations.

**Revisit if:** we add the OpenAI Responses API's stored mode, which would be opt-in with explicit
retention.

## 6. Route by marginal cost, including cache rebuild cost

**Why:** A running GPU's spare capacity is already paid for, so it's nearly free, even for a better
model than the task needs. Moving a session re-pays for its whole context, so the router counts that
before moving. Details in [03 — Routing](03-routing.md).

## 7. SkyPilot for GPUs, provisioning as a plugin

**Why:** SkyPilot handles multi-cloud GPUs, spot instances, and replica scaling (SkyServe), and can
target Kubernetes clusters. Our controller decides *whether* to run a model; SkyPilot handles *how*.
A Kubernetes-native option (llm-d or KServe) can be another plugin later.

## 8. Generic OIDC, Entra first

**Why:** Entra is the first customer need; Google and others are configuration on the same code
path. Harnesses get short-lived virtual keys via a device-code login.

## 9. Postgres and Redis are the only state

**Why:** Both are available as managed services everywhere and are easy to run in Compose.
ClickHouse may become an optional reporting backend for very large deployments.

## 10. Continuous batching only; async batch APIs out of scope

**Why:** The product is for day-to-day interactive use. vLLM/SGLang batch concurrent requests on
their own. Provider batch APIs (about 50% off for work that can wait hours) may come later.

## 11. AGPL-3.0-only license

**Why:** Changes that others are offered over a network come back to the project.

## 12. Reporting UI in React/TypeScript

**Why:** Interactive filters and charts are much easier to build well, and the UI only talks to the
reports API, so it stays replaceable. The rest of the project remains Python.

**Alternative considered:** server-rendered pages with htmx (all-Python, clunkier interactivity).

## 13. Opt-in response cache may store responses

**Why:** Exact-match caching saves real money for chatbots, RAG, and evals. It can't work without
keeping the response, so it's the one exception to decision 5: off by default, enabled per team or
per request, scoped to a team or user, and expired by TTL (Redis).

## 14. Open-weight catalog with prices from OpenRouter

**Why:** There are dozens of useful open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, MiMo,
Mistral, Gemma, Nemotron, Muse, gpt-oss) and their prices change often. `config/models-open.yaml`
lists them with their Hugging Face IDs (needed for self-hosting); `meritorder prices refresh` pulls
current prices and context windows from OpenRouter's public catalog into `prices.json`. A route with
no known price is never chosen by `auto`, so a missing price can't look free. OpenRouter is one
backend among many, not the system: it adds a fee, sends prompts through another company, and
doesn't count toward cloud commitments.

## 15. GPU scaling on addressable demand at API prices

**Why:** Counting only traffic already served by a model means a stopped model never looks worth
starting. The controller counts what all traffic the model *could* serve costs at API-equivalent
prices, excluding free upgrades. That number doesn't fall when GPUs take over the traffic, so it
doesn't flap. Two self-hosted models that address the same traffic are each credited with it; the
router then splits the traffic. Revisit if that over-provisions in practice.

## 16. Deterministic, rule-based compression first

**Why:** Compression must give identical output every turn or it breaks provider caching (and, on
recent Claude models, edited history can invalidate thinking). Rules (strip ANSI codes, collapse
repeated lines, keep head and tail of huge outputs) are deterministic, need no stored state, and add
no ML dependency. A model-based compressor (LLMLingua-2) can come later behind a content-hash cache.

## 17. Configuration versions in Postgres, YAML as the starting point

**Why:** Containers mount config read-only, and a fleet of gateways needs one source of truth. Saving
from the console validates the document, stores it as a new version (who, when, why), and every
gateway hot-reloads it within seconds; in-flight requests finish on the objects they started with.
Restore is one click. The YAML file is used until the first version is saved, and stays the format
for import, export, and GitOps. Secrets never enter the database: literal keys are refused and must
stay `${ENV}` references.

## 18. Control panel in Mantine, monitoring first

**Why:** Anyone running a company's LLM traffic through Merit Order will watch it far more than
they reconfigure it. The console opens on a live Dispatch view (the merit-order stack from real
traffic, a live request feed, backend health, the GPU fleet, and what needs attention), with
configuration one page among several. Mantine gives a complete admin component set with few
dependencies; charts stay hand-written SVG.

## 19. The IdP owns identity; Merit Order owns teams; user records decide team and role

**Why:** Enterprises expect Entra to be the source of truth for who exists and which groups they're
in, but budgets and model policy belong to Merit Order. People are created at first sign-in, their
team and role come from mapped groups, and admins can pin exceptions. Each request resolves team and
role from the user record (cached for a minute), not from the key, so moves and disables apply to
existing keys. **Next:** SCIM provisioning for immediate deprovisioning.

"""Hidden tests for c5-regex. Expected values were computed with Python's re (re.ASCII)."""

from solution import findall, fullmatch, search, sub


def S(p, t):
    m = search(p, t)
    return None if m is None else (m.span(), tuple(m.span(i) for i in range(1, len(m.groups()) + 1)))


def F(p, t):
    m = fullmatch(p, t)
    return None if m is None else (m.span(), tuple(m.span(i) for i in range(1, len(m.groups()) + 1)))


def G(p, t):
    m = search(p, t)
    return None if m is None else (m.group(), m.groups())


def FG(p, t):
    m = fullmatch(p, t)
    return None if m is None else (m.group(), m.groups())


def invalid(p):
    """Every entry point must reject the pattern with ValueError, even on empty text."""
    for call in (lambda: search(p, ""), lambda: fullmatch(p, ""), lambda: findall(p, "abc"), lambda: sub(p, "x", "")):
        try:
            call()
        except ValueError:
            continue
        return False
    return True


def test_literals_and_leftmost():
    assert S('abc', 'xxabcx') == ((2, 5), ())
    assert S('abc', 'ababab') is None
    assert S('A', 'a') is None
    assert S('é+', 'xééa') == ((1, 3), ())
    assert S('', 'abc') == ((0, 0), ())
    assert S('b+|a', 'cab') == ((1, 2), ())
    assert S('c|ab', 'xabc') == ((1, 3), ())
    assert G('x*', 'abc') == ('', ())

    assert F('.*\n.', 'ab\nc') == ((0, 4), ())
    assert S('...', 'a\nbcd') == ((2, 5), ())

# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports. Unknown, revoked, or expired keys get a 401. | Client | Auth | |---|---| | People with harnesses | `meritorder login` → virtual key (above) | | Services / apps | An Entra token directly as the bearer token, or a key from `meritorder keys create` | | Local dev / quickstart | `MERITORDER_DEV_KEY` (static admin key from the environment) | | Google (later) | Another OIDC issuer: same code path | Entra login switches on when `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` are set; map Entra group IDs to teams and roles in `auth.oidc` in the config. SCIM (later) revokes keys when people leave. ## People and teams | What | Where it's managed | |---|---| | Who exists, and their group membership | Your identity provider (Entra). People are created in Merit Order the first time they sign in with `meritorder login` (or when an admin issues them a key). | | Teams, with budgets, limits, and model policy | Merit Order: Config → Teams. An IdP has no notion of "$5,000 a month, these models only". | | Which team and role someone gets | Entra groups mapped to teams and roles in Config → Access, re-read at each sign-in. | | Exceptions | The People page: an admin can move someone, change their role (that pins it, so later sign-ins don't override it), let Entra decide again, or disable them. | The user record, not the key, decides a person's team and role. Moving or disabling someone takes effect within a minute on every gateway, including keys they already have. **SCIM provisioning** (`/scim/v2`, enabled by `MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN`): Entra pushes people and group changes as they happen. Group membership recomputes team and role with the same mappings as sign-in, and anyone deactivated or removed in Entra is disabled immediately (spend history is kept). Setup: Entra → Enterprise applications → your app → Provisioning → Automatic; Tenant URL `https:///scim/v2`, Secret token = `MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN`. ## Budgets ```mermaid flowchart TD ORG["Org budget
$/month"] --> T1["Team: platform
$/month"] ORG --> T2["Team: data-science
$/month"] T1 --> U1["User budget"] T1 --> U2["User budget"] T2 --> U3["User budget"] U1 --> K1["Key"] U1 --> K2["Key"] ``` - A request must fit **every** level above it: organization, team, and person. - Spend is checked before a request is sent and counted when it finishes (Redis counters seeded from the Postgres ledger, which stays the source of truth). - Alerts go out at 80% and 100%; at 100% requests are refused with a 429 that says which budget was reached. - Policy lives alongside budgets: allowed models, allowed providers, data residency (e.g. "DeepSeek weights only self-hosted or on Bedrock, never the vendor API"). ## Limits that stop runaway spend | Setting (per team) | What it does | |---|---| | `budget_usd_month`, `user_budget_usd_month` | Monthly caps; requests are refused at 100% (alerts at 80%) | | `max_session_usd` | Stops one session (typically an agent stuck in a loop) once it has spent this much | | `rate_limits: {user_rpm, user_tpm, team_rpm, team_tpm}` | Requests and prompt tokens per minute; 429 with `Retry-After` | ## Organization-wide safeguards Hard limits for everyone, set under `safeguards:` or on the console's **Controls** page (which shows each one next to this month's spend and the pace it's on, and saves changes as a new config version): | Setting | What it does | |---|---| | `org_budget_usd_month` | All spend in the ledger. At 100% every request is refused until the month ends or it's raised | | `gpu_budget_usd_month` | GPU time (replicas × hourly price). At 100% running GPUs drain and none start, pins included | | `max_gpu_usd_per_hour` | Burn-rate cap for the whole GPU fleet; deployments whose demand best covers their cost get capacity first | | `max_gpu_replicas` | Replica cap across all deployments | | `max_request_usd` | Worst case per request (context × input price + `max_tokens` × output price). Cheaper candidates are used instead; if none fit, the request is refused with what it would have cost | | `alert_at` | Fractions of the org and GPU budgets that send alerts (default 80% and 100%) | GPUs can also be stopped, pinned, or stopped all at once from the console; see [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md#controls-and-safeguards). ## What gets charged | Backend | Charged to the user's budget | |---|---| | API | Actual provider cost (cached / uncached / output tokens) | | Self-hosted | Chargeback: GPU-hour cost split by tokens served (so it's fair, not $0) | Budgets use chargeback; the router uses marginal cost. They answer different questions. ## The savings ledger One row per request, written async: | Field | Example | |---|---| | user, team, session | | | model requested / floor / served | `auto` / `coding:3` / `qwen3-coder-480b` | | backend | `self/qwen3-coder/replica-2` | | tokens: uncached in / cached in / out | 2,100 / 118,000 / 640 | | **actual marginal cost** | $0.0004 | | **chargeback cost** | $0.0090 | | **counterfactual cost** (floor model on API, no proxy caching) | $0.3700 | | upgraded for free? | yes | This is the dashboard that sells the project: *"$X spent, $Y avoided, Z% of requests upgraded at no cost."* How savings are calculated and reported is in [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md).

"""Background jobs: monthly ledger partitions and hourly rollups for reports."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import os
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from .alerts import check_budgets, check_spikes, weekly_digest
from .config import Config, load_config
from .state import make_state
from .store import make_store

log = logging.getLogger("meritorder.worker")


async def run_worker(once: bool = False, interval: int = 60, cfg: Config | None = None, backfill: bool = False) -> None:
    store = make_store(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL"))
    if store.kind != "postgres":
        raise SystemExit("the worker needs Postgres: set MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL")
    state = make_state(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_REDIS_URL"))
    cfg = cfg or load_config()
    await store.init()
    try:
        while True:
            try:
                await store.ensure_partitions()
                rows = await store.rollup(full=backfill)
                backfill = False
                log.info("rollup refreshed %d hourly rows", rows)
                await check_budgets(cfg, store, state)
                await check_spikes(store, state)
                now = datetime.now(UTC)
                if now.weekday() == 0 and now.hour >= 9:  # Monday morning, once per week
                    await weekly_digest(cfg, store, state, now)
            except Exception:
                log.exception("worker cycle failed")
            if once:
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)
    finally:
        await store.close()
        await state.close()

#
# Each model lists where it can be served today. Prices for OpenRouter routes come
# from prices.json (`meritorder prices refresh`); a route with no known price is
# only used when a client asks for that model by name, never by `auto`.
#
# hf_id is the Hugging Face repository: what the GPU tier serves when it decides
# self-hosting a model is cheaper than paying per token.
#
# quality (1-5) values are starting points. Tune them with evals on your own work.

backends:
  # Direct vendor APIs (OpenAI-compatible). Switched off until their key is set.
  # Vendor model IDs differ from OpenRouter's; run `meritorder models discover`
  # once a key is set, then add routes such as:

  deepseek:
    format: openai
    base_url: https://api.deepseek.com/v1

  mistral:
    format: openai

"""Backend adapters: pass-through first, translation only when formats differ."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

from ..config import Config
from .auth import make_auth
from .base import Backend, BackendError, UpstreamResponse
from .http import AnthropicBackend, OpenAIBackend
from .mock import MockBackend

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

__all__ = ["Backend", "BackendError", "UpstreamResponse", "build_backends"]


def build_backends(cfg: Config) -> dict[str, Backend]:
    out: dict[str, Backend] = {}
    for bc in cfg.backends:
        if not bc.enabled:
            continue
        if bc.kind == "mock":
            out[bc.name] = MockBackend(bc)
            continue
        try:
            auth = make_auth(bc.auth)
        except ImportError as e:
            log.warning("backend %s disabled: missing optional dependency (%s)", bc.name, e)
            bc.enabled = False
            bc.disabled_reason = f"missing optional dependency ({e})"
            continue
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("backend %s disabled: credentials unavailable (%s)", bc.name, e)
            bc.enabled = False
            bc.disabled_reason = f"credentials unavailable ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"[:200]
            continue
        if not auth.available():
            log.info("backend %s disabled: no credentials found", bc.name)
            bc.enabled = False
            bc.disabled_reason = "no credentials found"
            continue
        out[bc.name] = AnthropicBackend(bc, auth) if bc.format == "anthropic" else OpenAIBackend(bc, auth)
    return out

# 00 — How it all works (start here) Merit Order sits between your tools and the model providers. Your tools keep speaking the API they already speak; Merit Order translates when the chosen model speaks another. For every request sent with the model name `auto`, it asks two questions: 1. **How hard is this?** The request gets a **level** for its kind of work: coding or general, 1 to 5. 2. **What's the cheapest model that's good enough?** Every model has a **score** for each kind of work, 1 to 5. Models scoring at least the level, with room for the conversation, qualify, and the cheapest of those wins, counting the whole rest of the conversation, not just this request. Everything else in this document is detail on those two questions: how tools connect, where the levels, scores and prices come from, what "cheapest" really means, how long conversations are handled, what happens when something fails, and when your own GPUs are worth switching on. The numbers are from the live configuration on 11 November 2026; prices and scores refresh on their own, so yours will drift. A request that **names a model** (`claude-opus`, `gpt-sol`, …) skips both questions: it always gets that model, and Merit Order only chooses where to run it (section 10). ```mermaid flowchart LR T["Your tool
(any API format)"] --> R["Request
model: auto"] R --> L["2. Level
coding:3"] L --> Q["3–4. Models scoring ≥ 3,
with room, allowed for the team"] Q --> C["5. Cheapest for the rest
of the session"] C --> E["6. Effort and output limit
for that level"] E --> S["Send, translated if needed;
on failure, the next cheapest (8)"] ``` ## 1. Your tools connect as they are Point a tool's base URL at Merit Order and give it a Merit Order key. Nothing else about the tool changes, because Merit Order speaks both common APIs: | Your tool speaks | For example | Merit Order endpoint | |---|---|---| | Anthropic Messages | Claude Code, Anthropic SDKs | `/v1/messages` (and `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) | | OpenAI Chat Completions | pi, Cursor, OpenAI SDKs, most other tools | `/v1/chat/completions` | | OpenAI Responses | Codex CLI | `/v1/responses` | | Embeddings | RAG pipelines | `/v1/embeddings` | **The model's own format is Merit Order's problem, not the tool's.** Each provider speaks one of the two formats. When the tool and the chosen provider speak the same one, the request passes through untouched, so provider features such as Claude's cache markers and thinking signatures survive. When they differ, Merit Order converts the request, the reply and the stream both ways: messages, tool calls, images, streaming, usage and stop reasons. Two things don't cross: a model's reasoning from earlier turns (each turn still works; the model just thinks again), and `temperature`/`top_p`, which current Claude models reject. The Responses API is converted to Chat Completions inside the gateway; GPT models that need the Responses API for tools with reasoning are converted on the way out. **The model name says what you want:** - `auto`: Merit Order chooses (the rest of this document). - A model's name or one of its aliases: that model. Aliases cover the names tools already send, so `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` and `sonnet` all mean Claude Sonnet. - Anything else: an error saying the model isn't configured. `GET /v1/models` lists `auto` and every model your team may use, with each one's context window. **Every reply says what happened**, in headers: `X-MeritOrder-Model` (the model that answered), `X-MeritOrder-Backend` (the provider), `X-MeritOrder-Floor` (the level, for `auto`), `X-MeritOrder-Max-Tokens` and its source, `X-MeritOrder-Failed-Over` when a provider failed first, and for replies that aren't streamed `X-MeritOrder-Cost-Usd`. The console's Reports → Requests tab shows the model, provider, level and cost of every request. Setting up Claude Code and pi is in section 11. ## 2. Every request gets a level The level is how demanding the request is. It's worked out from the request itself, with simple rules and no model call, so it's instant and free: | The request | Level | |---|---| | Plain text, short (under ~400 tokens), no tools | general 1 | | Plain text | general 2 | | Plain text with words like analyze, compare, plan, strategy, trade-offs, evaluate or reason, or over 20,000 tokens long | general 3 | | Any tools, or text that looks like code (code fences, `def`, `import`, stack traces, file names, "refactor", "bug", SQL, …) | coding 3 | | 5 or more tools: an agent at work | coding 4 | | Coding with "hard" wording (architecture, race condition, security, performance, migration, concurrency, …) or over 60,000 tokens of context | one level higher, at most 5 | Clients can take over: `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` sets the level exactly, and `X-Route-Hint: cheap` or `smart` moves it one level down or up. Every `auto` response says what it got (`X-MeritOrder-Floor`). What that means in practice: | Request | Level | |---|---| | "What's the capital of Portugal?" | general 1 | | "Draft a reply to this customer email" (pasted) | general 2 | | "Compare these three vendor proposals" | general 3 | | "Why does this function return None?" with a code block | coding 3 | | A coding agent's turn: 20 tools, 30,000 tokens of conversation | coding 4 | | The same agent, 90,000 tokens into the session | coding 5 | **Claude Code's side jobs get lower levels.** Claude Code labels each request (when its hint headers are on; section 11): a turn of the conversation, a subagent's turn, the summary it writes when it compacts a long conversation, or a side request such as a session title or summary. Those last two don't need the level of the work itself, so `auto` caps them: | Claude Code request | Highest level | |---|---| | Side request (titles, summaries) | 1 | | Compaction summary | 3 | | Conversation or subagent turn | not capped | An explicit `X-Route-Floor` is never capped. Auto mode's permission checks name Claude Sonnet, so they never go through `auto` at all. The caps are under Config → Routing → Claude Code request types. The level rules themselves live in code (`src/meritorder/classifier.py`); the console doesn't show or change them yet. ## 3. Every model gets a score for each kind of work A score says how good a model is at a kind of work, **compared with the best model you have**. It isn't typed in: the worker works it out once a day from published benchmarks. **What a score means.** By default (source `epoch`), each model's score is based on its chance of solving a task as hard as **FrontierSWE**, a set of real, hard software-engineering tasks. The best model scores 5 and every other model scores in proportion: one that solves 60% as many such tasks as the best scores 3. | Model | Chance on a FrontierSWE-hard task (coding) | Coding score | General score | |---|---|---|---| | Claude Fable 5.2 | 70% | 5.0 | 5.0 | | Gemini 4 Carbon | 61% | 4.4 | 4.3 | | GPT-6.1 Terra | 58% | 4.2 * | 3.8 | | GPT-6 Astra | 58% | 4.1 | 4.1 | | Claude Opus 5.5 | 57% | 4.1 | 4.0 | | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 55% | 3.9 | 3.5 | | Gemini 4 Argon | 47% | 3.4 | 3.5 | | GPT-6.1 Sol | 44% | 3.2 | 4.0 | | Claude Haiku 5.5 | 41% | 3.0 † | 2.1 | | GPT-6 Luna | 31% | 2.3 | 1.3 | | Gemini 3.8 Flash | 24% | 1.7 | 1.7 | | Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite | 5% | 1.0 * | 1.0 | \* Estimated from the model's general ability: no coding results published yet. † Set by hand (`quality_override`). Epoch's refit of 12 November 2026 put it at 2.9, just under level 3, which would send ordinary coding to GPT-6.1 Terra at about ten times the price; our own coding evals had it pass 14 of 15 hard tasks. **Where the numbers come from.** [Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/benchmarks) (CC BY 4.0) places every model on one ability scale, fitted across about 40 benchmarks, and every benchmark on the same scale by difficulty. That's what makes models comparable even when they were tested on different benchmarks, and lets a model's ability be turned into a chance of solving tasks of a given difficulty. For coding, a model's own results on FrontierSWE and FrontierCode refine its general ability, so coding strength counts; results at the effort `auto` uses for hard work are preferred where published. A model with neither those results nor a place on the scale (some open models) gets its coding score from older coding benchmarks (Terminal Bench, GSO, MirrorCode); they come last because they predict FrontierSWE results less well than the scale does. The alternative source is the [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai) Intelligence Index (needs `ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY`). It's a single number per model, so coding and general get the same score. The third option is scores written on each model by hand (`config`), for example from your own eval runs ([11 — Evals](11-evals.md)). **Two choices shape the scores** (Config → Routing → Quality scores): - **Scale.** `best` (default): the best model is 5 and the rest in proportion; adding a weak model changes nobody else's score. `range`: the weakest model with data is 1 and the best 5, which depends on which weak models you happen to have configured. - **Reference task.** A harder reference spreads models further apart and sends more work up the ladder. Against Remote Labor Index (real paid remote work, which Fable solves 37% of the time), Opus would score 2.8 for general work, and ordinary level-3 work would go only to Fable. FrontierSWE keeps level 3 within reach of models like Sonnet. **Models the source doesn't cover** aren't picked by `auto`: a score nobody measured would compete with measured ones, and because the cheapest qualifying model wins, an optimistic guess would win. They still answer requests that name them. To put one back, give it a `quality_override` (Config → Models), which always wins over the source; that's also how to record that your own evals disagree with the benchmarks (Models → Evals → *Apply scores…* → *Write as override*). Measured scores use the same 1–5 scale, so the Evals page shows them beside the ones in use. On 11 November 2026, 10 open models weren't covered, among them Qwen3 Coder Next, Devstral and MiMo (Qwen3 Coder has a 1.0 for coding, from older coding benchmarks). Hover a score on the Models page to see how it was worked out. ## 4. Which models qualify A model qualifies for a request when: - its score for that kind of work is **at least the request's level**. A level-3 coding request can go to any model with a coding score of 3.0 or more; level 5 means "as good as the best", which today is only Fable; - the conversation **fits in its context window** (section 7); and - the team is allowed to use it (Config → Teams → allowed models and backends). ## 5. The cheapest qualifying route wins Each qualifying model has one or more **routes**: the providers that serve it (Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, your own GPUs, …). Merit Order prices every route and picks the cheapest. **Prices are live.** The worker refreshes them every 15 minutes: OpenRouter routes from OpenRouter's catalog, direct provider APIs from the price list LiteLLM maintains, cross-checked against each other. Long-prompt prices apply (Claude Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much above 100,000 prompt tokens), and a price change, a list that can't be fetched, or two lists that disagree raises an alert. **"Cheapest" means the rest of the session**, because in a conversation each turn resends everything before it, and providers charge far less for the part they still have cached: ``` cost of a route = rebuild + expected turns × cost per turn rebuild = what it costs to get this conversation into the provider's cache: zero if this provider already holds it, else the context at the full input price (or the cache-write price, for Claude, where caching is explicit), less the cache-read price the first turn already counts cost per turn = the cached part at the cache-read price + the new tokens at the input price (cache-write price for Claude): what the conversation grew by since its last turn, or about 2,000 for a new session + about 600 output tokens at the output price expected turns = the turns so far, kept between 3 and 30 (a long session will probably keep going) ``` Here's what that gives for a new coding session at level 3, 30,000 tokens in: | Model (route) | Score | Rebuild | Per turn | 3 turns | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Haiku 5.5 (Anthropic)** | 3.0 | $0.003 | $0.0008 | **$0.006** | | GPT-6.1 Terra (Azure) | 4.2 | $0.027 | $0.006 | $0.046 | | Gemini 4 Argon (OpenRouter) | 3.4 | $0.053 | $0.013 | $0.092 | | GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI) | 3.2 | $0.053 | $0.013 | $0.092 | And for an agent at level 4, 80,000 tokens in: | Model (route) | Score | Rebuild | Per turn | 3 turns | |---|---|---|---|---| | **GPT-6.1 Terra (Azure)** | 4.2 | $0.074 | $0.009 | **$0.101** | | Gemini 4 Carbon (OpenRouter) | 4.4 | $0.148 | $0.018 | $0.202 | | Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) | 4.1 | $0.374 | $0.038 | $0.487 | **Sessions stay put.** Once a session is on a route, the rebuild is already paid there, so moving it must save at least 10% plus $0.01 over the rest of the session. Within a task (while the tool is sending tool results back, before the next prompt from a person) the session keeps its model outright. In practice a session moves only when a new task starts and something is clearly cheaper, its cache has expired (after 5 idle minutes), the conversation was compacted, it no longer fits (section 7), or its model is busy or down on every route (section 8). That's what keeps a session from bouncing between Bedrock and Anthropic and paying to rebuild each time. **A session can hold several conversations.** Claude Code sends its subagents' turns and its side requests under the main session's id. Each keeps its own routing state (model, level, cache), so a subagent never resets the main conversation's; budgets, the per-session spend limit and reports still count the session as one. **Near-ties go to speed.** The same model often costs the same everywhere (Claude on Anthropic, Bedrock and Vertex), so price alone can't choose. Routes within a small margin of the cheapest compete on measured speed: 2% under the default `cost` priority (where a better model among them goes first), 20% under `balanced`, 100% under `speed`. A team or a single request (`X-MeritOrder-Priority`) can choose differently. Every 10th new session may try a route within that margin whose speed is unknown or out of date, so speeds stay known. **Unpriced routes never win** for `auto`: an unknown price must never look free. ## 6. Then: effort and output length **Reasoning effort** follows the level, so every model works the same way for the same work (their own defaults differ): low for levels 1–2, medium for 3, high for 4–5. A model that doesn't take that effort keeps its default. The effort is set once per session on a model, because changing it would invalidate the prompt cache. A client's own effort setting always wins; one sent in Anthropic's format (Claude Code sends one) to a GPT or other OpenAI-format model goes over at the nearest level that model takes. **Output length** isn't capped by a guess. A request without `max_tokens` may write as much as the model can (128,000 tokens for current Claude and GPT models), less what wouldn't fit in the context window, under the per-request cost limit (Controls), or within what a provider's prepaid balance covers. A client's own `max_tokens` is kept (lowered only to the model's maximum). The response says how much it got and why (`X-MeritOrder-Max-Tokens`, `X-MeritOrder-Max-Tokens-Source`). ## 7. Context windows: long conversations Every model has a **context window**: the most a conversation plus its reply can hold. The windows come from the live price data, refreshed with the prices: | Window | Models | |---|---| | about 1 million tokens | Claude (all), Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, MiMo, Muse Spark, Mistral Large 4, Qwen3.8 Flash, Nemotron 3.5 Super | | 922,000 | GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 (Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna) | | 524,288 | Llama 4 Maverick | | 500,000 | Grok 4.7 | | 262,144 | Qwen3 Coder (all three), Devstral 2, Mistral Small 4, Ministral 14B, Gemma 4 31B, Nemotron 3 Ultra | | 131,072 | gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b | Two parties decide what happens as a conversation grows: **the tool**, which decides when to compact (summarize the history and start over from the summary), and **Merit Order**, which decides where the conversation can still go. **What Merit Order does:** - **Models without room drop out.** For `auto`, a model whose window the conversation fills past 95% isn't a candidate (the token count is estimated at about 4 characters per token, and the reply needs room too). A 300,000-token conversation never goes to gpt-oss or Qwen3 Coder; most qualifying models have about a million tokens, so something always fits. - **A session that outgrows its model moves, even mid-task.** The next turn goes to a model with room at the same level, paying once to rebuild the cache there. - **A provider that says "too long" isn't the end.** If a provider refuses a prompt as too long anyway (the estimate can be off), an `auto` request goes to a qualifying model with a bigger window. A request that names a model can't move; its error is worded the way Anthropic's API words it ("prompt is too long: …"), whichever provider refused, because that's what makes Claude Code compact. - **The reply shrinks to fit.** When a request doesn't set `max_tokens`, the reply may use what's left of the window and no more, so the provider doesn't refuse prompt plus reply (section 6). **What the tool does.** A tool compacts when the conversation nears the window it believes it has. `/v1/models` reports each model's window, and for `auto` the largest window among the models `auto` can pick for your team (1,048,576 tokens today). That's safe because models without room drop out: a long conversation narrows the choice to the million-token models instead of failing. - **pi**: `meritorder setup pi` writes each model's window into pi's model list. - **Claude Code**: it knows the windows of Claude models by name. For a name it doesn't know, such as `auto`, it assumes 200,000 tokens unless told otherwise; `meritorder setup claude-code` tells it the gateway's window (section 11). - **Other tools**: give them the window from `/v1/models`, or leave their default; a smaller window than the real one only means compacting earlier. ## 8. When something fails Nothing reaches the client until the chosen route has started answering, so a failure moves the request on: - **Over capacity, rate-limited, missing, or down:** the next route in the cost ranking. For a named model, or a session in the middle of a task, that's another provider for the same model; for a new `auto` task, it's the next cheapest qualifying route, whatever its model. A request gets 3 tries at most (`routing.max_attempts`). An `auto` session whose model is busy or down on every route moves to another qualifying model at its next turn, even mid-task. The failing route is skipped for a while (the provider's `Retry-After`, or a growing back-off) and an alert says where its traffic went. - **Too long for the model:** for `auto`, a qualifying model with a bigger window (section 7). - **The model refuses:** for `auto`, the next qualifying model (the refusal is billed and logged); a named model's refusal is returned as it is. - **A provider can't cover the whole reply on its prepaid balance:** the same route again, asking for what it says it can pay for. - **Budgets and limits:** organization, team, person and session budgets, rate limits, and the per-request cost limit stop requests before they're sent, with a message saying which. Every rule and timing is in [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md). ## 9. Your own GPUs: when they start and stop Power grids run the cheapest generators all the time (baseload) and switch on expensive ones (peakers) only for peaks. Merit Order does the same: your own GPUs, running an open model, are the baseload when there's enough steady work to keep them busy, and the APIs are the peakers that are always there. **A GPU deployment starts only when sustained demand pays for it.** Every minute the controller asks: what does the traffic this model could serve cost me at API prices? - **Traffic it could serve** means requests whose level its score covers. A model with a coding score of 3.0 counts every coding request at levels 1–3, wherever it was actually sent. - **At API prices** means what you're paying for that traffic today. - One replica is worth starting when that spend, per hour, exceeds the replica's hourly price plus a 20% margin, **continuously for 10 minutes**. The number of replicas follows the throughput (enough to run at 70% load), as long as each one pays for itself by the same rule. For example, Qwen3 Coder Next on four H100s costs about $16 an hour per replica (SkyPilot's cheapest offer in the allowed clouds, or the configured fallback). It starts once the work it could do would cost you more than $19.20 an hour at API prices for 10 minutes straight. **While it runs, it's the first choice.** A GPU you're already paying for costs almost nothing per token while it has room, so the router prices it at 2% of the API price up to 60% load, rising to the full API price as it fills. Up to that point it wins every request it qualifies for; past it, the APIs take over, and at 100% new work spills to them. Requests that only went to the GPU because it had room (a better model than the level needed) don't count as demand, so idle capacity can't keep itself alive. **It stops when demand no longer pays for it.** When the work it could do drops below break-even for 10 minutes, and it has been running at least 30 minutes, it **drains**: no new sessions, existing ones finish, and after 15 minutes the GPUs are released. If demand comes back while draining, it simply stays. Starting takes 10–20 minutes for a big model, and traffic stays on the APIs meanwhile, so the delays and margins are there to avoid paying for start-ups that don't last. **A self-hosted model needs a score.** Demand is counted by level, so a model the quality source doesn't cover has none, and its GPUs never start for `auto` traffic. On 11 November 2026 that's the case for Qwen3 Coder Next: give it a `quality_override` (Config → Models) to have the controller consider it. Its window (262,144 tokens) also means conversations longer than about 249,000 tokens go to the APIs. **Whether a GPU can ever pay** shows on Models → **GPU break-even**. Each open-weight model gets a machine whose GPUs hold its weights (sizes from Hugging Face), priced from SkyPilot's catalog, spot or on-demand, across the clouds SkyPilot covers: of those, the one that pays from the least traffic. The weights can be served as published, in FP8, or in 4 bits; quantizing changes what fits, not the quality scores, so measure a quantized model with an eval before trusting its level. For each quality level and each model it shows the traffic one replica needs (tokens per minute and about how many requests an hour), your busiest hour of that traffic, and what the replica can serve. The price a GPU has to beat at a level is the cheapest API model good enough for it, because that's where `auto` would send the work otherwise. On 11 November 2026, with spot prices, only level-1 work could pay: gpt-oss-20b on one L4 ($0.12 an hour) from about 72,000 tokens a minute. The best level an open model could host was 2: Kimi K3.1 (coding 2.7), published in 4 bits, fits on eight B300s. Level 3 starts at Claude Haiku's 3.0, and quantizing doesn't change that, because the strongest open models already ship in 4 bits. *Get latest prices* has SkyPilot download its catalogs again. Admins can also stop a deployment (draining first or at once), pin a number of replicas, stop all GPUs, or cap GPU spend per month, per hour, or in replicas (GPUs page and Controls). Details: [05 — GPU autoscaling](05-gpu-autoscaling.md). ## 10. Requests that name a model A request for `claude-opus` gets Claude Opus, never another model. Merit Order still picks the route: the cheapest of Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and OpenRouter for the rest of the session, with the same stickiness, speed tie-breaks and failover between them. If none of its routes can run, the request fails with the reason for each, unless the team allows substituting a model at least as good. A named model is never skipped for its window: a conversation it can't hold gets the provider's error, worded so Claude Code compacts. Claude Code sends Claude model names unless it's set to `auto`, so by default it gets exactly what it asks for; `meritorder setup claude-code` sets it to `auto` (section 11). ## 11. Setting up Claude Code and pi Log in once (`meritorder login`, or `meritorder use-key` with a key from an admin), then: ```bash meritorder setup claude-code # Claude Code meritorder setup pi # pi ``` **Claude Code** isn't tied to Anthropic or Foundry: any gateway that speaks Anthropic's API can stand in via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and Merit Order does. The setup command writes these into Claude Code's settings file (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json`, or `~/.claude/settings.json`): | Setting | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | the gateway | Send every request to Merit Order | | `apiKeyHelper` | reads `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` | Your Merit Order key; logging in again rotates it | | `model` | `auto` | New sessions let Merit Order choose (`--model claude-sonnet-5-5` picks one; `--model none` leaves Claude Code's choice) | | `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` | the gateway's window for that model | Claude Code would otherwise assume 200,000 tokens for `auto` and compact early | | `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION`, `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME` | `auto`, `auto (Merit Order)` | Adds "auto (Merit Order)" to the `/model` picker | | `CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS` | `1` | Claude Code labels side requests and compaction only when asked (section 2) | With `--model` set to a Claude model name, it leaves out the window and `/model` settings (and removes earlier ones): Claude Code already knows those names. It changes every Claude Code session that uses that settings folder. To keep Merit Order in a separate profile (for example, away from work that uses another account): ```bash meritorder setup claude-code --config-dir ~/.claude-meritorder CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-meritorder claude ``` What to expect: - **Billing.** With the Merit Order key, Claude Code doesn't use your claude.ai login for these requests: subscription limits don't apply, and the cost is per token on the providers' accounts behind the gateway. - **Non-Claude models.** `auto` can send Claude Code's turns to GPT, Gemini or open models, translated. It works, but Anthropic doesn't support running Claude Code on non-Claude models, so expect rough edges. - **Cost display.** Claude Code's own cost figure guesses prices for a name it doesn't know (a test request it showed as $0.038 cost $0.0096). The gateway's numbers (My usage page, `meritorder usage`) are the real ones. - **Reply length.** For a model name it doesn't know, Claude Code asks for up to 32,000 output tokens per reply. `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` raises it (to 128,000 at most); Merit Order lowers a request to the chosen model's own maximum when that's smaller. - **Effort.** Claude Code sends its own reasoning effort (its `/effort` setting), and a client's setting always wins, so the per-level effort (section 6) doesn't apply to its turns. - **A startup line** `[claude-code:unrecognized_model] {"model":"auto"}` is informational. - **Subagents** each get their own routing thread within the session (section 5), and their own level. **pi** gets a "Merit Order" provider listing `auto` and every model with its context window, sends its session id so sessions stay on the backend that holds their cache, and adds cache markers that survive translation. **Codex CLI** and other OpenAI-compatible tools need only the base URL (`/v1`) and the key. ## 12. Where everything is set | What | Where in the console | In the config file | |---|---|---| | Quality source, scale, reference, refresh | Config → Routing → Quality scores | `quality:` | | A model's score override, its name in benchmark data | Config → Models | `quality_override`, `benchmark_name` | | The name that means "choose for me" | Config → Routing → Automatic routing | `routing.auto_model` | | How much cheaper a move must be | Config → Routing → Automatic routing | `routing.switch_margin_pct`, `switch_margin_usd` | | Expected turns and tokens per turn | Config → Routing → Automatic routing | `routing.min_expected_turns`, `est_output_tokens`, … | | Cost or speed | Config → Routing → Cost or speed; Config → Teams | `routing.priority`, team `priority` | | Effort by level | Config → Routing → Reasoning effort by task difficulty | `routing.effort_by_floor` | | Levels for Claude Code's side and compaction requests | Config → Routing → Claude Code request types | `routing.request_class_levels` | | GPU price curve | Config → Routing → Self-hosted pricing curve | `routing.shadow_knee`, `shadow_floor` | | Which models and providers a team may use | Config → Teams | `allowed_models`, `allowed_backends` | | Budgets, per-request cost limit | Controls; Config → Teams | `safeguards`, team budgets | | Routes, prices you've negotiated | Config → Models | `routes[].price` (an override) | | Context windows, output limits | live price data (Models page) | `context_window`, `max_output_tokens` (overrides) | | GPU deployments | Config → Backends; GPUs page | `backends.*.serve` | | How requests get a level | not yet in the console | `classifier.py` | | Pointing Claude Code or pi at the gateway | — | `meritorder setup claude-code` / `setup pi` | The Models page shows every model's live scores, prices and windows, with where each came from; Backends shows each route's measured speed and anything being skipped. ## 13. What `auto` does today The cheapest qualifying model for a typical request at each level, on 11 November 2026: | Level | Coding | General | |---|---|---| | 1 | GLM-5.3 Flash, gpt-oss-20b | GLM-5.3 Flash, gpt-oss-20b | | 2 | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 | Claude Haiku 5.5 | | 3 | Claude Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1 Terra | | 4 | GPT-6.1 Terra | GPT-6.1 Sol | | 5 | Claude Fable 5.2 only | Claude Fable 5.2 only | A Claude Code session on `auto` is coding level 4 (it always sends many tools): GPT-6.1 Terra, until the conversation passes 60,000 tokens and it becomes level 5 (Fable) at the next prompt. Its titles and summaries go to level-1 models, and compaction summaries to level-3 models. ## 14. Known gaps - **The level rules aren't in the console,** and they're keyword-based. A coding agent sending `auto` with more than 60,000 tokens of context lands on level 5, which today only Fable meets, at $8/$40 per million tokens. Clients that name a model aren't affected. - **Some scores are estimates.** A model without published coding results gets a coding score from its general ability (marked * on the Models page), and published results come from runs at different efforts. - **A threshold, not cost per solved task.** A cheaper model that solves a little less can still cost less per solved task than a dearer one. Merit Order now has each model's chance of solving hard work, so it could pick on expected cost per success; today it picks the cheapest model above the level, which is simpler to predict. - **Token counts for routing are estimates** (about 4 characters per token), so the window check can be off near the limit; a provider's "too long" is the backstop (section 7).

"""Eval grading edge cases, task runs that fail, suite loading; and tracing setup with an OTLP exporter."""

import json
import sys
import types

import httpx
import pytest

from meritorder import telemetry
from meritorder.evals.runner import grade, load_suite, run_task


def reply(text="", calls=()):
    msg = {"role": "assistant", "content": text}
    if calls:
        msg["tool_calls"] = [{"id": f"c{i}", "type": "function", "function": {"name": n, "arguments": a}} for i, (n, a) in enumerate(calls)]
    return {"choices": [{"message": msg}]}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("check, text, passed, why", [
    ({"number": 42}, "no digits here", False, "no number in the reply"),
    ({"number": 3.14, "tolerance": 0.01}, "pi is about 3.141", True, ""),
    ({"number": 10}, "first 3 then 10", True, ""),  # the last number is the answer
    ({"json": {"a": 1}}, "not json at all", False, "reply isn't valid JSON"),
    ({"json": {"a": 1}}, "[1, 2]", False, "reply isn't a JSON object"),
    ({"json": {"a": 1}}, '{"a": 1, "b": 2}', True, ""),
    ({"regex": r"^\d+ items$"}, "12 items", True, ""),
    ({"regex_behaves": {"match": ["a"]}}, "x" * 600, False, "regex too long"),
    ({"regex_behaves": {"match": ["a"]}}, "(unclosed", False, "not a valid regex"),
    ({"regex_behaves": {"match": ["ab"], "reject": ["abc"]}}, "/ab/", True, ""),
    ({"telepathy": True}, "anything", False, "unknown check telepathy"),
])
def test_grade_edge_cases(check, text, passed, why):
    ok, reason = grade(check, reply(text))
    assert ok is passed and why in reason


def test_tool_call_grading():
    want = {"tool_call": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Oslo"}}}
    assert grade(want, reply(calls=[("other", "{}"), ("get_weather", '{"city": " oslo "}')]))[0]  # skips other tools
    ok, why = grade(want, reply(calls=[("get_weather", "{broken")]))
    assert not ok and "aren't valid JSON" in why
    ok, why = grade(want, reply(calls=[("get_weather", '{"city": "Bergen"}')]))
    assert not ok and "expected {'city': 'Oslo'}" in why
    assert grade({"tool_call": {"name": "noop"}}, reply(calls=[("noop", None)]))[0]  # no arguments needed
    assert grade({"contains": "x"}, {})[0] is False  # an empty reply never passes


def test_load_suite_validation_and_names(tmp_path):
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.yaml"
    bad.write_text("tasks:\n  - id: t1\n    task: coding\n    prompt: hi\n")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="t1 needs id, task, level, prompt, and checks"):
        load_suite(bad)
    good = tmp_path / "my-suite.yaml"
    good.write_text("tasks:\n  - {id: t1, task: coding, level: 1, prompt: hi, checks: [{contains: hi}]}\n")
    assert load_suite(good)["name"] == "my-suite"
    named = tmp_path / "x.yaml"
    named.write_text("name: custom\ntasks: []\n")
    assert load_suite(named) == {"name": "custom", "tasks": []}


async def test_run_task_sends_tools_and_reports_failures():
    seen = []

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        seen.append((body, dict(request.headers)))
        if "boom" in body["messages"][0]["content"]:
            return httpx.Response(429, text="slow down", headers={"x-meritorder-cost-usd": "0"})
        return httpx.Response(200, json=reply("42"), headers={"x-meritorder-cost-usd": "0.0012"})

    task = {"id": "t", "task": "coding", "level": 2, "prompt": "what is 6*7", "checks": [{"number": 42}],
            "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "calc"}}], "max_tokens": 50}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler)) as c:
        ok = await run_task(c, "http://gw", "mo-key", "small", task, "suite-1")
        failed = await run_task(c, "http://gw", "mo-key", "small", {**task, "prompt": "boom"}, "suite-1")
    assert ok.passed and ok.cost == 0.0012 and ok.error is None
    body, headers = seen[0]
    assert body["tools"] == task["tools"] and body["max_tokens"] == 50
    assert headers["x-meritorder-cache"] == "off" and headers["x-meritorder-tags"] == "eval=suite-1"
    assert headers["x-session-id"].startswith("eval-")
    assert not failed.passed and failed.error == "HTTP 429: slow down"

    def down(request):
        raise httpx.ConnectError("refused")

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(down)) as c:
        res = await run_task(c, "http://gw", "k", "small", task, "s")
    assert res.skipped and res.error == "not graded: lost the connection to the gateway (after 1 try): ConnectError: refused"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tracing setup


def test_setup_tracing_with_an_otlp_exporter(monkeypatch, caplog):
    exporters = []

    class FakeExporter:
        def __init__(self):
            exporters.append(self)

        def export(self, spans):  # pragma: no cover - the batch processor isn't flushed here
            return None

        def shutdown(self):
            return None

    mod = types.ModuleType("opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter")
    mod.OTLPSpanExporter = FakeExporter
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter", mod)
    providers = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(telemetry.trace, "set_tracer_provider", providers.append)
    monkeypatch.setenv("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT", "http://collector:4318/v1/traces")
    monkeypatch.setenv("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME", "mo-test")
    caplog.set_level("INFO")
    assert telemetry.setup_tracing() is True
    assert exporters and providers
    assert providers[0].resource.attributes["service.name"] == "mo-test"
    assert "tracing on" in caplog.text
    for p in providers:
        p.shutdown()


def test_record_span_is_a_no_op_without_opentelemetry(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(telemetry, "trace", None)
    telemetry.record_span({"served_model": "small", "latency_ms": 5})  # must not raise
    assert telemetry.setup_tracing() is False

"""The ``meritorder`` command."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from .harness import KEY_FILE, save_key, saved


def load_dotenv(path: str | Path = ".env") -> None:
    """Load KEY=VALUE lines from .env without overriding variables already set."""
    try:
        lines = Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return
    for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key, value = key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        if key and value and key not in os.environ:
            os.environ[key] = value


def _setup_logging(level: str = "INFO") -> None:
    logging.basicConfig(level=level, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")


def _store():
    from .store import make_store

    store = make_store(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL"))
    if store.kind != "postgres":
        raise SystemExit("this command needs Postgres: set MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL")
    return store


def _saved() -> dict:
    return saved()


def _gateway(args) -> str:
    return (getattr(args, "gateway", None) or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_URL") or _saved().get("gateway") or "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")


def _key(args) -> str:
    key = getattr(args, "key", None) or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_API_KEY") or _saved().get("api_key")
    if not key:
        raise SystemExit("no API key: pass --key, set MERITORDER_API_KEY, or run 'meritorder login'")
    return key


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def cmd_serve(args) -> None:
    import uvicorn

    if args.config:
        os.environ["MERITORDER_CONFIG"] = args.config
    workers = args.workers or int(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_WORKERS", "1"))
    if workers > 1 and not (os.environ.get("MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL") and os.environ.get("MERITORDER_REDIS_URL")):
        raise SystemExit("--workers > 1 needs Postgres and Redis (MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL, MERITORDER_REDIS_URL): "
                         "worker processes share state through them")
    uvicorn.run("meritorder.app:create_app", factory=True, host=args.host, port=args.port, log_level=args.log_level.lower(),
                proxy_headers=True, workers=workers)


def cmd_migrate(args) -> None:
    async def run():
        store = _store()
        await store.init()
        await store.migrate()
        await store.close()
        print("database is up to date")

    asyncio.run(run())


def cmd_worker(args) -> None:
    from .worker import run_worker

    asyncio.run(run_worker(once=args.once, interval=args.interval, path=args.config, backfill=args.backfill))


def cmd_controller(args) -> None:
    from .controller import run_controller

    asyncio.run(run_controller(once=args.once, interval=args.interval, path=args.config))


def cmd_keys(args) -> None:
    async def run():
        store = _store()
        await store.init()
        try:
            if args.keys_cmd == "create":
                expires = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=args.expires_days) if args.expires_days else None
                tags = dict(t.split("=", 1) for t in args.tag or [])
                await store.upsert_user(args.user, args.team, args.role, source="ensure")
                key_id, secret = await store.create_key(args.user, args.team, args.role, args.name, tags, expires)
                print(f"key id:  {key_id}")
                print(f"api key: {secret}")
                print("Store it now; it is not shown again.")
            elif args.keys_cmd == "list":
                for k in await store.list_keys(args.user):
                    state = "revoked" if k["revoked_at"] else ("expired" if k["expires_at"] and k["expires_at"] < datetime.now(UTC) else "active")
                    print(f"{k['id']:18} {k['user_id']:24} {k['team']:16} {k['role']:10} {state:8} {k.get('name') or ''}")
            elif args.keys_cmd == "revoke":
                print("revoked" if await store.revoke_key(args.key_id) else "no active key with that id")
        finally:
            await store.close()

    asyncio.run(run())


def cmd_usage(args) -> None:
    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    resp = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/reports/me", headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=30)
    if resp.status_code != 200:
        raise SystemExit(f"{resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
    me = resp.json()
    budget = f" of ${me['budget_usd']:,.2f}" if me.get("budget_usd") is not None else ""
    print(f"{me['user']} ({me['team']}), {me['month']}")
    print(f"  spent     ${me['spend_usd']:,.4f}{budget}")
    print(f"  baseline  ${me['baseline_usd']:,.4f}   (what the same work would cost without Merit Order)")
    print(f"  saved     ${me['savings_usd']:,.4f}   across {me['requests']} requests")
    if me["by_model"]:
        print(f"\n  {'model':28} {'requests':>9} {'cost':>12} {'saved':>12}")
        for r in me["by_model"]:
            print(f"  {str(r['key']):28} {r['requests']:>9} {r['actual_cost']:>12.4f} {r['savings_total']:>12.4f}")


def cmd_login(args) -> None:
    gateway = (args.gateway or os.environ.get("MERITORDER_URL") or "http://localhost:8080").rstrip("/")
    with httpx.Client(timeout=30) as c:
        oidc = c.get(f"{gateway}/auth/config").json().get("oidc")
        if not oidc:
            raise SystemExit("this gateway has no OIDC login configured; ask an admin for an API key")
        disc = c.get(oidc["issuer"].rstrip("/") + "/.well-known/openid-configuration").json()
        dev = c.post(disc["device_authorization_endpoint"], data={"client_id": oidc["client_id"], "scope": " ".join(oidc["scopes"])}).json()
        print(dev.get("message") or f"Open {dev['verification_uri']} and enter code {dev['user_code']}")
        interval = int(dev.get("interval", 5))
        deadline = time.time() + int(dev.get("expires_in", 900))
        while time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(interval)
            tok = c.post(disc["token_endpoint"], data={
                "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
                "device_code": dev["device_code"],
                "client_id": oidc["client_id"],
            }).json()
            if "id_token" in tok:
                break
            err = tok.get("error")
            if err == "slow_down":
                interval += 5
            elif err != "authorization_pending":
                raise SystemExit(f"login failed: {tok.get('error_description') or err}")
        else:
            raise SystemExit("login timed out")
        resp = c.post(f"{gateway}/auth/exchange", json={"id_token": tok["id_token"]})
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"key exchange failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}")
        result = resp.json()
    save_key(gateway, result["api_key"], {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "api_key"})
    print(f"\nLogged in as {result['user']} (team {result['team']}); key expires {result['expires_at'][:10]}.")
    print(f"Key saved to {KEY_FILE}\n")
    print("Next: `meritorder setup pi` and/or `meritorder setup claude-code`.")

def cmd_export(args) -> None:
    """Download the ledger for a date range to a file or S3 (s3://bucket/key)."""
    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    params = {k: v for k, v in (("start", args.start), ("end", args.end)) if v}
    tmp = Path(args.out if not args.out.startswith("s3://") else f".meritorder-export-{os.getpid()}.jsonl")
    rows = 0
    with httpx.stream("GET", f"{gateway}/v1/reports/export.jsonl", params=params, headers={"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
                      timeout=None) as resp:
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            raise SystemExit(f"{resp.status_code}: {resp.read().decode()[:300]}")
        with open(tmp, "w") as f:
            for line in resp.iter_lines():
                if not line:
                    continue
                if args.format == "csv":
                    import csv as _csv

                    row = json.loads(line)
                    if rows == 0:
                        writer = _csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(row))
                        writer.writeheader()
                    row["tags"] = json.dumps(row.get("tags") or {})
                    writer.writerow(row)
                else:
                    f.write(line + "\n")
                rows += 1
    if args.out.startswith("s3://"):
        from botocore.session import Session

        bucket, _, obj = args.out[5:].partition("/")
        client = Session().create_client("s3", endpoint_url=os.environ.get("MERITORDER_S3_ENDPOINT") or None)
        with open(tmp, "rb") as f:
            client.put_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=obj, Body=f.read(),
                              ContentType="text/csv" if args.format == "csv" else "application/x-ndjson")
        tmp.unlink()
    print(f"exported {rows} requests to {args.out}")


def cmd_eval(args) -> None:
    """Measure model quality on a graded suite; suggest (or apply) quality scores."""
    from datetime import UTC, datetime

    from .evals.runner import load_suite, run_suite, score

    gateway, key = _gateway(args), _key(args)
    suite = load_suite(args.suite)
    h = {"authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}
    admin_cfg = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/config", headers=h, timeout=30)
    if admin_cfg.status_code != 200:
        raise SystemExit(f"needs an admin key ({admin_cfg.status_code}: {admin_cfg.text[:120]})")
    cfg = admin_cfg.json()
    live = {m["name"]: m for m in cfg["models"] if m.get("routes") and any(r["live"] for r in m["routes"])}
    models = [m.strip() for m in args.models.split(",")] if args.models else [
        n for n, m in live.items() if not n.startswith("mock-") and not m.get("kind") == "embedding"]
    missing = [m for m in models if m not in live]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"no live route for: {', '.join(missing)} (see `meritorder check`)")
    n_tasks = len(suite["tasks"]) * args.repeat
    est = 0.0
    for m in models:
        prices = [r["price"] for r in live[m]["routes"] if r["live"] and r.get("price")]
        if prices:
            p = min(prices, key=lambda x: x["input"])
            est += n_tasks * (150 * p["input"] + 500 * p["output"]) / 1e6
    print(f"Suite '{suite['name']}': {len(suite['tasks'])} tasks x {args.repeat} on {len(models)} models: {', '.join(models)}")
    print(f"Estimated cost: about ${est:.2f} (reasoning models can use several times more output)")
    if not args.yes and input("Run it? [y/N] ").strip().lower() != "y":
        raise SystemExit("cancelled")

    done = [0]

    def progress(res):
        done[0] += 1
        mark = "pass" if res.passed else ("ERROR" if res.error else "fail")
        print(f"  [{done[0]}/{n_tasks * len(models)}] {res.model:22} {res.task_id:14} {mark}")

    results = asyncio.run(run_suite(gateway, key, models, suite, args.concurrency, args.repeat, progress))
    scores = score(results, args.threshold)
    print(f"\n{'model':22} {'pass':>6} {'coding':>7} {'general':>8} {'cost':>9} {'latency':>8}  configured")
    for m, s in scores.items():
        configured = live[m].get("quality") or {}
        sug = {t: v["suggested"] for t, v in s["tasks"].items()}
        print(f"{m:22} {s['pass_rate']:>6.0%} {sug.get('coding', '-'):>7} {sug.get('general', '-'):>8} {s['cost']:>9.4f} {s['avg_latency_ms'] / 1000:>7.1f}s  {configured}")
        for f in s["failed"][: args.show_failures]:
            print(f"    x {f['id']}: {f['why'][:110]}")
    payload = {"suite": suite["name"], "ran_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "models": scores}
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str))
        print(f"\nResults saved to {args.out}")
    httpx.put(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/evals", headers=h, json=json.loads(json.dumps(payload, default=str)), timeout=30)
    if args.apply:
        src = httpx.get(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/config/source", headers=h, timeout=30).json()
        doc = src["document"]
        for m, s in scores.items():
            for task, v in s["tasks"].items():
                if v["suggested"]:
                    doc.setdefault("models", {}).setdefault(m, {}).setdefault("quality", {})[task] = v["suggested"]
        r = httpx.put(f"{gateway}/v1/admin/config", headers=h, timeout=60,
                      json={"document": doc, "comment": f"quality scores from eval '{suite['name']}'"})
        print(f"Applied: config version {r.json().get('version')}" if r.status_code == 200 else f"Not applied: {r.status_code} {r.text[:200]}")
    else:
        print("Re-run with --apply to write the suggested scores into the config (as a new version you can roll back).")

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="meritorder", description="Merit Order LLM gateway")

    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_serve)

    sub.add_parser("migrate", help="create or upgrade the database schema").set_defaults(func=cmd_migrate)

    w = sub.add_parser("worker", help="run background jobs (rollups, partitions)")

    w.add_argument("--interval", type=int, default=60)
    w.add_argument("--config")
    w.add_argument("--backfill", action="store_true", help="recompute all hourly rollups from the raw ledger")
    w.set_defaults(func=cmd_worker)

    c = sub.add_parser("controller", help="run the GPU capacity controller")

    k = sub.add_parser("keys", help="manage API keys")

    kc.add_argument("--name")

    kc.add_argument("--expires-days", type=int)
    kl = ksub.add_parser("list")
    kl.add_argument("--user")
    kr = ksub.add_parser("revoke")

    u = sub.add_parser("usage", help="show your spend and savings this month")
    u.add_argument("--gateway")
    u.add_argument("--key")
    u.set_defaults(func=cmd_usage)

    lg = sub.add_parser("login", help="sign in with your organization (OIDC device code) and get an API key")

    uk = sub.add_parser("use-key", help="save an API key an admin gave you")
    uk.add_argument("api_key")

    uk.set_defaults(func=cmd_use_key)

    tk = sub.add_parser("token", help="print your saved API key")

    st = sub.add_parser("setup", help="point a coding harness at Merit Order")
    st.add_argument("harness", choices=["pi", "claude-code"])

    st.add_argument("--key")

    ex = sub.add_parser("export", help="export per-request ledger rows (no content) to a file or s3://bucket/key")
    ex.add_argument("--start", help="YYYY-MM-DD (default: first of this month)")
    ex.add_argument("--end", help="YYYY-MM-DD, exclusive (default: tomorrow)")
    ex.add_argument("--format", choices=["jsonl", "csv"], default="jsonl")
    ex.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ex.add_argument("--gateway")
    ex.add_argument("--key")
    ex.set_defaults(func=cmd_export)

    ev = sub.add_parser("eval", help="measure model quality on a graded suite and suggest quality scores")
    ev.add_argument("--models", help="comma-separated model names (default: every chat model with a live route)")
    ev.add_argument("--suite", help="YAML suite (default: the built-in starter suite)")
    ev.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=1, help="run each task this many times (smooths out randomness)")
    ev.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=4)
    ev.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=0.75, help="pass rate needed at a level to earn it")
    ev.add_argument("--show-failures", type=int, default=3)
    ev.add_argument("--out", help="save results as JSON")
    ev.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true", help="write suggested quality scores into the config")
    ev.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="don't ask before spending money")
    ev.add_argument("--gateway")
    ev.add_argument("--key")
    ev.set_defaults(func=cmd_eval)

    pr = sub.add_parser("prices", help="refresh prices and context windows from OpenRouter's catalog")
    pr.add_argument("action", choices=["refresh"])
    pr.add_argument("--config")
    pr.set_defaults(func=cmd_prices)

    md = sub.add_parser("models", help="list the models each configured backend serves")
    md.add_argument("action", choices=["discover"])
    md.add_argument("--backend", action="append")
    md.add_argument("--grep")
    md.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=40)
    md.add_argument("--config")
    md.set_defaults(func=cmd_discover)

    cc = sub.add_parser("check", help="show which backends and models are usable with the current config and credentials")
    cc.add_argument("--config")
    cc.set_defaults(func=cmd_config_check)

    load_dotenv(os.environ.get("MERITORDER_ENV_FILE", ".env"))
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    _setup_logging(args.log_level.upper())
    args.func(args)
