# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports. Unknown, revoked, or expired keys get a 401. | Client | Auth | |---|---| | People with harnesses | `meritorder login` → virtual key (above) | | Services / apps | An Entra token directly as the bearer token, or a key from `meritorder keys create` | | Local dev / quickstart | `MERITORDER_DEV_KEY` (static admin key from the environment) | | Google (later) | Another OIDC issuer: same code path | Entra login switches on when `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` are set; map Entra group IDs to teams and roles in `auth.oidc` in the config. SCIM (later) revokes keys when people leave. ## People and teams | What | Where it's managed | |---|---| | Who exists, and their group membership | Your identity provider (Entra). People are created in Merit Order the first time they sign in with `meritorder login` (or when an admin issues them a key). | | Teams, with budgets, limits, and model policy | Merit Order: Config → Teams. An IdP has no notion of "$5,000 a month, these models only". | | Which team and role someone gets | Entra groups mapped to teams and roles in Config → Access, re-read at each sign-in. | | Exceptions | The People page: an admin can move someone, change their role (that pins it, so later sign-ins don't override it), let Entra decide again, or disable them. | The user record, not the key, decides a person's team and role. Moving or disabling someone takes effect within a minute on every gateway, including keys they already have. For the same reason, a team lead can issue keys only for themselves, for new people, or for people on their own team with the user role; keys for anyone else (another team, a lead, an admin) need an admin. | Role | Sees | Can change | |---|---|---| | user | Their own usage | Their own keys | | team lead | Their team: reports, requests, ledger export | Keys for their team's users | | finance | Every team, aggregated (no per-request rows or exports) | Nothing | | admin | Everything | Everything | **SCIM provisioning** (`/scim/v2`, enabled by `MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN`): Entra pushes people and group changes as they happen. Group membership recomputes team and role with the same mappings as sign-in, and anyone deactivated or removed in Entra is disabled immediately (spend history is kept). Setup: Entra → Enterprise applications → your app → Provisioning → Automatic; Tenant URL `https:///scim/v2`, Secret token = `MERITORDER_SCIM_TOKEN`. ## Budgets ```mermaid flowchart TD ORG["Org budget
$/month"] --> T1["Team: platform
$/month"] ORG --> T2["Team: data-science
$/month"] T1 --> U1["User budget"] T1 --> U2["User budget"] T2 --> U3["User budget"] U1 --> K1["Key"] U1 --> K2["Key"] ``` - A request must fit **every** level above it: organization, team, and person. - **Each person can have their own monthly limit.** Without one, the team's per-person default (`user_budget_usd_month`) applies. A person's own limit replaces that default, higher or lower; the team and organization budgets still apply on top. `$0` stops their requests. Set it in either place below; the People page wins when both are set, and changes apply within a minute on every gateway, keys already issued included: - The console's **People** page (admins), or `PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id}` with `{"budget_usd_month": 250}`. Send `null` to clear it and go back to the default. - `budget_usd_month` on a static key in the config file, for people who use one. - A person's limit counts everything they spent this month, on whichever team they were on. - Spend is checked before a request is sent and counted when it finishes (Redis counters seeded from the Postgres ledger, which stays the source of truth). - Alerts go out at 80% and 100%; at 100% requests are refused with a 429 that says which budget was reached. - Policy lives alongside budgets: allowed models, allowed providers, data residency (e.g. "DeepSeek weights only self-hosted or on Bedrock, never the vendor API"). ## Limits that stop runaway spend | Setting (per team) | What it does | |---|---| | `budget_usd_month`, `user_budget_usd_month` | Monthly caps for the team, and the default for each person on it; requests are refused at 100% (alerts at 80%). A person's own limit replaces the per-person default ([Budgets](#budgets)) | | `max_session_usd` | Stops one session (typically an agent stuck in a loop) once it has spent this much | | `rate_limits: {user_rpm, user_tpm, team_rpm, team_tpm}` | Requests and prompt tokens per minute; 429 with `Retry-After` | ## Organization-wide safeguards Hard limits for everyone, set under `safeguards:` or on the console's **Controls** page (which shows each one next to this month's spend and the pace it's on, and saves changes as a new config version). The shipped config reads them from the environment, so each install sets its own in `.env` without editing the file: `MERITORDER_ORG_BUDGET_USD`, `MERITORDER_GPU_BUDGET_USD`, `MERITORDER_MAX_GPU_USD_PER_HOUR`, `MERITORDER_MAX_GPU_REPLICAS`, and `MERITORDER_MAX_REQUEST_USD` (25 if unset). A blank or unset variable means no limit. These are the fastest stop there is: they act on the gateway's own ledger, request by request. Cloud budgets (AWS Budgets, Azure Cost Management) see spend hours later, and on their own only send email, so treat them as a backstop for anything that doesn't go through the gateway. | Setting | What it does | |---|---| | `org_budget_usd_month` | All spend in the ledger. At 100% every request is refused until the month ends or it's raised | | `gpu_budget_usd_month` | GPU time (replicas × hourly price). At 100% running GPUs drain and none start, pins included | | `max_gpu_usd_per_hour` | Burn-rate cap for the whole GPU fleet; deployments whose demand best covers their cost get capacity first | | `max_gpu_replicas` | Replica cap across all deployments | | `max_request_usd` | Per request. One that sets `max_tokens` is checked at its worst case (context × input price + `max_tokens` × output price): cheaper candidates are used instead, and if none fit it's refused with what it would have cost. One without `max_tokens` may write as much as the model can, less whatever wouldn't fit under the limit (`x-meritorder-max-tokens-source: cost limit` says it was trimmed); it's refused only if its input alone costs more | | `alert_at` | Fractions of the org and GPU budgets that send alerts (default 80% and 100%) | GPUs can also be stopped, pinned, or stopped all at once from the console; see [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md#controls-and-safeguards). ## What gets charged | Backend | Charged to the user's budget | |---|---| | API | Provider cost of the cached, uncached, and output tokens at catalog prices. OpenRouter picks among providers whose prices differ, so for OpenRouter the ledger records what it billed (`usage.cost`; with your own provider key, its fee plus the provider's charge). Set `billed_cost: reported` or `catalog` on a backend to choose | | Self-hosted | Chargeback: GPU-hour cost (SkyPilot's catalog price for the running replicas, else `gpu_cost_per_hour`) split by tokens served, so it's fair, not $0 | | Server-side tools | Anthropic web search at $10 per 1,000 searches (`price.web_search_per_1k`), on top of tokens. Web fetch adds only tokens; code-execution container time isn't modeled | Some `anthropic-beta` features change pricing (for example 1M-token context) in ways the cost model doesn't track. To keep them off, list the betas a backend may forward: `anthropic_betas: [...]` (prefix match; unset forwards everything the client sends). Budgets use chargeback; the router uses marginal cost. They answer different questions. ## The savings ledger One row per request, written async: | Field | Example | |---|---| | user, team, session | | | model requested / floor / served | `auto` / `coding:3` / `qwen3-coder-480b` | | backend | `self/qwen3-coder/replica-2` | | tokens: uncached in / cached in / out | 2,100 / 118,000 / 640 | | **actual marginal cost** | $0.0004 | | **chargeback cost** | $0.0090 | | **counterfactual cost** (floor model on API, no proxy caching) | $0.3700 | | upgraded for free? | yes | This is the dashboard that sells the project: *"$X spent, $Y avoided, Z% of requests upgraded at no cost."* How savings are calculated and reported is in [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md).

"""How the gateway authenticates to providers, which backends get built, and the exact-match response cache."""

import sys
import time
import types

import pytest

from meritorder.backends import build_backends
from meritorder.backends.auth import ApiKeyAuth, AzureADAuth, BackendAuthProvider, GoogleAuth, SigV4Auth, make_auth
from meritorder.backends.http import AnthropicBackend, OpenAIBackend
from meritorder.backends.mock import MockBackend
from meritorder.config import BackendAuth, BackendConfig, Config
from meritorder.response_cache import ResponseCacheConfig, cache_key, replay_stream, wanted

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ api keys


async def test_api_key_default_bearer_and_custom_header(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MO_TEST_KEY", "sk-test")
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_env="MO_TEST_KEY"))
    assert isinstance(a, ApiKeyAuth) and a.available()
    assert await a.apply("POST", "u", {"x": "1"}, b"") == {"x": "1", "authorization": "Bearer sk-test"}
    b = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="api_key", header="X-Api-Key", value_env="MO_TEST_KEY"))
    assert await b.apply("POST", "u", {}, b"") == {"x-api-key": "sk-test"}  # no prefix outside authorization
    c = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="api_key", header="authorization", prefix="Token ", value="lit"))
    assert await c.apply("POST", "u", {}, b"") == {"authorization": "Token lit"}


def test_api_key_missing_or_empty_env_is_unavailable(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("MO_TEST_MISSING", raising=False)
    assert not make_auth(BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_env="MO_TEST_MISSING")).available()
    monkeypatch.setenv("MO_TEST_MISSING", "")
    assert not make_auth(BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_env="MO_TEST_MISSING")).available()
    assert not make_auth(BackendAuth(type="api_key")).available()


async def test_no_auth_passes_headers_through():
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth())
    assert type(a) is BackendAuthProvider and a.available()
    assert await a.apply("POST", "u", {"h": "v"}, b"") == {"h": "v"}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ AWS


@pytest.fixture
def no_aws(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """No ambient AWS credentials from the developer's machine."""
    for var in ("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "AWS_SESSION_TOKEN", "AWS_PROFILE", "AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE",
                "AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK", "AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI", "AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI",
                "AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE", "AWS_ROLE_ARN"):
        monkeypatch.delenv(var, raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE", str(tmp_path / "none"))
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_CONFIG_FILE", str(tmp_path / "none"))
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED", "true")


async def test_bedrock_bearer_token_takes_priority(no_aws, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK", "brk-token")
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="aws_sigv4", region="us-west-2"))
    assert isinstance(a, ApiKeyAuth) and await a.apply("POST", "u", {}, b"") == {"x-api-key": "brk-token"}
    # Only for the Bedrock (Mantle) service: other services still sign.
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "AKIDEXAMPLE")
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "secret")
    assert isinstance(make_auth(BackendAuth(type="aws_sigv4", service="bedrock")), SigV4Auth)


def test_sigv4_without_credentials_is_unavailable(no_aws):
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="aws_sigv4"))
    assert isinstance(a, SigV4Auth) and not a.available()
    assert a.service == "bedrock-mantle" and a.region == "us-east-1"


async def test_sigv4_signs_the_request(no_aws, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "AKIDEXAMPLE")
    monkeypatch.setenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "secret")
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="aws_sigv4", service="bedrock", region="eu-west-1"))
    assert a.available()
    out = await a.apply("POST", "https://bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/model/x/invoke", {"content-type": "application/json"}, b"{}")
    assert out["Authorization"].startswith("AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=AKIDEXAMPLE/")
    assert "/eu-west-1/bedrock/aws4_request" in out["Authorization"] and "X-Amz-Date" in out


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Azure and Google (optional extras, faked)


def fake_module(monkeypatch, name: str, **attrs):
    mod = types.ModuleType(name)
    for k, v in attrs.items():
        setattr(mod, k, v)
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, name, mod)
    return mod


async def test_azure_ad_token_is_cached_until_near_expiry(monkeypatch):
    calls = []

    class Credential:
        async def get_token(self, scope):
            calls.append(scope)
            return types.SimpleNamespace(token=f"tok{len(calls)}", expires_on=time.time() + (100 if len(calls) == 1 else 3600))

    fake_module(monkeypatch, "azure")
    fake_module(monkeypatch, "azure.identity")
    fake_module(monkeypatch, "azure.identity.aio", DefaultAzureCredential=Credential)
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="azure_ad"))
    assert isinstance(a, AzureADAuth) and a.available()
    assert (await a.apply("POST", "u", {}, b""))["authorization"] == "Bearer tok1"
    # The first token expires in 100 s, inside the 120 s refresh window: fetch a new one.
    assert (await a.apply("POST", "u", {}, b""))["authorization"] == "Bearer tok2"
    assert (await a.apply("POST", "u", {}, b""))["authorization"] == "Bearer tok2"  # cached
    assert calls == ["https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default"] * 2
    b = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="azure_ad", scope="api://custom/.default"))
    await b.apply("POST", "u", {}, b"")
    assert calls[-1] == "api://custom/.default"


async def test_google_refreshes_invalid_credentials(monkeypatch):
    class Creds:
        valid, token, refreshed = False, None, 0

        def refresh(self, request):
            self.refreshed += 1
            self.valid, self.token = True, "ya29.test"

    creds = Creds()
    google = fake_module(monkeypatch, "google")
    google_auth = fake_module(monkeypatch, "google.auth", default=lambda scopes: (creds, "proj"))
    google.auth = google_auth
    fake_module(monkeypatch, "google.auth.transport")
    fake_module(monkeypatch, "google.auth.transport.requests", Request=lambda: object())
    a = make_auth(BackendAuth(type="google"))
    assert isinstance(a, GoogleAuth)
    assert (await a.apply("POST", "u", {}, b"")) == {"authorization": "Bearer ya29.test"}
    await a.apply("POST", "u", {}, b"")
    assert creds.refreshed == 1  # still valid: no second refresh


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ build_backends


def test_build_backends_picks_classes_and_disables_unusable_ones(no_aws, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MO_TEST_KEY", "k")
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "azure.identity.aio", None)  # the azure extra isn't installed

    def broken(scopes):
        raise RuntimeError("no ADC found")

    google = fake_module(monkeypatch, "google")
    google.auth = fake_module(monkeypatch, "google.auth", default=broken)
    cfg = Config(backends=[
        BackendConfig(name="mock", kind="mock", format="openai"),
        BackendConfig(name="anth", format="anthropic", base_url="https://a", auth=BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_env="MO_TEST_KEY")),
        BackendConfig(name="oai", format="openai", base_url="https://o/v1", auth=BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_env="MO_TEST_KEY")),
        BackendConfig(name="off", enabled=False, format="openai", base_url="https://x"),
        BackendConfig(name="bedrock", format="anthropic", base_url="https://b", auth=BackendAuth(type="aws_sigv4")),
        BackendConfig(name="azure", format="openai", base_url="https://z", auth=BackendAuth(type="azure_ad")),
        BackendConfig(name="vertex", format="anthropic", flavor="vertex", project="p", auth=BackendAuth(type="google")),
    ], models=[])
    out = build_backends(cfg)
    assert isinstance(out["mock"], MockBackend) and isinstance(out["anth"], AnthropicBackend) and isinstance(out["oai"], OpenAIBackend)
    assert set(out) == {"mock", "anth", "oai"}
    reasons = {b.name: b.disabled_reason for b in cfg.backends if not b.enabled}
    assert reasons["off"] is None  # disabled in config, not by us
    assert reasons["bedrock"] == "no credentials found"
    assert reasons["azure"].startswith("missing optional dependency")
    assert reasons["vertex"] == "credentials unavailable (RuntimeError: no ADC found)"


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ response cache


def test_cache_wanted_by_header_or_team_setting():
    off, on = ResponseCacheConfig(), ResponseCacheConfig(enabled=True)
    assert not wanted(off, {}) and wanted(on, {})
    assert wanted(off, {"x-meritorder-cache": "ON"}) and not wanted(on, {"x-meritorder-cache": "off"})
    assert wanted(on, {"x-meritorder-cache": "maybe"}) and not wanted(off, {"x-meritorder-cache": "maybe"})


def test_cache_key_ignores_transport_fields_and_respects_scope():
    team, user = ResponseCacheConfig(), ResponseCacheConfig(scope="user")
    body = {"model": "m", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}
    k = cache_key("openai", body, "t", "alice", team)
    assert k.startswith("rc:") and len(k) == 3 + 64
    assert k == cache_key("openai", {**body, "stream": True, "stream_options": {}, "metadata": {"a": 1}, "user": "u"}, "t", "bob", team)
    assert k == cache_key("openai", dict(reversed(list(body.items()))), "t", "alice", team)  # key order doesn't matter
    assert k != cache_key("anthropic", body, "t", "alice", team)
    assert k != cache_key("openai", {**body, "temperature": 0}, "t", "alice", team)
    assert k != cache_key("openai", body, "other-team", "alice", team)
    assert cache_key("openai", body, "t", "alice", user) != cache_key("openai", body, "t", "bob", user)


def test_replay_stream_anthropic_text_and_tool_use():
    resp = {"id": "msg", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": "m", "stop_reason": "tool_use",
            "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Let me look."}, {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "skip"},
                        {"type": "tool_use", "id": "tu1", "name": "read", "input": {"path": "a.py"}}],
            "usage": {"input_tokens": 5, "output_tokens": 9}}
    evs = replay_stream("anthropic", resp)
    assert [e.event for e in evs] == ["message_start", "content_block_start", "content_block_delta", "content_block_stop",
                                      "content_block_start", "content_block_delta", "content_block_stop", "message_delta", "message_stop"]
    assert evs[0].json()["message"]["content"] == []
    assert evs[2].json()["delta"] == {"type": "text_delta", "text": "Let me look."}
    assert evs[4].json()["content_block"] == {"type": "tool_use", "id": "tu1", "name": "read", "input": {}} and evs[4].json()["index"] == 2
    assert evs[5].json()["delta"] == {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": '{"path": "a.py"}'}
    assert evs[7].json()["delta"]["stop_reason"] == "tool_use" and evs[7].json()["usage"] == {"output_tokens": 9}


def test_replay_stream_openai_with_tool_calls():

# 03 — Routing The router answers: **which model, on which backend, for this request?** (Every rule and default, as diagrams: [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md).) It optimizes **marginal cost** — what this request adds to the bill *right now* — subject to a quality floor and team policy. ## Decision flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> B{"Harness pinned
a model?"} B -- "yes" --> FIX["Model is fixed
(only the backend can vary)"] B -- "no, model=auto" --> C{"Existing session,
mid-task, cache warm?"} C -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep session's model"] C -- "no" --> D["Classifier → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] D --> E["Candidates = models allowed for team
with quality ≥ floor"] FIX --> S KEEP --> S E --> S["Score every backend of every candidate
cost = rebuild + turns × per-turn"] S --> T{"Cheapest beats current
by more than hysteresis margin?"} T -- "yes" --> MOVE["Route to cheapest
(close on price → quality, then speed)"] T -- "no" --> STAY["Stay on current backend"] MOVE --> PRI{"Running above floor
only because it's free?"} STAY --> PRI PRI -- "yes" --> LOW["Send with low priority
(paid traffic preempts it)"] PRI -- "no" --> NORM["Send with normal priority"] ``` ## The cost function For each candidate backend `b`, over the session's expected remaining turns: ``` cost(b) = rebuild(b) + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn(b) ``` **Per-turn cost by backend type** | Backend state | `per_turn(b)` | |---|---| | API | uncached tokens × input price + cached tokens × cache-read price + output × output price | | Self-hosted, plenty of headroom | ≈ 0 (shadow price near zero) | | Self-hosted, filling up | shadow price rises toward the same model's API price | | Self-hosted, at latency target | unavailable (or priced as the API version of the same model) | **Rebuild cost** | Situation | `rebuild(b)` | |---|---| | `b` already holds a warm cache for this session | 0 | | API, cold | prefix tokens × (cache-write price − cache-read price) | | Self-hosted, cold | prefix tokens × shadow price + latency penalty for the prefill | Illustrative (check real prices): a 120k-token Claude session costs ~$0.04/turn in cache reads to stay. Moving it to another Claude backend costs ~$0.45 to rewrite the cache. A move has to save more than ~$0.41 over the rest of the session to be worth it. ## Shadow price Self-hosted tokens aren't literally free — capacity is finite. The shadow price makes spare capacity attractive while protecting latency: ![Shadow price vs replica utilization](img/shadow-price.svg) ## Free upgrades (and why they're safe) If a strong open model is running with headroom and the task only needs a medium model, the user gets the strong model at ~zero cost. Three guardrails keep this from backfiring: 1. **Low priority.** Opportunistic requests use vLLM priority scheduling, so traffic that *needs* that model always goes first. 2. **Doesn't keep GPUs alive.** The controller values upgraded traffic at its *floor* model's API price, so free traffic can't make a GPU look worth keeping. (See [05](05-gpu-autoscaling.md).) 3. **Only at boundaries.** Upgrades/downgrades happen at session start or task boundaries — never mid-task — so tool-calling behavior and caches stay stable. ## Free moments to re-route Moving costs nothing when the session's cache is already gone: - Session idle longer than the cache TTL. - The harness compacted history (prefix hash no longer matches). - The replica evicted the session's KV cache (from vLLM / llm-d KV events). - A natural task boundary. ## When a model refuses Some models decline requests through safety classifiers (Claude returns HTTP 200 with `stop_reason: "refusal"`; OpenAI-style APIs use `finish_reason: "content_filter"`). For `auto` requests, Merit Order retries on the next eligible model: - Streams are buffered only until the first content arrives, so a refusal before any content is retried invisibly; one that arrives after content has started streams through. - The refused attempt is recorded in the ledger (it cost tokens), and the response carries `x-meritorder-refused-by`. - A model the client named is never substituted. Teams can turn this off (`refusal_fallback: false`). ## Measuring quality scores The 1–5 quality scores in `config/` start as informed guesses. Evals measure them: graded tasks go through the gateway to each model (code checked by hidden tests in a sandbox, agent work by a scripted environment, open-ended work by two judges from different model families), and each model gets a suggested score per task type: the highest level L such that it passes at least 75% of tasks at every level up to L. Run them from the console (Models → Evals) or with `meritorder eval`; see [11 — Evals](11-evals.md). ## Harness overrides | Harness sends | Behavior | |---|---| | `model: "claude-sonnet-5-5"` (explicit) | No model substitution. Router picks the cheapest *backend* for that model. | | `model: "auto"` | Classifier + router choose. | | `model: "auto"` + `X-Route-Floor: coding:3` | Harness sets the floor; router chooses above it. | | `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges the classifier's floor down / up. | | `reasoning_effort` / `output_config.effort` | Always passed through (translated between formats). Merit Order only picks an effort for `auto` requests that don't set one: by floor level, low for 1–2, medium for 3, high for 4–5 (`routing.effort_by_floor`). | | `max_tokens` (or none) | A client's own limit is kept (lowered only to the model's maximum). Without one, the reply may be as long as the model can write (`max_output_tokens`, from the price catalog), less what won't fit in the context window or under the per-request cost limit. `x-meritorder-max-tokens` and `x-meritorder-max-tokens-source` on the reply say how much was allowed and why. | | `X-MeritOrder-Backend: ` (admins, and eval runs) | Pins the backend, e.g. to test one provider. | | `X-MeritOrder-Priority: cost` / `balanced` / `speed` | How much more a faster route may cost: 2%, 20%, or 100% ([how it decides](10-how-it-decides.md#which-backend-gpu-or-api)). Overrides the team's `priority`. | ## When a model's GPUs are stopped - `auto` traffic, including sessions in the middle of a task, moves to the next eligible model (the session's cache is rebuilt there). - A request that names a model whose only routes are stopped GPUs gets a 503 that says why for each route ("stopped by dana: cost review", "no API key") and suggests `auto`. A named model is never silently swapped. Teams can opt in to substitution (`substitute_unavailable: true`, or Config → Teams): the request then goes to a model at least as good for the task (never a weaker one), and the response carries `x-meritorder-substituted-for`. Give open models an API route (OpenRouter, the vendor, Bedrock) to keep them available; the GPUs page warns which models have none before anyone stops a deployment. Team policy (allowed models, allowed providers, data-residency rules) is applied **before** scoring, so an override can never escape policy.

# Merit Order

An open-source LLM gateway that cuts LLM spend for day-to-day use, without changing how
people work.

Power grids dispatch generators in **merit order**: cheapest marginal cost first, with expensive
peaker plants switched on only when demand requires them. Merit Order does the same with tokens:

- **Routes** every session to the cheapest model and backend that meets the task's quality bar,
  counting what it would cost to rebuild the prompt cache somewhere else.
- **Runs open-weight models on your own GPUs** (via SkyPilot) when steady load makes that cheaper
  than paying per token, and turns them off when it doesn't. APIs (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex,
  Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Mistral, ...) are always there for overflow.
- **Saves tokens**: automatic prompt caching, sticky sessions, cache-safe compression of huge tool
  outputs, and an optional response cache.
- **Shows the money**: every request is recorded with what it cost and what it would have cost
  without Merit Order, broken down by cause, per user, team, project, and day.

Point Claude Code, pi, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or anything that speaks either API at it.

## Quickstart (no keys needed)

```bash
uv sync
cp .env.example .env            # set MERITORDER_DEV_KEY (and any provider keys you have)
uv run meritorder serve         # http://localhost:8080, reports UI at /ui/
```

```bash
curl localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $MERITORDER_DEV_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}'
```

With no provider keys, requests go to built-in mock backends. `uv run meritorder check` shows
which backends and models are live with the keys you've set. Without `MERITORDER_DATABASE_URL`,
storage is in memory; use Docker Compose for the real thing.

## Run the full stack with Docker

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add at least one provider key
docker compose up -d            # gateway + worker + Postgres + Redis on :8080
docker compose exec gateway meritorder keys create --user you@example.com --role admin
```

Bedrock with your AWS profile (including SSO): `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.aws.yaml up -d`.
Kubernetes: `helm install mo charts/meritorder` (see [docs/07-deployment.md](docs/07-deployment.md)).

## Point your harness at it

```bash
meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com   # Entra sign-in; or: meritorder use-key <key>
meritorder setup pi                                    # adds a "meritorder" provider to pi
meritorder setup claude-code                           # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + apiKeyHelper
```

Or by hand: OpenAI-compatible clients use base URL `<gateway>/v1`; Claude Code uses
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway>`. Use `model: "auto"` to let Merit Order choose, or name a model
(`claude-sonnet`, `kimi-k3.1`, `qwen3-coder`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, ...) to pin it.

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `X-Session-Id` | Groups requests into a session (pi sends it; otherwise inferred) |
| `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | Minimum quality for `auto` routing |
| `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | Nudges `auto` routing down or up |
| `X-MeritOrder-Tags: project=foo` | Cost-allocation tags for reports |
| `X-MeritOrder-Cache: on` / `off` | Use or bypass the response cache |
| `X-MeritOrder-Backend: <name>` | Admins only: pin a backend (testing, debugging) |

Responses carry `x-meritorder-model`, `x-meritorder-backend`, and (non-streaming)
`x-meritorder-cost-usd` / `x-meritorder-savings-usd`.

## What's in the box

| Area | Built |
|---|---|
| APIs | OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (stateless), Anthropic Messages, and embeddings; streaming and not; pass-through when formats match, translation when they don't |
| Backends | Anthropic, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry, Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, OpenRouter (incl. opt-in free tier), DeepSeek, Mistral, Moonshot, Z.ai, MiniMax, any OpenAI-compatible server |
| Models | Claude, GPT, and an open-weight catalog: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Qwen3-Coder, MiniMax, MiMo, Muse, Mistral/Devstral, Gemma, Nemotron, gpt-oss |
| Routing | Rule-based classifier → quality floor; marginal-cost router with cache rebuild cost, context-window checks, sticky sessions, fallback across backends |
| GPUs | Break-even controller (addressable demand, hysteresis), SkyPilot/SkyServe + vLLM provisioner, static servers, utilization from vLLM metrics, spill to API when saturated |
| Savings | Automatic prompt caching, lower reasoning effort for simple `auto` tasks (stable per session), deterministic tool-output compression, opt-in response cache |
| Identity | Virtual API keys, Entra/OIDC device-code login with group → team/role mapping, roles (user, team lead, finance, admin), People page to move, pin, or disable anyone (applies to existing keys within a minute) |
| Spend | Team and user monthly budgets, per-session spend caps (stops runaway agents), requests/tokens-per-minute limits, policy allow/deny lists for models and backends |
| Control panel | Web console at `/ui/` (Mantine, dark by default): live Dispatch view (merit-order stack from real traffic, live request feed, backend health, GPU fleet, needs-attention), Reports, GPUs (incl. what-if), Backends, Models, Teams, People, Keys, and Config (forms for teams, models, backends, routing, and access plus raw YAML; validate, version history, restore; hot-reloads every gateway) |
| Reporting | Ledger with savings by cause, reports API, CSV, JSONL/CSV ledger export to a file or S3, `meritorder usage`, Prometheus metrics, budget/spike alerts, weekly digests |
| Deployment | Docker Compose, Helm chart, CI (tests, audits, Helm lint, Compose smoke test), signed multi-arch releases |

Not yet: billing reconciliation against provider invoices, Kubernetes-native GPU provisioning
(llm-d/KServe), a learned router. See [docs/](docs/README.md) for the design.

## Development

```bash
uv sync && uv run pytest                     # gateway
cd ui && npm ci && npm run build             # reporting UI (served at /ui/)
uv run python scripts/fake_vllm.py           # a stand-in vLLM server for the GPU path
uv run python scripts/smoke_providers.py     # test every enabled provider through a running gateway
```

## License

AGPL-3.0-only. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

"""Configuration stored in Postgres: versions, validation, hot reload.

The YAML file is the starting point. Once an admin saves a configuration from the
console, versions live in Postgres (who, when, why) and every gateway applies the
newest one within seconds. Secrets never go in: they stay in environment
variables, referenced as ${NAME}.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any

import yaml

from .config import Config, build_config, effort_format

log = logging.getLogger("meritorder.configstore")

_ENV_REF = re.compile(r"^\$\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?::-[^}]*)?\}$")


class ConfigError(Exception):
    pass


def secret_problems(raw: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Literal secrets in the document (they must be ${ENV} references instead)."""
    problems = []
    for name, b in (raw.get("backends") or {}).items() if isinstance(raw.get("backends"), dict) else []:
        value = ((b or {}).get("auth") or {}).get("value")
        if value and not _ENV_REF.match(str(value)):
            problems.append(f"backends.{name}.auth.value holds a literal secret; use value_env or ${{NAME}}")
    for i, k in enumerate(((raw.get("auth") or {}).get("static_keys")) or []):
        if (k or {}).get("key") and not _ENV_REF.match(str(k["key"])):
            problems.append(f"auth.static_keys[{i}].key holds a literal key; use key_env")
    return problems


def parse_and_validate(text: str, config_dir: str, prices: dict | None) -> tuple[dict, Config]:
    try:
        raw = yaml.safe_load(text)
    except yaml.YAMLError as e:
        raise ConfigError(f"not valid YAML: {e}")
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise ConfigError("the configuration must be a YAML mapping")
    if "include" in raw:
        raise ConfigError("`include:` isn't supported in stored configurations; paste the included sections in")
    problems = secret_problems(raw)
    if problems:
        raise ConfigError("; ".join(problems))
    try:
        cfg = build_config(raw, config_dir, prices_data=prices, quiet=True)
    except Exception as e:  # pydantic validation errors and friends
        raise ConfigError(str(e))
    return raw, cfg


def summarize(cfg: Config) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "backends_enabled": sorted(b.name for b in cfg.backends if b.enabled),
        "backends_disabled": {b.name: b.disabled_reason or "disabled in config" for b in cfg.backends if not b.enabled},
        "models": len([m for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "chat"]),
        "embedding_models": len([m for m in cfg.models if m.kind == "embedding"]),
        "unpriced_routes": sorted(f"{m.name}@{r.backend}" for m in cfg.models for r in m.routes if not r.priced),
        "teams": [t.name for t in cfg.teams],
        "effort": {b.name: effort_format(b) for b in cfg.backends if b.enabled},
    }


def to_yaml(raw: dict) -> str:
    return yaml.safe_dump(raw, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True, width=120)


def token(version: int | None, prices: dict | None) -> str:
    """Changes whenever the stored configuration or the stored prices change."""
    return f"{version or 'file'}:{(prices or {}).get('updated', '')}"


async def load_active(gw, publish: bool = False) -> bool:
    """Apply the newest stored configuration and prices unless already applied. Returns True if applied."""
    row = await gw.store.active_config()
    prices = await gw.store.get_setting("prices")
    tok = token(row["id"] if row else None, prices)
    if tok == getattr(gw, "config_token", None):
        return False
    if row is None and prices is None:
        gw.config_token = tok  # nothing stored: the YAML file stays in effect
        return False
    raw = row["body"] if row else gw.file_raw
    if raw is None:
        return False
    cfg = build_config(raw, gw.file_cfg.config_dir, prices_data=prices)
    await gw.apply_config(cfg, row["id"] if row else None)
    gw.config_token = tok
    if publish:
        await gw.state.set_config_token(tok)
    return True

# 10 — How it decides Every decision Merit Order makes, in the order it makes them, with the exact rules and defaults. Each rule names the setting that controls it. The code is the source of truth: `proxy.py` (request pipeline), `router.py` (model and backend choice), `gpu.py` and `controller.py` (GPU scaling). - [A request, start to finish](#a-request-start-to-finish) - [Which model](#which-model) - [Which backend: GPU or API](#which-backend-gpu-or-api) - [When a backend fails or a model refuses](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses) - [When GPUs start, scale, and stop](#when-gpus-start-scale-and-stop) - [What happens when…](#what-happens-when) - [Every threshold in one table](#every-threshold-in-one-table) ## A request, start to finish Checks run in this order. The first one that fails ends the request with the error shown. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Request arrives"] --> K{"Valid key?
person not disabled?"} K -- "no" --> E401["401"] K -- "yes" --> B{"Org, personal, and team
monthly budgets left?"} B -- "no" --> E429a["429: which budget, how much spent"] B -- "yes" --> RL{"Within requests/tokens
per minute?"} RL -- "no" --> E429b["429 + Retry-After"] RL -- "yes" --> SC{"Session under its
spend cap?"} SC -- "no" --> E429c["429: start a new session"] SC -- "yes" --> M["Pick the model
(next section)"] M --> BK["List and rank backends
(GPU or API)"] BK -- "nothing can serve it" --> E503["503 with the reason for each route"] BK --> MR{"Worst case under
max_request_usd?"} MR -- "no candidate fits" --> E400["400: what it could cost"] MR -- "yes" --> RC{"Response cache on
and a hit?"} RC -- "hit" --> HIT["Return the cached answer ($0)"] RC -- "miss / off" --> CP["Compress huge tool outputs
(deterministic, if on)"] CP --> TRY["Try candidates in order
(failures and refusals below)"] TRY --> OK["Stream the answer back
in the client's format"] OK --> LED["Record cost, baseline, savings;
update session and spend counters"] ``` ## Which model ```mermaid flowchart TD R{"What did the
client ask for?"} R -- "a model name" --> NAMED["That model, never swapped"] R -- "auto" --> SESS{"Existing session,
same task?"} SESS -- "yes" --> KEEP["Keep the session's model"] SESS -- "no: new session, new human prompt,
or the harness compacted history" --> CL["Classify the task → quality floor
e.g. coding:3"] CL --> CANDS["Every chat model the team may use
with quality ≥ floor"] CANDS -- "none meets the floor" --> BEST["The best models available"] KEEP -- "it has nowhere to run
(e.g. its GPUs were stopped)" --> CL NAMED -- "it has nowhere to run" --> SUB{"Team turned on
substitute_unavailable?"} SUB -- "no" --> E503["503: why, per route;
suggests auto"] SUB -- "yes" --> EQ["Models at least as good
for this task (never weaker);
response says which was replaced"] ``` **The classifier** (rules, no model call): | Request | Floor | |---|---| | Has tools or code-like text | `coding:3` | | …with 5+ tools (an agent) | `coding:4` | | …and "hard" wording (architecture, race condition, security, performance, migration, …) or > 60k tokens of context | +1 | | Anything else | `general:2` | | …short (< 400 tokens, no tools) | `general:1` | | …analysis wording (analyze, compare, trade-offs, plan, …) or > 20k tokens of context | `general:3` | | `X-Route-Hint: cheap` / `smart` | −1 / +1 | | `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` | exactly that, skipping the rules | Quality scores (1–5 per task type) come from config and can be measured with `meritorder eval`. **What the client can force** | Client sends | Effect | |---|---| | A model name | That model; only the backend varies | | `reasoning_effort` / `output_config.effort` | Passed through as-is. Merit Order only picks an effort for `auto` requests that don't set one | | `X-Route-Floor`, `X-Route-Hint` | Changes the floor for `auto` | | `X-MeritOrder-Backend` | Pins the backend (admins only) | | `X-MeritOrder-Cache: off` | Skips the response cache | Team policy (allowed models and backends) applies before any of this, so nothing above can escape it. ## Which backend: GPU or API Each candidate model lists its routes (backends that serve it). A route is dropped when: | Dropped when | Why | |---|---| | The backend isn't enabled (no key, no URL) or the team may not use it | Policy and credentials | | The backend is being skipped after failures (see [When a backend fails](#when-a-backend-fails-or-a-model-refuses)) | Bad credentials or a network-level outage: the whole backend. Retried when the wait is up | | This model is being skipped on this backend: over capacity (429/503/529), or its deployment doesn't exist there (404) | Only that model there; the backend's other models are unaffected. A busy route is kept as a **last resort** if nothing else can take the request | | It's a GPU deployment that isn't warm (not started, starting, or stopped now) | Nothing to send to | | It's draining and this session has no warm cache there | Draining only finishes sessions already there | | It's a GPU at 100% (see [When a GPU is full](#when-a-gpu-is-full)) | Saturated: new work spills to other routes. Kept as a **last resort** if nothing else can take the request | | It's a saturated GPU whose queue is also full | No room to wait either | | `auto` and the route has no known price | An unknown price must never look free | | The model's context window is too small (prompt > 95% of it) and other models fit | Avoid a guaranteed error | | `auto` and it's a mock backend while real ones exist | Mocks are for trying things out | The rest are ranked by **what this session will cost from here**: ``` cost = rebuild + expected_remaining_turns × per_turn rebuild = 0 if the backend holds this session's cache, else context × (cache-write − cache-read price) per_turn = cached context × cache-read + new tokens × cache-write (input price for OpenAI-format backends) + ~600 output tokens × output price turns = turns so far, clamped to 3…30 (a long session is expected to keep going) ``` A **GPU's price is a shadow price**: what one token "costs" given how busy the GPU is. ```mermaid flowchart LR U{"GPU utilization"} -- "≤ 60%" --> F["2% of the same model's API price
(nearly free: it's already paid for)"] U -- "60–100%" --> RISE["Rises toward 100% of API price
(quadratically)"] U -- "100% / queueing" --> OUT["Last resort only:
used when no other route can take it"] ``` So GPUs win whenever they have room, even for a **better** model than the task needs (a "free upgrade", sent at low vLLM priority so traffic that needs that model goes first). As they fill up, APIs win again. **Then two tie-breakers:** 1. Candidates within 2% of the cheapest go to the higher-quality model. 2. **Stickiness:** a session stays on its current backend unless the cheapest one saves more than 10% + $0.01 over the rest of the session, which is usually only true once its cache has expired (5 minutes by default, `cache_ttl_seconds` per backend). That's what stops a session bouncing between Bedrock and Anthropic and paying to rebuild its cache each time. ## When a backend fails or a model refuses ```mermaid flowchart TD S["Send to the top candidate"] --> R{"Result"} R -- "over capacity (429/503/529),
unknown model (404), 408/409/425/500" --> NEXTM["Count a failure against this model here;
skip it on this backend for this request;
try the next"] R -- "timeout, network error, 502/504,
bad key or no access (401/403)" --> NEXT["Count a failure against the backend;
skip every candidate on it;
try the next"] R -- "200, then an error before any content
(Anthropic's in-stream overload,
an OpenRouter error chunk or body)" --> NEXTM R -- "stream sends nothing within
first_byte_timeout_seconds" --> NEXT R -- "other 4xx (bad request)" --> STOP["Return the error:
another backend would reject it too"] R -- "200, but the model refused
(before any content)" --> REF{"auto and team allows
refusal_fallback?"} REF -- "yes" --> NM["Try the next model
(refused attempt is billed and logged)"] REF -- "no" --> PASS["Return the refusal"] R -- "200" --> DONE["Respond"] NEXT --> LIM{"Candidates left?"} NEXTM --> LIM NM --> LIM LIM -- "yes" --> S LIM -- "no" --> ERR["Return the last error
(with the provider's Retry-After)"] ``` The gateway reads the start of every stream, up to its first content, before passing it on. So an error that arrives after a `200` still goes to the next source, and nothing reaches the client twice. Once content has started, an error is passed through: switching then would repeat output. How long a failing backend or model is skipped: | Failure | Skipped | For | |---|---|---| | Over capacity (429, 503, 529) | That model on that backend | The provider's `Retry-After` if it sends one, else 10 s doubling to 5 min. Still tried as a last resort | | Model or deployment not found (404) | That model on that backend | 5 min | | Credentials rejected (401, 403) | The backend | 1 min doubling to 10 min | | Anything else (5xx, timeouts, network) | The model (500) or the backend (502, 504, network) | After 3 in a row: 5 s doubling to 60 s | When something starts being skipped, an alert goes to the console's "needs attention" list, the log, and `MERITORDER_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`. It says why and where its traffic goes meanwhile. That's at most once per backend and model every 30 minutes, with a second alert when it works again. The Backends page shows what's skipped and for how long. `meritorder_failovers_total{backend,status}` counts every failed attempt, and responses served after one carry `X-MeritOrder-Failed-Over: backend/model status`. At most `max_attempts` (3) models are tried for refusals. Once a stream has started sending content to the client, a failure can't be retried: the client gets an error event, and the partial usage is still recorded. ## When GPUs start, scale, and stop The capacity controller runs every 60 s (one active at a time) and wakes immediately when an admin changes a GPU control. ```mermaid flowchart TD C0["Add up what running replicas cost
since the last cycle"] --> C1["Addressable demand for each deployment:
traffic its model is good enough for,
valued at API prices (free upgrades excluded),
max of last hour and 4 × last 15 min"] C1 --> C2["Price of one replica:
cheapest SkyPilot catalog offer in allowed
clouds/regions, else gpu_cost_per_hour"] C2 --> C3["Wanted replicas = enough for the throughput
(at 70% load), but no more than demand pays for
with a 20% margin; within min/max_replicas"] C3 --> P1{"Stop all GPUs
is on?"} P1 -- "yes" --> OFF["Stop every deployment"] P1 -- "no" --> P2{"Admin control
on this deployment?"} P2 -- "stop" --> OFF1["Stop it (drain or now)"] P2 -- "pin N" --> ON["Run exactly N"] P2 -- "none / expired" --> AUTO["Follow demand"] OFF1 --> G1 ON --> G1 AUTO --> G1{"GPU budget for the
month used up?"} G1 -- "yes" --> DR["Drain and stop everything,
pins included"] G1 -- "no" --> G2{"Fleet over max $/hour
or max replicas?"} G2 -- "yes" --> CAP["Pins first, then the deployments whose
demand best covers their cost;
the rest are held back or stopped"] G2 -- "no" --> SM["State machine (below)"] CAP --> SM DR --> SM OFF --> SM SM --> PUB["Publish state, endpoint, where replicas run,
prices → Redis; gateways follow within 5 s"] ``` **The state machine** (per deployment): ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR [*] --> api_only api_only --> provisioning: start provisioning --> warm: ready provisioning --> api_only: failed, timed out, or stopped warm --> warm: scale warm --> draining: demand gone, or stop (drain) warm --> api_only: stop now warm --> provisioning: lost readiness draining --> warm: demand returns draining --> api_only: drained, or stop now ``` | Transition | Exactly when | |---|---| | **start** | Wanted ≥ 1 continuously for 10 min and not in a cooldown. At once, ignoring any cooldown, when an admin pins replicas or `min_replicas > 0` | | **ready** | The replicas answer `/v1/models` | | **failed, timed out** | SkyPilot reports failure, or 45 min pass; the replicas are shut down and the deployment cools down for 30 min | | **stopped** (while starting) | An admin stop, Stop all GPUs, the GPU budget, or a fleet cap: provisioning is cancelled at once | | **scale** | Wanted changes while warm: `sky serve update` to the new count | | **demand gone** | Wanted = 0 for 10 min, and the deployment has been warm at least 30 min | | **stop (drain)** | An admin stop with "drain first", the GPU budget, or a fleet cap. Skips the 30-minute hold | | **stop now** | An admin stop with "stop now", or Stop all GPUs (unless set to drain) | | **lost readiness** | Replicas stop answering (e.g. a spot preemption SkyServe is replacing); traffic goes to APIs until they're back | | **demand returns** | Wanted ≥ 1 again while draining, unless it was stopped | | **drained** | 15 min after draining started | | State | Gets traffic? | Billing? | |---|---|---| | `api_only` | No; its models' traffic goes to APIs (or other models for `auto`) | No | | `provisioning` | No | Yes, from the moment `sky serve up` runs | | `warm` | Yes, first choice while it has headroom | Yes | | `draining` | Only sessions whose cache is already there | Yes | ## When a GPU is full **How "full" is measured.** Two signals; a backend is saturated when either reaches 100%: | Signal | Source | How fresh | |---|---|---| | vLLM's own load: KV-cache use, pushed to 100% by ~10 waiting requests | The controller reads `/metrics` once per cycle | Up to one cycle (60 s) old | | Requests in flight ÷ (`max_concurrency` × replicas) | Every gateway counts its own requests to the backend and publishes the count to Redis every 2 s | Live for this gateway, ≤ 2 s for others | The second signal only exists when the backend sets `max_concurrency` (vLLM's `--max-num-seqs`, or what its KV cache fits). Without it, a burst can pile up in vLLM for up to a minute before the gateways notice. Set it. **Where requests wait.** Merit Order has no queue of its own, in Redis or anywhere else: LLM calls are interactive and streaming, so the gateway forwards each request at once and holds the connection open. The only queue is **vLLM's scheduler**, on the GPU. ```mermaid flowchart TD S{"GPU saturated?"} -- "no" --> USE["Candidate at its shadow price"] S -- "yes" --> OTHER{"Another route can take it?
(same model on an API, or
another model for auto)"} OTHER -- "yes" --> SPILL["Goes there.
Warm sessions too: rebuilding the cache
beats waiting behind a full GPU"] OTHER -- "no" --> Q{"Waiting requests <
max_waiting × replicas?"} Q -- "yes" --> QUEUE["Sent to the GPU anyway: waits in vLLM.
Response header x-meritorder-queued: 1"] Q -- "no" --> REJ["503 overloaded_error:
saturated and its queue is full"] ``` Waiting requests are in-flight requests beyond `max_concurrency × replicas`; without `max_concurrency`, the controller's last count of vLLM's waiting requests is used. With neither, a saturated GPU that's the only route takes everything and each request waits up to the backend's `timeout_seconds`. Meanwhile the controller sees the demand and adds replicas (after `scale_up_after_minutes`, up to `max_replicas`). ## What happens when… | When | What happens | |---|---| | **A GPU is saturated** | New requests go to an API route for the same model, or (for `auto`) another model; sessions on it move too and rebuild their cache. If nothing else can take a request, it waits in vLLM's queue (`x-meritorder-queued: 1`) | | **A GPU is saturated, it's the only route, and its queue is full** | 503 `overloaded_error` saying so; the client retries. The controller adds replicas if the demand lasts | | **A burst hits a GPU** | With `max_concurrency` set, gateways see it within 2 s and spill the excess; without it, up to a minute of requests queue in vLLM first | | **Demand drops** | After 10 min below break-even (and 30 min warm), the deployment drains for 15 min, then stops | | **Demand rises** | After 10 min above break-even, GPUs start; traffic stays on APIs until they're ready (10–20+ min for big models) | | **An admin stops a GPU (drain)** | No new sessions there at once; warm sessions finish for up to 15 min; then it's shut down | | **An admin stops a GPU (now)** | Gateways stop sending to it within seconds; the next request in each session goes elsewhere and rebuilds its cache there; shutdown starts within seconds (the cloud takes a few minutes) | | **An admin pins N replicas** | Started at once (no 10-min wait, no cooldown), kept regardless of demand, until unpinned or the pin expires; safeguards still apply | | **Stop all GPUs** | Every deployment stops, none start, until someone resumes | | **An `auto` session's model has nowhere to run** | It's routed again from scratch to another model meeting the floor | | **A named model has nowhere to run** | 503 explaining each route ("stopped by dana: cost review", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set") unless the team turned on `substitute_unavailable`; everyone else is unaffected | | **An agent loops** | The session stops at `max_session_usd`; a spend-spike alert fires when someone's hour is 5× their norm | | **A request could cost more than `max_request_usd`** | Cheaper candidates are used; if none fit, a 400 says what it could have cost | | **Provisioning fails or takes > 45 min** | Shut down, 30-min cooldown, alert; traffic stays on APIs | | **A spot replica is preempted** | SkyServe replaces it; if no replica is ready, the deployment shows "starting" and traffic goes to APIs meanwhile | | **A stop fails at the cloud** | The deployment stays marked running and the controller keeps retrying; the console shows it in red | | **The controller isn't running** | GPUs stay as they are (nothing scales or stops them); gateways keep using the last published state; the console flags it if GPUs are up | | **A provider is over capacity** (429/529, or overloaded inside a stream) | Next backend for the same model (e.g. Anthropic → Bedrock), then the next model for `auto`. That model is skipped there for `Retry-After` (or 10 s doubling); its other models keep working; alert | | **A provider is down** (timeouts, connection errors, 5xx) | Same: next backend; skipped after 3 failures in a row; alert, and another when it recovers | | **A provider accepts a stream but never answers** | Abandoned after `first_byte_timeout_seconds` (120 s; off for self-hosted GPUs) and sent to the next backend | | **A provider rejects the key (401/403)** | Next backend; the backend is skipped for a minute (doubling). """Saturated GPUs: spill to other routes, queue as a last resort (bounded), and see load within seconds."""

import time

import pytest
from conftest import auth

from meritorder.backends.mock import MockBackend
from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, ModelConfig, Route
from meritorder.gpu import vllm_load
from meritorder.router import RoutingError
from meritorder.sessions import Session
from meritorder.state import MemoryState, _live_inflight

BODY = {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}


def add_gpu(gateway, max_concurrency=None, max_waiting=32, api_route=False):
    """A self-hosted (in-process) backend serving model 'gpu-only', optionally also on the mock API."""
    b = MockBackend(BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai", mock_latency_ms=0,
                                  max_concurrency=max_concurrency, max_waiting=max_waiting))
    gateway.backends["gpu"] = b
    routes = [Route(backend="gpu", model="m", price={"input": 1, "output": 1})]
    if api_route:
        routes.append(Route(backend=gateway.cfg.models[0].routes[0].backend, model="m", price={"input": 1, "output": 1}))
    gateway.cfg.models.append(ModelConfig(name="gpu-only", quality={"coding": 5, "general": 5}, routes=routes))
    return b


def decide(gateway, model, util, queue_full=frozenset(), session=None, boundary=True):
    return gateway.router.decide(model, gateway.cfg.team("default"), BODY, {}, session, 10, boundary, util, time.time(), queue_full)


def test_saturated_gpu_spills_to_api_route_first(gateway):
    add_gpu(gateway, api_route=True)
    d = decide(gateway, "gpu-only", {"gpu": 1.0})
    assert [c.backend.name for c in d.candidates] == [gateway.cfg.models[0].routes[0].backend]
    assert not d.candidates[0].queued


def test_only_route_saturated_queues_until_the_queue_is_full(gateway):
    add_gpu(gateway)
    d = decide(gateway, "gpu-only", {"gpu": 1.0})
    assert [c.backend.name for c in d.candidates] == ["gpu"] and d.candidates[0].queued
    assert "every route is saturated, queued on gpu" in d.reason
    with pytest.raises(RoutingError) as e:
        decide(gateway, "gpu-only", {"gpu": 1.0}, queue_full={"gpu"})
    assert e.value.status == 503 and "saturated and its queue is full" in e.value.message


def test_auto_session_on_full_gpu_moves_to_a_model_with_room(gateway):
    add_gpu(gateway)
    s = Session(id="s")
    s.model, s.backend, s.turns, s.floor = "gpu-only", "gpu", 3, "coding:3"
    d = decide(gateway, "auto", {"gpu": 1.0}, session=s, boundary=False)
    assert d.candidates[0].model.name != "gpu-only" and not d.candidates[0].queued
    assert "saturated; re-routed" in d.reason


def test_gateway_load_counts_inflight_across_gateways(gateway):
    add_gpu(gateway, max_concurrency=2, max_waiting=2)
    releases = [gateway.inflight.acquire("gpu", 600) for _ in range(2)]
    pre = {"util": {"gpu": 0.1}, "inflight": {"other-gw": {"gpu": 1}, gateway.gateway_id: {"gpu": 99}}}
    util, full = gateway.load(pre)
    assert util["gpu"] == 1.5 and not full  # 2 local + 1 elsewhere over 2 slots; our own published count is ignored
    pre["inflight"]["other-gw"]["gpu"] = 2
    util, full = gateway.load(pre)
    assert full == {"gpu"}  # 4 in flight, 2 running, 2 waiting = max_waiting
    gateway.backends["gpu"].replicas = 2  # twice the slots
    assert gateway.load(pre) == ({"gpu": 1.0}, set())
    for r in releases:
        r()
        r()  # releasing twice is harmless
    assert gateway.inflight.count("gpu") == 0


def test_inflight_entries_expire():
    from meritorder.proxy import InFlight

    f = InFlight()
    f.acquire("gpu", -1)  # already past its deadline: a leaked release
    f.acquire("gpu", 60)
    assert f.count("gpu") == 1 and f.counts() == {"gpu": 1}


def test_without_max_concurrency_the_controller_waiting_count_bounds_the_queue(gateway):
    b = add_gpu(gateway, max_waiting=4)
    b.reported_waiting = 3
    assert gateway.load({"util": {"gpu": 1.0}})[1] == set()
    b.reported_waiting = 4
    assert gateway.load({"util": {"gpu": 1.0}})[1] == {"gpu"}


async def test_end_to_end_queue_header_then_503_and_slots_released(gateway, client):
    add_gpu(gateway, max_concurrency=1, max_waiting=1)
    body = {"model": "gpu-only", **BODY}
    hold = gateway.inflight.acquire("gpu", 600)  # one long request already running
    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=auth())
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.headers["x-meritorder-queued"] == "1"
    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json={**body, "stream": True}, headers=auth())
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.headers["x-meritorder-queued"] == "1"
    assert gateway.inflight.count("gpu") == 1  # both finished and released their slots
    hold2 = gateway.inflight.acquire("gpu", 600)  # now one running, one waiting: the queue is full
    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=auth())
    assert r.status_code == 503 and "queue is full" in r.json()["error"]["message"]
    hold(), hold2()
    r = await client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=auth())
    assert r.status_code == 200 and "x-meritorder-queued" not in r.headers


async def test_state_shares_inflight_and_forgets_dead_gateways():
    s = MemoryState()
    await s.publish_inflight("a", {"gpu": 3})
    await s.publish_inflight("b", {"gpu": 0})
    pre = await s.admit([], [], None)
    assert pre["inflight"] == {"a": {"gpu": 3}}

def _then(close, release):
    """A stream's close callback that also releases its in-flight slot, exactly once."""
    async def wrapped() -> None:
        try:
            if close is not None:
                await close()
        finally:

NEXT_BACKEND_ON = {401, 402, 403, 404}  # the backend's fault, not the request's: try the next one
# How providers say a prompt doesn't fit the model's context window (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, vLLM).
_TOO_LONG = re.compile(r"prompt is too long|input is too long|context.length|context.window|maximum context|"
                       r"too many (input )?tokens|exceeds the (maximum|max)", re.IGNORECASE)


def too_long(e: "BackendError") -> bool:
    """The prompt doesn't fit the model: a model with a bigger window can take it; the same one can't."""
    return e.status in (400, 413) and bool(_TOO_LONG.search(e.message or ""))
AFFORD_TRIES = 3  # retries of one route at what its account can afford (see _handle)
_AFFORD = re.compile(r"can only afford (\d+)")  # OpenRouter: "You requested up to 599400 tokens, but can only afford 538612"


def affordable(e: BackendError) -> int | None:
    """The output tokens a provider says its account can pay for, when it refuses a request for asking more (HTTP 402)."""
    m = _AFFORD.search(e.message or "") if e.status == 402 else None
    return int(m.group(1)) if m and int(m.group(1)) > 0 else None
_TAG_PAIR = re.compile(r"^\s*([A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64})\s*=\s*([^,]{0,200}?)\s*$")


class GatewayError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status: int, message: str, kind: str = "invalid_request_error", headers: dict | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status
        self.message = message
        self.kind = kind
        self.headers = headers or {}


def error_body(fmt: str, status: int, message: str, kind: str) -> dict:
    if fmt == "anthropic":
        return {"type": "error", "error": {"type": kind, "message": message}}
    return {"error": {"message": message, "type": kind, "code": status}}


def error_response(fmt: str, status: int, message: str, kind: str = "api_error") -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse(error_body(fmt, status, message, kind), status_code=status)


EFFORT_ORDER = ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max")


def fit_effort(effort: str | None, accepted: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """The client's effort if the model accepts it, else the highest accepted level below it (or the lowest)."""
    if not effort or not accepted or effort not in EFFORT_ORDER:
        return None
    if effort in accepted:
        return effort
    rank = EFFORT_ORDER.index(effort)
    known = sorted((e for e in accepted if e in EFFORT_ORDER), key=EFFORT_ORDER.index)
    below = [e for e in known if EFFORT_ORDER.index(e) <= rank]
    return (below[-1] if below else known[0]) if known else None


def kind_for_status(status: int) -> str:
    return {400: "invalid_request_error", 401: "authentication_error", 403: "permission_error", 404: "not_found_error",

    tags: dict[str, str] = {}

        m = _TAG_PAIR.match(part)

            tags[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
