# 00 — How it all works (start here) Merit Order sits between your tools and the model providers. Your tools keep speaking the API they already speak; Merit Order translates when the chosen model speaks another. For every request sent with the model name `auto`, it asks two questions: 1. **How hard is this?** The request gets a **level** for its kind of work: coding or general, 1 to 5. 2. **What's the cheapest model that's good enough?** Every model has a **score** for each kind of work, 1 to 5. Models scoring at least the level, with room for the conversation, qualify, and the cheapest of those wins, counting the whole rest of the conversation, not just this request. Everything else in this document is detail on those two questions: how tools connect, where the levels, scores and prices come from, what "cheapest" really means, how long conversations are handled, what happens when something fails, and when your own GPUs are worth switching on. The numbers are from the live configuration on 11 November 2026; prices and scores refresh on their own, so yours will drift. A request that **names a model** (`claude-opus`, `gpt-sol`, …) skips both questions: it always gets that model, and Merit Order only chooses where to run it (section 10). ```mermaid flowchart LR T["Your tool
(any API format)"] --> R["Request
model: auto"] R --> L["2. Level
coding:3"] L --> Q["3–4. Models scoring ≥ 3,
with room, allowed for the team"] Q --> C["5. Cheapest for the rest
of the session"] C --> E["6. Effort and output limit
for that level"] E --> S["Send, translated if needed;
on failure, the next cheapest (8)"] ``` ## 1. Your tools connect as they are Point a tool's base URL at Merit Order and give it a Merit Order key. Nothing else about the tool changes, because Merit Order speaks both common APIs: | Your tool speaks | For example | Merit Order endpoint | |---|---|---| | Anthropic Messages | Claude Code, Anthropic SDKs | `/v1/messages` (and `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) | | OpenAI Chat Completions | pi, Cursor, OpenAI SDKs, most other tools | `/v1/chat/completions` | | OpenAI Responses | Codex CLI | `/v1/responses` | | Embeddings | RAG pipelines | `/v1/embeddings` | **The model's own format is Merit Order's problem, not the tool's.** Each provider speaks one of the two formats. When the tool and the chosen provider speak the same one, the request passes through untouched, so provider features such as Claude's cache markers and thinking signatures survive. When they differ, Merit Order converts the request, the reply and the stream both ways: messages, tool calls, images, streaming, usage and stop reasons. Two things don't cross: a model's reasoning from earlier turns (each turn still works; the model just thinks again), and `temperature`/`top_p`, which current Claude models reject. The Responses API is converted to Chat Completions inside the gateway; GPT models that need the Responses API for tools with reasoning are converted on the way out. **The model name says what you want:** - `auto`: Merit Order chooses (the rest of this document). - A model's name or one of its aliases: that model. Aliases cover the names tools already send, so `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` and `sonnet` all mean Claude Sonnet. - Anything else: an error saying the model isn't configured. `GET /v1/models` lists `auto` and every model your team may use, with each one's context window. **Every reply says what happened**, in headers: `X-MeritOrder-Model` (the model that answered), `X-MeritOrder-Backend` (the provider), `X-MeritOrder-Floor` (the level, for `auto`), `X-MeritOrder-Max-Tokens` and its source, `X-MeritOrder-Failed-Over` when a provider failed first, and for replies that aren't streamed `X-MeritOrder-Cost-Usd`. The console's Reports → Requests tab shows the model, provider, level and cost of every request. Setting up Claude Code and pi is in section 11. ## 2. Every request gets a level The level is how demanding the request is. It's worked out from the request itself, with simple rules and no model call, so it's instant and free: | The request | Level | |---|---| | Plain text, short (under ~400 tokens), no tools | general 1 | | Plain text | general 2 | | Plain text with words like analyze, compare, plan, strategy, trade-offs, evaluate or reason, or over 20,000 tokens long | general 3 | | Any tools, or text that looks like code (code fences, `def`, `import`, stack traces, file names, "refactor", "bug", SQL, …) | coding 3 | | 5 or more tools: an agent at work | coding 4 | | Coding with "hard" wording (architecture, race condition, security, performance, migration, concurrency, …) or over 60,000 tokens of context | one level higher, at most 5 | Clients can take over: `X-Route-Floor: coding:4` sets the level exactly, and `X-Route-Hint: cheap` or `smart` moves it one level down or up. Every `auto` response says what it got (`X-MeritOrder-Floor`). What that means in practice: | Request | Level | |---|---| | "What's the capital of Portugal?" | general 1 | | "Draft a reply to this customer email" (pasted) | general 2 | | "Compare these three vendor proposals" | general 3 | | "Why does this function return None?" with a code block | coding 3 | | A coding agent's turn: 20 tools, 30,000 tokens of conversation | coding 4 | | The same agent, 90,000 tokens into the session | coding 5 | **Claude Code's side jobs get lower levels.** Claude Code labels each request (when its hint headers are on; section 11): a turn of the conversation, a subagent's turn, the summary it writes when it compacts a long conversation, or a side request such as a session title or summary. Those last two don't need the level of the work itself, so `auto` caps them: | Claude Code request | Highest level | |---|---| | Side request (titles, summaries) | 1 | | Compaction summary | 3 | | Conversation or subagent turn | not capped | An explicit `X-Route-Floor` is never capped. Auto mode's permission checks name Claude Sonnet, so they never go through `auto` at all. The caps are under Config → Routing → Claude Code request types. The level rules themselves live in code (`src/meritorder/classifier.py`); the console doesn't show or change them yet. ## 3. Every model gets a score for each kind of work A score says how good a model is at a kind of work, **compared with the best model you have**. It isn't typed in: the worker works it out once a day from published benchmarks. **What a score means.** By default (source `epoch`), each model's score is based on its chance of solving a task as hard as **FrontierSWE**, a set of real, hard software-engineering tasks. The best model scores 5 and every other model scores in proportion: one that solves 60% as many such tasks as the best scores 3. | Model | Chance on a FrontierSWE-hard task (coding) | Coding score | General score | |---|---|---|---| | Claude Fable 5.2 | 70% | 5.0 | 5.0 | | Gemini 4 Carbon | 61% | 4.4 | not measured yet | | GPT-6.1 Terra | 62% | 4.4 * | 3.8 | | Claude Opus 5.5 | 58% | 4.2 | 3.9 | | GPT-6 Astra | 59% | 4.2 | 4.1 | | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 56% | 4.0 | 3.4 | | Gemini 4 Argon | 48% | 3.4 | 3.4 | | GPT-6.1 Sol | 46% | 3.3 | 4.0 | | Claude Haiku 5.5 | 41% | 3.0 | 2.0 | | GPT-6 Luna | 32% | 2.3 | 1.3 | | Gemini 3.8 Flash | 24% | 1.7 | 1.6 | | Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite | 4% | 1.0 * | 1.0 | \* Estimated from the model's general ability: no coding results published yet. **Where the numbers come from.** [Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/benchmarks) (CC BY 4.0) places every model on one ability scale, fitted across about 40 benchmarks, and every benchmark on the same scale by difficulty. That's what makes models comparable even when they were tested on different benchmarks, and lets a model's ability be turned into a chance of solving tasks of a given difficulty. For coding, a model's own results on FrontierSWE and FrontierCode refine its general ability, so coding strength counts; results at the effort `auto` uses for hard work are preferred where published. The alternative source is the [Artificial Analysis](https://artificialanalysis.ai) Intelligence Index (needs `ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY`). It's a single number per model, so coding and general get the same score. The third option is scores written on each model by hand (`config`), for example from your own eval runs ([11 — Evals](11-evals.md)). **Two choices shape the scores** (Config → Routing → Quality scores): - **Scale.** `best` (default): the best model is 5 and the rest in proportion; adding a weak model changes nobody else's score. `range`: the weakest model with data is 1 and the best 5, which depends on which weak models you happen to have configured. - **Reference task.** A harder reference spreads models further apart and sends more work up the ladder. Against Remote Labor Index (real paid remote work, which Fable solves 37% of the time), Opus would score 2.8 for general work, and ordinary level-3 work would go only to Fable. FrontierSWE keeps level 3 within reach of models like Sonnet. **Models the source doesn't cover** aren't picked by `auto`: a score nobody measured would compete with measured ones, and because the cheapest qualifying model wins, an optimistic guess would win. They still answer requests that name them. To put one back, give it a `quality_override` (Config → Models), which always wins over the source; that's also how to record that your own evals disagree with the benchmarks (Models → Evals → *Apply scores…* → *Write as override*). Measured scores use the same 1–5 scale, so the Evals page shows them beside the ones in use. On 11 November 2026, 11 open models weren't covered, among them Qwen3 Coder, Devstral and MiMo. Hover a score on the Models page to see how it was worked out. ## 4. Which models qualify A model qualifies for a request when: - its score for that kind of work is **at least the request's level**. A level-3 coding request can go to any model with a coding score of 3.0 or more; level 5 means "as good as the best", which today is only Fable; - the conversation **fits in its context window** (section 7); and - the team is allowed to use it (Config → Teams → allowed models and backends). ## 5. The cheapest qualifying route wins Each qualifying model has one or more **routes**: the providers that serve it (Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, your own GPUs, …). Merit Order prices every route and picks the cheapest. **Prices are live.** The worker refreshes them every 15 minutes: OpenRouter routes from OpenRouter's catalog, direct provider APIs from the price list LiteLLM maintains, cross-checked against each other. Long-prompt prices apply (Claude Haiku 5.5 costs five times as much above 100,000 prompt tokens), and a price change, a list that can't be fetched, or two lists that disagree raises an alert. **"Cheapest" means the rest of the session**, because in a conversation each turn resends everything before it, and providers charge far less for the part they still have cached: ``` cost of a route = rebuild + expected turns × cost per turn rebuild = what it costs to get this conversation into the provider's cache: zero if this provider already holds it, else the context at the full input price (or the cache-write price, for Claude, where caching is explicit), less the cache-read price the first turn already counts cost per turn = the cached part at the cache-read price + the new tokens at the input price (cache-write price for Claude): what the conversation grew by since its last turn, or about 2,000 for a new session + about 600 output tokens at the output price expected turns = the turns so far, kept between 3 and 30 (a long session will probably keep going) ``` Here's what that gives for a new coding session at level 3, 30,000 tokens in: | Model (route) | Score | Rebuild | Per turn | 3 turns | |---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Haiku 5.5 (Anthropic)** | 3.0 | $0.003 | $0.0008 | **$0.006** | | GPT-6.1 Terra (Azure) | 4.4 | $0.027 | $0.006 | $0.046 | | Gemini 4 Argon (OpenRouter) | 3.4 | $0.053 | $0.013 | $0.092 | | GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI) | 3.3 | $0.053 | $0.013 | $0.092 | And for an agent at level 4, 80,000 tokens in: | Model (route) | Score | Rebuild | Per turn | 3 turns | |---|---|---|---|---| | **GPT-6.1 Terra (Azure)** | 4.4 | $0.074 | $0.009 | **$0.101** | | Gemini 4 Carbon (OpenRouter) | 4.4 | $0.148 | $0.018 | $0.202 | | Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Anthropic) | 4.0 | $0.187 | $0.019 | $0.244 | | Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) | 4.2 | $0.374 | $0.038 | $0.487 | **Sessions stay put.** Once a session is on a route, the rebuild is already paid there, so moving it must save at least 10% plus $0.01 over the rest of the session. Within a task (while the tool is sending tool results back, before the next prompt from a person) the session keeps its model outright. In practice a session moves only when a new task starts and something is clearly cheaper, its cache has expired (after 5 idle minutes), the conversation was compacted, it no longer fits (section 7), or its model is busy or down on every route (section 8). That's what keeps a session from bouncing between Bedrock and Anthropic and paying to rebuild each time. **A session can hold several conversations.** Claude Code sends its subagents' turns and its side requests under the main session's id. Each keeps its own routing state (model, level, cache), so a subagent never resets the main conversation's; budgets, the per-session spend limit and reports still count the session as one. **Near-ties go to speed.** The same model often costs the same everywhere (Claude on Anthropic, Bedrock and Vertex), so price alone can't choose. Routes within a small margin of the cheapest compete on measured speed: 2% under the default `cost` priority (where a better model among them goes first), 20% under `balanced`, 100% under `speed`. A team or a single request (`X-MeritOrder-Priority`) can choose differently. Every 10th new session may try a route within that margin whose speed is unknown or out of date, so speeds stay known. **Unpriced routes never win** for `auto`: an unknown price must never look free. ## 6. Then: effort and output length **Reasoning effort** follows the level, so every model works the same way for the same work (their own defaults differ): low for levels 1–2, medium for 3, high for 4–5. A model that doesn't take that effort keeps its default. The effort is set once per session on a model, because changing it would invalidate the prompt cache. A client's own effort setting always wins; one sent in Anthropic's format (Claude Code sends one) to a GPT or other OpenAI-format model goes over at the nearest level that model takes. **Output length** isn't capped by a guess. A request without `max_tokens` may write as much as the model can (128,000 tokens for current Claude and GPT models), less what wouldn't fit in the context window, under the per-request cost limit (Controls), or within what a provider's prepaid balance covers. A client's own `max_tokens` is kept (lowered only to the model's maximum). The response says how much it got and why (`X-MeritOrder-Max-Tokens`, `X-MeritOrder-Max-Tokens-Source`). ## 7. Context windows: long conversations Every model has a **context window**: the most a conversation plus its reply can hold. The windows come from the live price data, refreshed with the prices: | Window | Models | |---|---| | about 1 million tokens | Claude (all), Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, MiMo, Muse Spark, Mistral Large 4, Qwen3.8 Flash, Nemotron 3.5 Super | | 922,000 | GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 (Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna) | | 524,288 | Llama 4 Maverick | | 262,144 | Qwen3 Coder (all three), Devstral 2, Mistral Small 4, Ministral 14B, Gemma 4 31B, Nemotron 3 Ultra | | 131,072 | gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b | Two parties decide what happens as a conversation grows: **the tool**, which decides when to compact (summarize the history and start over from the summary), and **Merit Order**, which decides where the conversation can still go. **What Merit Order does:** - **Models without room drop out.** For `auto`, a model whose window the conversation fills past 95% isn't a candidate (the token count is estimated at about 4 characters per token, and the reply needs room too). A 300,000-token conversation never goes to gpt-oss or Qwen3 Coder; most qualifying models have about a million tokens, so something always fits. - **A session that outgrows its model moves, even mid-task.** The next turn goes to a model with room at the same level, paying once to rebuild the cache there. - **A provider that says "too long" isn't the end.** If a provider refuses a prompt as too long anyway (the estimate can be off), an `auto` request goes to a qualifying model with a bigger window. A request that names a model can't move; its error is worded the way Anthropic's API words it ("prompt is too long: …"), whichever provider refused, because that's what makes Claude Code compact. - **The reply shrinks to fit.** When a request doesn't set `max_tokens`, the reply may use what's left of the window and no more, so the provider doesn't refuse prompt plus reply (section 6). **What the tool does.** A tool compacts when the conversation nears the window it believes it has. `/v1/models` reports each model's window, and for `auto` the largest window among the models `auto` can pick for your team (1,048,576 tokens today). That's safe because models without room drop out: a long conversation narrows the choice to the million-token models instead of failing. - **pi**: `meritorder setup pi` writes each model's window into pi's model list. - **Claude Code**: it knows the windows of Claude models by name. For a name it doesn't know, such as `auto`, it assumes 200,000 tokens unless told otherwise; `meritorder setup claude-code` tells it the gateway's window (section 11). - **Other tools**: give them the window from `/v1/models`, or leave their default; a smaller window than the real one only means compacting earlier. ## 8. When something fails Nothing reaches the client until the chosen route has started answering, so a failure moves the request on: - **Over capacity, rate-limited, missing, or down:** the next route in the cost ranking. For a named model, or a session in the middle of a task, that's another provider for the same model; for a new `auto` task, it's the next cheapest qualifying route, whatever its model. A request gets 3 tries at most (`routing.max_attempts`). An `auto` session whose model is busy or down on every route moves to another qualifying model at its next turn, even mid-task. The failing route is skipped for a while (the provider's `Retry-After`, or a growing back-off) and an alert says where its traffic went. - **Too long for the model:** for `auto`, a qualifying model with a bigger window (section 7). - **The model refuses:** for `auto`, the next qualifying model (the refusal is billed and logged); a named model's refusal is returned as it is. - **A provider can't cover the whole reply on its prepaid balance:** the same route again, asking for what it says it can pay for. - **Budgets and limits:** organization, team, person and session budgets, rate limits, and the per-request cost limit stop requests before they're sent, with a message saying which. Every rule and timing is in [10 — How it decides](10-how-it-decides.md). ## 9. Your own GPUs: when they start and stop Power grids run the cheapest generators all the time (baseload) and switch on expensive ones (peakers) only for peaks. Merit Order does the same: your own GPUs, running an open model, are the baseload when there's enough steady work to keep them busy, and the APIs are the peakers that are always there. **A GPU deployment starts only when sustained demand pays for it.** Every minute the controller asks: what does the traffic this model could serve cost me at API prices? - **Traffic it could serve** means requests whose level its score covers. A model with a coding score of 3.0 counts every coding request at levels 1–3, wherever it was actually sent. - **At API prices** means what you're paying for that traffic today. - One replica is worth starting when that spend, per hour, exceeds the replica's hourly price plus a 20% margin, **continuously for 10 minutes**. The number of replicas follows the throughput (enough to run at 70% load), as long as each one pays for itself by the same rule. For example, Qwen3 Coder Next on four H100s costs about $16 an hour per replica (SkyPilot's cheapest offer in the allowed clouds, or the configured fallback). It starts once the work it could do would cost you more than $19.20 an hour at API prices for 10 minutes straight. **While it runs, it's the first choice.** A GPU you're already paying for costs almost nothing per token while it has room, so the router prices it at 2% of the API price up to 60% load, rising to the full API price as it fills. Up to that point it wins every request it qualifies for; past it, the APIs take over, and at 100% new work spills to them. Requests that only went to the GPU because it had room (a better model than the level needed) don't count as demand, so idle capacity can't keep itself alive. **It stops when demand no longer pays for it.** When the work it could do drops below break-even for 10 minutes, and it has been running at least 30 minutes, it **drains**: no new sessions, existing ones finish, and after 15 minutes the GPUs are released. If demand comes back while draining, it simply stays. Starting takes 10–20 minutes for a big model, and traffic stays on the APIs meanwhile, so the delays and margins are there to avoid paying for start-ups that don't last. **A self-hosted model needs a score.** Demand is counted by level, so a model the quality source doesn't cover has none, and its GPUs never start for `auto` traffic. On 11 November 2026 that's the case for Qwen3 Coder Next: give it a `quality_override` (Config → Models) to have the controller consider it. Its window (262,144 tokens) also means conversations longer than about 249,000 tokens go to the APIs. **Whether a GPU can ever pay** shows on Models → **GPU break-even**: for each quality level and each open-weight model, the traffic one replica needs (tokens per minute and about how many requests an hour), your busiest hour of that traffic, and one replica's capacity. The price a GPU has to beat at a level is the cheapest API model good enough for it, because that's where `auto` would send the work otherwise. On 11 November 2026, with a $16-an-hour replica doing 4,000 tokens a second at 70% load ($1.59 per million tokens), that was never true below level 5: the cheapest good-enough API models for levels 1–4 cost $0.03–$0.92 per million tokens with this gateway's traffic mix (Fable-class level-5 work costs $7.31, but no open model scores high enough to take it). Admins can also stop a deployment (draining first or at once), pin a number of replicas, stop all GPUs, or cap GPU spend per month, per hour, or in replicas (GPUs page and Controls). Details: [05 — GPU autoscaling](05-gpu-autoscaling.md). ## 10. Requests that name a model A request for `claude-opus` gets Claude Opus, never another model. Merit Order still picks the route: the cheapest of Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and OpenRouter for the rest of the session, with the same stickiness, speed tie-breaks and failover between them. If none of its routes can run, the request fails with the reason for each, unless the team allows substituting a model at least as good. A named model is never skipped for its window: a conversation it can't hold gets the provider's error, worded so Claude Code compacts. Claude Code sends Claude model names unless it's set to `auto`, so by default it gets exactly what it asks for; `meritorder setup claude-code` sets it to `auto` (section 11). ## 11. Setting up Claude Code and pi Log in once (`meritorder login`, or `meritorder use-key` with a key from an admin), then: ```bash meritorder setup claude-code # Claude Code meritorder setup pi # pi ``` **Claude Code** isn't tied to Anthropic or Foundry: any gateway that speaks Anthropic's API can stand in via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and Merit Order does. The setup command writes these into Claude Code's settings file (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json`, or `~/.claude/settings.json`): | Setting | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | the gateway | Send every request to Merit Order | | `apiKeyHelper` | reads `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` | Your Merit Order key; logging in again rotates it | | `model` | `auto` | New sessions let Merit Order choose (`--model claude-sonnet-5-5` picks one; `--model none` leaves Claude Code's choice) | | `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` | the gateway's window for that model | Claude Code would otherwise assume 200,000 tokens for `auto` and compact early | | `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION`, `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME` | `auto`, `auto (Merit Order)` | Adds "auto (Merit Order)" to the `/model` picker | | `CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS` | `1` | Claude Code labels side requests and compaction only when asked (section 2) | With `--model` set to a Claude model name, it leaves out the window and `/model` settings (and removes earlier ones): Claude Code already knows those names. It changes every Claude Code session that uses that settings folder. To keep Merit Order in a separate profile (for example, away from work that uses another account): ```bash meritorder setup claude-code --config-dir ~/.claude-meritorder CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-meritorder claude ``` What to expect: - **Billing.** With the Merit Order key, Claude Code doesn't use your claude.ai login for these requests: subscription limits don't apply, and the cost is per token on the providers' accounts behind the gateway. - **Non-Claude models.** `auto` can send Claude Code's turns to GPT, Gemini or open models, translated. It works, but Anthropic doesn't support running Claude Code on non-Claude models, so expect rough edges. - **Cost display.** Claude Code's own cost figure guesses prices for a name it doesn't know (a test request it showed as $0.038 cost $0.0096). The gateway's numbers (My usage page, `meritorder usage`) are the real ones. - **Reply length.** For a model name it doesn't know, Claude Code asks for up to 32,000 output tokens per reply. `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` raises it (to 128,000 at most); Merit Order lowers a request to the chosen model's own maximum when that's smaller. - **Effort.** Claude Code sends its own reasoning effort (its `/effort` setting), and a client's setting always wins, so the per-level effort (section 6) doesn't apply to its turns. - **A startup line** `[claude-code:unrecognized_model] {"model":"auto"}` is informational. - **Subagents** each get their own routing thread within the session (section 5), and their own level. **pi** gets a "Merit Order" provider listing `auto` and every model with its context window, sends its session id so sessions stay on the backend that holds their cache, and adds cache markers that survive translation. **Codex CLI** and other OpenAI-compatible tools need only the base URL (`/v1`) and the key. ## 12. Where everything is set | What | Where in the console | In the config file | |---|---|---| | Quality source, scale, reference, refresh | Config → Routing → Quality scores | `quality:` | | A model's score override, its name in benchmark data | Config → Models | `quality_override`, `benchmark_name` | | The name that means "choose for me" | Config → Routing → Automatic routing | `routing.auto_model` | | How much cheaper a move must be | Config → Routing → Automatic routing | `routing.switch_margin_pct`, `switch_margin_usd` | | Expected turns and tokens per turn | Config → Routing → Automatic routing | `routing.min_expected_turns`, `est_output_tokens`, … | | Cost or speed | Config → Routing → Cost or speed; Config → Teams | `routing.priority`, team `priority` | | Effort by level | Config → Routing → Reasoning effort by task difficulty | `routing.effort_by_floor` | | Levels for Claude Code's side and compaction requests | Config → Routing → Claude Code request types | `routing.request_class_levels` | | GPU price curve | Config → Routing → Self-hosted pricing curve | `routing.shadow_knee`, `shadow_floor` | | Which models and providers a team may use | Config → Teams | `allowed_models`, `allowed_backends` | | Budgets, per-request cost limit | Controls; Config → Teams | `safeguards`, team budgets | | Routes, prices you've negotiated | Config → Models | `routes[].price` (an override) | | Context windows, output limits | live price data (Models page) | `context_window`, `max_output_tokens` (overrides) | | GPU deployments | Config → Backends; GPUs page | `backends.*.serve` | | How requests get a level | not yet in the console | `classifier.py` | | Pointing Claude Code or pi at the gateway | — | `meritorder setup claude-code` / `setup pi` | The Models page shows every model's live scores, prices and windows, with where each came from; Backends shows each route's measured speed and anything being skipped. ## 13. What `auto` does today The cheapest qualifying model for a typical request at each level, on 11 November 2026: | Level | Coding | General | |---|---|---| | 1 | GLM-5.3 Flash, gpt-oss-20b | GLM-5.3 Flash, gpt-oss-20b | | 2 | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 | Claude Haiku 5.5 | | 3 | Claude Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1 Terra | | 4 | GPT-6.1 Terra | GPT-6.1 Sol | | 5 | Claude Fable 5.2 only | Claude Fable 5.2 only | A Claude Code session on `auto` is coding level 4 (it always sends many tools): GPT-6.1 Terra, until the conversation passes 60,000 tokens and it becomes level 5 (Fable) at the next prompt. Its titles and summaries go to level-1 models, and compaction summaries to level-3 models. ## 14. Known gaps - **The level rules aren't in the console,** and they're keyword-based. A coding agent sending `auto` with more than 60,000 tokens of context lands on level 5, which today only Fable meets, at $8/$40 per million tokens. Clients that name a model aren't affected. - **Some scores are estimates.** A model without published coding results gets a coding score from its general ability (marked * on the Models page), and published results come from runs at different efforts. - **A threshold, not cost per solved task.** A cheaper model that solves a little less can still cost less per solved task than a dearer one. Merit Order now has each model's chance of solving hard work, so it could pick on expected cost per success; today it picks the cheapest model above the level, which is simpler to predict. - **Token counts for routing are estimates** (about 4 characters per token), so the window check can be off near the limit; a provider's "too long" is the backstop (section 7).

"""Provider keys from mounted files: picked up on change (no restart), with env fallback."""

import os

from meritorder.backends.auth import ApiKeyAuth
from meritorder.config import BackendAuth, BackendConfig, Config, read_secret_file


def write(path, text, bump=0):
    path.write_text(text)
    st = os.stat(path)
    os.utime(path, ns=(st.st_atime_ns, st.st_mtime_ns + bump))  # make sure the change is visible


async def test_rotated_key_file_is_used_on_the_next_request(tmp_path):
    f = tmp_path / "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
    write(f, "sk-old\n")
    auth = ApiKeyAuth(BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_file=str(f)))
    assert auth.available()
    assert (await auth.apply("POST", "u", {}, b""))["authorization"] == "Bearer sk-old"
    write(f, "sk-new-longer", bump=1_000_000)
    assert (await auth.apply("POST", "u", {}, b""))["authorization"] == "Bearer sk-new-longer"


def test_kubernetes_style_symlink_swap(tmp_path):
    """A mounted Secret's file is a symlink into a ..data directory that Kubernetes swaps atomically."""
    v1, v2 = tmp_path / "..2026_11_01", tmp_path / "..2026_11_09"
    v1.mkdir(), v2.mkdir()
    (v1 / "KEY").write_text("first")
    (v2 / "KEY").write_text("second")
    os.utime(v2 / "KEY", ns=(1, 2_000_000_000_000_000_000))
    data = tmp_path / "..data"
    data.symlink_to(v1.name)
    (tmp_path / "KEY").symlink_to("..data/KEY")
    assert read_secret_file(str(tmp_path / "KEY")) == "first"
    tmp = tmp_path / "..data_tmp"
    tmp.symlink_to(v2.name)
    os.replace(tmp, data)
    assert read_secret_file(str(tmp_path / "KEY")) == "second"


def test_file_falls_back_to_env_and_explains_what_is_missing(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    missing = str(tmp_path / "nope")
    spec = BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_file=missing, value_env="MO_TEST_KEY")
    monkeypatch.delenv("MO_TEST_KEY", raising=False)
    assert spec.key() is None and spec.describe() == f"{missing} or MO_TEST_KEY"
    monkeypatch.setenv("MO_TEST_KEY", "from-env")
    assert spec.key() == "from-env"
    empty = tmp_path / "empty"
    empty.write_text("  \n")
    assert BackendAuth(type="api_key", value_file=str(empty), value_env="MO_TEST_KEY").key() == "from-env"

    monkeypatch.delenv("MO_TEST_KEY")
    from meritorder.config import _disable_unusable_backends

    cfg = Config(backends=[BackendConfig(name="p", format="openai", base_url="https://x.test/v1", auth=spec)], models=[])
    _disable_unusable_backends(cfg, quiet=True)
    assert not cfg.backends[0].enabled and cfg.backends[0].disabled_reason == f"{missing} or MO_TEST_KEY is not set"


def test_stored_config_may_reference_key_files():
    from meritorder.configstore import secret_problems

    doc = {"backends": {"p": {"format": "openai", "auth": {"type": "api_key", "value_file": "/run/secrets/meritorder/K"}}}}
    assert secret_problems(doc) == []
    doc["backends"]["p"]["auth"]["value"] = "sk-literal"
    assert secret_problems(doc)

"""Console endpoints: scoping (team lead vs organization), the merit stack, backend health, teams, and attention items."""

import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

from conftest import ADMIN_KEY, LEAD_KEY, auth, ledger_row

from meritorder.backends.mock import MockBackend
from meritorder.config import BackendConfig, ModelConfig, Route, ServeConfig


async def get(client, path, key=ADMIN_KEY, **params):
    r = await client.get(path, params=params, headers=auth(key))
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


async def seed_spend(gateway, team="default", cost=85.0, user="alice"):
    await gateway.store.record(ledger_row(user_id=user, team=team, actual_cost=cost, baseline_cost=cost * 2,
                                          savings_routing=cost, input_tokens=1000, cache_read_tokens=3000, output_tokens=200))
    await gateway.store.rollup()


def titles(att):
    return [i["title"] for i in att["items"]]


async def test_every_console_endpoint_needs_a_lead(client):
    for path in ("overview", "merit", "feed", "backends", "teams", "attention"):
        assert (await client.get(f"/v1/console/{path}", headers=auth())).status_code == 403, path
        assert (await client.get(f"/v1/console/{path}")).status_code == 401, path


async def test_overview_scope_budget_and_cache_hit_rate(client, gateway):
    await seed_spend(gateway, "default", 40.0)
    await seed_spend(gateway, "ops", 10.0, user="carol")
    org = await get(client, "/v1/console/overview")
    assert org["scope"] == "organization" and org["month"]["spend"] == 50.0 and org["today"]["requests"] == 2
    assert org["month"]["cache_hit_rate"] == 0.75  # 3000 cached of 4000 prompt tokens
    assert org["month"]["savings_by_cause"]["routing"] == 50.0
    lead = await get(client, "/v1/console/overview", LEAD_KEY)
    assert lead["scope"] == "default" and lead["month"]["spend"] == 40.0 and lead["budget"] == 100
    elapsed = (datetime.now(UTC) - datetime.now(UTC).replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)).total_seconds()
    assert (lead["forecast"] is None) == (elapsed <= 0.25 * 86400)


async def test_overview_with_no_traffic(client, gateway):
    ov = await get(client, "/v1/console/overview")
    assert ov["today"] == {"spend": 0, "baseline": 0, "saved": 0, "requests": 0, "cache_hit_rate": 0}
    assert ov["requests_per_minute"] == 0


async def test_merit_stack_orders_by_price_and_flags_gpus(client, gateway):
    gpu = MockBackend(BackendConfig(name="gpu", kind="self_hosted", format="openai", mock_latency_ms=0))
    gateway.backends["gpu"] = gpu
    gateway.cfg.models.append(ModelConfig(name="coder", quality={"coding": 4}, routes=[Route(backend="gpu", model="m")]))
    for model, cost, tokens in (("big", 3.0, 100_000), ("coder", 0.01, 400_000), ("small", 0.05, 100_000), ("idle", 1.0, 0)):
        await gateway.store.record(ledger_row(served_model=model, actual_cost=cost, input_tokens=tokens))
    m = await get(client, "/v1/console/merit", minutes=15)
    assert [t["model"] for t in m["tiers"]] == ["coder", "small", "big"]  # cheapest per token first; no-token rows dropped
    assert [t["gpu"] for t in m["tiers"]] == [True, False, False]
    assert m["clearing_price_per_m"] == m["tiers"][-1]["price_per_m"] == 30.0
    assert abs(m["blended_price_per_m"] - 3.06 / 600_000 * 1e6) < 1e-9
    assert (await client.get("/v1/console/merit?minutes=0", headers=auth(ADMIN_KEY))).status_code == 422
    empty = await get(client, "/v1/console/merit", LEAD_KEY, minutes=1)
    assert empty["tiers"] == [] or all(t["requests"] for t in empty["tiers"])


async def test_feed_limit_and_team_filter(client, gateway):
    for i in range(5):
        await gateway.state.push_event({"i": i, "team": "default" if i % 2 else "ops"})
    assert [e["i"] for e in (await get(client, "/v1/console/feed", limit=2))["events"]] == [4, 3]
    lead = (await get(client, "/v1/console/feed", LEAD_KEY, limit=10))["events"]
    assert [e["i"] for e in lead] == [3, 1]


async def test_backends_health_circuit_and_reasons(client, gateway):
    now = time.time()
    for _ in range(3):
        gateway.backends["mock-openai"].record_failure(now)
    gateway.backends["mock-anthropic"].draining = True
    await gateway.state.record_backend("mock-anthropic", True, 200, 50)
    await gateway.state.record_backend("mock-anthropic", False, 400, None)
    gateway.cfg.backends.append(BackendConfig(name="off", format="openai", base_url="https://off.example.com/v1",
                                              enabled=False, disabled_reason="OFF_KEY is not set"))
    b = {x["name"]: x for x in (await get(client, "/v1/console/backends", LEAD_KEY))["backends"]}

    assert b["off"]["live"] is False and b["off"]["reason"] == "OFF_KEY is not set" and b["off"]["host"] == "off.example.com"
    assert b["off"]["avg_latency_ms"] is None and b["off"]["avg_ttft_ms"] is None


async def test_teams_spend_next_to_limits(client, gateway):

async def test_attention_backend_problems(client, gateway):
    for _ in range(3):
        gateway.backends["mock-openai"].record_failure(time.time())

        await gateway.state.record_backend("mock-anthropic", ok, 100, None)
    att = await get(client, "/v1/console/attention")
    assert titles(att)[0] == "mock-openai is failing" and att["items"][0]["level"] == "critical"
    assert "mock-anthropic: 40% errors" in titles(att)


async def test_attention_budgets(client, gateway):
    await seed_spend(gateway, "default", 85.0)
    att = await get(client, "/v1/console/attention", LEAD_KEY)
    [item] = [i for i in att["items"] if i["title"].startswith("Team default")]
    assert item["level"] == "warning" and "85%" in item["title"]
    await seed_spend(gateway, "default", 20.0)

    # Team leads don't see organization-wide budgets.
    assert not any("Organization" in t for t in titles(await get(client, "/v1/console/attention", LEAD_KEY)))


async def test_attention_gpu_items(client, gateway):

                                              serve=ServeConfig(model="small", provisioner="static", static_url="http://a/v1")))
    gateway.cfg.backends.append(BackendConfig(name="gpu-b", kind="self_hosted", format="openai",
                                              serve=ServeConfig(model="small", provisioner="static", static_url="http://b/v1")))
    await gateway.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-a", {"state": "warm", "reason": "stop failed: cloud API timeout"})
    await gateway.state.set_json("deploy:gpu-b", {"state": "api_only", "reason": "provision failed: no capacity"})
    att = await get(client, "/v1/console/attention")

    assert [(i["title"], i["level"]) for i in gpu_items] == [("GPU deployment gpu-a", "critical"), ("GPU deployment gpu-b", "warning")]

    await gateway.state.set_json("controller:heartbeat", {"at": time.time(), "host": "c", "interval": 60})
    assert "Capacity controller is not running" not in titles(await get(client, "/v1/console/attention"))
    levels = [i["level"] for i in att["items"]]
    assert levels == sorted(levels, key={"critical": 0, "warning": 1, "info": 2}.get)


async def test_attention_recent_alerts_scoped_and_aged(client, gateway):
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    await gateway.state.push_alert({"ts": (now - timedelta(hours=30)).isoformat(), "title": "old", "level": "warning"})
    await gateway.state.push_alert({"ts": now.isoformat(), "title": "ops only", "team": "ops", "level": "info"})
    await gateway.state.push_alert({"ts": now.isoformat(), "title": "everyone", "level": "warning", "page": "teams"})
    await gateway.state.push_alert({"title": "no timestamp"})
    await gateway.state.push_alert({"ts": "not a date", "title": "bad timestamp"})
    org = titles(await get(client, "/v1/console/attention"))
    assert "everyone" in org and "ops only" in org and "old" not in org and "no timestamp" not in org
    lead = titles(await get(client, "/v1/console/attention", LEAD_KEY))
    assert "everyone" in lead and "ops only" not in lead

# 06 — Auth & spend ## Getting a key into pi and Claude Code Harnesses can't do interactive SSO, so people log in once with the CLI and get a short-lived **virtual key** tied to their identity. The harness sends it like any API key. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant CLI as meritorder CLI participant E as Entra ID (OIDC) participant G as Gateway participant P as Postgres U->>CLI: meritorder login CLI->>E: Device-code flow E-->>U: "Go to microsoft.com/devicelogin, enter code" U->>E: Signs in (MFA, conditional access) E-->>CLI: ID token (user, groups) CLI->>G: POST /auth/exchange G->>G: Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience G->>P: Map groups → team and role G->>P: Create virtual key (expires in 30 days) G-->>CLI: Virtual key CLI->>CLI: Save to ~/.config/meritorder/api_key (mode 600) U->>CLI: meritorder setup pi / setup claude-code ``` ```bash meritorder login --gateway https://llm.example.com # or: meritorder use-key meritorder setup pi # adds a "meritorder" provider to ~/.pi/agent/models.json meritorder setup claude-code # sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and apiKeyHelper in ~/.claude/settings.json ``` Both harness configs read the key from `~/.config/meritorder/api_key` at request time (`!cat ...` for pi, `apiKeyHelper` for Claude Code), so logging in again rotates the key without touching them. pi is configured to send its session ID as `X-Session-Id` and to add cache breakpoints, which Merit Order uses for sticky routing and caching. How the gateway knows who's calling: every request carries a key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`). The gateway hashes it, looks it up (cached for a minute), and gets the user, team, and role, which drive budgets, policy, and reports. Unknown, revoked, or expired keys get a 401. | Client | Auth | |---|---| | People with harnesses | `meritorder login` → virtual key (above) | | Services / apps | An Entra token directly as the bearer token, or a key from `meritorder keys create` | | Local dev / quickstart | `MERITORDER_DEV_KEY` (static admin key from the environment) | | Google (later) | Another OIDC issuer: same code path | Entra login switches on when `MERITORDER_OIDC_ISSUER` and `MERITORDER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` are set; map Entra group IDs to teams and roles in `auth.oidc` in the config. SCIM (later) revokes keys when people leave. ## People and teams | What | Where it's managed | |---|---| | Who exists, and their group membership | Your identity provider (Entra). People are created in Merit Order the first time they sign in with `meritorder login` (or when an admin issues them a key). | | Teams, with budgets, limits, and model policy | Merit Order: Config → Teams. An IdP has no notion of "$5,000 a month, these models only". | | Which team and role someone gets | Entra groups mapped to teams and roles in Config → Access, re-read at each sign-in. | | Exceptions | The People page: an admin can move someone, change their role (that pins it, so later sign-ins don't override it), let Entra decide again, or disable them. | The user record, not the key, decides a person's team and role. Moving or disabling someone takes effect within a minute on every gateway, including keys they already have. Planned: SCIM, so Entra pushes changes (including people who leave) without waiting for a sign-in. ## Budgets ```mermaid flowchart TD ORG["Org budget
$/month"] --> T1["Team: platform
$/month"] ORG --> T2["Team: data-science
$/month"] T1 --> U1["User budget"] T1 --> U2["User budget"] T2 --> U3["User budget"] U1 --> K1["Key"] U1 --> K2["Key"] ``` - A request must fit **every** level above it. - Each request **reserves** an estimate up front (Redis counter) and **settles** to actual cost after the response. Postgres is the source of truth; Redis counters are reconciled async. - Soft limit → warn (response header, notification). Hard limit → reject or downgrade to a cheaper model, per team policy. - Policy lives alongside budgets: allowed models, allowed providers, data residency (e.g. "DeepSeek weights only self-hosted or on Bedrock, never the vendor API"). ## Limits that stop runaway spend | Setting (per team) | What it does | |---|---| | `budget_usd_month`, `user_budget_usd_month` | Monthly caps; requests are refused at 100% (alerts at 80%) | | `max_session_usd` | Stops one session (typically an agent stuck in a loop) once it has spent this much | | `rate_limits: {user_rpm, user_tpm, team_rpm, team_tpm}` | Requests and prompt tokens per minute; 429 with `Retry-After` | ## What gets charged | Backend | Charged to the user's budget | |---|---| | API | Actual provider cost (cached / uncached / output tokens) | | Self-hosted | Chargeback: GPU-hour cost split by tokens served (so it's fair, not $0) | Budgets use chargeback; the router uses marginal cost. They answer different questions. ## The savings ledger One row per request, written async: | Field | Example | |---|---| | user, team, session | | | model requested / floor / served | `auto` / `coding:3` / `qwen3-coder-480b` | | backend | `self/qwen3-coder/replica-2` | | tokens: uncached in / cached in / out | 2,100 / 118,000 / 640 | | **actual marginal cost** | $0.0004 | | **chargeback cost** | $0.0090 | | **counterfactual cost** (floor model on API, no proxy caching) | $0.3700 | | upgraded for free? | yes | This is the dashboard that sells the project: *"$X spent, $Y avoided, Z% of requests upgraded at no cost."* How savings are calculated and reported is in [08 — Reporting](08-reporting.md).

"""Live data for the control panel (the Dispatch page and friends).

Admins and finance see the whole organization; team leads see their own team.
Users don't get these endpoints (they have /v1/reports/me).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, Request

from .auth import AuthError, Principal
from .config import effort_format
from .store import month_start


def build_router(gateway) -> APIRouter:
    router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1/console", tags=["console"])

    async def principal(request: Request) -> Principal:
        try:
            p = await gateway.authn.authenticate({k.lower(): v for k, v in request.headers.items()})
        except AuthError as e:
            raise HTTPException(e.status, e.message)
        if not p.at_least("team_lead"):
            raise HTTPException(403, "the control panel is for team leads, finance, and admins")
        return p

    def team_scope(p: Principal) -> str | None:
        return None if p.at_least("finance") else p.team

    @router.get("/overview")
    async def overview(request: Request):
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        today = now.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
        tomorrow = today + timedelta(days=1)
        store = gateway.store

        async def totals(start):
            rows = await store.summary(start, tomorrow, "none", team=team)
            return rows[0] if rows else None

        t_today, t_month = await totals(today), await totals(month_start(now))
        teams = [t for t in gateway.cfg.teams if team is None or t.name == team]
        budget = sum(t.budget_usd_month or 0 for t in teams) or None
        elapsed_days = (now - month_start(now)).total_seconds() / 86400
        days_in_month = ((month_start(now) + timedelta(days=32)).replace(day=1) - month_start(now)).days
        month_spend = t_month["actual_cost"] if t_month else 0.0
        health = await gateway.state.backend_health(list(gateway.backends), minutes=5)
        rpm = sum(h["requests"] for h in health.values()) / 5

        def pack(t):
            if not t:
                return {"spend": 0, "baseline": 0, "saved": 0, "requests": 0, "cache_hit_rate": 0}
            prompt = t["input_tokens"] + t["cache_read_tokens"] + t["cache_write_tokens"]
            return {"spend": t["actual_cost"], "baseline": t["baseline_cost"], "saved": t["savings_total"],
                    "requests": t["requests"], "cache_hit_rate": t["cache_read_tokens"] / prompt if prompt else 0,
                    "savings_by_cause": {c: t.get(f"savings_{c}", 0) for c in
                                         ("routing", "caching", "self_hosting", "compression", "response_cache")}}

        return {
            "scope": team or "organization",
            "today": pack(t_today),
            "month": pack(t_month),
            "budget": budget,
            "forecast": month_spend / elapsed_days * days_in_month if elapsed_days > 0.25 else None,
            "requests_per_minute": round(rpm, 1),
            "gateways": await gateway.state.live_gateways(),
            "config_version": gateway.config_version,
        }

    @router.get("/merit")
    async def merit(request: Request, minutes: int = Query(15, ge=1, le=240)):
        """The dispatch stack: models in order of what a token actually cost, widths = tokens served."""
        p = await principal(request)
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        rows = await gateway.store.summary(now - timedelta(minutes=minutes), now + timedelta(seconds=1), "model", team=team_scope(p))
        gpu_models = {m.name for m in gateway.cfg.models for r in m.routes
                      if r.backend in gateway.backends and gateway.backends[r.backend].kind == "self_hosted"
                      and gateway.backends[r.backend].available}
        tiers = []
        for r in rows:
            tokens = r["input_tokens"] + r["cache_read_tokens"] + r["cache_write_tokens"] + r["output_tokens"]
            if tokens <= 0:
                continue
            tiers.append({"model": r["key"], "tokens": tokens, "tokens_per_second": tokens / (minutes * 60),
                          "cost": r["actual_cost"], "price_per_m": r["actual_cost"] / tokens * 1e6,
                          "requests": r["requests"], "gpu": r["key"] in gpu_models})
        tiers.sort(key=lambda t: t["price_per_m"])
        total = sum(t["tokens"] for t in tiers)
        meaningful = [t for t in tiers if total and t["tokens"] / total >= 0.01]
        return {"minutes": minutes, "demand_tokens_per_second": total / (minutes * 60), "tiers": tiers,
                "clearing_price_per_m": meaningful[-1]["price_per_m"] if meaningful else None,
                "blended_price_per_m": sum(t["cost"] for t in tiers) / total * 1e6 if total else None}

    @router.get("/feed")
    async def feed(request: Request, limit: int = Query(60, ge=1, le=500)):
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        events = await gateway.state.recent_events(500 if team else limit)
        if team:
            events = [e for e in events if e.get("team") == team][:limit]
        return {"events": events}

    @router.get("/backends")
    async def backends(request: Request, minutes: int = Query(5, ge=1, le=30)):
        await principal(request)
        names = [b.name for b in gateway.cfg.backends]
        health = await gateway.state.backend_health(names, minutes=minutes)
        now = time.time()
        out = []
        for b in gateway.cfg.backends:
            live = gateway.backends.get(b.name)
            h = health.get(b.name, {})
            n = h.get("requests", 0)
            out.append({
                "name": b.name, "kind": b.kind, "format": b.format, "host": urlparse(b.base_url).hostname if b.base_url else None,
                "enabled": b.enabled, "live": bool(live and live.available), "reason": b.disabled_reason,
                "circuit_open": bool(live and not live.healthy(now)), "draining": bool(live and live.draining),
                "effort_format": effort_format(b),
                "models": sorted({m.name for m in gateway.cfg.models for r in m.routes if r.backend == b.name}),
                "requests": int(n), "errors": int(h.get("errors", 0)),
                "error_rate": h.get("errors", 0) / n if n else 0.0,
                "avg_latency_ms": h.get("latency_ms", 0) / n if n else None,
                "avg_ttft_ms": h.get("ttft_ms", 0) / h["ttft_n"] if h.get("ttft_n") else None,
            })
        return {"minutes": minutes, "backends": out}

    @router.get("/attention")
    async def attention(request: Request):
        p = await principal(request)
        team = team_scope(p)
        items = []
        health = await gateway.state.backend_health(list(gateway.backends), minutes=5)
        now = time.time()
        for name, b in gateway.backends.items():
            h = health.get(name, {})
            n, errs = h.get("requests", 0), h.get("errors", 0)
            if not b.healthy(now):
                items.append({"level": "critical", "title": f"{name} is failing", "detail": "Circuit open after repeated errors; traffic goes to other backends.", "page": "backends"})
            elif n >= 5 and errs / n >= 0.2:
                items.append({"level": "warning", "title": f"{name}: {errs / n:.0%} errors", "detail": f"{int(errs)} of {int(n)} requests failed in the last 5 minutes.", "page": "backends"})
        start = month_start()
        by_team = {r["key"]: r["actual_cost"] for r in await gateway.store.summary(start, datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1), "team", team=team)}
        for t in gateway.cfg.teams:
            if t.budget_usd_month and (team is None or t.name == team):
                used = by_team.get(t.name, 0.0) / t.budget_usd_month
                if used >= 0.8:
                    items.append({"level": "critical" if used >= 1 else "warning", "title": f"Team {t.name} at {used:.0%} of budget",
                                  "detail": f"${by_team.get(t.name, 0):,.2f} of ${t.budget_usd_month:,.0f} this month.", "page": "teams"})
        for b in gateway.cfg.backends:
            if b.kind == "self_hosted" and b.serve is not None and b.enabled:
                rec = await gateway.state.get_json(f"deploy:{b.name}") or {}
                if "failed" in (rec.get("reason") or ""):
                    items.append({"level": "warning", "title": f"GPU deployment {b.name}", "detail": rec["reason"], "page": "gpus"})
        cutoff = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(hours=24)
        for a in await gateway.state.recent_alerts(20):
            try:
                ts = datetime.fromisoformat(a["ts"])
            except (KeyError, ValueError):
                continue
            if ts >= cutoff and (team is None or a.get("team") in (None, team)):
                items.append({"level": a.get("level", "info"), "title": a.get("title", "Alert"), "detail": a.get("text", ""), "page": a.get("page"), "ts": a["ts"]})
        order = {"critical": 0, "warning": 1, "info": 2}
        items.sort(key=lambda i: order.get(i["level"], 3))
        return {"items": items}

    return router
